why_it_matters: Investment control/influence tests catch nominees, investment managers acting for the Principal, and controlled trusts/companies, so routing the collar or loan through a related vehicle does not escape the Policy.

company: PM CAPITAL GLOBAL OPPORTUNITIES FUND LIMITED
clause: Each trading window opens one hour after the Company announces to the ASX its estimated Net Tangible Assets and closes at the end of the last Trading Day before the day on which the Company announces its next estimated Net Tangible Asset value.
why_it_matters: Because NTA is announced weekly and monthly, the default 'open' trading window is narrow and recurring; even if consent for a collar were obtained, execution timing would still need to fit within these short windows and outside the separate results/DRP/buy-back Blackout Periods.

clause: No person shall purchase or sell or otherwise monetize securities of the Company while in possession of Undisclosed Material Information.
why_it_matters: This is the only clause that plainly reaches an OTC collar (naming 'monetize'), but it only bars entry while the individual holds undisclosed material information; the separate quarterly blackout provision is worded narrower ('purchasing or selling') and does not on its face use the word 'monetize', creating a textual gap for collar entry during the blackout window if no MNPI is held.

clause: The Policy imposes no requirement to seek clearance or give notice before dealing, other than the Chief Executive Officer's written consent needed to deal during a blackout period.
why_it_matters: Outside the quarterly blackout and while free of undisclosed material information, a director or executive can enter, unwind or roll a collar without company approval, which simplifies timing but leaves the bank with no company sign-off trail confirming the trade is compliant.

clause: This Policy covers all written or oral communications and applies to any director, officer or employee of the Company. It also applies to any consultant or contractor (a 'Representative').
why_it_matters: Spouses, trusts and controlled entities are not mentioned, so routing the collar or its security through a related vehicle is not addressed or restricted by the document.

clause: the Company complies with its timely disclosure obligations as required under applicable Canadian securities laws, including the Securities Act (British Columbia)
why_it_matters: The Policy is drafted for a TSX-listed, BCSC-regulated issuer with no reference to ASX Listing Rules or the Australian insider trading regime, so an Australian bank should confirm which regime actually governs the executive's holding before relying on this document alone.

topic: silence on secured financing and derivatives
clause: (No provision addresses margin loans, pledges, encumbrances, derivatives, hedging, short selling, stock lending or CFDs.)
why_it_matters: None of the structural elements of a funded collar (the put, the call, or the loan secured on the shares) is expressly prohibited, permitted or made subject to clearance, so the transaction is not blocked by the Policy but also receives no express safe harbour.

topic: outright hedging ban on held securities
clause: Directors, key management personnel and any other designated Restricted Persons covered under this policy are also prohibited from entering into any transaction to hedge securities held in the Company.
why_it_matters: This is an absolute, non-waivable ban with no clearance route; a purchased put and written call are squarely a hedge of securities held, so a funded collar cannot be structured for directors, KMP or any other designated Restricted Person even with company consent.

clause: Directors, officers and employees of the Company are prohibited from entering into arrangements for the hedging, or otherwise limiting their exposure to risk in relation to unvested shares, options or rights issued or acquired under the Company's employee equity scheme.
why_it_matters: Closes off a collar over unvested equity incentives for the entire workforce, not just Restricted Persons, so vesting must complete before any collar discussion.

clause: a disposal of securities that is a result of a secured lender exercising its rights, for example, under a margin loan arrangement [is excluded from the operation of the share trading policy].
why_it_matters: Suggests the loan/security leg of a structure is not itself barred by the trading policy (only the derivative hedge legs are), though enforcement remains subject to general insider trading law and could occur while the executive holds inside information.

clause: clearance may be given for a Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) securities when they would otherwise be prohibited from doing so
why_it_matters: Even where a closed-period exception is granted for hardship or court order, it only ever permits a sale, so collar legs (a purchased put and a written call) could not be entered under this route during a Closed Period.

clause: the Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or employees and/or their respective associated parties trading in Company securities at any time.
why_it_matters: An unscheduled, discretionary embargo could freeze collar entry, unwind or roll at any time, with no stated notice period or confidentiality treatment.

clause: Each Restricted Person has a personal responsibility to ensure that their 'associated parties' ... complies with the same respective restrictions as apply to Restricted Persons
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its security through a spouse, family company or trust does not avoid the hedging ban or Closed Period restrictions.

clause: A clearance to trade can be given, withdrawn, or refused without a reason being given. The decision is final and binding. Any clearance refusal or withdrawal must be kept confidential by the person who sought clearance, and may not be disclosed to anyone.
why_it_matters: Even though both collar legs and the loan are only subject to clearance (not an outright ban), the Company Secretary's decision cannot be reasoned, appealed, or discussed once refused, so a bank should plan for the possibility of an unexplained rejection with no recourse.

topic: both collar legs and the loan are separately gated
clause: may not enter into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding LIT Units, unless prior clearance ... may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved
why_it_matters: The derivative hedge and the secured loan are each independently subject to the same five-business-day clearance, so both must be documented, cleared and executed within that narrow window for the structure to close.

topic: Connected Persons must clear through sponsor
clause: a Connected Person must seek clearance through their EQT Person, LIT Person or LIT Partner in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure prior to trading in Units.
why_it_matters: A family trust or related entity cannot independently apply for clearance to enter the collar or grant security; the application must run through the individual's own EQT/LIT Person channel.

topic: broad insider trading scope across vehicles
clause: For the avoidance of doubt, all forms of insider trading in relation to the Units of any entity or vehicle are prohibited.
why_it_matters: Suggests the Responsible Entity treats economic exposure obtained via any vehicle -- potentially including a bank's OTC derivative book -- as within the insider trading prohibition, reinforcing that clearance and inside-information checks apply regardless of how the collar is structured.

clause: LIT Partners and LIT Persons may trade in a LIT's Units provided ... the trade has been executed in accordance with the LIT Partner's trading policy, procedures and/or controls which have been agreed with the Responsible Entity [yet section 6 separately names LIT Partners as needing the Responsible Entity's own Trading Request Procedure clearance for hedging, margin lending and short-term trading].
why_it_matters: It is unclear whether an external LIT Partner seeking a funded collar over its own LIT Unit holding applies to its own internal compliance function or to the Responsible Entity's Company Secretary; written confirmation of the applicable regime should be obtained before relying on either clearance.

clause: EQT Persons who have knowledge of the buy-back and are involved in the day to day management of the buy-back, are subject to a further Black-out Period commencing from the date the Responsible Entity makes the decision to buy-back the units in a LIT, to the next full business day after the buy-back has been completed.
why_it_matters: An unscheduled buy-back-related blackout for informed EQT Persons could freeze collar entry, unwind or roll for a period whose length tracks the buy-back timetable rather than the standard quarterly/annual calendar.

topic: derivatives named in Closed Period ban
clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in DTL securities (nor trade in financial products issued or created over, or in respect of, DTL securities) during the following Closed Periods
why_it_matters: The put/call legs of a collar are expressly caught by the Closed Period ban but are otherwise unrestricted outside the two Closed Periods (absent Inside Information), so timing -- not an outright ban -- is the primary constraint on a funded collar.

clause: If a Restricted Person enters into a margin lending arrangement involving DTL shares or otherwise encumbers DTL shares (a "Security Arrangement"), then the Restricted Person must provide details of the Security Arrangement to the Chairman ... immediately.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is not prohibited but triggers an immediate written disclosure obligation, and DTL may separately need to notify the ASX if the number of shares involved is material.

topic: forced sale permitted at any time
clause: A Restricted Person may sell securities at any time where the disposal is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights under a margin lending or similar arrangement.
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is expressly permitted even during a Closed or Prohibited Period, giving the lender a clear, policy-sanctioned right to liquidate the collateral regardless of the executive's own trading restrictions at the time.

clause: (the terms 'hedge' and 'hedging' do not appear anywhere in the Policy)
why_it_matters: A collar is analysed purely as 'dealing'/'trading' in DTL securities or financial products over them; the Closed Period and 12-month short-term rules are the operative constraints, not a separate hedging prohibition.

clause: A Restricted Person must immediately notify the Chairman or the Company Secretary in writing if he or she receives a margin call that can only be satisfied by the sale of DTL's securities.
why_it_matters: If the bank's facility has margin-call mechanics rather than being fully secured to a fixed level, any call forcing a sale must be reported immediately even though clearance for the sale itself is not required.

clause: GPG Persons may at any time ... dispose of GPG securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that treat a lender's enforcement sale as a breach, this exemption lets a bank liquidate collateral shares at any time, including during a Blackout Period, provided the underlying secured financing was itself validly entered into (i.e. over vested, unlocked shares with consent).

clause: for the purposes of clause 3 only, a spouse (including a de facto spouse), child ... a close relative, a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with any of the persons referred to in clause 1(b)(i)
why_it_matters: Natural-person associates (spouse, children, dependants) are only brought within clause 3 (Blackout Periods/notification); the express clause 4 bans on protection arrangements and secured financing/margin lending apply only to the GPG Person and entities they control, so a collar or loan booked in a spouse's own name arguably sits outside clause 4's literal wording, though general insider trading law and the acting-in-concert language would still need to be checked case by case.

clause: a company or trust controlled by any of the persons referred to in clause 1(b)(i) above
why_it_matters: Unlike natural-person associates, a company or trust the executive controls is included in the GPG Person definition without limitation, so routing the collar/loan through a family trust or investment vehicle does not escape clause 4's bans.

clause: GPG may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on trading ... even where the proposed trade would otherwise take place outside a Blackout Period ... must be kept strictly confidential.
why_it_matters: A scheduled collar entry, roll or unwind date can be blocked by an undisclosed ad hoc restriction with no advance warning and no stated end date.

clause: If an GPG Person comes into possession of Inside Information after receiving a clearance to trade, they must not trade despite having received the clearance.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar or financing transaction can become unexecutable if inside information arises between clearance and signing, with no stated re-clearance mechanism.

clause: In exceptional circumstances the Authorising Officer has discretion to approve dealings in GPG securities during a Blackout Period ... may include, without limitation, severe financial hardship, or a requirement to comply with a court order.
why_it_matters: Offers a narrow, wholly discretionary and unreviewable route to execute, unwind or settle a collar during a closed period, but cannot be relied upon as a matter of right.

clause: If an GPG Person undertakes any of the actions described in paragraph 5(a), that GPG Person must advise the relevant Authorising Officer.
why_it_matters: Even exempt dealings (e.g. a secured lender's enforcement sale) must still be reported to the Authorising Officer after the event, creating an ongoing disclosure trail for any financing arrangement.

clause: (not addressed anywhere in the policy)
why_it_matters: There is no minimum shareholding requirement to preserve, simplifying sizing of the collar and loan against the full vested, unlocked holding.

clause: Senior Management is required to obtain prior written approval from the Chairman ... prior to any trading being undertaken.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that only require clearance inside a closed period, MLX requires the Chairman's (or two directors') written approval before every trade by Senior Management, so entry, roll, and unwind of a collar and its loan each need fresh clearance regardless of the calendar.

clause: Senior management must not put in place a non-discretionary trading plan in respect of Company Securities without first obtaining prior written approval ... Senior management must not cancel any such trading plan during a Prohibited Period, unless the circumstances are exceptional and the procedure for prior written approval ... has been met.
why_it_matters: If a collar's settlement or unwind mechanics are structured as a non-discretionary trading plan, separate approval is required, and it cannot be cancelled inside a closed period without exceptional-circumstances approval.

clause: Dealing in Metals X securities during a prohibited period by a family member is to be discouraged.
why_it_matters: This is soft, non-binding language rather than a prohibition, so routing a collar or loan through a family member during a closed period is not itself a breach of this policy, though general insider trading law and reputational risk still apply.

clause: (the policy distinguishes only 'unvested entitlements' from a general 'security holding'; it never refers to a holding lock)
why_it_matters: Once shares vest, they appear to be treated as an ordinary security holding available for hedging or security with clearance, with no intermediate holding-locked state to navigate.

clause: This Policy only provides a summary of applicable legal and regulatory issues which are complex, and should therefore only be used as a general guide, not as legal advice.
why_it_matters: The policy disclaims completeness, so a collar structure cleared under this policy still needs independent Corporations Act and market-manipulation analysis.

clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: Even though only 'margin lending arrangements' are named in section 4.5, a bespoke bank loan secured on the collared shares that achieves the same economic effect is likely to be treated as caught by the same absolute prohibition, regardless of how it is documented.

topic: absolute margin lending ban, no carve-out
clause: All Employees are prohibited from: (a) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; and (b) transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan.
why_it_matters: This is a blanket ban with no vesting distinction and no consent, clearance or exceptional-circumstances route, unlike the hedging ban in 4.3 — the funded collar's loan leg has no path to approval under this policy if characterised as margin lending or an economic equivalent.

clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
why_it_matters: A monetisation structured as a forward contract risks being treated as short-term dealing regardless of its actual tenor, which is relevant if a collar or its unwind is documented as forward-like.

topic: Front Page Test gates all approvals
clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even a technically compliant collar or approval request can be refused if it would look like the executive is taking advantage of their position, adding a subjective, unappealable filter on top of the formal rules.

clause: the sale of a significant volume of Company securities (i.e. a volume that represents in excess of 10% of the total shares held by the seller prior to the sale, or a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume of the shares of the Company on the ASX for the preceding 20 trading days) by a Director needs to be approved by the Board prior to any sale.
why_it_matters: Unwinding or settling a sizeable collar by a Director may separately require Board approval on volume grounds even where ordinary section 5.3/5.4 approval has already been obtained.

clause: Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their "Connected Persons" only deal in securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a spouse, family member or controlled entity does not avoid the Policy's restrictions, including the absolute margin lending ban.

clause: (the Policy names only 'margin lending arrangements' in section 4.5; it does not separately address granting a charge, mortgage or pledge over Company securities)
why_it_matters: A non-margin-loan secured facility might arguably sit outside the literal wording of 4.5, but the substance-over-form clause in section 1 makes reliance on that gap risky.

clause: (the policy contains no reference anywhere to margin loans, security, charges, pledges or other secured financing arrangements over Company securities)
why_it_matters: The funded collar's loan leg, secured on the collared shares, is not expressly regulated by this policy at all; a bank cannot point to any clearance pathway or prohibition, and would need to rely on the general law and any unwritten company practice.

topic: hedging clause names put and call options
clause: hedging arrangements (including, for example, the use of put and call options or other derivative instruments) over unvested Securities issued pursuant to any employee or Director option or share plan
why_it_matters: The wording is directly on point for a collar's two derivative legs; the ban is absolute pre-vesting but hedging vested securities is expressly permitted subject to complying with the rest of the policy (written acknowledgement for Restricted Employees).

clause: any securities (i.e. shares or options) in the Company, its Subsidiaries or related Companies
why_it_matters: The written acknowledgement process is defined only for shares or options in the Company itself; an OTC put/call written by a bank is caught only via the separate hedging clause's express reference to derivative instruments, not by the general dealing/acknowledgement definition.

clause: clearance may be given for them to sell (but not to purchase) Company securities ... valid for 48 hours, or less if the Company becomes aware of Inside Information
why_it_matters: Any exceptional-circumstances clearance is unavailable for buying (relevant to entering a collar) and, even for a sale/unwind, expires quickly and cannot survive new inside information.

clause: The Insider Trading and Closed Period provisions will not usually apply to the exercise of employee or executive options ... The policy does however, apply to any sale of Company securities acquired on the exercise of options or vesting of share rights, including sales as part of a broker-assisted cashless exercise of an option.
why_it_matters: Exercising options to create the underlying shares for a collar is largely unrestricted, but any subsequent sale (including a cashless-exercise sale) remains fully subject to the policy's notification/acknowledgement and Closed Period rules.

clause: Adopted by DYL Board on 17 November 2010
why_it_matters: This is the only version of the policy available in this batch; it references the since-renumbered ASX Listing Rule 3.19A, indicating the document may predate DYL's current policy, so the analysis should be confirmed against any more recent version before being relied upon.

clause: enter into agreements that provide lenders with rights over their interests in securities in the Company (such as margin loans or secured financing arrangements) without first seeking and obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
why_it_matters: This is directly on point for a funded collar's loan leg: a secured financing arrangement over the collared shares is expressly contemplated and permitted with the Approving Officer's prior written clearance, with no vesting distinction stated.

clause: The Approving Officer will not grant written clearance if the Company is likely, in the short term, to release a periodic financial report, other financial data or make an announcement of market sensitive information under ASX Listing Rule 3.1.
why_it_matters: This is an additional, informal screening period beyond the fixed Blackout Periods during which clearance requests for the collar or its financing will be refused, adding timing risk on top of the scheduled windows.

clause: Any written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for the period of 5 business days from the time in which it is given ... The written clearance may, however, be withdrawn by the Approving Officer if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar or financing transaction must be executed within 5 business days and can be revoked before then if new information emerges, requiring careful timing of execution.

topic: post-trade notification for directors and SLT
clause: Following any trade by a director or SLT member, or any trade of which they are aware by their Connected Persons, the relevant director or SLT member must notify the Company Secretary of the details of the trade within one business day of the trade having occurred.
why_it_matters: Fast (1 business day) disclosure is required for any resulting trade under the collar or its unwind, supporting the Company's ASX reporting obligations.

clause: a disposal of the Company's securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under margin lending arrangements
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale on default is excluded from the Blackout Period, approval and short-term dealing rules entirely, so enforcement is not blocked by a subsequent closed period.

clause: Each Restricted Person must take reasonable steps to ensure his or her Connected Persons are aware of and comply with the restrictions in this policy that apply to them, and must not procure, encourage or assist a Connected Person to trade in breach of this policy.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a family member or a controlled trust/company does not avoid the clearance requirements in 4.9(a) and (b).

topic: margin lending ban is KMP-only and margin-loan-specific
clause: directors, officers and other “Key Management Personnel” ... of the Group are prohibited from using his or her holding in any of the Group's securities as collateral for any margin lending.
why_it_matters: The express prohibition is confined to KMP and to 'margin lending'; other employees and contractors face no express bar on pledging shares, and even for KMP whether a bank's collar-secured loan counts as 'margin lending' (rather than another form of secured financing) is undefined and would need to be tested.

clause: A Key Management Person with security over his or her holding ... in connection with margin lending which is in existence prior to 1 March 2016 will not be in breach ... provided that the Key Management Person notifies the Chairman ... within five business days of becoming aware that his or her margin loan facility ... is subject to a margin call, in material breach, or reaches 90% or above of any applicable loan-to-value ratio.
why_it_matters: Any new collar-secured loan post-dates 1 March 2016 and so cannot rely on this grandfathering; it confirms the general rule is a forward-looking ban on new KMP margin/secured lending against Group shares.

topic: hedging ban tied to vesting/restriction status only
clause: must not enter into a transaction if the transaction effectively operates to hedge or limit the economic risk of securities allocated under the Group's employee incentive plans during the period those securities remain unvested or subject to restrictions under the terms of the plan.
why_it_matters: Once plan securities vest and restrictions lapse, hedging is no longer expressly banned and only ordinary Dealing clearance and Closed Period rules apply, so the collar's put/call legs over vested unrestricted shares are structurally available subject to clearance.

clause: Dealing in securities is a broad concept and covers more than simply buying or selling securities. It extends to exercising options over securities and entering agreements to buy or sell securities.
why_it_matters: Granting a charge or lien is not listed as a form of Dealing, so outside the KMP margin lending clause, pledging shares to secure a loan is not independently regulated by this policy.

clause: A Relevant Person must notify the Company Secretary: before, or immediately after, any buying or selling by them ... of Group securities at any time.
why_it_matters: Entry into, unwind of, or settlement under a collar (to the extent treated as buying or selling) must be notified to the Company Secretary regardless of Closed Period status, creating an ongoing disclosure trail for the bank's structure.

clause: trading in the Company's shares also extends to trading in other securities issued by the Company including options
why_it_matters: The policy's coverage is limited to shares and Company-issued options; a bank's OTC put/call and its secured loan are not securities issued by the Company and are not otherwise mentioned, so they likely sit entirely outside the express Share Trading Policy.

clause: Participants are prohibited from entering into any scheme or arrangement to protect the value or lock in a price of those options or shares before the exercise or award date.
why_it_matters: The only express hedging restriction ends at exercise/award, so a collar over already-vested shares is not caught by this clause.

clause: (no clause addresses margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, charges, liens or pledges)
why_it_matters: There is no policy-based obstacle to pledging vested shares to secure the bank's loan, though the director's own duties, general law and ASX Listing Rule disclosure of security interests over director-held securities remain separately relevant.

clause: the takeover provisions which restrict dealings in Company securities when their combined shareholding interest exceeds 20%
why_it_matters: A cash-settled collar should not itself create a relevant interest, but a physically-settled structure or security interest granted to the bank should be checked against this 20% threshold.

clause: Directors, officers and employees must advise the Company Secretary in writing of the details of any completed transactions within 2 working days of the transaction.
why_it_matters: If entry into, or unwind/settlement of, the collar is treated as 'trading in the Company's shares', it must be disclosed to the Company Secretary within 2 working days regardless of tier.

clause: Otherwise enable a NEC Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.
why_it_matters: The purchased-put leg of a collar is squarely within this catch-all, ensuring a bank collar is treated as a 'protection arrangement' under 5.2 rather than escaping the policy through creative structuring.

clause: for the purposes of section 4 only, a spouse, dependent child, a close relative or a person acting in concert with any of the persons referred to in sub-paragraph (i) to (iii) above.
why_it_matters: The hedging (5.2) and security/margin lending (5.3) restrictions apply only to the NEC Person, not their associates as extended for section 4; routing the collar or loan through a spouse or controlled entity would not itself trigger 5.2/5.3, though the underlying shares remain the NEC Person's.

clause: a disposal of NEC Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement.
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale on default is an exempt dealing permitted at any time, including in a Closed Period, removing the enforcement-timing risk that other issuers' policies create by treating a lender's forced sale as a breach.

topic: vested/unlocked carve-in for financing and hedging
clause: Unless paragraph (a) applies, NEC Persons may, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any NEC securities, to secure any obligation of that NEC Person or any third party; or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving NEC securities, with consent under paragraph 4.2.
why_it_matters: Confirms a funded collar (loan secured on vested, unlocked shares) is expressly contemplated and permitted subject only to ordinary Authorising Officer consent, not an outright ban as under many peer policies.

clause: Derivative means: (a) derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars); and (b) any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
why_it_matters: The policy's own definition of Derivative expressly names 'collars', removing any ambiguity that a bank equity collar is within scope and subject to the section 9.2 protection-arrangements regime and section 7 clearance.

topic: clearance expressly extends to vested-security derivatives
clause: For the avoidance of doubt, this requirement includes any proposed dealing in derivatives in respect of fully vested Waypoint REIT securities.
why_it_matters: Confirms a bank collar over fully vested shares needs prior written clearance via the Securities Trading Form and cannot be argued to fall outside the ordinary clearance process.

clause: a disposal of the Waypoint REIT securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, a margin call under the terms of a margin loan against Waypoint REIT securities.
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale on a margin call is an Excluded Dealing usable even during a Closed Period without prior clearance, provided the Relevant Person is not then in possession of inside information, materially reducing enforcement-timing risk.

clause: Relevant Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... over any Waypoint REIT securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that Relevant Persons or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Waypoint REIT securities, except with the approval of the Authorising Officer.
why_it_matters: Confirms the funded collar's loan, secured on vested, unlocked shares, is expressly permitted with Authorising Officer approval rather than banned outright.

topic: blackout clearance extends beyond Restricted Persons
clause: all Waypoint REIT Employees (not just Restricted Persons) must seek approval to deal in Waypoint REIT's Securities during a blackout period.
why_it_matters: Even a non-Restricted-Person employee entering into a collar must seek clearance if a Board-imposed blackout period is in effect at the relevant time.

topic: ordinary lending carve-out from margin lending ban
clause: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where the Company's Securities may be included as security in an ordinary lending scenario. Designated Persons should consult the Company Secretary if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: A funded collar's loan, if structured as an ordinary secured facility rather than a margin loan with LVR-triggered calls, falls outside the 7.1 prohibition entirely for Designated Persons.

clause: a disposal of the Company's Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement, where such agreements are prohibited by this policy.
why_it_matters: If the bank's loan is an ordinary secured facility (not a margin loan), its enforcement sale on default is an exempt dealing usable at any time including a Prohibited Period; structuring it as a margin loan forfeits both the 7.1 permission and this exemption.

clause: deal at any time in financial products associated with the Company's Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy. Financial products includes derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with the Company's Securities by third parties.
why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put/call for a Designated Person must independently fit within a dealing type the policy otherwise permits (an open trading window with prior notification, or an exceptional-circumstances approval); it is not exempted merely by being off-market or third-party issued.

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested/locked remuneration
clause: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that: has not vested; or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: Once remuneration securities vest and any holding lock lifts, the hedging-specific ban no longer applies by its terms, and the collar is then assessed only under the general financial-products restriction (7.3(b)), satisfied by ordinary window-compliant, notified dealing.

topic: Part 7 restrictions do not apply to ordinary Personnel
clause: part 4 (prior notification) and part 7 (further restrictions) apply to all directors, officers and other key management personnel of the Company (including the CEO and CFO), and any other persons designated by the board ... ('Designated Person').
why_it_matters: An employee holding vested shares who is not a Designated Person faces none of the margin lending, hedging, short-selling or short-term trading restrictions in Part 7, and needs no prior notification to deal, only compliance with the trading windows and the insider trading prohibition.

topic: clearance route ambiguity for LIT Persons
clause: Restricted trading (short-term, hedging, margin lending/security) requires clearance 'in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure' for EQT Persons, LIT Persons and LIT Partners alike (s.6), but the defined term 'Trading Request Procedure' is drafted as the clause-5 process EQT Persons must follow, while s.2 instead routes LIT Persons/Partners to the LIT Partner's own agreed trading policy.
why_it_matters: For a DigiCo director or executive (a LIT Person under the manager, not an EQT Person of Equity Trustees), the bank cannot be certain from this document alone who actually approves a collar or its secured loan leg; the manager's own trading policy (not in this PDF) needs to be obtained and checked.

clause: The Policy governs trading in LIT Units generally; there is no employee equity incentive scheme, unvested holding or holding lock referenced anywhere.
why_it_matters: There is no unvested-collateral prohibition or vesting-based carve-out to negotiate around; the only conditions on a funded collar are the blackout periods, clearance and Inside Information rules that apply to any holding.

clause: may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that ban secured financing outright, this Policy makes both the collar derivatives and the loan's security interest a clearable, not prohibited, category, so a funded collar is structurally available subject to clearance and timing.

clause: The Policy contains no clause addressing a lender's or counterparty's forced sale, margin call liquidation, or price triggers.
why_it_matters: There is no drafted consequence if the bank's collateral call or exercise falls inside a Black-out Period; this residual risk should be raised with the Company Secretary when seeking clearance.

clause: EQT Persons who have knowledge of the buy-back and are involved in the day to day management of the buy-back are subject to a further Black-out Period from the buy-back decision date to the next full business day after completion.
why_it_matters: If the Fund is conducting a unit buy-back, collar timing for an informed manager-side individual must clear an additional, narrower blackout window.

clause: A Connected Person must seek clearance through their EQT Person, LIT Person or LIT Partner in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure prior to trading in Units.
why_it_matters: A collar or loan structured through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the clearance requirement.

clause: Designated Persons may only Deal in Service Stream Securities if: (a) the Dealing is outside a Closed Period ... or you have obtained clearance ...; (b) you have obtained the relevant permission to trade ...; and (c) you do not possess any Price Sensitive Information
why_it_matters: Even where a Dealing is not independently banned, it needs both Closed Period clearance (hardship/exceptional circumstance only) and routine permission to trade; but derivatives, hedging and margin loans are separately and absolutely banned by 4.4/4.5, so neither gate can cure those bans for a collar.

clause: Designated Persons are prohibited from entering into agreements or other arrangements ... to hedge their existing holdings of or entitlements to Service Stream securities. These prohibitions also include derivatives on the Service Stream securities.
why_it_matters: This is a blanket, all-times, no-exception ban on hedging and derivatives, including an OTC put and call, for every director, the CEO, CEO direct reports and any employee with permanent price-sensitive-information access; there is no clearance mechanism that reaches this substantive prohibition.

topic: margin loan ban tied to forced-sale risk
clause: Designated Persons are prohibited from entering into or maintaining margin loan arrangements over Service Stream securities due to the risk of forced sale of those securities, in breach of this policy.
why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on the collared shares, if structured as a margin loan, is permanently prohibited for Designated Persons with no carve-out; a facility not structured as a margin loan is not expressly addressed, but the stated rationale (forced-sale risk) would apply equally to it.

topic: directors and company secretaries are automatically Designated Persons
clause: A Designated Person is any Officer; the Chief Executive Officer; an Employee who reports directly to the Chief Executive Officer; or an Employee who ... permanently has access to confidential or price sensitive information
why_it_matters: Every director and company secretary is caught by the absolute hedging/derivatives/margin-loan bans as a matter of definition; there is no route for a director to fall outside Designated Person status.

topic: absolute hedging ban, vested or unvested
clause: ASK and Manager Personnel and associates are prohibited from entering into any transaction to hedge their exposure to Stapled Securities [whether received under an equity based remuneration scheme or otherwise and whether vested or unvested].
why_it_matters: The collar's derivative legs are banned outright for everyone, at all times, with no Chair-approval or clearance mechanism at all (unlike the margin loan/secured funding regime), so the derivative component of a funded collar cannot be structured under this Policy regardless of tier or vesting status.

clause: Margin loans used to fund the purchase of Stapled Securities may give the lender the right to require the sale of those securities at a time during the Blackout Period ... or at a time when the borrower has knowledge of market sensitive information. Such a sale may amount to insider trading (or create a perception of insider trading).
why_it_matters: Even though the loan leg is clearable with Chair approval, the Policy itself flags that the bank's or a lender's enforcement sale during a closed period or while the executive holds inside information could itself constitute insider trading, so enforcement/foreclosure mechanics need bespoke drafting and Chair sign-off.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would create a perception risk outlined above.
why_it_matters: The Chair can refuse to approve the loan/secured-funding leg purely on the ground it might be perceived as trading on inside information, an additional discretionary hurdle beyond the express legal tests.

clause: Restricted Persons must notify the ASK Company Secretary prior to any dealing, including periods outside of the Blackout Period ... Notwithstanding prior notification of a proposed dealing, the Chair ... may direct the person ... not to deal, or to impose conditions on the dealing in their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons.
why_it_matters: A director or KMP wanting the (permitted) loan leg must clear this notify-and-await-decision gate even outside a Blackout Period, with a discretionary veto or conditions and only a 5-business-day execution window once cleared.

clause: this trading policy will also apply to any trading in Abacus Group securities in the same way as it applies to Stapled Securities, including restricting trading during a Blackout Period of Abacus Group
why_it_matters: If the manager relationship means the individual also holds Abacus Group Limited securities, the same absolute hedging ban and Chair-approval-for-financing regime applies to those securities too.

clause: 'BKI securities' means shares, options and other securities issued by BKI. Dealing ... [means] Directly buying, selling, or otherwise trading in BKI securities.
why_it_matters: An OTC put and call written by a bank are not securities issued by BKI, so on the Policy's own wording they may fall entirely outside 'dealing in BKI securities' and outside the Policy's restrictions, leaving only the general Corporations Act insider trading prohibition (which does not turn on the instrument's form) as an independent constraint.

topic: no financing or hedging provisions at all
clause: The Policy's Restrictions on Trading, Allowable Dealings, Excluded Trading and Exceptional Circumstances sections make no mention of hedging, derivatives, margin loans, security, encumbrance, short selling, stock lending or CFDs.
why_it_matters: There is no express prohibition and no clearance gate on granting security over BKI shares to a lender, so the loan leg of a funded collar is unaddressed either way; this silence should not be read as an unambiguous green light, and a forced sale on default would still need to avoid the insider trading and short-term dealing prohibitions that do apply.

clause: Restricted Persons are prohibited from engaging in short term dealing in BKI securities; ... never engage in short term dealing of the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: Unlike the Prohibited Period restriction, which has a notification path and an Exceptional Circumstances override, the short-term dealing ban is stated as an absolute rule with no defined length and no listed exception, so an early unwind or short-dated structure risks breaching it with no cure available.

topic: light notification gate outside Prohibited Periods
clause: notify the Company Secretary or Chairman of any intended dealings prior to entering into the transaction; notify the Company Secretary of completed dealings.
why_it_matters: Outside Prohibited Periods, dealing in the shares themselves requires only notice, not approval or a right of refusal, a materially lighter gate than seen in most peer policies, though it applies to dealing in the shares rather than to derivatives or security as such.

topic: broad Securities definition sweeps in OTC derivatives
clause: Securities: Shares, preference shares, options, derivatives, bonds and other financial products that can be traded on a financial market and include shares issued by the Company or any other company, redeemable rights, financial products issued or created by third parties over Securities, and products designed to limit economic risk in Securities holdings.
why_it_matters: This expressly captures a bank-created OTC put and call ('financial product... created by third parties over Securities') and any hedge ('products designed to limit economic risk'), so the derivative legs of a collar over vested, unrestricted shares are Trading requiring Trading Window timing and notification/clearance rather than falling outside the Policy's scope.

topic: margin lending is an absolute, no-exception ban
clause: Personnel and their Associates must not include Navigator Securities in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in Securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: Unlike the short-term trading restriction in the same section, which is expressly 'without permission from the relevant approvers', the margin lending ban carries no equivalent carve-out, so a bank loan secured on the collared shares, if it is or resembles a margin lending arrangement, cannot be cleared under this Policy at all.

topic: transfer into margin account and margin-call sale are dealings
clause: Transferring Securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account; and Selling Securities in the Company to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan
why_it_matters: Pledging the collared shares into a margin-style facility, and any forced sale on a margin call, are both expressly listed as prohibited dealings, so the enforcement mechanics of a secured funded-collar loan would themselves breach the Policy if structured as, or characterised as, a margin lending arrangement.

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested/locked remuneration
clause: an element of their remuneration that has either not vested or is a vested holding which remains subject to a holding lock
why_it_matters: The absolute hedging ban does not extend to vested, unrestricted shares (including on-market purchases or shares no longer subject to plan restrictions), so a collar over such shares is not banned outright and is instead assessed as ordinary Trading.

topic: forward contract named as short-term dealing
clause: Personnel and Associates may not buy and sell Navigator Securities nor enter into any other short-term dealings (such as a forward contract) within a three-month period.
why_it_matters: The Policy expressly treats a forward-type instrument as short-term dealing, so a short-tenor collar or one unwound within three months of the shares' acquisition needs section 5.5 approver clearance; a tenor beyond three months avoids this issue.

clause: Each Trading Window is open for a period of four weeks [after annual results, the AGM, or interim results]. ... All other periods are prohibited periods.
why_it_matters: Absent Pre-trade Clearance for exceptional circumstances, entry, unwind or exercise of a funded collar must be scheduled within one of three narrow four-week windows a year, materially constraining execution timing.

clause: or securities of a company in a "special relationship" with the Company when they are in possession of price sensitive information which is not generally available to the market
why_it_matters: The insider-trading-based restriction (and its division 3 financial products sweep) also reaches securities of, and by extension derivatives over, companies in a defined special relationship with Kingsgate, which is broader than the Company's own stock alone.

clause: At all other times the Board must receive prior notice of transactions, which are subject to Board veto.
why_it_matters: Entering, unwinding, or settling a collar outside the recommended four-week post-results window requires prior notice to the Board and can be blocked outright, with no stated process, timeframe, or right of review.

topic: no secured financing or hedging regime
clause: Policy for trading in the Company's securities [contains no reference to margin lending, encumbrance, secured financing, or hedging]
why_it_matters: This 2010-era policy predates any restriction on collateralising or hedging Company securities, so the loan leg of a funded collar is not itself prohibited by this document, though the derivative legs remain subject to the insider trading and closed period rules and general notification to the Chairman.

clause: [No reference anywhere to unvested, vested, restricted, or equity incentive scheme securities]
why_it_matters: The policy does not distinguish vested from unvested holdings, so it provides no separate gating for a collar over vested shares versus other holdings; general rules apply uniformly to all securities held.

topic: hedging ban is absolute and vesting-state-blind
clause: entering into transactions or arrangements, including by way of derivatives or similar financial products, which operate to limit the economic risk of an Employee's holdings of either unvested or vested Group Securities ... Irrespective of whether Employees enter into such arrangements outside of a Closed Period
why_it_matters: Because the ban covers both unvested and vested holdings and applies at all times, a collar's put and call legs are prohibited outright for every Employee, with no clearance, notification or waiver route referenced anywhere in section 4.2, and the section 4.7 Closed Period exceptions do not reach this standalone prohibition.

clause: Directors and Senior Executives may not include their Group Securities in a Margin Loan portfolio or otherwise Deal in Group Securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement ... without first obtaining the written consent of the Chair.
why_it_matters: Even if the hedging ban were somehow avoided, a bank loan secured on the collared shares would be a Margin Lending Arrangement requiring the Chair's prior written consent, which may be made conditional (e.g. dictating the circumstances in which shares can be sold on a margin call).

topic: forced sale exception is conditional on lawful financing
clause: an involuntary disposal of Group Securities that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights. However, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending arrangement where such arrangement is prohibited by this Policy.
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of collared shares during a Closed Period is excused from the Closed Period ban only if the underlying financing was itself validly consented to; an unauthorised or non-compliant facility would leave the forced sale in breach.

topic: ad hoc restrictions reach collar-adjacent parties
clause: The Company may also impose ad hoc trading restrictions on ... staff who work closely with, or in close proximity to, Senior Executives ... Closely Connected Persons or Entities to Senior Executives.
why_it_matters: Discretionary, unannounced trading freezes can extend to family trusts or related entities that might otherwise be used to hold the collared shares or receive the loan proceeds.

clause: If an Employee may not Deal in Group Securities under this Policy, he or she must use all reasonable endeavours to prohibit any dealing in Group Securities by ... their Closely Connected Persons or Entities.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a spouse, family trust, or controlled company does not escape the hedging ban, notification duties, or Chair-consent regime; the Employee remains responsible for that entity's dealing.

topic: exceptional circumstances test makes clearance hard
clause: What constitutes an exceptional circumstance is a matter for the discretion of the Authorising Officer. However, exceptional circumstances may exist where the proposed trade is: to realise cash in a time of exceptional financial hardship; or to comply with the requirement of a court order or enforceable undertaking; or sought because delaying the trade would ...
why_it_matters: A discretionary funded collar entered for portfolio risk management, rather than hardship or legal compulsion, does not obviously fit the listed exceptional circumstances, so Written Clearance for the hedge may be difficult to obtain even though the mechanism formally exists.

clause: enter into any arrangement designed to profit from a decrease in the share price of Superloop.
why_it_matters: This prohibition is listed separately from the hedging/derivatives bullet and is not expressly qualified by the Written Clearance carve-out attached to that bullet, creating a real risk that the purchased put leg of a collar is treated as an absolute, unwaivable prohibition.

topic: secured lender disposal wholly outside policy
clause: Disposal of Superloop Securities by a secured lender under a loan agreement secured by the Superloop Securities.
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares under a properly secured loan sits entirely outside this Policy's application, so no Closed Period breach or Written Clearance is needed for that sale, though entering into the underlying secured loan itself is not separately addressed.

clause: WARNING: If you are in possession of inside information you must not trade in the Superloop Securities irrespective of whether it is not a Restricted Period.
why_it_matters: Even a Written-Clearance-approved or policy-excluded collar transaction cannot proceed if the director or executive holds inside information at the relevant time.

clause: the exercise (but not the sale of securities following exercise) of an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme ... where the final date for the exercise ... falls during a Restricted Period
why_it_matters: Beyond this narrow exercise carve-out, the policy does not distinguish unvested from vested holdings, so it provides no separate gating specific to a collar over already-vested shares.

topic: derivatives dealing ban has no clear collar pathway
clause: deal at any time in financial products associated with Ingenia's securities, except for a type of dealing permitted by law or a permitted dealing under this policy.
why_it_matters: The ordinary approval process in section 4.10 governs dealing in 'INA securities' generally and does not obviously extend to a bespoke OTC put/call structure, so the 'permitted dealing under this policy' carve-out is unlikely to legitimise a collar even over fully vested, unrestricted shares.

topic: margin loan ban is absolute for Directors/Executives
clause: Directors and Executives may not enter into margin loans or similar financing facilities using INA securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio).
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, if secured on INA shares, is prohibited outright for Directors and Executives (the tier that also includes the CEO for clearance purposes), with no waiver or clearance route referenced anywhere in the policy.

clause: Have you pledged INA securities for a margin loan / similar funding arrangement?
why_it_matters: Any Designated Person seeking approval for a subsequent trade must disclose an existing pledge of INA securities, surfacing a funded collar structure to the CFO, Company Secretary or Chair.

clause: the Chairman may at their discretion decide to place these entities on an exclusion list whereby all directors and other meeting attendees will be prohibited from trading in these entities.
why_it_matters: Because Ingenia sits in the A-REIT sector and directors discuss other funds/trusts at Board level, a bank counterparty active in that sector could itself become subject to an ad hoc, Board-minuted trading exclusion affecting timing.

clause: This policy extends to self-managed super funds and investment companies where the Designated Person has a direct influence over the investment process.
why_it_matters: Holding the collared shares through an SMSF or investment company does not avoid the approval process or the margin loan ban if the Designated Person controls the investment decisions.

topic: margin loan ban covers both acquisition financing and security
clause: Designated Persons may not: enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is barred twice over: a Designated Person may not borrow against Company Securities, nor use existing (vested or unvested) Company Securities as loan security, with no clearance or exceptional-circumstances route referenced for this clause.

topic: Disposal Consent cannot override inside information
clause: A person who possesses Inside Information is prohibited from trading and this applies even where ... Disposal Consent has been given under this Policy (whether in exceptional circumstances or otherwise).
why_it_matters: Even a Board- or Chair-approved unwind or settlement of a collar cannot proceed if the director or executive holds Inside Information at the time.

clause: Any restriction communicated by the Company to any or all Designated Persons under this clause must be kept strictly confidential.
why_it_matters: An undisclosed ad hoc trading freeze can block execution, unwind or settlement of a collar at any time, including outside the fixed Black-out Periods.

topic: protection arrangements reach beneficially held securities
clause: including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Designated Person's behalf
why_it_matters: Routing the collared shares through a trust or custody structure does not avoid the hedging ban or the clause 6 clearance requirement.

clause: the order must be completed within five trading days otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
why_it_matters: A collar leg placed as an order but not completed before a Black-out Period begins has only five trading days to complete unchanged, or it lapses entirely.

clause: Employees must not enter into any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is prohibited outright for all Directors, officers and employees with no vesting-state or approval carve-out.

clause: Employees must not enter into an arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to either unvested remuneration, or vested remuneration which remains subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: A purchased put (or a full collar) over unvested or vested-but-locked shares is expressly banned; only vested and unrestricted shares are even candidates, and even then subject to Chair consent.

clause: There are no exceptions to the Policy.
why_it_matters: This blanket statement (6.4(a)) sits alongside a Chair waiver power (10(c)) and a narrow court-order exemption (6.6(k)), creating real uncertainty about whether any bespoke financing structure could ever be authorised.

clause: the management of the trade of any significant volume of the Company's securities (i.e., a volume that would represent a volume in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller prior to the trade, or a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume ... for the preceding 20 trading days) by an Employee must be discussed with the Board prior to the execution of any trade.
why_it_matters: Unwinding or delivering a large collared position (or a lender's enforcement sale) above these thresholds requires prior Board discussion and a documented file note, adding a procedural step before any settlement.

clause: Exceptional circumstances may apply to the disposal of the Company's securities by an Employee or a Restricted Person...
why_it_matters: The term 'Restricted Person' is used in the court-order exception but is not a defined term anywhere else in the Policy, so its scope (and whether it could extend to a bank counterparty or trustee) should be clarified with the Company before relying on it.

clause: The Policy never defines 'Dealing' or 'dealing in shares' and contains no reference to derivatives, hedging, margin lending, secured financing or encumbrance of any kind.
why_it_matters: As drafted, the Policy does not itself restrict entering an OTC collar or a loan secured on Macquarie Telecom shares; the only textual constraints are the two blackout windows and general insider trading law if an actual sale or transfer of the shares is involved.

clause: The issue of shares or the grant or exercise of options under share incentive schemes is not deemed to be dealing in Macquarie Telecom shares. The subsequent sale of shares is, however, a dealing which is subject to this policy.
why_it_matters: Vesting and exercise of incentive plan securities is free of the Policy, but any subsequent sale (e.g. to fund a collar premium, or on settlement) is a dealing subject to blackout timing and the notification/approval regime.

clause: Exceptional Circumstances means severe financial hardships or other circumstances considered to be exceptional, including a court order or court enforceable undertakings in a bona fide family settlement to transfer Macquarie Telecom shares or some other overriding legal or regulatory requirements to transfer Macquarie Telecom shares.
why_it_matters: Provides a narrow gateway for a forced or lender-driven sale of the collared shares to proceed during a blackout period, at the sole discretion of the relevant Appropriate Officer.

clause: Attached is the Macquarie Telecom Group Limited Share Trading Policy, which is provided so as to comply with ASX Listing Rule 12.9 when it comes into effect on 1 January 2011.
why_it_matters: This is a very old (2010), minimal document; given its silence on derivatives, hedging and secured financing (all now standard in modern ASX policies), the bank should confirm this is still the company's current lodged policy before relying on its silence.

clause: the Derivative is used for the purposes of protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out for the exercise price of options granted by LIN or to protect the value of the security in respect of tax liabilities that may become due and payable
why_it_matters: A funded collar sought for general liquidity or diversification would not literally satisfy this narrow purpose test; the structure would need to be framed (and evidenced) as protecting collateral value for an exercise-price loan or a tax liability to fit within the permitted use.

clause: LIN is not a counterparty to the Derivative
why_it_matters: This condition expressly contemplates (and requires) a third-party counterparty such as a bank, which is exactly the structure of an OTC funded collar.

clause: disposing of securities: ... as a result of a secured lender exercising their right under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from the operation of this policy]
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default of the secured loan is entirely excluded from the Prohibited Period and clearance requirements, removing the main practical obstacle other companies' policies impose on lender enforcement.

clause: Within ten days of a key management personnel or a Related Person entering into a margin lending arrangement involving LIN securities, the relevant key management personnel must provide the company secretary with the following information: the number of LIN securities that are subject to such arrangement; the trigger events for disposal of such securities; and any other information that may be relevant to LIN's continuous disclosure obligations, including the ability ... to meet any margin call.
why_it_matters: No Board pre-approval is required to grant security over the shares for financing (only for dealing that must occur during a Prohibited Period); a post-entry disclosure regime is the only gate, which is materially easier to satisfy than an outright ban.

topic: purpose statement vs operative rule mismatch
clause: never engage in short term trading of LIN securities [section 1, applying to all Applicable Persons] versus key management personnel and their Related Persons are generally prohibited from short-term trading at all times [section 6]
why_it_matters: Worth confirming with the company secretary whether the short-term trading ban is intended to bind non-KMP Applicable Persons, since the only substantive, defined prohibition (three-month rule) is scoped to key management personnel.

clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights). Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.
why_it_matters: A funded collar is precisely a transaction in financial products (a purchased put and written call) that limits the economic risk of holding the shares, so it is banned outright for every Restricted Person, with no clearance mechanism, vesting-state carve-out, or exceptional-circumstances gateway available at all.

clause: A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Company's consent.
why_it_matters: Unlike hedging, financing secured against the shares is not banned outright but merely requires the Company's prior (potentially conditional) consent; however, the clause is framed narrowly around 'margin loans' and it is unclear whether a bespoke bank facility not styled as a margin loan needs the same consent, though seeking it is the prudent course.

clause: clearance may be given for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) securities in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so.
why_it_matters: Even genuine hardship or a court order can only ever authorise a sale during a prohibited period, never a purchase, which is relevant to how any collar unwind or settlement mechanics are structured if they fall inside a prohibited period.

clause: The Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their respective associated parties trading in the Company's securities at any time.
why_it_matters: This unconditional, open-ended embargo power (separate from the fixed 5-business-day dividend/capital-management blackout) means the timing of a collar's entry, roll or unwind could be blocked without stated reason or notice.

clause: Derivative has the meaning in section 761D of the Corporations Act and includes options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, cash settled swaps, caps and collars.
why_it_matters: This is the only policy in this batch to expressly name 'collars' as a covered instrument, removing definitional doubt that a funded equity collar with a bank is a Derivative and hence a Security requiring ordinary Trade approval once vested, not an outright-banned instrument.

clause: Directors and Restricted Employees must not use, or allow to be used, any Derivatives or other products which operate to limit the economic risk of unvested Company Securities.
why_it_matters: The absolute hedging/derivatives ban applies only to unvested Company Securities; once shares vest, a collar is not banned at all and is treated as ordinary Trading requiring standard prior written approval, materially more favourable than a blanket hedging ban regardless of vesting.

clause: No Director or Restricted Employee may enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities, or grant lenders any rights over their Company Securities without first obtaining prior written approval.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is not prohibited, only subject to Designated Officer approval, ongoing LVR/drawdown disclosure, and at least annual reporting of amount drawn and securities covered.

topic: forced sale carve-out with residual approval tension
clause: An involuntary disposal of Securities that results from a margin lender or similar financier exercising its rights under a margin loan or similar funding arrangement [is permitted during a Prohibited Period]. (Please note that the Policy requirements with respect to prior written approval and subsequent notification continue to apply to Trading under one of these exceptions.)
why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale on default is excluded from the Prohibited Period ban, but the Policy states prior-approval and notification duties technically continue to apply even to this exception, a practical tension (an involuntary sale cannot easily obtain prior approval) worth clarifying with the Company Secretary before relying on it.

clause: A tax liability relating to Securities received under an employee incentive scheme would also not normally constitute severe financial hardship or otherwise be considered an exceptional circumstance for the purpose of obtaining proper written approval to sell or otherwise dispose of Securities during a Prohibited Period.
why_it_matters: A collar or sale timed specifically to fund tax due on vesting of incentive securities cannot rely on the Exceptional Circumstances gateway to trade inside a Prohibited Period; timing must fall within an open window instead.

clause: Any approval for the Trading will be valid for 7 days from the date it is given.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar (or its unwind) must be priced and executed within 7 days of Designated Officer approval or the approval lapses and must be sought again.

clause: the use of Company Securities as security or collateral for the funding used to acquire Company Securities or the shares or other securities of another entity
why_it_matters: The only express financing restriction is tied to funding an acquisition of securities; a loan secured on already-vested shares to raise cash (rather than to buy more securities), as in a funded collar, arguably falls outside the literal scope of clause 15, though a cautious Designated Officer would still seek clearance under its 'other arrangement' language.

clause: Dealing in securities includes: (a) applying for, acquiring or disposing of, securities; (b) entering into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of, securities; and (c) granting, accepting, acquiring, disposing, exercising or discharging an option or other right or obligation to acquire or dispose of securities.
why_it_matters: Granting a security interest or charge is not itself listed as a dealing, so outside the narrow Scrip Finance Facility clause, pledging collared shares to a bank is not clearly regulated by this policy at all.

clause: If a Designated Officer is not permitted to deal in the Company Securities, he or she must prohibit any dealing in the Company Securities by any associated person (including family or nominee companies, private investment funds and family trusts).
why_it_matters: A collar or loan structured through a family trust or private investment vehicle does not escape the Designated Officer's own dealing restrictions or the (narrow) financing clearance requirement.

clause: Where the Chairman ... believes that the circumstances warrant a temporary halt or restriction on dealing ... he or she may: (a) revoke any earlier clearance given under clause 10 for a Designated Officer to deal in Company Securities
why_it_matters: A cleared collar transaction can be blocked at any time before execution if the Chairman revokes clearance, even absent inside information, creating execution timing risk for the bank.

clause: The Approving Officer may give clearance for a Designated Officer to sell (but not buy) Company Securities in exceptional circumstances where the Designated Officer would otherwise not be able to do so under this policy.
why_it_matters: Provides a plausible route for a forced or margin-call-driven sale of collared shares during an otherwise prohibited period, though it is discretionary and refused if inside information exists.

clause: MMS Staff who possess inside information must not ... apply for, acquire or dispose of MMS Securities or enter into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of MMS Securities ('Trade')
why_it_matters: 'MMS Securities' means shares, options and other securities in MMS; a third-party OTC put/call written by a bank over vested, unrestricted MMS shares is arguably not itself an MMS Security and so may not be a 'Trade' at all, leaving the derivative legs of a collar over such shares outside the Closed Period and clearance regime altogether.

clause: MMS Staff must not enter into a transaction that is designated or intended to hedge that employee's exposure to the MMS Security that is subject to retention arrangements or an unvested MMS option.
why_it_matters: The hedging ban only reaches shares still under retention arrangements or unvested options; once a share has vested and any retention period has ended, entering a collar over it is not expressly prohibited by this clause.

clause: Key Management Personnel and their Associated Parties must not grant a security interest over MMS Securities they own, including any margin loan without first receiving the written consent of the Chairman.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on KMP-owned vested shares, needs the Chairman's prior written consent; no criteria, process or refusal grounds are stated, and non-KMP staff face no such restriction.

clause: Approval may be granted in circumstances in which the relevant MMS Staff is in severe financial hardship or other circumstances deemed by the Chairman to be exceptional ... Approval, if granted, will be valid for a period of 7 days.
why_it_matters: Gives a discretionary route to trade, unwind or settle a collar during a Closed Period, but it is time-limited to 7 days and conditional on a signed no-inside-information declaration.

clause: The policy contains no provision addressing a lender's forced sale of MMS Securities on a margin call or default.
why_it_matters: It is unclear whether a bank's enforcement sale during a Closed Period would itself breach the policy or would require separate Chairman consent, creating uncertainty for the bank's security enforcement rights.

topic: hedging ban vs Financing Arrangement approval
clause: Restricted Persons may not enter into any other transaction that operates to limit the economic risk of their security holding in GrainCorp. [cf] no Restricted Person nor any of their Associates may enter into any Financing Arrangement [including a cap and collar] unless [Chairman/ARC Chair approval obtained].
why_it_matters: Section 9.3 appears to impose an unconditional, unqualified ban on any hedge of a Restricted Person's holding, while section 9.1 separately names 'cap and collar' as a type of Financing Arrangement that can be approved by the Chairman/ARC Chair; the two clauses are in tension and GrainCorp would need to confirm in writing whether a Chairman-approved collar financing is treated as an exception to the section 9.3 hedging ban before a bank could rely on it.

topic: third-party derivatives caught regardless of structure
clause: Securities means ... financial products ... relating to, or which operate to limit, leverage or increase the economic risk in holding, those securities ... whether or not the securities or the financial products are issued or created by GrainCorp or third parties.
why_it_matters: The definition is deliberately structured to prevent avoidance through a bank-issued OTC instrument; a funded collar cannot escape the policy merely because the put/call are written by a third party rather than GrainCorp.

clause: Indirect and incidental dealing that occurs as a consequence of a Restricted Person dealing in securities issued by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party that happens to hold GrainCorp Securities.
why_it_matters: Confirms the policy does not reach indirect exposure through a genuinely third-party-managed fund, but this carve-out would not extend to a bespoke bilateral collar structured for the individual.

clause: On retirement or departure from GrainCorp, former Restricted Persons and their Associates are restricted from dealing in GrainCorp Securities for either a period of 12 weeks or the commencement of a Trading Window, whichever is earlier.
