why_it_matters: A collar entered pre-departure cannot be unwound, rolled or settled by dealing in the underlying shares during this post-employment restriction without falling back into the Trading Window/clearance regime.

clause: an involuntary disposal of GrainCorp Securities that results from the margin lender or financier exercising its rights under the arrangement [is not a breach and clearance is not required, though notification requirements may apply]
why_it_matters: Gives the bank comfort that enforcement of security under an approved Financing Arrangement (including outside a Trading Window) will not itself put the executive in breach, unlike policies with no forced-sale carve-out.

topic: hedging and secured financing consent regime
clause: Helia Employees must not, without the prior written consent of the Approvers set out in Table 1 above, enter into or agree to enter into: (a) any hedging arrangements in relation to any Helia Securities ...; or (b) any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in connection with any Helia Securities. Any request ... should include full details of the proposed arrangements and provide reasons why giving consent is appropriate.
why_it_matters: Both legs of a funded collar (the hedge and the secured loan) are permitted only with prior written consent from a senior approver, on a full-disclosure, discretionary, no-reasons-required basis, so the bank's product would need to be presented in detail and could be refused or later revoked.

clause: any trading pre-clearance, consent or exemption under this Policy can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances
why_it_matters: Consent for the collar/loan structure is not durable; Helia can withdraw it mid-transaction or during the facility's life if circumstances change, creating unwind risk for the bank.

clause: Directors and certain Senior Management must also comply with Helia’s Minimum Shareholding Policy and are not permitted to Deal in Helia Securities if such Dealing will cause them to breach their minimum shareholding requirement.
why_it_matters: If the collar or its physical settlement/forced-sale counts as a Dealing that reduces the holding, it could breach the MSR and be blocked at pre-clearance stage regardless of hedging consent; the policy does not say whether hedged (but not disposed) shares still count.

topic: no consent overrides insider trading law
clause: Irrespective of the trading pre-clearance, consent, or an exemption under this Policy being granted, nothing in such pre-clearance, consent or exemption, or in this Policy, shall relieve or purport to relieve an individual from their obligations to comply with applicable Insider Trading laws or with the other sections of this Policy.
why_it_matters: Even fully consented and pre-cleared, the collar's entry, unwind or roll must independently satisfy insider trading law each time, e.g. if inside information later arises.

clause: The Company Secretary may declare at any time that a Trading Window has closed ... The fact that the Trading Window has closed and that there is a restriction on Dealing may itself constitute Inside Information ... and must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: A Trading Window can close without notice or public disclosure, so a collar counterparty relying on execution during an open window bears undisclosed timing risk.

clause: indirect and incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of a Helia Employee trading securities issued by a management investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that happens to hold as part of its portfolio Helia Securities.
why_it_matters: Confirms the exemption is narrow (incidental fund lookthrough only) and does not extend to a bespoke OTC collar structured through an intermediary vehicle.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even if the collar/loan structure otherwise complies with the approval process, it can still be refused on a subjective reputational-perception test applied by the approver.

clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: A loan structured to avoid the literal words 'margin lending arrangement' (e.g. a bank collar loan) is still likely to be treated as requiring clause 3.5 approval.

clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement ... [excluded from Blackout Periods, approval-required dealing, and short-term dealing rules]
why_it_matters: If the bank's loan is treated as a margin lending arrangement, its enforcement sale on default is expressly excluded from the Blackout Period ban, the pre-approval requirement and the short-term dealing rule, giving the bank a clear enforcement path even during a closed period.

clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in under this clause 3.5 conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: The Company can impose bespoke conditions on when and how the bank may sell the collared shares to satisfy a shortfall, which should be negotiated into the approval before the facility is put in place.

clause: Following any trade, Directors must promptly notify the Company Secretary, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into.
why_it_matters: Entry into, adjustment of, or unwind of the collar by a director must be reported same-day to the Company Secretary to support the Company's ASX disclosure obligations.

clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: Approval for the collar/loan can be withdrawn without reasons at any time, and the executive cannot disclose a refusal or revocation, creating unwind risk for the bank that is not publicly visible.

clause: Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their 'Connected Persons' only deal in securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
why_it_matters: A collar or loan cannot be routed through a spouse, family member or controlled entity to escape the approval regime; the Restricted Person remains responsible for ensuring the same clearance is obtained.

clause: Derivative means: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars); and any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
why_it_matters: The policy expressly names 'collars' as a Derivative, so a bank-provided equity collar is unambiguously regulated dealing, not merely swept in by residual wording.

clause: Financing equity poses risks to the compliance of Aussie Broadband Persons with this Policy, particularly where the terms of the financing arrangements may place these persons in a position of conflict with their obligations under this Policy and/or with the insider trading laws (e.g. if a call is made under a margin loan which results in Securities being sold while the relevant person possesses Inside Information).
why_it_matters: The bank's loan and collar must be drafted so a forced sale on a margin call, or on collar settlement, cannot occur while the executive holds inside information or during a Blackout Period.

clause: the relevant individual must ensure that the terms of the financing arrangements do not require, or allow for, the disposal of the relevant Securities at any time when this Policy would prohibit the person from trading the relevant Securities ... and the relevant individual must promptly inform the Chair and Company Secretary of Aussie Broadband ... of any call that is made under the financing arrangements, and of the terms of that call.
why_it_matters: The bank's facility documents must contractually preclude enforcement sale during Blackout Periods, and any margin call must be reported to the Chair and Company Secretary promptly, which the bank should build into notice/cure mechanics.

clause: Aussie Broadband may publicly disclose the terms and nature of any financing arrangements to which an Aussie Broadband Director is a party, and the terms and circumstances of any call made or likely to be made under those arrangements.
why_it_matters: If the collar counterparty is a Director, the company may publicly disclose the collar/loan terms and any margin call, which affects confidentiality expectations for the bank and executive.

clause: Approval to trade will be confirmed in writing and is valid for five (5) business days (inclusive of the approval date) unless otherwise stated.
why_it_matters: For Directors, ELG and SLG, the collar (and any loan) must be priced and executed within a 5-business-day approval window, requiring tight coordination with the bank.

clause: individuals who wish to trade in Aussie Broadband Securities and are members of any of the following groups must first seek approval in writing ... each Director ... the Executive Leadership Group ... the Senior Leadership Group
why_it_matters: Only Directors and senior executives (the likely collar counterparties) face the prior-approval gate; other staff can enter vested, unrestricted Derivatives without seeking clearance, subject to the general dealing rules.

clause: any Financial Products issued over or in respect of the above securities which are able to be traded on a financial market, (collectively, the HMC Capital Group Securities)
why_it_matters: A bespoke, bilateral OTC bank collar is arguably not a Financial Product 'able to be traded on a financial market', so once the underlying shares are vested and unrestricted the collar itself may fall entirely outside the defined 'HMC Capital Group Securities' and therefore outside the Trade/pre-approval/Blackout Period regime.

clause: entering into transactions or arrangements, including by way of derivatives or similar financial products, which operate to limit the economic risk relating to HMC Capital Group Securities granted under an employee, executive or director incentive plan ... which either have not vested or have vested but remain subject to a holding lock or other restriction
why_it_matters: Unlike the general Trade definition, this hedging ban has no 'financial market' qualifier, so an OTC collar over unvested or still-restricted incentive securities is banned regardless of the scope gap identified above.

clause: Directors and Senior Executives may not include their HMC Capital Group Securities in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise Trade in HMC Capital Group Securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the consent of the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary
why_it_matters: The secured-financing control is drafted around 'margin lending arrangements'; a bespoke bank loan secured on collared shares is analogous but not identical, so whether section 8 consent is legally required is uncertain, though the company would likely treat it as caught given the same forced-sale-during-Blackout concern the section addresses.

clause: an involuntary disposal of HMC Capital Group Securities that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights. However, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending arrangement where such arrangement is prohibited by this Policy.
why_it_matters: If the underlying financing arrangement had the required consent, a lender's enforcement sale during a Blackout Period is expressly excluded from breaching the Policy - but only if the arrangement was properly consented to in the first place.

clause: When permitted to Trade in accordance with this Policy, or where Trading is proposed during a Blackout Period, all Directors and Employees must give a prior written request for pre-approval to the Group Chief Executive Officer and the Group Company Secretary of any proposed Trading
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that reserve pre-clearance for directors/executives, HMC requires prior written approval for essentially all Trading by all Employees, so even routine sales to fund or unwind a collar need clearance, not just derivative or financing legs.

clause: the opportunity to make the Trade expires five trading days from the date the approval is received
why_it_matters: Both trading pre-approval and margin/financing consent are effectively time-boxed, requiring tight coordination between clearance and execution of the loan and collar with the bank.

topic: margin loan ban does not extend to other secured financing
clause: The restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where OIG Securities may be included as security. Designated Persons should consult Director Legal, Risk & Compliance if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on the collared shares, if not structured as a classic margin loan, falls outside the absolute margin-lending ban and is not otherwise expressly regulated - the only step suggested is an optional consultation with Compliance on classification.

topic: blanket derivatives ban for non-OIG-staff Designated Persons
clause: Subject to the law, Designated Persons who are not OIG Staff must not ... deal at any time in financial products associated with OIG Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or a permitted dealing under this policy.
why_it_matters: If the collar counterparty is a Designated Person who is not an OIG employee (e.g. an external Investment Manager director), the put/call legs are prohibited outright with no clearance route available.

topic: possible gap for OIG-employed Designated Persons
clause: OIG Securities: Financial Products issued by an OIG Licensee and listed, quoted or traded on a Relevant Market.
why_it_matters: Because a bespoke OTC derivative is not itself 'issued by' the OIG Licensee, an OIG-employed Designated Person's collar may not be clearly caught by either the Prohibited Period regime or the Clause 8.6 ban (limited to non-OIG-staff); this should be confirmed with Compliance rather than assumed.

clause: a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender (or financier) exercising their rights, however, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement where such agreements are prohibited by this policy.
why_it_matters: Provided the bank's facility is not a 'margin lending agreement', its enforcement sale of the collared units is expressly excluded from the Prohibited Period ban and needs no prior notification or clearance.

clause: OIG does not remunerate its Staff with OIG Securities.
why_it_matters: There is no unvested or holding-locked incentive stock issued by OIG itself; any OIG-employed collar candidate would be dealing in already-vested, open-market-acquired units.

clause: Designated Persons must avoid short term (less than 12 months) trading in OIG Securities or in Financial Products associated with the relevant Fund or OIG Securities.
why_it_matters: Entering or unwinding a collar within 12 months of acquiring the underlying units could itself be characterised as prohibited short-term trading, independent of the derivative-specific analysis above.

clause: Where Company Securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is expressly excused from both the insider trading prohibition and the Closed Period restriction, which materially de-risks the lender's security position under a funded collar.

clause: Securities is defined as ordinary shares and other securities in the Company; the policy contains no hedging clause and does not name derivatives or third-party financial products anywhere.
why_it_matters: An OTC put and call with a bank over Company shares falls outside the policy's Dealing, Closed Period and approval mechanics entirely, so the derivative legs of the collar are not independently restricted (though general insider trading law still applies).

clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company Securities (i.e. a volume that would represent a volume in excess of 10% of the total Securities held by the seller prior to the sale, or a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume ... for the preceding 20 trading days) by Staff needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
why_it_matters: Unwinding or physically settling a large collar position could trigger this pre-execution Board/legal-adviser discussion requirement, adding a further approval step beyond ordinary clearance.

clause: short-term or speculative trading refers to trading in Company where the shares are held for less than 6 months.
why_it_matters: A collar structured to unwind or be exercised within 6 months of the shares being acquired could be characterised as prohibited short-term trading.

clause: A Restricted Person under this Trading Policy must not enter into any financial arrangement under which Securities in the company are provided as security.
why_it_matters: This bans the secured loan leg of a funded collar outright for all Restricted Persons (Directors, Senior Executives and other notified restricted staff), with no clearance or exemption route anywhere in the policy.

clause: The Exempted Dealings (s10.1) list no carve-out for a secured lender's forced sale on default, and the exceptional-circumstances exemption power (s10.2) is limited to the Closed Period (s4) and short-term trading (s5) prohibitions, not the section 7 prohibition itself.
why_it_matters: If a secured financing arrangement existed in breach of section 7 and were enforced, the resulting sale would not fall within any listed exemption, unlike some peer policies that expressly excuse a lender's enforcement sale.

clause: Directors, employees and contractors of the Company must not engage in hedging arrangements, Deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration scheme.
why_it_matters: The absolute hedging ban is confined to unvested equity-scheme entitlements; hedging vested shares is only caught as an ordinary Dealing requiring clearance, so the derivative legs of a collar over vested shares are not independently prohibited.

clause: Persons to whom this Trading Policy applies must not cause or permit any related party or entity over which they have control (including a trust, superannuation fund, company, dependent family member or any other entity over which they have control), to enter into any transaction in Securities in circumstances where they would have been prohibited from entering into the transactions in their own name.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust, superannuation fund or controlled company does not escape the section 7 prohibition or the clearance requirement for Restricted Persons.

clause: Any FDC Personnel who holds FDC securities subject to binding restrictions on transfer (either as ASX restricted securities or through voluntary escrow arrangements) must comply with the terms of any applicable escrow arrangements and will be unable to trade in those securities during that time.
why_it_matters: Escrowed shares (common for a recently listed company) cannot be pledged, sold or delivered into a collar until the escrow period ends, regardless of vesting status.

clause: Any dealing in FDC's securities by Restricted Persons pursuant to a margin lending arrangement is not permitted ... entering into a margin lending arrangement ... transferring securities ... into an existing margin loan account; and selling securities ... to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
why_it_matters: The outright ban targets 'margin lending arrangements' specifically; a bank facility structured and documented as a different form of secured lending may fall outside this ban and instead only need Trading Window timing or exceptional pre-clearance, which is decisive for whether the collar's loan leg is feasible.

clause: Trading Windows are the only times when Restricted Persons may deal in FDC's securities ... Provided that even when a Trading Window is operating, if you are in possession of Inside Information, you cannot trade.
why_it_matters: No approval or notification is required to execute, unwind or roll a collar inside an open window (only outside-window dealing needs exceptional pre-clearance), simplifying bank execution timing.

clause: closely related parties (as that term is defined in the Corporations Act) of all Relevant Personnel, ... the persons listed above are called Restricted Persons.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, dependant or controlled entity does not escape the Trading Window or margin-lending restrictions, since associates are Restricted Persons in their own right.

clause: Where a Restricted Person enters into a hedging arrangement in respect of FDC securities, FDC may, where appropriate, disclose the fact and nature of the hedge (eg, in its Annual Report or to the ASX).
why_it_matters: FDC retains discretion to publicly disclose the existence and nature of a director's or executive's collar.

clause: is proven to have breached this Policy could face disciplinary action (including forfeiture of securities and / or suspension or termination of employment).
why_it_matters: A collar or loan structured to evade the margin lending ban or Trading Window timing risks forfeiture of the underlying securities in addition to employment sanctions.

clause: Derivatives includes: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars); and any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
why_it_matters: The policy expressly identifies a 'collar' as a Derivative, so a bank-provided equity collar over Elders securities issued as remuneration is unambiguously and absolutely banned under Section 3.6, irrespective of vesting state or Designated Person status.

topic: derivatives ban limited to remuneration securities
clause: you must not use, nor allow to be used, any Derivatives in relation to any Elders Securities issued as part of your remuneration whether vested or unvested.
why_it_matters: The absolute derivatives ban is textually confined to securities 'issued as part of your remuneration'; a collar over Elders shares an executive acquired other than as remuneration (e.g. purchased on-market) is not caught by this ban and is instead only an ordinary 'deal' subject to Open Period timing and, for Designated Persons, the Section 4.2 clearance procedure.

clause: Designated Persons must not acquire Elders Securities subject to a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: This bans only acquiring shares using margin finance; pledging already-held vested shares as collateral for a bank loan is not literally an 'acquisition subject to margin lending' and instead falls within the general 'use of Securities as security' limb of the dealing definition, which is only permitted_with_clearance, not banned outright — a critical distinction for structuring the collar's loan leg.

clause: deal includes ... the use of the Securities as security or the grant of any encumbrance over the Securities
why_it_matters: Pledging vested shares to the bank as security for the loan is expressly a 'deal', so it must occur inside an Open Period, outside possession of Inside Information, and (for a Designated Person) after Section 4.2 written approval — but it is not prohibited.

clause: Designated Persons must take steps to ensure that their Related Persons understand and act in accordance with the terms of this Policy ... A Designated Person might sometimes act as trustee of a trust ... a trust of which a Designated Person acts as trustee may deal in Securities if the decision to deal ... is taken without reference to, and independently of, the Designated Person.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or a pledge through a spouse, controlled company or family trust does not avoid the restrictions unless the narrow independent-trustee criteria are met; otherwise the Designated Person remains responsible for the Related Person's compliance.

clause: a director of Elders must notify the Company Secretary of Elders ... as soon as practicable after any dealing in Elders Securities occurs and, in any case, no more than two days afterwards.
why_it_matters: Entry into, or unwind of, a collar or its financing by a director will be reported internally within 2 days and is likely to feed into ASX disclosure of director's interest changes.

clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities or transfer securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is banned only if characterised as 'margin lending'; unlike broader ASX-listed peer policies, this does not extend to 'any secured financing arrangement', so a bespoke bank loan secured by a pledge of the collared shares (not documented as a margin loan) arguably sits outside the express prohibition, though the Company's substance-over-form approach creates real risk it would be treated the same way.

clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: This excluded-dealing carve-out lets a secured lender force-sell collateral even during a blackout period without breaching the Policy or requiring fresh clearance, which favours the bank's enforcement rights if a security interest can lawfully be granted.

clause: 4. Additional restriction applying to Restricted Persons
why_it_matters: Margin lending, hedging and short-term/speculative dealing bans apply only to Restricted Persons; a plan participant who is not a Director, KMP, senior executive or nominated employee faces none of these structural barriers under this Policy, though insider trading law still applies to everyone.

clause: entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts)
why_it_matters: Naming forward contracts as short-term dealing signals the Company would likely characterise an OTC collar (economically similar to a forward) as short-term/speculative dealing for a Restricted Person, particularly with a short tenor or if entered shortly after vesting.

clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: Even where a collar or its financing is not literally 'margin lending' or 'hedging' as used in the Policy, the Company can still treat it as caught by the Policy's intent, so structuring around the literal wording carries residual risk.

clause: the approved dealing must occur within 7 days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective
why_it_matters: A cleared collar trade with the bank must be priced and executed within 7 days of approval, tighter than typical bank documentation timelines.

clause: If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: An executive cannot disclose to the bank why clearance for a collar was refused or revoked, complicating trade certainty for the counterparty.

clause: Company Securities includes shares, debentures, rights, options and any other financial products of the Company traded on any stock exchange.
why_it_matters: An OTC put and call written by a bank are neither 'of the Company' nor 'traded on any stock exchange', so on a literal reading they are not 'Company Securities' and the Policy's Dealing, Black Out Period and clearance regime does not apply to them at all, outside the separate Key Management Personnel hedging prohibition.

topic: no margin lending or secured financing prohibition
clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX-listed peer policies, this Policy contains no prohibition on margin lending, granting security over, or otherwise financing against Company Securities; this excluded-trading carve-out for a secured lender's forced sale positively assumes such arrangements exist and are lawful, so the loan leg of a funded collar is not restricted by this Policy.

clause: A member of the Key Management Personnel must not enter into an arrangement with anyone if that arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that: (a) has not vested in the member; or (b) has vested in the member but remains subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: This is broader than the 'Company Securities' Dealing regime (it catches any arrangement with anyone, not just exchange-traded Company Securities) and would catch an OTC collar over unvested or holding-locked equity remuneration, but it does not reach vested, unrestricted shares.

clause: Notwithstanding clauses 9(a) and 9(c) but subject to clause 9(b), the following types of trading are excluded from the operation of this policy: ... a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights
why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale of the collared shares is excluded from the Black Out Period and clearance requirements (though it remains subject to the insider trading prohibition in clause 9(b)), giving the bank a clear enforcement path even during a closed period.

clause: This form is valid for a period of three business days from the date of approval.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar trade must be priced and executed within 3 business days of approval, a tight window for documenting an OTC derivative with a bank.

clause: Key Management Personnel means a person having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company... Designated Person means a Director or person having authority for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company...
why_it_matters: The two defined terms are nearly identical but not declared coextensive; in practice the same director or executive is likely both a Designated Person (subject to Black Out Periods and clearance) and a member of Key Management Personnel (subject to the separate hedging ban), so both regimes need to be checked for any individual counterparty.

clause: engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to PEXA Securities including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of PEXA Securities
why_it_matters: Put and call options, and 'other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of PEXA Securities', are expressly named as requiring prior written approval – an OTC equity collar with a bank is squarely and expressly caught, not merely swept in by a general dealing definition.

topic: hedging permitted with approval, even pre-vesting
clause: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that would have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with PEXA Securities including securities which are unvested, subject to a holding lock or issued pursuant to an equity based remuneration scheme.
why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies that flatly ban hedging of unvested or holding-locked equity, PEXA only requires prior written approval from the Authorising Officer even for unvested or locked securities, leaving room in principle for a cleared collar over such securities subject to the Authorising Officer's discretion.

clause: Any dealing in PEXA Securities by any Personnel pursuant to a margin lending arrangement is not permitted. Such dealings would cover: ... selling PEXA Securities in the Company to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
why_it_matters: Unlike typical ASX policies, PEXA's Annexure of excluded dealings contains no carve-out for a secured lender's forced sale; a margin call sale is itself listed as a prohibited dealing, so the bank could not rely on enforcement/forced sale rights without exposing the executive to a policy breach.

clause: Any dealing in PEXA Securities by any Personnel pursuant to a margin lending arrangement is not permitted.
why_it_matters: The prohibition is confined to 'margin lending arrangement[s]'; it does not extend in terms to 'any other secured financing arrangement', so a bespoke bank loan secured by a pledge of the collared shares that is not documented as a margin loan may sit outside the literal wording, though the breadth of 6.8's 'vary economic risk' language creates residual risk it would still require, or be refused, approval.

clause: Any clearance to trade can be given, withdrawn or refused by the Company in its discretion without giving any reasons ... If clearance to trade PEXA Securities is refused, the person seeking the clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: Clearance for a collar trade is entirely discretionary, revocable without reasons, and any refusal must be kept confidential from the bank counterparty, adding execution uncertainty.

clause: in the case of Directors, provided with sufficient information to enable the Company to comply with its ASX reporting obligations ... no later than five business days after the date of the change. The Company requires the notification to reach the Reporting Officer within 3 days of the trade or other change of interest.
why_it_matters: A Director's collar trade will need to be reported to ASX within the standard change-of-interest timeframe, and the Company requires internal notice within 3 days, both of which the bank's documentation timetable needs to accommodate.

clause: Designated Persons are not permitted to deal at any time in financial products such as options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over the Company’s Securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions. An exception may apply where the Company’s Securities form a component of a listed portfolio or index product.
why_it_matters: This is a standalone, unconditional prohibition (not merely a Dealing requiring clearance) that squarely covers a bank-written OTC put and call over Karoon shares, and unlike the closed-period regime it has no exceptional-circumstances or clearance override, so a funded collar cannot be structured under this policy regardless of vesting state or timing.

clause: Designated Persons are not permitted to enter into transactions in products associated with the Company’s Securities which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company over unvested entitlements (eg hedging arrangements).
why_it_matters: Even if 5.1's absolute ban were read narrowly, this separate clause independently blocks any hedge of unvested holdings, confirming a collar can only ever be contemplated (subject to 5.1) over vested shares.

clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending agreement, is excluded trading and may be undertaken at any time.
why_it_matters: If a lender could ever hold security (which 5.1 does not directly forbid but the derivative ban makes moot for a collar), its enforcement sale would not itself breach the closed-period rules, though entering the security arrangement is otherwise unaddressed by the policy.

clause: The Chairman or the Company Secretary may specify additional periods when Designated Persons are prohibited from trading including during periods when the Company or its subsidiaries are involved in the drilling or testing of exploration wells.
why_it_matters: For an exploration company these ad hoc blackouts can be frequent and of undefined length, adding timing risk to any entry, roll or unwind of a collar structure even where one were otherwise permitted.

clause: the period from the close of trading 10 days before the Company’s annual general meeting.
why_it_matters: The lodged text does not state when this closed period ends, creating uncertainty as to open-window timing for any dealing (including collar execution) around the AGM.

clause: Officers and Connected Entities must not grant a security interest over Nick Scali securities they own, including any margin loan without first receiving the written consent of the Chairman.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar for an Officer is only possible with the Chairman's prior written consent to the security interest over the collared shares; the clause does not on its face extend to Directors.

clause: Nick Scali Directors, Officers and employees must not enter into a transaction that is designated or intended to hedge that employee’s exposure to the Nick Scali security that is subject to retention arrangements or an unvested Nick Scali option.
why_it_matters: The hedging ban, and therefore the collar's put/call legs, only bites on unvested or retention-locked securities; hedging fully vested, unrestricted shares is not expressly prohibited, which is the state a funded collar would target.

clause: Officers and Connected Entities must not grant a security interest over Nick Scali securities they own, including any margin loan without first receiving the written consent of the Chairman.
why_it_matters: Because Directors are not named in this clause, a Director's secured loan against vested shares is not addressed by any express prohibition or consent requirement in the policy, unlike an Officer's.

clause: Officers and Connected Entities must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in Nick Scali securities.
why_it_matters: An Officer's collar should be structured with sufficient tenor and a clear non-speculative rationale to avoid characterisation as short-term or speculative trading; this restriction does not apply to Directors on its face.

clause: Directors and Officers are encouraged to give prior notification to the Company Secretary of any proposed dealing in Nick Scali Limited’s securities. Directors and Officers are to advise the Company Secretary as soon as possible after a trade has occurred.
why_it_matters: Outside Blackout Periods there is no mandatory pre-clearance system for Directors or Officers, only mandatory post-trade notice (to support ASX Appendix 3Y reporting for Directors), which eases execution timing for a collar entered in an open window.

clause: each Director or Officer must take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Connected Entity complies with this Policy in relation to Nick Scali Limited Securities.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the security-interest consent requirement or the hedging ban, since Connected Entities are directly bound and the Director/Officer must ensure their compliance.

clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 7.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that ban secured financing outright, the loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is structurally available here, subject only to obtaining prior written clearance.

clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities at any time, including in the exceptional circumstances referred to in section 6, unless the Restricted Person first obtains prior written clearance

clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement... is excluded from the restrictions outlined in section 5

why_it_matters: A cleared collar (and its secured loan) must be priced and executed within roughly 30 days of clearance or a fresh approval will be needed.

clause: As Judo is an authorised deposit-taking institution, Judo and its Securities are subject to the Financial Sector (Shareholdings) Act 1998 (Cth), meaning that any shareholding interest in Judo which exceeds 20% could attract penalties.

clause: If a clearance to deal is granted, clearance will last for 5 business days from the date given.

why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is independently and absolutely prohibited with no Company consent or clearance mechanism.

clause: Notwithstanding any of the prohibitions contained in this Policy, Marimaca Personnel may trade ... pursuant to a trading plan ... properly adopted and ... administered in accordance with National Instrument 55-104
why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, the only relief mechanism in the entire document is the Pre-Approved Trading Plan; there is no severe-financial-hardship or court-order exception to the trading, hedging or margin bans.

topic: controlled entities and associates swept in
clause: partnerships, trusts, corporations, RRSP's and other accounts or entities over which any of the above-mentioned individuals exercise control or direction
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust, holding company or RRSP does not avoid the hedging or pledging bans, as these entities are themselves 'Marimaca Personnel'.

topic: Canadian-law policy referencing no ASX regime
clause: Marimaca Copper Corp. ... is a publicly traded company listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (the "TSX"). As such, trades in Marimaca's securities are subject to Canadian rules and regulations, as well as the rules and regulations of the TSX.
why_it_matters: The policy contains no ASX Listing Rule references, ASX blackout alignment or ASX notification regime; if Marimaca's ASX-quoted securities are covered by the same defined term 'Marimaca's securities', the hedging and pledging bans apply identically to them even though this document is drafted around Canadian and TSX requirements.

clause: (lender disposal) arises through the disposal of PWR Securities by a lender exercising their rights, except under a margin lending or other funding arrangement that is not permitted under this Policy.
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale on default is an excepted Trade even in a closed period, but only if the underlying secured financing arrangement was itself permitted under the Policy (i.e. Board-approved), so Board approval must be secured up front to preserve the lender's enforcement rights.

topic: Board approval regime for secured financing
clause: You must obtain the Board’s approval to enter into a margin lending, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement in relation to PWR Securities, providing the Board with the material terms of the proposed arrangements, including the right of the lender to sell unilaterally and trigger events.
why_it_matters: Unlike an outright ban, PWH allows a funded collar over vested unrestricted shares if the Board pre-approves the structure and is shown the loan's unilateral sale rights and trigger events, giving the bank a workable (if discretionary) approval pathway.

clause: You must not enter into margin lending, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement in relation to PWR Securities that would have the effect of limiting your exposure to risk in relation to part or all of your remuneration that has not vested, or has vested but remains subject to a restriction arrangement (eg a holding lock).
why_it_matters: A collar cannot be written over unvested equity or shares still under a plan holding lock; the bank must confirm vesting and lock release before structuring.

clause: If you have entered into any margin lending arrangement, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement with the Board’s approval, you must keep the Company Secretary informed of any change in circumstances that may be relevant to PWR’s continuous disclosure obligations.
why_it_matters: Re-margining, restructuring or early termination of the collar/loan must be reported to the Company Secretary throughout its life, not just at inception.

clause: you are required to notify PWR of intended dealings in PWR Securities, by yourself or your Closely Connected Persons, at least three days prior to the intended Trading. ... Following completion of the proposed Trade, you must confirm to the Authorising Officer and the Company Secretary that the Trade has occurred, and details of the price per Security.
why_it_matters: Entry, unwind or roll of the collar's derivative legs each need at least three business days' advance notice and post-trade confirmation of price and quantity, adding lead time to execution.

clause: The Board may vary the prohibited periods from time to time by providing notice (written or electronic) to all Restricted Persons.
why_it_matters: The Board can shorten open trading windows at will, adding timing risk to when the collar can be entered, unwound or rolled.

clause: This policy applies to both the sale and purchase of any securities of the Company and its subsidiaries on issue from time to time.
why_it_matters: Because the policy's scope is limited to buying, selling or exercising rights in company-issued securities and never mentions derivatives, hedging or margin lending as regulated activities, an OTC put/call with a bank falls outside its express approval and closed-period regime, though the bank should confirm this reading with the Company Secretary before relying on it.

topic: lender default sale and insider law
clause: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
why_it_matters: This gives unusually strong comfort that the bank's enforcement sale on default will not itself constitute insider trading by the executive even if inside information exists at the time, and 3.4(a)(xii) separately excepts such a sale from the Closed Period restriction.

clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company securities (ie a volume that would represent a volume in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller prior to the sale, or a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume of the shares of the Company on the ASX for the preceding 20 trading days) by a Key Management Personnel needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company’s legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
why_it_matters: Unwinding or settling a sizeable collar by physical delivery/sale could cross the 10%-of-holding or 10%-of-ADV thresholds, triggering a mandatory pre-sale discussion with the Board and legal advisers, adding a step and lead time to execution.

clause: Any Key Management Personnel (other than the Chairman) wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company’s securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Chairman or the Board before doing so.
why_it_matters: It is untested whether writing a call or buying a put (which does not itself buy, sell or exercise rights in ELS shares) triggers this approval requirement; the bank should seek company confirmation rather than assume the derivative legs are unregulated.

clause: This Policy provides guidance for Directors, Senior Executives and employees in relation to their dealing in securities of the Company.
why_it_matters: The policy never mentions margin lending, hedging, encumbrance or secured financing, so the loan leg of a funded collar secured on TUA shares is not directly regulated by any express prohibition or approval regime; the bank should confirm treatment with the Company Secretary rather than assume it is unregulated.

clause: Securities include shares of any class, options, bonds, derivatives, managed investments and superannuation products and any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market.
why_it_matters: Because 'derivatives' is listed as a Security in its own right, an OTC put/call referencing TUA shares is a Security and entering it is 'dealing' subject to the Window Period/Closed Period/written acknowledgement regime, just like a share trade.

clause: Directors and Senior Executives are only permitted to deal in the Company’s securities during a six week period following the release of the Company’s half yearly and annual results ... and the Company’s Annual General Meeting.
why_it_matters: Entry, unwind or roll of the collar's derivative legs, or any settlement sale, is normally confined to those six-week windows unless separate written acknowledgement is obtained for out-of-window trading.

clause: Subsequent dealing in the underlying security is restricted as outlined in this Policy.
why_it_matters: Shares obtained through an excluded dealing (e.g. exercise of options) remain subject to the ordinary Window Period/Closed Period regime for any later sale or delivery under the collar.

clause: Directors must advise the Company of details of any trading in securities by them or by persons or entities controlled by them ... within 2 business days ... to notify the ASX of details of any transaction on behalf of a Director within 5 business days of the trade.
why_it_matters: Entry or unwind of the collar by a Director (or an entity they control) must be reported to the Company Secretary within 2 business days for prompt ASX notifiable-interest disclosure.

clause: Where a clearance is requested for a Dealing under this policy, clearance will not be granted where the Dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even a technically compliant collar structure can be refused clearance if Kelsian judges it would look inappropriate if reported publicly, adding a discretionary reputational screen on top of the formal criteria.

clause: Kelsian may, at its discretion, make any clearance conditional upon such terms and conditions as Kelsian sees fit, including (without limitation) with regard to the circumstances in which Kelsian Securities may be sold to satisfy a margin loan call.
why_it_matters: Kelsian can constrain in advance when and how the bank's collateral could be sold on a call, which may limit the bank's enforcement flexibility on the secured loan leg of a collar.

clause: they have considered their duties to Kelsian, the risk of insider trading and that they, having regard to their own personal circumstances, consider that the risks of a forced sale of Kelsian Securities on a margin loan call is low.
why_it_matters: The Restricted Person must be able to represent in writing that the risk of a forced sale is low before clearance will be sought, which may constrain loan-to-value ratios or require additional collateral/margin buffers on the bank's facility.

topic: absolute hedging ban for Restricted Persons
clause: Restricted Persons and their Related Parties must not enter into hedging arrangements in relation to Kelsian Securities.
why_it_matters: This forecloses the put/call legs of a funded collar for directors, KMP, Senior Executives and Senior Managers entirely, regardless of vesting state or Board approval; only non-restricted employees may hedge (subject to conditions).

clause: Deal / Dealing: Includes ... entering into a contract to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations ... using as security, or otherwise granting a charge, lien or other encumbrance ... entering, terminating, assigning or novating any Securities lending agreement ... any transaction ... effecting change of ownership of a beneficial interest.
why_it_matters: Every leg of a funded collar (the OTC put/call, the loan security grant, and any unwind) is squarely captured as a 'Dealing', so no leg escapes the closed period, clearance or Front Page Test regime by structuring around a narrower securities definition.

clause: In this policy "Company Securities" includes ... derivatives and other financial products issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares, debentures and options.
why_it_matters: An OTC put/call written by a bank over UOS shares is expressly, not merely inferentially, a 'Company Security', so entering it is squarely a regulated dealing requiring the Chairman's consent for directors/executives.

clause: To "deal" in the Company Securities includes ... entering into agreements or transactions which operate to limit the economic risk of a person's holdings in the Company Securities.
why_it_matters: This clause is a direct description of a collar; it confirms the hedge is a 'deal' subject to the same consent/notification regime as an outright sale, with no separate vesting-based hedging ban.

clause: the recommended time (in terms of avoiding suggestions of insider trading) for any Designated Person to deal in the Company Securities is during the 4 week period from [AGM/quarterly/half-year/annual results/prospectus release].
why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, there is no binding closed period; timing of collar entry, unwind or roll is governed mainly by Chairman consent and the absence of inside information, not by a hard blackout calendar, giving more scheduling flexibility.

clause: This policy applies to all directors, executives, employees, contractors, consultants and advisors ... of United Overseas Australia Limited.
why_it_matters: Margin lending, encumbrance and secured financing are never mentioned, so the loan leg of a funded collar is not directly regulated by this document; the bank should confirm the Company Secretary's view before relying on this silence.

topic: no lender forced-sale or takeover carve-out
clause: (no equivalent clause found in the policy)
why_it_matters: Unlike many ASX peers, there is no express exception for a secured lender's forced sale on default, or for dealing under a takeover/scheme of arrangement, so enforcement of the loan against the collateral shares would still require the Chairman's consent (or, for an employee, notification) even on default.

clause: Please find attached a copy of the "Securities Dealing Policy" ... (letter addressed to both the Australian Securities Exchange and the Singapore Stock Exchange).
why_it_matters: The Company also reports to the Singapore Stock Exchange and has a Malaysian office; this policy text does not reference SGX-specific dealing restrictions, so the bank should independently confirm whether additional overlay requirements apply.

clause: subject to paragraph 4.2, a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from the blackout, trading-window and short-term dealing rules].
why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, a lender's enforcement sale during a blackout period is expressly excluded from breaching the Policy, which reduces enforcement risk for the bank on the collar's secured loan leg.

clause: Directors and Senior Executives must obtain approval in accordance with the procedure set out in section 3.6 for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement, irrespective of any trading window.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar for Directors/Senior Executives always needs prior approval (never just notification), even inside an open trading window, adding a timing dependency to closing.

clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with 4.2(b) conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: The Company can impose bespoke conditions on how and when the bank may sell collared shares to satisfy a call, which could constrain the lender's enforcement mechanics.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Approval for the collar can be refused on reputational grounds even if it otherwise complies with the technical rules.

clause: Employees must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Persons do not breach this Policy.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the Policy; the Employee remains responsible for the Connected Person's compliance.

clause: Hedging includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Company securities.
why_it_matters: There is no defined term for 'securities' or 'dealing' that expressly extends to OTC derivatives generally; an OTC put/call collar is caught only via the hedging concept, so any collar-like structure not framed as risk-limiting could arguably fall outside the Policy's express hooks.

clause: (short positions) Trading in Securities which enable a Staff member to profit from or limit the economic risk of a decrease in the market price of Securities;
why_it_matters: This clause has no vesting or tier qualifier, so it independently bans the purchased-put leg of any collar over any Securities (vested or unvested) for every Staff member, making a funded collar impossible under this Policy regardless of approval sought.

clause: Derivatives has the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act and includes options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars.
why_it_matters: The Policy expressly recognises a 'collar' as a Derivative and therefore a Security in scope; there is no argument that an OTC collar falls outside the Policy's defined terms.

clause: an involuntary disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights. However, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending arrangement where such arrangement is prohibited by this Policy.
why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale is excluded from breach only if the underlying secured loan was itself properly Board-approved; an unapproved or informally structured funded facility would leave the bank's enforcement sale in breach of the Policy.

clause: the Corporations Act prohibits a Senior Executive and their “closely related parties” from entering into arrangements that would have the effect of limiting the Senior Executive’s exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration ... that has not vested, or has vested but remains subject to a disposal restriction.
why_it_matters: This is a non-waivable statutory prohibition (not merely a Policy rule) that extends to a Senior Executive's spouse, children, dependants and controlled trusts/companies/super funds, so routing the collar through such an entity does not avoid it for unvested or restricted remuneration securities.

clause: Any Staff who hold Securities subject to binding restrictions on transfer (either as ASX restricted securities or through voluntary escrow arrangements) must comply with the terms of any applicable escrow arrangements and will be unable to trade in Securities during that time.
why_it_matters: Shares under ASX or voluntary escrow cannot be collared at all during the escrow period, independent of the vesting analysis.

clause: Directors and employees are prohibited from entering into an arrangement (including short selling Aspen Group Securities or dealing in Derivatives) that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk in relation to vested or unvested Aspen Group Securities (including any such Securities granted as part of their remuneration).
why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, there is no carve-out for vested, unrestricted securities and no clearance route at all - the purchased-put leg of a collar is banned for every director and employee regardless of vesting state.

clause: Directors and employees must not enter into a margin lending arrangement or any other form of financing arrangement secured against Aspen Group Securities.
why_it_matters: This is broader than a margin-loan-only restriction and has no Board-approval pathway or disclosure regime, so the loan leg of a funded collar secured on the shares is prohibited outright for every director and employee.

clause: What is a "Derivative"? Means, in relation to Aspen Group Securities, options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars as defined in section 761D of the Corporations Act.
why_it_matters: The Policy expressly recognises a 'collar' as a Derivative within the defined 'Aspen Group Securities', closing off any argument that an OTC collar structure falls outside scope.

clause: All employees and directors must make sure that their spouses, children, parents and trustees are informed of this policy and to take reasonable steps to make sure they comply.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or related entity does not avoid the Rule 5 or Rule 6 prohibitions.

clause: KMP are prohibited at all times from Dealing in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's Securities. For the avoidance of doubt this clause does not apply to an option over unissued capital granted by the Company.
why_it_matters: This stands apart from, and is not curable by, the Policy's clearance regimes for ordinary Dealing or margin lending - there is no route for any KMP (which includes every director and the CEO, CFO and company secretary) to obtain approval for an OTC put, call or collar.

clause: An Employee (who is not a KMP) may Deal in Company Securities ... if he or she does not have information that he or she knows, or ought reasonably to know, is Inside Information.
why_it_matters: Employees who are not KMP face no Closed Period, clearance, hedging or margin-lending restriction at all, so a funded collar could in principle be offered to a non-KMP employee subject only to the insider trading law overlay - a materially different (and better) answer than for the executive/director population a bank would typically target.

clause: the Approving Officer does not believe that there are appropriate arrangements in place between the KMP and the margin lender or financier to enable the KMP to comply with the terms of this Policy and with applicable securities laws, including clause 6.1 if there is any Dealing in any Company Securities by the margin lender or financier;
why_it_matters: Clearance for the funding leg can be refused unless the loan documents ensure the bank's own enforcement sale will itself respect Closed Periods and the no-inside-information rule, and there is no stated exception allowing a forced sale to proceed during a Closed Period.

clause: Relevant Interest A person has a Relevant Interest in securities if they: are the holder of the securities; or have power to exercise ... a right to vote attached to the securities; or have power to dispose of ... the securities.
why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, there is no express 'associate', 'connected person' or family-member extension - only the KMP's own Relevant Interest is captured - so the Policy's text may not on its face bind a spouse or family trust trading independently, though general securities law would still apply to them.

topic: Protection Arrangement scoped to unvested/locked only
clause: The entering into of any type of Protection Arrangements for any Cuscal Securities (or Cuscal products in the derivatives markets) is prohibited at all times in respect of any Cuscal Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock otherwise.
why_it_matters: Unlike several peer policies, this ban does not reach vested, unrestricted Securities, so a collar's put/call legs over such shares are treated as an ordinary Dealing requiring only a Trading Window and Authorising Officer consent, not an outright prohibition.

topic: absolute margin lending ban regardless of vesting
clause: Cuscal Persons are prohibited at all times from entering into any margin lending arrangement involving Cuscal Securities.
why_it_matters: This sentence has no vesting qualifier, unlike the security-granting sentence beside it, so if the bank's loan is characterised as a margin lending arrangement it is banned even over vested, unrestricted shares - the facility should be structured, or specifically cleared, to avoid that characterisation.

clause: the Authorising Officer, has discretion to approve Dealings in Cuscal Securities outside a Trading Window, or other Dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this Policy (except if granting such approval would be likely to result in a breach of any applicable insider trading laws).
why_it_matters: This is broad enough to arguably extend to overriding the 6.2/6.3 absolute prohibitions, but the 'at all times' wording in those clauses creates real interpretive tension; the bank should obtain an express written ruling rather than assume the override applies.

clause: for the purposes section 5 of this Policy only, a spouse (including a de facto spouse), child (including a stepchild or adopted child), a close relative, a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with any of the persons referred to above.
why_it_matters: A spouse, family trust or controlled company is itself directly bound by the Trading Window and clearance requirements, so routing the collar or loan through them does not avoid the Policy.

clause: a disposal of Cuscal Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement;
why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale is exempted from the Policy's Trading Window and other restrictions (subject to insider trading law), with only a post-transaction notice to the Authorising Officer required, which favours the bank's enforcement position once the underlying facility is properly established.

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested entitlements and prohibited periods
clause: The dealing in financial products issued or granted over or in respect of Pacific Niugini securities which have the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements is prohibited during a prohibited period.
why_it_matters: The only express hedging restriction targets unvested entitlements and only bites during a prohibited period; a collar over vested, unrestricted shares taken outside a prohibited period is not expressly banned by this clause.

topic: no secured financing or encumbrance provisions
clause: (the policy contains no reference to margin loans, secured financing, granting security, or a lender's forced sale)
why_it_matters: On the face of this policy a bank loan secured on the collared shares is not addressed and therefore not prohibited, though Senior Management would still need pre-approval to enter into the collar/loan transaction itself as 'trading', and a forced sale by the bank during a prohibited period would still be a dealing needing separate justification.

clause: securities are any listed or unlisted class of share, right, option, warrant, convertible note, bond, debenture, or any financial products issued or created over or in respect of Pacific Niugini securities.
why_it_matters: Because this definition has no venue limitation, an OTC put and call are dealings requiring the same clearance and window compliance as an on-market trade.

clause: Dealing in Pacific Niugini securities by a family member is to be discouraged, except outside a prohibited period.
why_it_matters: A collar or loan routed through a spouse or family trust is not formally prohibited, only discouraged, and there is no enforceable associate-dealing regime to navigate around.

clause: Once you have completed a transaction you must report details of the transaction to the Company Secretary. Directors ... all changes in Pacific Niugini securities they hold directly or indirectly within 2 days of the transaction occurring.
why_it_matters: Entry into, and any variation or close-out of, the collar or loan must be reported to the Company Secretary (within 2 days for Directors), making the bank relationship visible to the Company even though it is not itself restricted.

clause: KMP are prohibited at all times from Dealing in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's Securities.
why_it_matters: This is an unconditional, closed-period-independent ban on any derivative over the Company's securities for KMP, with no clearance carve-out anywhere in the Policy, so a funded collar's put and call legs cannot lawfully be entered by a KMP.

clause: A KMP may not deal in Company Securities on considerations of a short-term nature or engage in hedging or short-sale transactions with respect to Company Securities.
why_it_matters: Independently reinforces the derivatives ban and would separately catch the written call leg of a collar as akin to a short-sale transaction.

clause: KMP are prohibited from entering into margin lending or similar arrangements in respect to Company Securities they hold or in which they have a Relevant Interest without first obtaining prior clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded structure would likely qualify as a 'similar arrangement' to margin lending and could be cleared with 10 Business Days' notice and document review, but this only addresses the financing leg; the derivative legs remain absolutely banned by clause 6.3, so the funded collar as a whole cannot proceed for a KMP.

clause: the Approving Officer does not believe that there are appropriate arrangements in place between the KMP and the margin lender or financier to enable the KMP to comply with the terms of this Policy ... including clause 6.1 if there is any Dealing in any Company Securities by the margin lender or financier
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale on collateral shares is itself treated as a Dealing subject to the insider trading and Closed Period rules, so enforcement mechanics must be built into the facility documentation reviewed at clearance stage.

clause: written requests and clearances ... are valid for a period the earlier of: (a) 5 Business Days; (b) the Business Day before the Company enters a Closed Period; and (c) the time that the KMP comes into possession of Inside Information.
why_it_matters: Any cleared dealing (were the derivatives ban not absolute) would need to complete within a short and conditional window, relevant to timing the loan clearance and any related transfer of shares.

clause: An Employee (who is not a KMP) may Deal in Company Securities or the Securities of a Transaction Entity if he or she does not have information that he or she knows, or ought reasonably to know, is Inside Information
why_it_matters: A senior executive who does not meet the AASB 124 KMP definition faces none of the Closed Period, clearance, derivatives-ban, or hedging/short-sale restrictions, so a funded collar may be executable for that person subject only to the general insider trading rule.

topic: hedging ban has no clearance route
clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights).
why_it_matters: Unlike ordinary share dealing (which goes through the notify-and-confer process) or margin loans (which can be consented to), hedging is an absolute ban with no clearance, waiver or exceptional-circumstances mechanism reaching a derivative transaction; the only clearance available under clause 1.8 permits a sale, not entry into a hedge.

topic: margin loan consent scope uncertain for a bespoke bank facility
clause: otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Company's consent
why_it_matters: Clause 1.11 is drafted around a conventional margin loan portfolio and margin account; it is unclear whether a bespoke bilateral loan from a bank secured by a pledge over the collared shares (not a standard margin lending facility) is covered by this consent regime at all, leaving a structuring gap the Company would need to address by extension or analogy.

clause: Each Restricted Person has a personal responsibility to ensure that his or her associated parties ... complies with the same respective restrictions as apply to Restricted Persons.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or family company does not escape the hedging ban or the margin lending consent requirement.

clause: The Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their respective associated parties trading in the Company's shares at any time.
why_it_matters: Even if a structuring workaround to the hedging ban were found, the Board could unilaterally freeze all dealing at any time with no stated notice or confidentiality requirement, adding execution risk to any financing timeline.

clause: The use of derivatives or any other hedging instrument over Iress equity ... is prohibited and those entering into such schemes will be in breach of the terms and conditions of the grant. As a consequence, the Board will exercise its right to cancel / clawback the hedged unvested or restricted equity.
why_it_matters: This is an unconditional ban reaching every tier and every security state, with a clawback penalty attached to unvested or restricted equity; it leaves no structural path for either leg of a funded collar.

topic: margin lending ban has no clearance route
clause: Directors and Restricted Persons must not enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire Iress Securities ... or grant lenders any rights over Iress Securities.
why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies that allow margin/secured lending subject to company consent, IRE bans it outright for Directors and Restricted Persons with no clearance mechanism at all, so the loan leg cannot be structured for those tiers regardless of the collar's economics; the ban is not stated to extend to plain employees, though the separate 5.4 derivatives ban would still block their collar's option legs.

topic: minimum shareholding requirement named in the hedging ban
clause: The use of derivatives or any other hedging instrument over Iress equity (including Iress Securities subject to a minimum shareholding requirement ...) is prohibited
why_it_matters: Shows the Board specifically anticipated and shut down the argument that MSR-mandated holdings could be hedged while nominally satisfying the requirement.

topic: Associate coverage may not extend to the margin lending ban
clause: Directors and Restricted Persons must not enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement ... (clause 5.3, no reference to Associates, contrasted with clause 2.2 which expressly extends approval requirements to 'Directors and Restricted Persons (and their Associates)')
why_it_matters: Clause 5.3's text does not repeat the Associate extension used elsewhere in the policy, creating textual ambiguity as to whether a family trust or company associated with a Director could enter a secured facility, though the general clause 1.1 statement that the whole policy applies to Associates would likely be read to close this gap.

topic: refusal confidentiality runs the other way
clause: If approval to trade is refused, you must keep that information confidential.
why_it_matters: The confidentiality obligation on a refused approval binds the individual, not just the Company, which is relevant to how a bank counterparty could be told about a declined clearance.

clause: no employee or director of the Company or its subsidiary companies may, directly or through other persons or entities: (a) buy or sell Air New Zealand securities
why_it_matters: The operative prohibition is confined to buying or selling shares; there is no dealing definition extending to derivatives, agreements to deal or encumbrances, so on its text an OTC put/call collar and a share-secured loan are not clearly caught, though the Company would likely still expect Approved Trading Procedure consent given the policy's insider-trading purpose.

clause: (policy contains no reference to unvested securities, performance rights, options or equity incentive schemes)
why_it_matters: There is no vesting-based restriction to navigate, but also no guidance on how the Company would treat a collar over vested holdings; the outcome would depend entirely on how 'buy or sell' is interpreted case by case.

clause: Securities Trading Policy Updated November 2010
why_it_matters: This document predates the derivatives, hedging and margin-lending language now standard in ASX-listed issuers' policies; a current version lodged more recently should be checked before relying on this silence.

clause: If you are not a Restricted Person and intend to trade Air New Zealand shares with a total value of $10,000 or more, you must also obtain prior written consent
why_it_matters: Non-restricted staff below this threshold face no consent requirement at all, which is immaterial for directors/executives (who are Restricted Persons) but shows the policy's consent regime is value-triggered rather than instrument-triggered.

clause: a disposal of Catapult Securities that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights under a loan agreement
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is expressly carved out of the policy's Dealing restrictions, so it is not blocked by a Blackout Period, Pre-Clearance failure, or possession of Inside Information by the executive.

clause: Any approval by the Designated Approvers may be subject to the condition that Catapult be permitted to disclose to the ASX the existence of the margin loan or security arrangement, and ... any relevant terms such as the trigger points or right of the financier to sell unilaterally.
why_it_matters: The bank should expect the loan secured on the collared shares, and its trigger/enforcement terms, may be required to be disclosed publicly as a condition of Catapult's approval.

clause: Catapult Team Members and Adhering Contractors may only enter into a margin loan or other security arrangement in respect of Catapult Securities with the prior written approval of the Designated Approvers
