why_it_matters: Section 9.1's approval requirement applies to every Team Member/Contractor, but 'Designated Approvers' is only defined (7.2) for people who are themselves Designated Persons, leaving unclear who approves a financing arrangement for an executive who is not a Designated Person; the bank should have this confirmed before relying on the approval process.

clause: Catapult prohibits Catapult Team Members and Adhering Contractors from entering into transactions in associated products that operate to limit the economic risk of Catapult Securities over unvested entitlements.
why_it_matters: A collar can only be written over Catapult Securities that have already vested; unvested awards cannot be the reference security under any approval.

clause: The Company Secretary may, from time to time, establish, amend and remove rules to provide prospective approval to Dealings in Catapult Securities during permitted periods by one or more Designated Persons ... (the Prospective Rules)
why_it_matters: If a Prospective Rule were established for a Designated Person, the derivative legs of a collar could in principle be pre-approved on a standing basis rather than needing case-by-case Pre-Clearance, though this would need to be arranged with the Company Secretary/Chairman.

clause: this policy applies, for example, to Dealings in Catapult Securities by a Catapult Team Member's spouse ... I request the Designated Approvers' approval for the following proposed transaction to be undertaken by me, my Related Parties or Associates
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or its financing through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the Pre-Clearance or section 9 financing approval requirements.

clause: not enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company's Securities, or grant lenders any rights over their Company Securities
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the shares is expressly and absolutely prohibited for Directors and Restricted Employees, with no exception listed among Permitted Dealings or Exceptional Circumstances, so this population cannot grant the bank security over their holdings.

clause: Any clearance for the trading will be valid for 7 days from the date it is given. Prior written clearance may be withdrawn at the discretion of the Designated Officer without giving any reasons.
why_it_matters: The derivative legs of a collar must be priced and executed within a 7-day clearance window and remain vulnerable to withdrawal without explanation at any time before completion.

clause: Where prior written clearance is withdrawn or written clearance is refused, the decision ... must be kept confidential by the person seeking clearance and must not be disclosed to anybody.
why_it_matters: If clearance for the collar legs is refused, the executive cannot tell the bank why, which complicates coordinating deal timing and pricing with a counterparty bank.

clause: dealing in a company's securities (which includes shares and options)
why_it_matters: The policy never formally defines 'Securities' or 'Dealing'; whether an OTC cash-settled put and call over vested shares counts as 'trading in the Company's securities' at all is not addressed, so the bank should have this confirmed by the Company Secretary before relying on any clearance.

clause: During a Prohibited Period, Directors and Restricted Employees may trade in the Company's securities in the circumstances described below
why_it_matters: Unlike some peer policies, there is no Permitted Dealing carve-out for a disposal forced by a secured lender/financier exercising rights under a loan agreement; since 4.1(c) bans the underlying security grant outright for this tier in any event, the forced-sale scenario should not arise, but there is no fallback exception if it did.

topic: incentive scheme tax liability excluded from hardship
clause: A tax liability relating to Securities received under an employee incentive scheme would also not normally constitute severe financial hardship or otherwise be considered an exceptional circumstance for the purpose of obtaining proper written clearance to sell or otherwise dispose of securities during a Prohibited Period
why_it_matters: An executive cannot rely on incentive-scheme tax obligations as Exceptional Circumstances to trade around or unwind a collar during a Prohibited Period.

clause: Ridley employees, directors and officers must not enter into any derivative contract relating to a Ridley Security, or any other transaction that is designed or intended to securitise, or limit the economic risk of holding, a Ridley Security.
why_it_matters: Both legs of a funded collar (the purchased put and the written call) are OTC derivative contracts relating to a Ridley Security, so they are prohibited outright for every Ridley Staff member with no clearance path, which alone defeats the structure regardless of financing terms.

clause: (policy contains no section on margin loans, security arrangements or secured financing)
why_it_matters: There is no express prohibition, approval requirement or disclosure obligation for a loan secured against Ridley shares, but this is moot because the derivative legs of the collar cannot be entered into under section 5 in any event.

clause: any other transaction that is designed or intended to securitise, or limit the economic risk of holding, a Ridley Security
why_it_matters: This broad language would likely also catch a non-derivative monetisation structure (e.g. a prepaid forward) even if it were not technically a 'derivative contract', closing off alternative structures too.

clause: each director and Senior Executive must take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Close Associates comply with this Policy in relation to Ridley Securities
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a spouse, family trust or a controlled entity does not avoid the section 5 ban, since directors and Senior Executives are responsible for ensuring their Close Associates also comply.

clause: (no hardship, court order or exceptional-circumstances carve-out is stated anywhere in the policy)
why_it_matters: There is no discretion anywhere in the policy to permit a banned derivative, or to bring forward dealing during a Specific Prohibited Period, in exceptional circumstances.

topic: margin loan carve-out for other secured loans
clause: This prohibition includes all arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements but does not extend to other types of loan arrangements which may be secured by a security interest granted in respect of Group Securities.
why_it_matters: The section 14 ban targets only classic margin lending with value-triggered security rights; a bank's fixed-collateral loan secured on the collared shares is not 'properly described as a margin lending arrangement' and so falls outside the prohibition, though it must still be cleared as a Dealing.

clause: Directors and employees are prohibited from entering into an arrangement that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that is unvested, or which remains subject to a trading lock, forfeiture condition, restriction period or other restriction in a Group employee security scheme.
why_it_matters: A collar cannot be written over unvested remuneration or vested shares still subject to a trading lock or other scheme restriction; only fully vested, unrestricted holdings can be the reference security.

clause: If a director or an employee may not deal in the Group Securities, they must prohibit any dealing in the Group Securities by any associated person ... or any investment manager on their behalf
why_it_matters: If the individual is restricted (closed period or inside information), the collar cannot be executed through a spouse, family trust or discretionary investment manager on their behalf during that period.

clause: The Disclosure Officer may give clearance for a director or an employee to sell (but not buy) Group Securities in exceptional circumstances
why_it_matters: The only discretionary relief from a closed period is a sale-only clearance for pressing financial need; there is no equivalent route to write a call or buy a put during a closed period, so collar entry must occur in an open window.

clause: Directors and employees may be asked to keep as confidential the details of any such closed period.
why_it_matters: Cromwell can impose undisclosed extra closed periods, including ones triggered by inside information about another listed entity, creating execution timing risk that cannot be explained to the bank while confidential.

clause: An employee who deals in securities should use only one broker. Employees may not use broker credit.
why_it_matters: Financing for the collar cannot be structured as broker credit; it must come through a separate facility such as a bank loan, reinforcing reliance on the section 14 carve-out for non-margin secured loans.

clause: A Restricted Person must not engage in transactions designed to hedge their exposure to Company Securities.
why_it_matters: Unlike blackout periods or short-term trading, the hedging ban is not among the section 6.8 exceptions and section 6.9 expressly confines its waiver mechanism to sections 6.5(b) and 6.6 only, so the hedge legs of a collar cannot be entered into by a Restricted Person under any circumstance contemplated by the policy.

topic: financing has its own approval gate
clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities, unless the prior approval of the Chair (or his or her delegate) has been obtained.
why_it_matters: The loan secured on the shares can be approved by the Chair, unlike the hedge itself, but this approval route is of no practical use for a funded collar while the hedge legs remain absolutely banned.

clause: where a Restricted Person has been granted approval to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangement (refer section 6.11), an involuntary disposal of securities that result from the margin lender or financier exercising its rights under the arrangement.
why_it_matters: An enforcement sale by the lender is excepted from blackout periods only if Chair approval for the underlying financing arrangement was obtained beforehand; an unapproved arrangement gets no forced-sale protection.

topic: contractors may fall outside Restricted Persons
clause: Restricted Persons are: (a) all Directors including the CEO; (b) all other key management personnel of the Company; and (c) all employees are Restricted Persons
why_it_matters: Section 6.2 does not list contractors, even though section 2's rationale separately refers to 'Directors, employees and contractors'; a genuine non-employee contractor executive may fall outside the section 6.11 hedging/margin lending restrictions altogether, though this edge case would need confirmation from the Company Secretary.

clause: Each Restricted Person must: (a) ensure that any trading by their Closely Connected Persons is undertaken in accordance with this Policy
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a spouse, family trust or family company does not escape the Restricted Person's restrictions, since compliance by Closely Connected Persons is the Restricted Person's own responsibility.

clause: Derivatives ... includes ... put or call options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement.
why_it_matters: An equity collar (purchased put plus written call) is expressly captured as a 'Derivative' and therefore a Dealing under this policy regardless of venue, so OTC execution with a bank requires Clearance like any other Dealing.

clause: Save where expressly permitted by the Board, Relevant Persons are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Company Securities or in relation to which Company Securities may be used as security against loan repayments.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the shares is banned by default; a funded structure is only possible if the Board expressly approves it, and no criteria for that approval are stated.

topic: forced sale risk flagged but unresolved
clause: Margin loans to support an investment in Company Securities (and other types of margin lending arrangements) can compromise compliance with this policy, as the loan's terms may compel the sale of Company Securities during a blackout period or when the Relevant Person has relevant Inside Information.
why_it_matters: The policy flags but does not resolve the risk that a lender's enforcement sale during a blackout period would breach the policy; any Board approval of financing should address this gap contractually since no exception in clause 10.1 covers a lender-forced sale.

clause: [Clearance] will remain in force for the date of approval only, unless otherwise notified by the Clearance Officer (if the Dealing is not placed within this time, the Clearance will no longer have effect and a new Clearance must be requested and obtained).
why_it_matters: Absent an extended validity notified by the Clearance Officer, the collar's execution must occur on the same day Clearance is granted, tightening timing for pricing and documentation with the bank.

clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances surrounding the Company, could the proposed Dealing be perceived by the market as the Relevant Person or his or her Associate taking advantage of his or her position in an inappropriate way?
why_it_matters: Clearance may be refused under clause 11.5(c) if a collar or its unwind would fail this subjective public-perception test, independent of the Inside Information analysis.

clause: If a Relevant Person is a director of the Company, he or she must ensure that an Appendix 3Y Change of Directors' Interest Notice is completed ... and provided to the Company Secretary within two business days after any Dealing in Company Securities.
why_it_matters: Granting security to the bank or entering the derivative legs of a collar as a director triggers a public Appendix 3Y filing within two business days, disclosing the structure to the market.

clause: If a Relevant Person may not Deal in Company Securities, he or she must also prevent such Dealing by his or her Associate.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled company does not avoid the policy; the Relevant Person remains responsible for preventing the Associate from dealing when they themselves could not.

topic: near-total hedging ban for Designated Persons
clause: deal at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law and under this policy.
why_it_matters: This unqualified limb of the 'No hedging' clause appears to ban an OTC put/call collar for Designated Persons regardless of whether the underlying shares are vested, unless it can be characterised as a dealing type otherwise permitted under the policy.

clause: Everyone - including all employees, contractors, family and their Associates | The whole Trading Policy with the exception of paragraphs 1.4, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3 and 5.3
why_it_matters: Employees who are not Designated Persons face no margin-lending, short-term or hedging restriction at all, but the directors and executives targeted for a funded collar will almost always be Designated Persons, so this carve-out is unlikely to be available to the client base.

topic: secured financing gateway for vested shares
clause: The restrictions above do not prohibit other funding arrangements under which Company Securities may be included as security, however if a Designated Person proposes to enter into any such security arrangement the prior approval of the General Counsel or Company Secretary must be obtained prior to agreeing to provide Company Securities as security under any arrangement.
why_it_matters: This is the key gateway: a bank loan secured on vested, unrestricted Company Securities is expressly contemplated, subject only to prior GC/Company Secretary approval, separate from and additional to the ordinary Part 5 dealing clearance.

clause: you may request, and the Notification Officer may give, confirmation for you to ... dispose of Company Securities even if otherwise prohibited under Part 4.
why_it_matters: Gives a discretionary route to force an unwind sale despite the margin-lending/hedging prohibitions in Part 4, for example on severe financial hardship or court order, though a tax liability alone does not qualify and the outcome is at the Notification Officer's discretion.

clause: A confirmation confirms that the proposed dealing is within the terms of the Trading Policy but does not otherwise constitute approval or endorsement by the Company or the Notification Officer for the proposed dealing.
why_it_matters: The bank cannot treat a policy confirmation as validating the commercial terms of the collar or loan; the executive remains personally responsible for compliance with the insider trading law.

topic: short position ban catches a protective put
clause: represents a short position, which is Trading that enables an Employee to profit from or limit the economic risk of a decrease in the market price of Securities.
why_it_matters: The purchased put leg of a collar squarely limits the economic risk of a price decrease, so it falls within the 'short position' prohibition, which applies 'at any time' with no stated clearance or waiver route, unlike the Closed Period restrictions.

clause: Employees may not include their Securities ... in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise Trade ... pursuant to a margin or secured lending arrangement without first obtaining the consent of the Chairperson or their delegate/s.
why_it_matters: Unlike a flat ban, CCP allows a loan secured on the Securities with Chairperson (or delegate) consent, which the Company may make conditional, e.g. on the circumstances in which the shares may be sold to satisfy a call - the loan leg is achievable even though the put leg is not.

clause: disposal that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example under a margin lending arrangement where the Employee has no control over the disposal
why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale is an excluded Trade needing no clearance and permitted even during a Closed Period, provided the employee retains no control over the disposal - loan documentation should preserve the lender's unilateral enforcement right accordingly.

clause: Trading or Trade means, in respect of Securities and related financial instruments, buying or selling, entering into an agreement to buy or sell and exercising options, rights or awards to acquire Securities or related financial products.
why_it_matters: 'Related financial instruments'/'related financial products' is used throughout but never defined in clause 3.0, creating some uncertainty as to scope; in practice it is treated as covering third-party derivatives such as forward contracts and short positions, so an OTC collar and its financing are likely to be swept in.

clause: Directors are required to immediately notify the Company Secretary of any Trades undertaken by them (whether these occur during or outside of a Closed Period and whether with or without prior clearance (including excluded Trades)) to enable the Company to comply with its ASX reporting obligations.
why_it_matters: A director must immediately disclose any Trade, including a lender's forced sale, so the encumbrance and any enforcement will promptly become public via ASX reporting (e.g. Appendix 3Y).

topic: no hardship excuse for insider trading
clause: The existence of a personal financial emergency or hardship does not excuse non-compliance with this Policy.
why_it_matters: Financing or margin-call pressure cannot be used to justify dealing while in possession of inside information, so unwind timing must still respect information barriers regardless of the loan's terms.

clause: The policy governs 'dealing in the Company's shares' and use of 'the Company's securities as security'; it contains no defined 'Dealing' term and never mentions derivatives, options, swaps or hedging.
why_it_matters: There is no textual basis to determine whether an OTC put/call collar over CIN shares is caught by the policy at all; the safest assumption is that it would be treated as within the spirit of the blackout and margin-lending rules, but this is not addressed.

topic: unqualified ban on shares as loan security
clause: Directors and employees are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.
why_it_matters: This is an outright, unqualified prohibition on encumbering CIN shares for any loan, with no Board approval carve-out, exemption authority or waiver process identified anywhere in the policy - fatal to the loan leg of a funded collar.

clause: Should a Director also be a Director of an investee entity, where the holding in that entity exceeds 10% of the Company's total portfolio holding by market value, that Director should also consider the Trading Policy of the investee entity as if it related to shares in the Company.
why_it_matters: As CIN is an investment company, a director dealing in (or collaring) shares of a greater-than-10%-of-portfolio investee must separately comply with that investee's own, potentially different, trading policy.

clause: Such requests, which must be in writing, will generally be refused unless exceptional circumstances exist.
why_it_matters: Entering into or unwinding a collar during any of the four blackout periods is presumptively refused; only severe financial hardship or a court-ordered sale are given as examples of sufficient exceptional circumstances.

clause: The Company Secretary is to lodge an Appendix 3Y - Change of Director's Interest Notice with the ASX detailing whether a trade occurred during a closed period where prior written clearance was required and, if prior written clearance was required, whether that clearance was provided and the date on which it was provided.
why_it_matters: Any dealing connected to the collar by a director is publicly disclosed together with whether blackout clearance applied and was granted, and the date of that clearance.

clause: the use by any St Barbara Personnel of any derivative product or hedging in relation to St Barbara Securities designed to limit the economic risk of that St Barbara Personnel is prohibited.
why_it_matters: This clearance-proof, tier-blind ban prohibits both legs of an OTC collar (purchased put and written call) outright, regardless of vesting state, tier, or any clearance obtained, and has no exemption authority capable of overriding it.

clause: This prohibition does not extend to exchange traded options in St Barbara Securities which are acquired, disposed of and reported, provided that the effect of those exchange traded options does not limit or reduce the economic risk of that St Barbara Personnel.
why_it_matters: Too narrow to help: a collar is designed precisely to limit/reduce economic risk, so it falls outside this carve-out even if exchange-traded.

clause: Designated Employees may also be subject to a statutory prohibition in section 206J of the Corporations Act, which prohibits a member of key management personnel of St Barbara and their closely related parties from entering into an arrangement which would have the effect of limiting exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that has not vested, or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: An independent statutory prohibition for KMP on unvested/locked incentive securities cannot be waived by any policy clearance.

clause: a Designated Employee is not permitted to use their St Barbara Securities as collateral or to enter into a margin loan or similar arrangement ... without: a. obtaining confirmation from the lender ... that the St Barbara Securities will not be sold or disposed of by it in contravention of the Designated Employee's obligations under this Policy; and b. seeking and obtaining, in writing, formal clearance
why_it_matters: The secured-loan leg of a funded collar is structurally available (unlike the option legs) for Designated Employees who obtain lender confirmation and written clearance, and for other personnel merely by giving the lender a copy of the Policy.

clause: subject to the St Barbara Personnel or Connected Person having complied with section 7.2 of this Policy, a disposal of St Barbara Securities by a secured lender without the permission or authority of the St Barbara Personnel or Connected Person ... that is the result of that lender exercising its rights under a lending arrangement [is excluded from the Policy and may be undertaken] at any time, without prior written clearance
why_it_matters: If the loan (not the banned option legs) were ever put in place compliantly, a lender's enforcement sale on default would not itself breach the Policy or need fresh clearance, even inside a Blackout Period.

topic: voluntary margin-call sale gets no hardship relief
clause: a general tax liability, a tax liability relating to St Barbara Securities received under an employee incentive scheme or an obligation to sell under a collateralisation arrangement will not constitute Exceptional Circumstances.
why_it_matters: If the executive (rather than the lender) needs to sell to meet a margin call, no hardship exemption is available; the sale must still wait out any Blackout Period.

clause: A Clearance Notice may be given or refused by the persons listed in the table above, in their absolute discretion, without the need to provide reasons.
why_it_matters: Even for the permitted loan leg, approval is not guaranteed and the bank cannot treat clearance as a formality.

clause: the 12 month period referred to in section 4.3 [section 6.2] vs. 'within any 3 month period' [section 4.3]; the ASX cover letter notes the prior version lodged 3 June 2026 'contained errors in section 4.3'.
why_it_matters: The short-term dealing period is internally inconsistent following a recent, imperfect amendment; confirm the current 3- or 12-month figure directly with the company before relying on it for collar tenor.

clause: Any Dealings by Directors of St Barbara or any of their associates ... must be disclosed to the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) as required by Listing Rule 3.19A ... to report changes in a Director's holding within five (5) Business Days of a change occurring.
why_it_matters: Any permitted secured-loan leg entered into by a director becomes public within 5 business days, limiting confidentiality of the financing arrangement.

clause: The policy contains no reference anywhere to margin loans, collateral, pledges, charges, liens or secured financing arrangements over Alpha HPA Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares faces no express prohibition, clearance requirement or lender-disclosure obligation under this policy, unlike most peer policies.

topic: hedging ban is scoped to unvested plan securities
clause: Restricted Persons must not engage in hedging arrangements ... over unvested Securities issued pursuant to any employee or director option or share plan. In addition, any hedging over vested Securities must comply with this Policy.
why_it_matters: A collar over vested shares (rather than unvested incentive securities) is not banned outright; it is treated as an ordinary dealing subject to the section 8 notification/consent regime and blackout periods.

clause: If granted, trading consent is only valid for a period of 5 trading days after notification of approval.
why_it_matters: Any cleared dealing connected with the collar (entry, unwind, or a lender's exercise if treated as a dealing) must be completed within 5 trading days of consent, requiring tight coordination with the bank.

topic: no short-term dealing or minimum shareholding rule
clause: No provision of the policy imposes a minimum holding period, short-term dealing restriction, or minimum shareholding requirement.
why_it_matters: There is no policy-driven minimum tenor or floor that would constrain the collar's structure or duration.

topic: cashless exercise restriction while holding inside information
clause: Where an employee or executive director exercises options while in the possession of price sensitive information, he/she will have to fund the exercise of the options without the financial assistance of a simultaneous sale of some or all shares just acquired.
why_it_matters: If the executive holds inside information at option exercise, sell-to-cover funding is unavailable, which may affect the timing of when shares become available to be collared.

clause: Notwithstanding any other provision of this Policy, the CFO may exercise discretion to waive any provision of this Policy as it relates to any employee, officer or director in exceptional circumstances, and on such terms as the CFO considers appropriate.
why_it_matters: This is the only route by which the outright bans on hedging and secured financing could be waived for a funded collar; it is a case-by-case discretion, must be reported to the Board, and cannot be exercised while the individual holds undisclosed Material Information.

clause: any other hedging or equity monetization transaction in which the individual's economic interest and risk exposure in Patriot Securities or equity-based incentive arrangements is changed (such as collars or forward sales contracts)
why_it_matters: The policy names 'collars' directly as a prohibited transaction, leaving no room to argue a put/call collar falls outside the hedging ban.

clause: Subject to Section 5(b) herein, there are no exceptions under which a Reporting Insider or Designated Insider may be permitted to trade during a fixed or discretionary blackout period.
why_it_matters: Even if a waiver were obtained, execution, unwind or settlement of a collar or loan could not occur during a blackout period except under the narrow court-order exemption.

clause: Any individual who has ceased to be an employee, officer or director of Patriot ... must continue to comply with this Policy, including the obligation to pre-clear any trade and observe the blackout period ... and, in any event, for a period of 30 calendar days from the date of termination.
why_it_matters: The hedging and secured financing bans, and pre-clearance obligations, survive a departing director or executive for at least 30 days, affecting timing of any collar unwind around departure.

clause: If pre-clearance to trade in Patriot Securities is refused, the Reporting Insider or Designated Insider must keep this decision confidential and not disclose to any other person that the request for pre-clearance to trade has been refused.
why_it_matters: Even for aspects of a structure that could in principle be pre-cleared, a refusal cannot be disclosed to the bank, limiting transparency in structuring discussions.

clause: must not engage in any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Patriot Securities or equity-based incentive arrangements
why_it_matters: The secured financing and hedging bans expressly extend to unvested equity-based incentive arrangements as well as ordinary shares, closing off any vesting-based route to the structure.

clause: Designated Personnel are prohibited from trading in securities issued or created over the Company's Securities by third parties, or trading in associated products. In addition, Designated Personnel may not enter into a transaction that operates to limit the economic risk of their Security holding in the Company
why_it_matters: This clearance-free, tier-specific ban prohibits both a bank-issued OTC put/call (a third-party-created product) and the collar's risk-limiting effect, for any vesting state, with no exception in section 6 itself.

clause: The Policy contains no provision requiring approval or disclosure before a Designated Person grants security over, or margin-loans, Company Securities; only the resulting forced sale by a secured lender (7.7) is addressed.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is not independently regulated or blocked by this Policy, unlike the derivative legs which are expressly banned under section 6.

clause: a disposal of Securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is exempt from sections 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 3.8 and 4]
why_it_matters: If a secured loan against SunRice shares were in place, the lender's enforcement sale would be excluded entirely from blackout periods, trading windows and pre-trade approval.

topic: narrow trading windows for Designated Personnel
clause: Designated Personnel may only trade ... during the following periods (trading windows) ... All other times ... are referred to as prohibited periods and ... Designated Personnel are not permitted to buy or sell the Company's Securities at any of those times.
why_it_matters: Even where a trade were otherwise permitted, entry, unwind or settlement of any permitted leg is confined to ~4-week windows after results/AGM or an offer period, materially constraining timing.

clause: Where any approval is required for a trade under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the trade would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even a structurally permitted transaction (e.g. the loan) can be refused approval on reputational grounds independent of the strict legal rules.

clause: Designated Personnel must take appropriate steps to ensure that their 'Connected Persons' only trade in Securities in circumstances where the Designated Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to trade under this Policy
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family member or a controlled entity does not escape the section 6 prohibition or the approval regime.

clause: KMP and its Associates must not enter into transactions or arrangement which operate to limit the economic risk of its holdings of the Company's securities at any time
why_it_matters: This bans a put/call collar for KMP (and their Associates) in any vesting state, reinforced by the section 206J statutory prohibition for unvested or holding-locked incentive remuneration.

clause: no dealing in unvested securities (including hedging unvested securities) is permitted.
why_it_matters: Separately from the hedging ban, KMP cannot deal at all in unvested securities, foreclosing any collar or loan over unvested incentive awards regardless of clearance.

clause: where this policy permits KMP to enter into a margin lending or other secured financial arrangement in relation to the Company's securities, an involuntary disposal of securities that results from the margin lender or financier exercising its rights under the arrangement [is excluded from the policy's restrictions]
why_it_matters: The policy assumes KMP can be permitted to enter secured financing but never states the conditions for that permission elsewhere; the bank should have the Company confirm the applicable clearance process before relying on the loan leg being available.

clause: an involuntary disposal of securities that results from the margin lender or financier exercising its rights under the arrangement
why_it_matters: If a compliant secured loan were in place, the lender's enforcement sale is excluded from the policy's restrictions (including Closed Periods), giving certainty for lender enforcement timing.

clause: If approval to trade Company securities is refused, the KMP seeking the approval must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: A refused clearance for any permissible leg cannot be disclosed to the bank, limiting transparency in structuring discussions.

clause: If written clearance is granted, it is only valid for a period of one week after notification of approval ... Written clearance is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of inside information prior to trading.
why_it_matters: Any cleared step in structuring must be completed within one week (or a specified alternative period) and is automatically voided if inside information arises before execution.

clause: This policy also extends (in certain respects) to the immediate family members of Civmec People, and to companies, trusts and entities controlled by them ("Associates"). ... KMP and its Associates must not enter into transactions or arrangement which operate to limit the economic risk
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family member, trust or controlled entity does not escape the hedging ban or Closed Period restrictions.

clause: You are not permitted to enter into a margin loan or other financing arrangement where there is a risk that Bannerman securities will be traded pursuant to the terms of the margin loan or financing arrangement ... unless you have obtained prior written consent of the Chairman
why_it_matters: Unlike an outright ban, the loan leg of a funded collar is achievable with Chairman consent and disclosure of the Loan Information, making BMN more accommodating than policies with a blanket secured-financing prohibition.

clause: disclose to the Chairman the following information regarding the Margin Loan (Loan Information): key terms; number of Bannerman securities involved; the trigger points; the right of the lender to sell the securities unilaterally; and any other material details.
why_it_matters: The bank's collar-linked loan documentation (LVR triggers, enforcement/unilateral sale rights) would need to be disclosed to the Chairman up front and kept current if terms change.

topic: vested-holding hedge expressly permitted for directors
clause: you can deal in Bannerman securities (or financial products issued by third parties in relation to Bannerman securities which operate to limit the economic risk of a vested holding in Bannerman securities)
why_it_matters: The put/call legs of a collar over a director's vested shares are expressly contemplated by the policy, not merely swept in by a general dealing definition, reducing interpretive risk.

clause: If you are the Chairman of Bannerman and you intend to enter into a Margin Loan, you must obtain the prior written consent of the Chairman of the Audit Committee
why_it_matters: If the collar counterparty relationship involves the Chairman personally, sign-off shifts to the Audit Committee Chairman rather than creating a self-approval conflict.

clause: this approval to trade is valid for only five (5) clear business days from the date indicated below, unless otherwise revoked earlier by notice in writing.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar (and its loan) must be executed within 5 business days and can be revoked before then, so timing certainty is lower than a longer or open-ended clearance window.

clause: “director” means a director of Bannerman and includes any related party of the director.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a related party or family entity of a director does not avoid the director-level consent and disclosure requirements.

clause: the right of the lender to sell the securities unilaterally
why_it_matters: The policy requires disclosure of the lender's unilateral sale right but does not state whether a lender-triggered forced sale during a blackout period is excused, leaving enforcement timing risk unresolved.

topic: no derivatives, hedging or secured financing regime
clause: "security" includes shares, debentures, rights, options, employee options, prescribed interests and warrants. "deal" includes any transaction associated with buying, selling or converting a security.
why_it_matters: The policy has no concept of derivatives, hedging, margin loans or secured financing, so an OTC collar and a loan secured on the collared shares sit entirely outside its express dealing definition and are tested only against the general insider-trading ban, Closed Periods and short-term trading discouragement, with no bespoke approval or disclosure route.

clause: This approval, shall be valid for a period of no longer than two weeks and is to be reported at the next Board meeting
why_it_matters: Any Closed Period sale executed to fund or unwind part of a collar under the hardship/exceptional-circumstances route becomes a matter of Board record and must complete within two weeks of approval.

clause: a director must notify the Australian Stock Exchange Limited of the acquisition or disposal of any security of Lycopodium Limited. A copy of any such notification should be forwarded ... to the Lycopodium Limited Company Secretary within 2 business days of a deal occurring.
why_it_matters: Collar entry or unwind by a director triggers a separate s205G ASX notification and internal reporting duty within 2 business days, independent of the general 2-business-day post-trade notice.

clause: in a period, other than a Closed Period, should advise the Company Secretary, or in his absence, a director, of any purchase or sale of securities in Lycopodium Limited within two business days.
why_it_matters: Outside a Closed Period there is no prior-approval gate at all for dealing in Lycopodium securities, only a post-trade notice, so collar execution timing is not constrained by a clearance process (only by the insider-trading ban and Closed Periods).

clause: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions, arrangements or the use of financial derivatives which limit the economic risk in relation to their holding of Turaco's securities.
why_it_matters: Because the ban is absolute, applies to Applicable Persons and Related Persons alike, and draws no distinction between vested and unvested holdings or between exchange-traded and OTC instruments, the purchased put and written call legs of a collar are prohibited outright with no clearance mechanism to permit them.

topic: margin lending ban extends to Related Persons
clause: Applicable Persons and Related Persons are prohibited from entering into a margin lending arrangement involving Turaco's securities.
why_it_matters: Routing the loan leg of a funded collar through a spouse, family member or controlled entity does not avoid the prohibition.

clause: The Board may seek information from Key Management Personnel about their level of ownership of Turaco's securities and about any encumbrances granted or margin loans taken out in respect of those securities. The Board may also require them to keep the Company Secretary informed of changes to such information.
why_it_matters: A non-margin-loan secured facility (e.g. a bank loan secured on collared shares) is not itself banned, but the Board can compel disclosure of the security interest and its terms on request, and can impose an ongoing update obligation.

clause: A Trading Approval may only be granted to deal in the Company's securities for a maximum of five (5) business [days] ... Should dealing not be completed within five (5) business days, the Trading Approval shall lapse automatically
why_it_matters: Any dealing component of a collar structure that is not itself hedging-prohibited (e.g. an outright sale) would need to be completed within 5 business days of clearance or re-cleared.

topic: no margin lending or secured financing provision
clause: (no reference to margin loans, encumbrances or secured financing anywhere in the policy)
why_it_matters: A loan secured on the collared shares is not itself regulated by this policy, so the bank's financing leg faces no express prohibition, consent or disclosure gate, only the general insider-trading and blackout rules applicable to any resulting dealing.

clause: these may only be hedged once they are exercised into shareholdings and only on the condition that the details of the hedge are fully disclosed (eg: to the ASX and in the Annual Report, as appropriate), and that the hedge transaction is treated as a sale or purchase of securities
why_it_matters: The collar's put/call legs on exercised (vested) shares must be publicly disclosed to the ASX and in the Annual Report and treated as a notifiable sale/purchase, so the structure cannot be kept confidential and triggers the Director's 5-business-day ASX notice.

clause: EDL Group Directors and EDL Group employees must not engage in hedging arrangements over unvested securities issued pursuant to any Company share scheme, Performance Rights Plan or Option Plan.
why_it_matters: A collar cannot be written over unvested plan entitlements at all; the underlying equity must first vest and be exercised into an actual shareholding before a collar can be considered.

clause: (the policy nowhere mentions spouses, dependants, family trusts or controlled entities)
why_it_matters: Unlike most comparable ASX policies, this one does not expressly extend any restriction to associates, so structuring the collar or loan through a spouse or family entity may fall outside its stated scope, though this creates interpretive risk given the policy's stated fairness purpose.

clause: entering into protection arrangements includes entering into transactions which: (a) amount to "short selling" ... ; (b) operate to limit the economic risk of any Designated Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) ...; or (c) otherwise enable a Designated Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.
why_it_matters: The definition is written to catch the substance of a collar's put and call legs however structured, is absolutely banned while the shares are unvested or holding-locked, and even once vested and free requires prior approval under clause 6 as a 'protection arrangement' rather than an ordinary dealing.

clause: Designated Persons may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.
why_it_matters: The phrase 'or similar funding arrangement' is broad enough to likely catch a bank loan secured on the collared shares even if it is not a conventional margin loan, prohibiting the financing leg of a funded collar outright with no approval or exemption route.

clause: The Company may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on Dealing in Company Securities by any or all Designated Persons ... even where the proposed Dealing would otherwise take place outside a Black-out Period ... must be kept strictly confidential.
why_it_matters: Entry, roll or unwind of a collar can be blocked at any time by an undisclosed restriction that the Designated Person cannot be told the reason for.

clause: their spouse (including a de facto spouse) or any of their children ... under the age of 18 years; a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with any of those persons; and a trust or company which they or any close family members control or have an interest in [are] deemed to be Designated Persons
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a spouse, minor child, dependant or a controlled trust or company does not escape any of the hedging, margin loan or approval restrictions, since such persons are themselves Designated Persons.

topic: secured financing is approvable, not banned
clause: A Relevant Person must not enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities, or grant lenders any rights over their Company Securities without obtaining prior written clearance from the Board.
why_it_matters: Unlike many ASX policies that ban secured financing outright, FPR permits it with Board clearance, so the loan leg of a funded collar is structurally available subject to Board approval and ongoing LVR disclosure.

clause: Involuntary disposals caused by margin lender: An involuntary disposal of Securities that results from a margin lender or similar financier exercising its rights under a margin loan or similar funding arrangement (excluded from sections 2.2, 2.6 and 2.8).
why_it_matters: A bank enforcing security or exercising collar-related rights over the shares is expressly excluded from the clearance requirement, blackout ban and short-term trading ban, giving the lender a clean enforcement path even during a closed period.

clause: Securities means securities, derivatives or any other financial product able to be traded on a financial market.
why_it_matters: It is unclear whether a bespoke bilateral OTC put/call negotiated with a bank (not itself traded on any market) falls within 'Securities' and therefore within the general Trade/clearance regime at all, though the KMP hedging ban in 2.10 uses broader, unqualified language and would still catch it for unvested or locked shares.

topic: KMP hedging ban limited to unvested/locked shares
clause: KMP and their Connected Persons must not use ... any derivatives or other products ... which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding unvested Company Securities or Securities that are subject to a holding lock or similar trading restriction under a Company incentive plan.
why_it_matters: A collar can only be written once the shares are both vested and free of any plan holding lock; KMP hedging of vested, unrestricted shares is only caught generally as a Trade requiring ordinary clearance.

topic: vesting sale carve-out from short-term rule
clause: Selling shares received following the vesting of entitlements under an employee, executive or director equity plan within 3 months of the vesting date is not short-term trading.
why_it_matters: Physical settlement of a written call or exercised put shortly after vesting will not itself trigger the 3-month short-term trading ban, easing timing around collar inception.

clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could I be perceived to be taking advantage of my position in an inappropriate way? ... Where any approval is required for a trade under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the Designated Officer considers that the trade would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even where a collar and loan otherwise comply with the Policy's rules, the Designated Officer or Board could refuse clearance on reputational grounds if a funded collar is seen as speculative or as circumventing incentive plan restrictions.

clause: Approval to trade will ordinarily be valid for 7 calendar days from the approval date, unless a different period is specified by the Designated Officer or the approval is revoked prior to the expiry of the original approval period.
why_it_matters: The derivative legs of the collar must be priced and executed within 7 calendar days of clearance (or a bespoke period the Designated Officer sets), a tight window for negotiating bank documentation.

topic: absolute hedging ban vs. vested-derivatives permission
clause: Hedging of Company Securities by Employees, Designated Officers or their Associates is prohibited at all times. [cf.] Employees and Designated Officers may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company Securities, provided any Dealing complies with the balance of this policy.
why_it_matters: The policy contains an internal tension: 13.2 bans all hedging without a vesting carve-out, while 14.3 generally permits derivatives on vested shares; since collars are expressly named as a hedging arrangement in the Derivatives definition, the specific and more restrictive 13.2 ban should control, meaning an OTC collar is prohibited even over vested, unrestricted shares.

clause: Derivatives ... includes the following if they relate to or derive their value from Company Securities: put or call options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement.
why_it_matters: The policy drafter clearly contemplated collar structures and classed them as hedging/Derivatives, removing any argument that a bank collar falls outside scope; there is also no venue qualifier, so the definition catches bespoke OTC products.

topic: secured financing ban not limited to 'margin loan'
clause: Employees and Designated Officers are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Company Securities or in relation to which Company Securities may be used as security against loan repayment.
why_it_matters: The prohibition extends to any arrangement where the shares secure loan repayment, not just formally-labelled margin loans, so a bespoke bank loan secured on the collared shares is independently and absolutely prohibited, with no Board or Clearance Officer discretion to approve it.

clause: Additionally, the hedging of remuneration by key management personnel of the Group is prohibited by Part 2D.7 of the Corporations Act.
why_it_matters: For Designated Officers who are KMP, the statutory ban on hedging unvested remuneration securities under the Corporations Act operates independently of, and in addition to, the Policy's own hedging ban.

clause: If a Designated Officer is a director, they must ensure that an Appendix 3Y Change of Directors' Interest Notice is completed and provided to the Company Secretary within 2 business days ... The Company Secretary must provide the Appendix 3Y notice to ASX within 5 business days.
why_it_matters: Even if a Dealing were otherwise permissible, director-level participants face a market disclosure timeline (2 then 5 business days) that a bank would need to build into settlement and confidentiality planning.

topic: clearance cannot be retrospective and lapses on inside information
clause: Clearance will not be given retrospectively ... A Clearance ... cannot extend for more than 10 business days ... and lapses immediately if the applicant begins to possess Inside Information.
why_it_matters: Even for any permitted Dealing (e.g. the general share sale itself), execution is constrained to a 10 business day window from grant and clearance evaporates automatically if inside information arises, a timing risk for any collar-adjacent settlement.

clause: The guidelines contain no provision on margin loans, security interests, charges or any other financing arrangement in respect of Peet securities.
why_it_matters: A loan secured on the collared shares is not expressly regulated, and granting security is arguably outside the Dealing definition (buy/sell, agreement to buy or sell, exercising an option) altogether, so the loan leg may fall wholly outside this policy's clearance and window requirements - a benefit for structuring, but also a source of legal uncertainty since no process, disclosure or forced-sale carve-out is provided if the bank ever needs to enforce.

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested securities
clause: no schemes are entered into by any Employee that specifically protects the value of unvested shares, options and performance rights granted under any equity-based remuneration plans.
why_it_matters: A collar can be written over vested shares without breaching 2.7, since the ban does not reach vested holdings or a 'holding lock' concept, which this policy does not use.

clause: Employees may buy or sell Peet's securities on the ASX in the period of 60 days commencing immediately following the announcement of half-yearly results, annual results, or the AGM ... dealing in Peet's securities outside of the 'window' period is prohibited, unless Employees receive clearance.
why_it_matters: Unlike a typical blackout-period model, trading is closed by default and only opens in three 60-day windows a year (or with Managing Director clearance outside them), so collar inception and any physical settlement should be timed to a window or separately cleared.

clause: Unless there are exceptional circumstances, approval will not be given to enable Key Management Personnel and the Leadership Team to trade in Peet's securities outside the 'windows'.
why_it_matters: For KMP and Leadership Team participants the Board applies a materially stricter standard than the Managing Director's approval available to other Employees, so collar execution or unwind for this tier should be planned within a window wherever possible.

topic: ambiguous scope of 'Securities' for bank-issued OTC derivatives
clause: Securities ... also extends to items relating to securities issued by Peet (for example, warrants and other derivative products).
why_it_matters: The extension is framed around instruments 'issued by Peet'; it is unclear whether a bespoke bilateral OTC put/call issued by a bank (not by Peet) referencing Peet shares is 'Securities' under this policy at all, though the general insider trading law prohibition on dealing in 'securities' would still apply independently.

clause: Policy Number: RMP03. Version 5. Revised 12 August 2015.
why_it_matters: This is the only version of the policy lodged in the dataset and is over a decade old with no evident amendments addressing derivatives, CFDs, short selling, securities lending or financing; the bank should confirm no newer, unlodged version exists before relying on its silence on these topics.

clause: Employees are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Company securities provided that the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Company securities for the purposes of this Policy, and the relevant approvals and notifications required under section 3 are made on that basis.
why_it_matters: This is an express structural bridge: once shares are vested and unrestricted, an OTC collar is permitted provided it is run through the same notification/approval and window machinery as an ordinary share trade.

topic: margin lending approval overrides trading window
clause: Employees must obtain approval in accordance with the procedure set out in section 3.6 for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement, irrespective of any trading window.
why_it_matters: Unlike an ordinary share sale (which only needs notification during an open trading window), any dealing connected with the secured loan - entering the facility, transferring shares into it, or selling to meet a call - always needs the heavier CEO/Chair/Board approval, even inside a trading window.

clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with 4.2(b) conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: The Company can attach bespoke conditions to its approval of the secured facility, potentially including price triggers or notice requirements for enforcement, which the bank's facility documentation should anticipate.

clause: Paragraphs 3.3, 3.5, 3.6 and 4.1 of this Policy do not apply to ... subject to paragraph 4.2, a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale is excluded from the blackout, window, approval and short-term dealing rules, but only 'subject to paragraph 4.2' - meaning the underlying facility must itself have been approved as a margin lending arrangement; an unapproved or non-conforming facility may not benefit from the carve-out.

clause: Any dealing in the Company's securities by Employees or their Connected Persons pursuant to a margin lending arrangement must be conducted in accordance with this Policy.
why_it_matters: The policy never uses broader language like 'any other secured financing arrangement'; whether a bespoke bank loan secured on the collared shares (not conventionally marketed as a 'margin loan') falls within section 4.2's approval regime, or is simply unaddressed, should be confirmed with the Company Secretary before structuring.

clause: This restriction will apply even if the dealing would otherwise be permitted under this Policy, such as where it would occur within a permitted trading window, outside a black-out period, fall within an exclusion, or if the Employee has been given clearance to trade.
why_it_matters: Any clearance already obtained for the collar or loan becomes ineffective if the executive comes into possession of inside information before execution or settlement.

clause: Designated Persons must not ... deal at any time in financial products associated with the Company's Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or a permitted dealing under this policy. ... Financial products includes derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with the Company's Securities by third parties.
why_it_matters: This is the central obstacle to a funded collar: a bank-issued put and call is squarely a 'financial product ... issued ... by third parties' and is banned at any time, for any tier, at any vesting state, with essentially no clearance route - the Part 5 permitted-dealings list contains nothing resembling a derivative.

topic: margin lending ban does not extend to other secured financing
clause: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where the Company's Securities may be included as security. Designated Persons should consult the Company Secretary if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: Unlike the derivative ban, the loan leg has real headroom: a bespoke bank facility secured on the collared shares, if not classified as a 'margin lending arrangement', is expressly not restricted by 6.1 - though the classification should be confirmed with the Company Secretary before proceeding.

clause: A Designated Person may request, and the Notification Officer may give, prior confirmation for the Designated Person to: (a) deal in the Company's Securities during a Prohibited Period; or (b) dispose of the Company's Securities even if otherwise prohibited under part 6.
why_it_matters: This carve-out could assist an unwind (selling shares to close out or settle the collar) but on its face does not permit entering into a new financial product under 6.6(b) in the first place, so it does not rescue the derivative legs.

clause: Designated Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading in the Company's Securities or in financial products associated with the Company's Securities. Short term means less than a 12 month period.
why_it_matters: Even if the financial-products ban were somehow overcome, any collar or related trading with a tenor under 12 months would separately breach the short-term/speculative trading rule, which is unusually long compared to peer policies.

topic: narrow definition of Company's Securities vs. broad financial products concept
clause: Company's Securities means ... securities of the Company that are able to be traded on a financial market. ... Financial products includes derivatives ... issued or created over or associated with the Company's Securities by third parties.
why_it_matters: The ordinary Part 3 notification/clearance system is built around 'Company's Securities' (market-tradable instruments); the bank's OTC collar is not itself a 'Company Security' but is caught by the separate, broader and unconditional 'financial products' ban in Part 6, which has no clearance mechanism at all.

clause: Designated Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Company Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is expressly and unconditionally prohibited for all Designated Persons, with no clearance or exemption route, so the secured-financing component of the structure cannot lawfully be implemented.

clause: a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights ... does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement if the agreement is prohibited by this policy.
why_it_matters: The exclusion for a secured lender's enforcement sale gives no comfort here because the underlying loan arrangement (any secured financing over Company Securities) is itself banned outright under 6(a).

clause: Any director or KMP must not trade in the Company Securities ... unless the director or KMP obtains prior written approval by the Board of Directors ... This is the case even if the proposed transaction is outside of a Prohibited Period.
why_it_matters: Even outside any blackout, a director or KMP needs Board approval, granted or refused at the Board's unfettered discretion, before entering the derivative legs of a collar.

clause: If a written clearance to trade is refused, the person seeking the clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: A refusal of clearance to enter, unwind or roll a collar cannot be disclosed by the executive, complicating coordination with the bank on timing.

clause: will be valid for the period of not longer than 10 business days from the time which it is given ... Should the intended dealing in Weebit's securities not take effect within the clearance period then the permission to trade must be refreshed.
why_it_matters: Execution of the derivative legs (and any later unwind or roll) must occur within the default 10 business day clearance window or fresh clearance must be sought, adding execution-timing risk.

clause: a Designated Person must confirm in writing to the relevant Approving Officer or the Board of Directors in the case of a director or KMP, within 1 business day from when the dealing in Company Securities has occurred, the number of Company Securities affected and the relevant parties to the dealing.
why_it_matters: The bank counterparty's identity and the trade's terms would need to be reported internally within 1 business day of dealing.

clause: Designated Persons should consult with the Chief Executive Officer if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement is prohibited under this policy.
why_it_matters: There is an informal escalation path to test whether a bespoke collar structure would be treated as prohibited secured financing before entering it.

clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights).
why_it_matters: Both legs of a collar (purchased put and written call) are hedging arrangements banned outright for Restricted Persons, with no clearance or exemption route, so the derivative overlay cannot be implemented while the person is a Restricted Person.

clause: A Restricted Person must not include their Company securities in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: The ban is expressly limited to margin lending arrangements and does not use broader 'any other secured financing arrangement' wording, so a bespoke bilateral bank loan secured by a pledge of the collared shares, not structured as a margin loan, arguably sits outside the literal wording -- though this is academic given the hedging ban already blocks the derivative legs.

clause: Restricted Persons and their Associated Parties must not deal in the Company's securities until written approval has been given by the relevant Authorising Officer. This obligation operates at all times (whether the Trading Window is open or not).
why_it_matters: Even a permitted, unhedged sale of vested shares by a Restricted Person needs written clearance at all times, so any unwind or settlement also requires fresh clearance.

clause: any employees of IPH Limited (including any member of the IPH Group finance team)
why_it_matters: The hedging and margin-loan bans extend to rank-and-file IPH Limited employees, not just directors and the Executive Leadership Team, though employees of member firms outside IPH Limited itself are not automatically caught.

clause: If clearance is granted, the transaction must be initiated within five trading days and completed without delay.
why_it_matters: Any cleared dealing (e.g. a sale of unhedged vested shares) must be executed within 5 trading days or fresh clearance must be sought, adding execution-timing risk.

clause: if a member of the IPH Personnel is in possession of Inside Information, an Authorising Officer will not grant consent.
why_it_matters: Clearance for entry into, or unwind of, any arrangement is unavailable whenever the executive holds Inside Information, regardless of exceptional circumstances.

clause: trade in Securities ... includes ... granting options or security over the shares (such as mortgaging them or using them as collateral)
why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, oOh! does not ban secured financing generally -- only margin lending arrangements are prohibited outright. Granting security over vested, unlocked shares to a bank (not via a margin loan) is expressly treated as an ordinary 'trade' requiring only the standard approval (Higher risk staff) or notification (other employees) process, making the loan leg of a funded collar structurally available.

topic: forced sale carve-out for secured lenders
clause: a disposal of oOh! Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights (except that the prohibitions on margin lending arrangements in this Policy still apply)
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares under a non-margin-loan secured facility is excluded from the black-out period, short-term dealing, notification and approval requirements, giving the bank a clean enforcement path even during a closed window, provided the facility is not characterised as a margin loan.

clause: oOh! Employees and their Related Parties are permitted to limit the risk of holding oOh! Securities by hedging
why_it_matters: Hedging (and by extension a collar) is affirmatively permitted over vested, unlocked shares, subject only to no Inside Information and the applicable approval/notification process, a materially more permissive starting point than an outright hedging ban.

clause: trade in oOh!'s Securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement (including not using oOh! Securities as collateral for a margin loan nor selling them to meet a margin call)
why_it_matters: If the bank's loan were structured or documented as a margin loan, it would be banned outright; the facility should be papered as a bespoke secured loan rather than a margin lending arrangement.

topic: approval automatically withdrawn on inside information
clause: Approval is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if you become aware of 'Inside Information' prior to trading.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar or loan drawdown lapses automatically if inside information arises before execution, without any separate notice.

topic: black-out period bars hedging absent hardship
clause: If oOh! is in a black-out period approval will not be given except in exceptional circumstances
why_it_matters: Entry, unwind or roll of the collar by Higher risk staff during a black-out period needs a hardship/exceptional-circumstances waiver, not routine approval.

clause: Company Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... over any Company securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that Company Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Company securities.
why_it_matters: The secured-financing ban applies only to unvested or holding-locked shares; once vested and unlocked, granting security over the shares to secure a bank loan is expressly permitted with prior consent, so the loan leg of a funded collar over vested, unrestricted shares is achievable.

topic: broad scope of secured financing ban
clause: grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Company securities ... to secure any obligation of that Company Person or any third party
why_it_matters: The ban (and its consent-based release once vested) is not limited to margin loans -- it covers any secured financing including a bilateral bank loan -- so the bank's collar loan is squarely regulated by, and can rely on, section 5.3 rather than sitting in a gap.

clause: a disposal of Company securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares is exempt from the Blackout Period and consent requirements, though the Company Person must still notify the Authorising Officer after the event.

clause: the Company Person seeking authorisation cannot be their own Authorising Officer.
why_it_matters: Confirms a layered approval chain (e.g. the Board Chair is cleared by the Audit & Risk Committee Chair) that cannot be bypassed by self-approval.

clause: after dealing with Company securities, provide the Authorising Officer with a transaction confirmation.
why_it_matters: Entry into, and settlement or unwind of, the collar and loan must be reported to the Authorising Officer, though no specific deadline is stated.

clause: The Policy prohibits Key Management Personnel from dealing 'in any GUD security' but never defines 'deal', 'Dealing' or 'Securities', and does not mention derivatives, hedging, margin lending, short selling, securities lending, CFDs, encumbrance or secured financing anywhere in the document.
why_it_matters: Because no defined term expressly sweeps in an OTC put/call or the loan securing it, the collar and its financing are not expressly prohibited, but nor is there any clearance pathway calibrated to them, so the bank should obtain the Company's written confirmation of treatment rather than rely on the Policy's silence.

clause: Key Management Personnel of the Company must not deal in any GUD security during the following periods ('prohibited periods')
why_it_matters: The absolute closed-period ban is drafted to bind only Key Management Personnel; if the collar counterparty is a non-KMP senior employee the closed period is not literally an outright bar on them, though clause 4 never blesses dealing by anyone during a prohibited period absent exceptional-circumstances approval.

clause: if that person is a Key Management Person or their associate, during any period which is not a prohibited period or a period referred to in clause 4(a)i. of this Policy, with the consent of the Chairman
why_it_matters: Outside the open 30-day post-results trading window, dealing (if the collar were treated as a dealing) needs the Chairman's prior consent for KMP, or Managing Director/Company Secretary consent for other employees, even when no prohibited period is in effect.

clause: the Chairman has complete discretion in deciding whether or not approval is to be given, and the period (not to exceed one month) in which the dealing may occur
why_it_matters: If entry, unwind or physical settlement of a collar had to occur during a prohibited period under exceptional-circumstances relief, the approved execution window cannot exceed one month.

clause: a Director must notify the Company Secretary of the acquisition or disposal of any GUD security and the Company is obliged to notify the ASX (LR 3.19A). ... Each Director is required to enter into a Disclosure Agreement with the Company to supply such information.
why_it_matters: A director entering into, unwinding, or having shares called away under a collar must notify the Company Secretary for an Appendix 3Y announcement, giving the market visibility of the derivative and loan structure.

clause: the insider must not (whether as principal or agent) apply for, acquire or dispose of, or enter into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of any such securities
why_it_matters: Independent of the Policy's silence on derivatives, entering the collar while in possession of inside information remains a criminal and civil contravention under Corporations Act s1043A, with penalties up to $1.11 million for an individual noted in the document.

clause: any other period determined by resolution of the Board ... any other circumstances determined by the Board and notified to the ASX
why_it_matters: The Board retains open-ended authority to impose extra blackout periods or bless further excluded trading categories, so the Company could add or remove flexibility for a collar at its discretion; the Policy does not say whether a Board-imposed additional prohibited period is confidential before it binds a director.

clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities, including for the exceptional circumstances referred to in section 6, unless the Restricted Person first obtains prior written clearance ... A written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for the period of 5 business days.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that only require clearance in blackout periods, RXL requires fresh 5-business-day written clearance for every dealing at any time, so entry, unwind and settlement of a collar each need separate, freshly-timed approvals.

clause: The clearance acknowledgement form states the signatory 'will not engage in activity that is prohibited ... including ... obtaining margin loans ... or enter into any other secured financing arrangements', while section 10 of the policy body permits such arrangements with prior written clearance.
why_it_matters: This drafting inconsistency creates real risk that Approving Officers administer the form as an absolute ban; the bank should obtain company confirmation that section 10's clearance route (not the form's blanket wording) governs before structuring the loan leg.

clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement ... is excluded from the restrictions outlined in section 5
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is excluded from the Prohibited Period ban, giving a clean enforcement path even during a blackout or confidential Additional Period.

clause: Where this policy requires a Restricted Person to do an act or thing, the relevant Restricted Person must do that act or thing in respect of the Connected Person.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled company does not avoid the clearance and secured-lending requirements.

clause: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.
why_it_matters: The express hedging ban is confined to unvested plan entitlements, so a collar over already-vested shares is not caught by section 9 and falls back to the general clearance regime instead.

clause: Restricted Persons must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.
why_it_matters: The bank may not be told why a clearance request for collar execution is delayed or refused, complicating timing certainty for trade entry.
