clause: Employees may not, at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... over any Vulcan securities to secure any obligation of that Employee or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Vulcan securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is prohibited outright for all Employees and Associates at all times, with no clearance mechanism referenced anywhere in the policy.

clause: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Vulcan securities (or Vulcan products in the derivatives markets) ... is prohibited in respect of any Vulcan securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock; and otherwise, requires consent under clause 5.2.
why_it_matters: A collar's put and call together fall squarely within 'protection arrangements', so even absent the financing ban, the derivative legs are absolutely barred over unvested or holding-locked shares and, over vested unrestricted shares, need Board-level exceptional-circumstances consent rather than routine preclearance.

clause: What constitutes "exceptional circumstances" will be assessed on a case-by-case basis within the absolute discretion of the Board, and may include, without limitation, severe financial hardship or a requirement to comply with a court order or court enforceable undertaking.
why_it_matters: Consent for a protection arrangement over vested shares is not a routine sign-off but requires the Board to find genuinely exceptional circumstances, making timing and certainty of execution for a bank-structured collar unpredictable.

clause: a company or trust controlled by a Director, Senior Manager and Employee; and a spouse ... child ... a close relative (if acting in concert), a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with any Director, Senior Manager or Employee (and any company or trust controlled by any of them)
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the secured-financing ban or the protection-arrangement restrictions.

clause: Employees may not, at any time ... enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Vulcan securities.
why_it_matters: Because secured lending is banned outright, the policy contains no exemption for a lender's enforcement sale (unlike policies that permit margin loans with clearance), so there is no fallback mechanism for lender enforcement to rely on.

clause: A Restricted Person must not trade in Securities at any time (including in the exceptional circumstances referred to in section 6) unless they first obtain prior written clearance from [the Approving Officer table].
why_it_matters: Clearance is required for every dealing at any time, not just during Blackout or Additional Periods, so entry, unwind and settlement of a collar each need fresh 5-business-day clearance.

clause: a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is excluded from the Prohibited Period ban, giving a workable enforcement path even during a blackout or confidential Additional Period.

clause: Before entering into any transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of your security holding ... clearance ... A Restricted Person is prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements.
why_it_matters: A collar is only categorically barred while the underlying shares are unvested scheme entitlements; once vested, hedging (and by extension a collar) is expressly permitted subject to clearance, unlike policies with a blanket hedging ban.

clause: The Company Secretary will maintain a register of clearances given in accordance with this section 7, and must report all clearances given to the Board at its next following meeting.
why_it_matters: Unlike comparable policies, NMG does not appear to require the Restricted Person to confirm trade details after dealing, reducing post-execution administrative friction for the bank's collar settlement, though clearance withdrawal risk (below) remains.

clause: Written clearance may be withdrawn by the Approving Officer at any time during the clearance period should the Approving Officer consider that the circumstances have changed, having regard to the broader reputational, governance and other implications of the proposed trading in Securities.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar transaction can be pulled by the Approving Officer for broad reputational or governance reasons even within the 5-business-day validity window, before the trade is executed.

clause: indirect and incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of a Restricted Person dealing in Securities issued by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle ... that happens to hold ... Securities in the Company
why_it_matters: Confirms indirect exposure via pooled vehicles is not itself regulated dealing, though a bespoke bilateral OTC collar with a bank would not qualify for this carve-out.

topic: secured financing carve-out for vested shares
clause: Unless clause 4.3(a) applies, WA1 Persons may, directly or indirectly, grant security (whether by charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any of WA1's securities, to secure any obligation of that WA1 Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangements involving WA1 securities, with consent provided under clause 3.3.
why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, WA1 expressly permits the loan leg of a funded collar secured on vested, unrestricted shares, subject only to ordinary Authorising Officer consent, not an exceptional-circumstances gate.

clause: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any WA1 securities (or WA1 products in the derivatives markets): is prohibited at any time in respect of any WA1 securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock; and otherwise, requires consent under clause 3.3.
why_it_matters: A collar's put and call fall within 'protection arrangements'; over vested, unrestricted shares they need only ordinary clause 3.3 consent (the same regime as for dealing outside a Blackout Period), not the narrower 'exceptional circumstances' standard used elsewhere in the policy for Blackout Period trading.

clause: prior to dealing in WA1 securities outside a Blackout Period or where clause 4 requires the person to obtain a consent under clause 3.3, notify the relevant person ... and obtain consent from the Authorising Officer.
why_it_matters: Both the derivative/hedging consent and the secured-financing consent for vested shares are gated by the routine notify-and-consent process, materially easier to obtain than a hardship/court-order threshold.

clause: a disposal of WA1 securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is excluded from Blackout Period and other policy restrictions, giving a clean enforcement path.

clause: WA1 may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on trading ... Any restriction communicated ... must be kept strictly confidential.
why_it_matters: An undisclosed ad-hoc restriction can block collar entry, unwind or settlement at any time without the executive being able to explain the delay to the bank.

clause: If an WA1 Person comes into possession of Inside Information after receiving a clearance to trade, they must not trade despite having received the clearance.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar transaction can become unexecutable if inside information arises before signing, even after consent is granted.

clause: Designated Persons and their Associates are prohibited from entering into margin loans or other financing arrangements involving SGR securities or in relation to which SGR securities may be used as security of any type against loan repayments.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is banned outright for Designated Persons and their Associates, with no clearance mechanism anywhere in the policy.

clause: You must not enter into any financial arrangements involving SGR securities which may lead to the ownership and rights of the securities being transferred to a third party.
why_it_matters: This standalone sentence (not limited to financing) would also catch a physically-settled call, forward, or other monetisation structure under which the bank could ultimately take the shares, closing off even an unfunded, physically-settled collar structure.

clause: If prior written clearance for a proposed trade is required to be obtained under this policy, the clearance will not be granted if the proposed trade would not satisfy the Corporate Reputation Test.
why_it_matters: Even a technically permitted collar over vested, unrestricted shares can be refused clearance on a subjective perception-based test (how the trade would look if reported in the media).

clause: Clearance to trade: ... will remain in force for 3 business days from and including the date it is given ... [section 13] Any trading that is the subject of prior written clearance must be executed within five business days from and including the date the written clearance is granted.
why_it_matters: The policy states two different execution deadlines (3 vs 5 business days) for the same clearance, creating timing uncertainty for scheduling collar execution that should be clarified with the Company Secretary before relying on either figure.

clause: you are prohibited from hedging the value of restricted shares and unvested performance rights or options ... Breaches of this prohibition will result in the relevant shares, performance rights or options being forfeited by you.
why_it_matters: Unlike ordinary disciplinary consequences, breaching the hedging ban on unvested/restricted incentive securities results in forfeiture of those securities themselves, a severe additional risk if a collar were mistakenly written over still-restricted shares.

clause: SGR will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through an associate, trust or offshore counterparty to avoid the section 17 financing ban or section 19 hedging ban is unlikely to succeed given this express substance-over-form mandate.

clause: any person or entity that might in the circumstances be reasonably associated with the Designated Person (for example, joint venture partners or their employees or contractors)
why_it_matters: The Associates net is unusually broad, extending beyond family and controlled entities to any 'reasonably associated' person, making it harder to structure the collar counterparty relationship around the restriction.

clause: a disposal of SiteMinder securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of collared shares under the loan is a policy-exempt dealing rather than a breach, even during a Blackout Period, though the executive must still advise the relevant Authorising Officer(s) afterwards.

clause: Otherwise enable a SiteMinder Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities
why_it_matters: The catch-all wording is broad enough to capture the purchased-put leg of a collar (which profits on a price fall) even if it is not badged as a hedge, reinforcing that clearance (or an outright ban if unvested/locked) applies to that leg.

clause: a company or trust controlled by any of the persons referred to in sub-paragraph (i) above
why_it_matters: Unlike natural-person associates (caught only for section 4 purposes), a controlled company or trust is a SiteMinder Person for all purposes, so routing the collar or loan through a family entity does not avoid the section 5.2/5.3 bans.

clause: Chair of the Board: The chair of the Audit and Risk Committee and one other Board director. Other directors, Company Secretary and any other Key Management Personnel: The chair of the Board or, in his/her absence, the chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, and one other Board Director.
why_it_matters: Director/KMP clearance for the collar's derivative and security-granting legs needs two named approvers rather than one, which can add time to structuring and requires both to accept the 10-business-day execution window.

clause: This policy will be regarded seriously and may lead to disciplinary action, including dismissal.
why_it_matters: Outside the narrow hardship/court-order exceptional-circumstances route, there is no standing waiver mechanism for the policy's bans on unvested/locked hedging and secured financing, so a funded collar over such shares cannot be cleared by consent alone.

topic: hedging permitted with consent even when unvested
clause: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that would have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with Company Securities including Securities which are unvested, subject to a holding lock or issued pursuant to an equity based remuneration scheme.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that ban hedging of unvested securities outright, BMC's policy only requires prior written approval regardless of vesting state, so a collar over unvested or holding-locked plan securities is not automatically barred, only gated by approval.

clause: an involuntary disposal of securities that results from a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement that has previously been approved in accordance with this policy
why_it_matters: Once the loan securing the collar has been approved, the bank's later enforcement sale is a pre-approved 'permitted dealing' available at any time, including in a Closed Period, removing forced-sale timing risk for the lender.

clause: Trading consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of inside information prior to trading.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be executed within 5 trading days and before any inside information arises, or the clearance evaporates automatically without notice.

clause: The insider trading prohibitions apply even when a trade falls within an exclusion to the restrictions on trading detailed in this policy if it is undertaken by, or procured by, someone in possession of inside information at the time of the trade.
why_it_matters: Even the margin-lender forced-sale exemption could be challenged if the disposal is 'procured by' an executive who holds inside information at the time, so enforcement timing during blackout-adjacent periods carries residual risk.

clause: the affiliates (as such term is used in the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) ...) of any of the foregoing
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through an affiliated entity or controlled company does not escape the approval requirement, as BCBCA-style affiliates are Associates under the policy.

topic: granting security is not a regulated 'dealing'
clause: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
why_it_matters: Because the approval regime in section 5.1 is confined to 'buy, sell or exercise rights', granting security over shares to secure the collar's loan appears to fall outside the clearance requirement entirely, and a subsequent forced sale on default is expressly carved out of both the Closed Period ban and insider trading exposure.

topic: forced sale exemption applies 'at any time'
clause: Key Management Personnel may at any time: ... dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale under the loan secured on the collared shares can proceed even during a Closed Period, without needing an exceptional-circumstances application.

clause: it is not permissible to provide the exercise price of options by selling the shares acquired on the exercise of these options unless the sale of those shares occurs outside the periods specified in paragraph 4.1
why_it_matters: If the collared shares originate from option exercise, a cashless-exercise sale to fund the strike price must occur outside Closed Periods, which can affect the timing of when shares become available to post as collateral.

clause: This policy applies to both the sale and purchase of any securities of the Company and its subsidiaries on issue from time to time.
why_it_matters: The policy has no express hedging, derivatives, CFD or short-selling regime, so the OTC put and call legs of a collar are not clearly 'securities' dealings requiring approval under this document, though ordinary insider trading law still applies to their execution.

clause: use Wagners Securities in connection with a margin loan or similar financing arrangement or product which may be subject to a margin call or loan to value ratio (LVR) breach
why_it_matters: Unlike the hedging/derivatives restriction, this prohibition has no Written Clearance carve-out, so a loan secured on the collared shares that could be subject to a margin call or LVR breach is banned outright with no approval route.

topic: hedging clearance gated by exceptional circumstances
clause: Written Clearance can only be given if the proposed trade is not ... and exceptional circumstances exist justifying the issue of the Written Clearance.
why_it_matters: The put/call legs of a collar can only be cleared by satisfying the same high 'exceptional circumstances' bar (financial hardship, court order, etc.) that applies to trading during a Restricted Period, not by routine sign-off, materially narrowing when a collar can be entered.

clause: This Policy applies to all securities issued by Wagners of any kind, including ordinary or preference shares, debentures, convertible notes, options and hedging or derivative instruments.
why_it_matters: The policy draws no distinction between unvested, holding-locked and freely held shares, so the same exceptional-circumstances gate for hedging applies uniformly regardless of the collared shares' vesting status.

topic: insider trading overlay on cleared arrangements
clause: enter into any arrangement of the nature described in paragraph 7(a) or (b) above if to do so would be in breach of the Corporations Act
why_it_matters: Even a cleared hedge or otherwise-permitted arrangement remains void if it would independently breach insider trading law, an overlay the bank's collar documentation should not assume away.

clause: An Employee who is prohibited from trading under this Policy must not trade through any member of their family, or through a trust or company over which they have influence or control.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the paragraph 7 restrictions where the Employee would otherwise be prohibited.

topic: margin lending ban has no waiver route
clause: Any Dealing in the Company's Securities by Restricted Persons pursuant to a margin lending arrangement is not permitted. Such Dealings would cover: (a) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's Securities; (b) transferring Securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account; and (c) selling Securities in the Company to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
why_it_matters: The exceptional-circumstances waiver in Section 5.1(b) applies only to the Blackout Period restriction in 5.1(a), not to Section 5.3, so a margin-style loan secured on the collared shares cannot be structured, transferred into, or unwound by forced sale under any circumstances, hardship included.

clause: Company Securities must never be hedged prior to the vesting of those Company Securities ... Company Securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on Dealing under the terms of any employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company.
why_it_matters: The 'must never' language and absence of any waiver mechanism for Section 5.4 means a collar cannot be entered over unvested or holding-locked incentive securities under any circumstances, unlike the Blackout Period timing restriction which can be waived.

clause: Where a Restricted Person enters into a hedging arrangement in respect of Company Securities, the Company may, where appropriate, disclose the fact and nature of the hedge (e.g. in its Annual Report or to the ASX).
why_it_matters: A cleared collar over vested unrestricted shares may become publicly disclosed by the Company at its discretion, a reputational factor for the executive and the bank to consider in structuring.

clause: Where clearance is required for a Dealing under this Policy, clearance will not be granted where the Dealing would not satisfy the considerations above.
why_it_matters: Even a collar over vested, unrestricted shares that is otherwise compliant can be refused clearance on a subjective 'front page of the newspaper' reputational test.

clause: Any Company Personnel who holds Company Securities subject to binding restrictions on transfer (either as ASX restricted Securities or through voluntary escrow arrangements) must comply with the terms of any applicable escrow arrangements and will be unable to trade in those Securities during that time.
why_it_matters: If the shares intended for the collar are ASX-restricted or under voluntary escrow, no Dealing (including granting security or a derivative) is possible until escrow ends, regardless of vesting status.

topic: broad Dealing definition includes varying terms
clause: issuing, underwriting or varying the terms of Securities
why_it_matters: Restructuring, rolling or amending the collar or its strike/tenor after inception would itself be a fresh Dealing requiring clearance and compliance with Blackout Periods.

clause: Nanosonics Staff are not permitted to Deal in any Derivatives or other financial products issued over the Securities by third parties, such as banks and other institutions, without the prior approval of the Board.
why_it_matters: An OTC put and call written with a bank falls squarely within this clause; the collar's derivative legs need Board approval, not merely Notification Officer clearance, for every tier and any vesting state.

clause: An exception may apply where the Securities form a component of a listed portfolio or index product.
why_it_matters: This narrow carve-out would not cover a bespoke bilateral OTC collar written specifically over Nanosonics shares.

clause: Nanosonics Staff must not enter into a margin loan or stock loan arrangement, or similar funding arrangement, without prior approval of the Board. In order to obtain such approval, they must disclose the key terms of any such arrangement to the Company Secretary.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies with an outright ban, the loan leg of a funded collar is permitted subject to Board pre-approval and disclosure of trigger points and the lender's unilateral sale rights.

clause: an involuntary disposal of Nanosonics Securities that results from a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under an approved arrangement (Excluded Dealing)
why_it_matters: Provided the financing was Board-approved beforehand, the bank's enforcement sale on a default or knock-out is excluded from the Blackout Period ban rather than being a breach.

clause: The Company will disclose margin lending or stock lending arrangements to the market where required by law or good practice, having regard to the materiality of the arrangements to the Company.
why_it_matters: A sizeable collar loan secured on an executive's shareholding may trigger public ASX disclosure of the arrangement's existence and terms.

clause: unless, in the meantime, the Designated Person becomes in possession of Inside Information
why_it_matters: A cleared collar for a Designated Person must be executed within the 5-business-day validity window and becomes unexecutable if inside information arises before signing.

topic: insider trading exemption for plan securities
clause: the insider trading provisions do not apply to applications for, and acquisitions under those applications of, Nanosonics Securities by Nanosonics Staff under any Nanosonics employee equity plan ... Notwithstanding this exemption ... Designated Persons must still give notice and seek approval of proposed acquisitions of Nanosonics Securities under an employee equity plan pursuant to section 5.
why_it_matters: Even where the statutory insider-trading bar does not apply to acquiring vested plan securities, internal notification/approval is still required, affecting timing of a collar entered around vesting or exercise.

clause: This Policy extends to the Close Associates of a Designated Person in relation to Nanosonics Securities ... Designated Persons must take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Close Associates comply with this policy.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, dependant or controlled entity does not avoid the Board-approval and notification requirements.

topic: no clearance route for third-party derivatives
clause: deal at any time in financial products associated with the Company's Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or a permitted dealing under this Policy.
why_it_matters: An OTC put/call collar with a bank is a 'financial product' under 8.5 and is banned outright for Designated Persons; none of the Part 7 permitted dealings covers a bespoke bank derivative, so there is no clearance route at all.

topic: hedging ban tied to vesting, but backstopped
clause: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that: (i) has not vested; or (ii) has vested but remains subject to a holding lock
why_it_matters: The named hedging ban targets unvested/locked incentive remuneration specifically, but the separate 8.3(b) financial-products ban independently prohibits hedging of already-vested, unrestricted shares too, closing any gap for a collar over free shares.

topic: margin lending vs other secured financing
clause: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where the Company's Securities may be included as security. Designated Persons should consult the Secretary if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: A loan secured on the collared shares is not automatically banned if it is not characterised as 'margin lending' -- but this only helps the loan leg; the bank's option legs remain banned as financial products regardless of how the loan is characterised.

clause: a disposal of the Company's Securities that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights under a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement permitted by this Policy
why_it_matters: If a secured financing arrangement were permitted, the lender's enforcement sale would be an excluded/permitted dealing not requiring fresh clearance or breaching a Prohibited Period.

clause: If clearance to trade is refused, the person seeking the clearance must keep the information relating to the refusal (including the refusal itself) confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: An executive whose derivative dealing is refused cannot disclose that refusal, complicating coordination with a bank counterparty on structuring a collar.

clause: Ultimate discretion rests with the Chair in respect of granting a waiver to the requirements of this Policy to allow persons restricted by this Policy to trade in the Company's Securities, provided that to do so would not be illegal.
why_it_matters: Even though 8.3/8.4 read as absolute prohibitions, the Chair retains an overriding, unreviewable waiver power that could in principle permit a collar structure, subject to legality.

clause: Designated Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading in the Company's Securities or in financial products associated with the Company's Securities. Short term means, in less than a 12 month period.
why_it_matters: Any hedge or collar structure would need a term of at least 12 months to avoid being characterised as short-term/speculative trading, materially longer than the 3-month standard seen in many peer policies.

clause: A Designated Person must communicate on behalf of their associate with the Notification Officer for the purposes of this Policy.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or related entity does not bypass the bans; the Designated Person remains responsible for their associate's dealings.

clause: arrangements that you entered into prior to you becoming a Designated Person that would otherwise be prohibited under paragraph 8 are permitted to continue for a 12 month period from the date that you became a Designated Person or until the date of expiry of the relevant arrangement, whichever is the earlier to occur.
why_it_matters: A funded collar entered into before someone becomes a Designated Person can continue for up to 12 months (or until its stated expiry) without an Approval Request, but a new collar entered into while already a Designated Person is a Prohibited Dealing requiring exceptional-circumstances approval.

clause: using MYS shares as collateral in any financial transaction, including margin loan arrangements
why_it_matters: Not limited to margin loans - 'any financial transaction' captures the loan leg of a funded collar, making it a Prohibited Dealing for Designated Persons absent an approved Approval Request or paragraph 10 grandfathering.

clause: An Approval Request will only be granted: in exceptional circumstances; where the Approval Request is accompanied by sufficient evidence that the proposed purchase, sale or other dealing in MYS shares is the only reasonable course of action available in the circumstances.
why_it_matters: The bar for permission to enter a prohibited dealing (including a collar's loan leg or short-term derivative legs) is high; a voluntary wealth-diversification or monetisation strategy is unlikely to qualify as the 'only reasonable course of action'.

clause: must not exercise rights under these share plans and sell (or otherwise dispose of your interest in) MYS shares within the same window period, unless approved pursuant to an Approval Request.
why_it_matters: Even after vesting/exercise, disposing of the resulting shares in the same window period as the exercise is itself restricted, which could delay unwinding a collar timed around vesting.

topic: forced sale carve-out conditional on approved arrangement
clause: a disposal of MYS shares that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights pursuant to an arrangement that was permitted under paragraph 10
why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale is only an excluded dealing if the underlying secured arrangement was itself 'permitted' (grandfathered or separately approved); an unapproved arrangement's enforcement sale would not benefit from this carve-out.

clause: Upon receipt of approval, you must undertake the proposed purchase, sale or other dealing in MYS shares immediately but at least within 5 business days. If the dealing is not undertaken within 5 business days, the approval will no longer have effect.
why_it_matters: Any approved collar leg must be executed within 5 business days of approval or a fresh Approval Request is required.

clause: It also extends to financial products relating to securities issued by the Company whether or not the financial products are created by the Company or by third parties.
why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put/call over MYS shares is itself 'MYS shares' for policy purposes, so dealing in it triggers the full blackout/notification/approval regime that applies to ordinary share trades.

topic: no equity scheme, so no hedging carve-out needed
clause: The Company does not operate any equity-based remuneration schemes. As such, there is no need to have restrictions in place to prohibit KMP from using financial products to protect against or limit the risk associated with unvested Company securities (hedging).
why_it_matters: This is not a permission to hedge; it simply notes unvested securities do not exist at Djerriwarrh. All KMP-held shares are ordinary market-acquired ('vested, unrestricted') holdings, so a collar would need to be assessed against the general dealing prohibitions rather than any hedging-specific carve-out, and that assessment is largely silent.

topic: outright ban on using shares as security
clause: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.
why_it_matters: This is an absolute, unqualified ban with no clearance route, exemption authority, or carve-out anywhere in the policy; the loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is squarely prohibited for all KMP.

clause: Section 3 lists specific exclusions from the policy (superannuation transfers, discretionary managed funds, Board-approved pro rata offers, no change of beneficial interest, trustee trading, takeover acceptance, gifts, family transactions) but includes no carve-out for a disposal resulting from a secured lender or financier exercising rights.
why_it_matters: Because secured financing is banned outright, the policy has no provision addressing a lender's enforcement sale, so a bank collar-related forced sale would have no protected route out of a prohibited period.

clause: the intention in undertaking transactions should be to hold the Company's securities for a reasonable period rather than actively, promptly or repetitively buying and selling them.
why_it_matters: Absence of a fixed month threshold gives the Company discretion to characterise a collar's term as too short if it resembles trading rather than investment.

clause: For the purposes of sections 7.1 to 7.3, no KMP may be the recipient of the prior notification of their own transaction or be the approver of their own transaction involving exceptional circumstances.
why_it_matters: Ensures a genuine second signature is needed on any exceptional-circumstances sale clearance connected to a collar (e.g. to fund a margin call or hardship), though the policy does not specify who approves the Chairman's own exceptional-circumstances request.

clause: Such approval will be for 5 business days beginning the business day after approval is given.
why_it_matters: Any cleared sale (e.g. to unwind or settle a permitted structure) must be executed within a narrow 5-business-day window.

clause: The Company may be required to notify the existence of exceptional circumstances to the Australian Securities Exchange.
why_it_matters: A hardship-driven sale connected to a funded position could trigger public ASX disclosure of the exceptional circumstances behind it.

topic: securities definition expressly includes third-party derivatives
clause: derivative securities relating to the Company's common stock such as put and call options (whether or not issued by the Company)
why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put and call collar is expressly 'Company securities' under this policy's own definition, so the full dealing regime (insider trading, blackout, approval, confirmation) applies to it directly, without needing to argue by analogy from a general dealing definition.

clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or its financing to nominally avoid a defined term (e.g. calling the loan something other than a 'margin loan') will not avoid the Policy's restrictions.

clause: Employees must not pledge Company securities as collateral for a loan, purchase Company securities on margin ... or place Company securities in a margin account. Approval of any such transactions must be obtained in accordance with the procedure set out in section 4.4.
why_it_matters: Although housed in the 'Restricted Persons' part of the policy, this clause is drafted to bind all Employees, so the loan leg of a funded collar needs 4.4 approval regardless of whether the executive is technically a Restricted Person.

clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with section 4.5(a) conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which the Company's securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: The Company can pre-negotiate, as a condition of approving the loan, the circumstances in which the bank may enforce and sell the collared shares -- directly relevant to drafting the loan/collar documentation.

topic: Front Page Test overlay on approval
clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even a technically compliant collar structure can be refused approval if it would look bad publicly, adding a subjective reputational filter on top of the objective rules.

clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: A collar's approval can be revoked without explanation at any time before execution, and the executive cannot disclose a refusal, creating execution-timing risk for the bank counterparty.

clause: Following receipt of approval to deal, the approved dealing must occur within three (3) business days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective and fresh approval must be sought.
why_it_matters: A very tight execution window applies to any approved collar leg or loan drawdown, so pricing and documentation must be ready before seeking approval.

clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: If the loan was itself approved under 4.5, the lender's enforcement sale is excluded from the blackout/approval rules, giving the bank a clear enforcement path once the arrangement is properly approved.

clause: This Policy is designed to ensure compliance with both Australian and US securities laws, including the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) (Australian Corporations Act), ASX Listing Rules, and the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (US Exchange Act).
why_it_matters: A collar structured with a bank must also be assessed against US insider trading and disclosure considerations given the company's dual Australian/US securities law exposure (CDIs plus US common stock).

clause: Aurelia Personnel and their closely related parties are not permitted at any time to ... enter margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Aurelia Group Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured against the collared shares, is banned outright for every Aurelia Personnel and their closely related parties at all times, with no clearance route, tier carve-out or reference to vesting status.

clause: Restricted Persons who are given Prior Written Clearance must Deal no later than five business days from clearance being received.
why_it_matters: Any cleared derivative leg of a collar must be priced and executed within 5 business days of approval, which constrains how a bank can time execution against its own documentation and hedging process.

clause: The Company reserves the right to impose restrictions on Dealing in Aurelia Group Securities during any period, including one that would otherwise fall within a permitted Trading Window.
why_it_matters: Even a scheduled open Trading Window can be closed at the Company's discretion, so the timing of collar entry, roll or unwind cannot be guaranteed in advance.

clause: the persons listed above are called "Restricted Persons" ... Where this Policy requires a Restricted Person to do something (e.g. obtain Prior Written Clearance), the Relevant Personnel must also do so for their closely related parties.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the secured loan through a spouse, dependant or controlled entity does not avoid the secured financing ban or clearance requirement, since closely related parties are bound by the same rules.

clause: enter margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Aurelia Group Securities
why_it_matters: Because secured financing is banned outright rather than merely restricted in closed periods, the policy never reaches the question of a lender's forced sale during a Prohibited Trading Period, unlike policies that separately address that scenario.

clause: Securities – Include, but are not limited to shares, hybrids, debt securities, options, derivatives, interests in managed investment schemes, or any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market.
why_it_matters: The closing qualifier 'able to be traded on a financial market' creates some interpretive uncertainty over whether a bespoke OTC put/call is caught as a 'derivative' or only as part of the market-traded catch-all, though the separate listing of 'derivatives' supports inclusion.

clause: directors, employees and associates are prohibited from entering into any transaction to hedge their exposure to Abacus Securities.
why_it_matters: A purchased put and written call limiting exposure to the shares is squarely a hedging transaction; this ban applies to every tier, both vested and unvested holdings, and has no approval or exemption route, so it blocks a funded collar outright regardless of the financing question.

clause: directors, employees and associates are prohibited from holding Abacus Securities which are subject to margin loans or similar funding arrangements unless they have prior written approval from the Chair to do so.
why_it_matters: Unlike the hedging ban, the loan leg secured on the collared shares is only conditionally restricted and could in principle be approved by the Chair, but this is moot while the derivative legs remain absolutely prohibited.

clause: Margin loans used to fund the purchase of Abacus Securities may give the lender the right to require the sale of those securities at a time during the Blackout Period ... Such a sale may amount to insider trading (or create a perception of insider trading).
why_it_matters: Abacus's own rationale for gating secured financing is the risk of a lender-triggered forced sale landing in a Blackout Period; any facility agreement would need to build in trading-window-aware enforcement mechanics even if the hedging ban were ever lifted.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would create a perception risk outlined above.
why_it_matters: Even a technically permitted structure (such as an approved secured loan) can still be refused if the market might perceive the director or employee as taking advantage of their position, adding a discretionary layer on top of the express rules.

clause: Restricted Persons must notify the Company Secretary prior to any dealing, including periods outside of the Blackout Period ... the Chair, Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, the Managing Director or the Company Secretary (as relevant) may direct the person ... not to deal, or to impose conditions on the dealing in their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons.
why_it_matters: Even outside Blackout Periods, Restricted Persons (including directors) must pre-notify any dealing and can be blocked or have conditions imposed without reasons, adding execution-timing uncertainty for a bank-structured trade even before reaching the hedging ban.

topic: hedging of vested unrestricted shares expressly permitted
clause: Restricted Persons and their Connected Persons are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Company securities provided that the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Company securities for the purposes of this Policy, and the relevant approvals and notifications required under section 5 are made on that basis.
why_it_matters: This is the key collar-relevant clause: the policy expressly contemplates hedging vested, unrestricted shares by Restricted Persons subject only to ordinary section 5 dealing approvals, which is unusually favourable compared to policies that ban hedging outright.

topic: margin lending scope narrower than secured financing
clause: Restricted Persons and their Connected Persons must not deal in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: The express ban only reaches arrangements badged as margin lending; a bank collar loan structured as a general secured facility may sit outside the literal wording, though the section 10 substance-over-form approach creates real risk the Company would still treat it as caught.

clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: Even if the collar's secured loan is not literally a 'margin lending arrangement', this clause signals the Company would likely still treat an economically equivalent secured facility as caught by the section 6.2 ban.

clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is expressly excluded from the blackout-period and pre-approval requirements, giving the bank a clean enforcement path even during a closed period, provided the sale is genuinely lender-driven rather than voluntary.

clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
why_it_matters: The short-term dealing ban expressly extends to forward-contract-style arrangements, so a short-tenor collar entered and unwound by a Restricted Person within three months would independently breach this rule regardless of the hedging permission.

topic: transfer into margin account is a dealing
clause: transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account;
why_it_matters: If a bank requires the collared shares to be moved into a collateral or margin-style account to secure the loan, that transfer is itself treated as a prohibited dealing for Restricted Persons, so custody arrangements need careful structuring.

clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights). Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.
why_it_matters: A purchased put and written call limiting exposure to the shares is squarely a hedging arrangement; the ban is unconditional, applies regardless of vesting, and has no clearance or exemption route, so it blocks a funded collar's derivative legs entirely.

clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any clearance granted in accordance with this Clause 1.11 conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, in regards to the circumstances in which the securities in the Company may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: Even though the loan leg is only conditionally restricted (not banned outright), the Company can attach bespoke conditions to any consent, including around when a lender may force a sale, which is moot while the derivative legs remain absolutely prohibited.

topic: transfer into margin account is a dealing
clause: transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account;
why_it_matters: Moving the collared shares into a bank's collateral or margin account is itself treated as a dealing requiring the Company's prior consent under 1.11.

clause: The Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their respective associated parties trading in the Company's securities at any time.
why_it_matters: Even outside the narrow 5-business-day dividend/capital-management blackout, the Board can embargo trading at any time in its absolute discretion, adding timing uncertainty for entry, roll or unwind of any structure.

clause: As the Company is a listed investment company which will announce its investment updates and Net Tangible Assets (NTA) at least monthly on the ASX, the Board believes the Shareholders are generally fully informed.
why_it_matters: Because of monthly NTA disclosure, the policy has no standard results-based closed period, only the narrow dividend/capital-management window and ad hoc Board embargoes, which somewhat simplifies timing outside of the hedging ban itself.

topic: no express hedging or margin lending ban
clause: Dealing Includes any acquisition or disposal of, or agreement to acquire or dispose of securities or to grant, accept, acquire, dispose, exercise or discharge an option or other right or obligation to acquire or dispose of securities.
why_it_matters: Unlike most trading policies, RFF does not prohibit hedging or margin lending outright; a funded collar's derivative legs are simply a 'Dealing' via the option/right language and subject only to the ordinary Prohibited Period, no-Inside-Information and (for KMP/Directors) Compliance Certificate gate, making this an unusually permissive framework.

clause: disposals by a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under an approved margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: The only reference to margin lending is this phrase in the excluded-dealing carve-out; the policy does not specify who approves a margin loan or on what terms, leaving a bank's secured facility without a clearly defined approval pathway, though also without an express prohibition.

topic: secured lender forced sale excluded from the whole policy
clause: This Policy does not apply to: ... disposals by a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under an approved margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: Because Excluded Dealings sit outside the policy altogether, a lender's enforcement sale under an approved margin lending arrangement is excluded even from the Compliance Certificate and Prohibited Period requirements, giving the bank an unusually clean enforcement path on default.

topic: compliance certificate is not an approval
clause: Receipt of the Compliance Certificate by the Company is intended as a compliance monitoring function only, and is not an endorsement of the proposed transaction: individuals remain responsible for their own investment decisions and their compliance with the law.
why_it_matters: Even for Directors/KMP there is no discretionary company approval step to negotiate around for a collar's derivative legs; the only gate is self-certification of no Inside Information, then a 10-business-day window to execute.

topic: board and company secretary ad hoc discretion
clause: The Board reserves the right, in its absolute discretion, to impose an ad-hoc restriction on Dealing during any period outside the Prohibited Periods under this policy.
why_it_matters: Even outside the fixed half-year/preliminary-results black-out periods, the Board or Company Secretary can impose additional restrictions at any time, adding timing risk to entry, roll or unwind of a collar.

clause: AUC Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in relation to Company Securities.
why_it_matters: Outright bars the loan leg of a funded collar secured on the shares for all AUC Persons and their Connected Persons, with no clearance route or exemption.

clause: a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights ... this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending agreement if the agreement is prohibited by this Policy.
why_it_matters: Even if a secured facility somehow existed, this carve-out is moot because 7.1 already bans the underlying secured financing arrangement, so a bank could never lawfully hold enforceable security to sell against.

clause: must not ... enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that has not vested ... or has vested ... but remains subject to a holding lock
why_it_matters: The collar's put/call legs cannot be written over incentive securities until they are both vested and free of any holding lock.

clause: deal in financial products over or in respect of Company Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this Policy.
why_it_matters: Once vested and unlocked, an OTC put/call is only lawful if it qualifies as ordinary cleared Dealing under the Policy, so the bank's derivative documentation and timing must fit within the standard clearance procedure.

clause: Any clearance to trade can be granted or refused by Ausgold in its discretion, without giving any reasons. ... If a written clearance to trade is refused, the person seeking the clearance must keep that information confidential.
why_it_matters: Clearance for the derivative legs (and any later roll or unwind) can be refused without explanation and is capped at 10 business days, creating execution timing risk for a bank-facing collar.

clause: each Designated Person is required to obtain prior written clearance ... even if the proposed transaction is outside of a Prohibited Period.
why_it_matters: Director/officer/KMP executives must clear every leg of a collar (entry, roll, unwind) at any time, not just during open windows, unlike other staff.

clause: The AUC Persons (including Designated Persons) must ensure their Connected Persons comply with this Policy to the same standard and obligations that apply to that AUC Person.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, controlled entity or family trust does not escape the secured-financing ban or the clearance requirement.

clause: For the purpose of this Policy, reference to Dexus Securities includes reference to Dexus (ASX:DXS), Dexus Industria REIT (ASX:ADI) and Dexus Retail Convenience REIT (ASX:DXC). ... All trades by Employees in listed and unlisted financial products managed by Dexus require prior approval.
why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put/call over DXI units is not itself a Dexus Security nor a product managed by Dexus, so the trading-window and Business Approval Table machinery may not apply to the derivative legs at all, leaving only the general insider trading law and the unvested-securities hedging ban as constraints.

clause: trading in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities
why_it_matters: The ban is confined to margin lending; a bespoke bank loan secured by pledge or charge over the collared shares, not structured as a margin loan, is not expressly prohibited by this Policy.

clause: entering into a transaction or arrangement for the purpose of hedging exposure to movements in the price of un-vested securities
why_it_matters: Hedging of vested Dexus securities is not restricted by this clause at all, so a collar can only be written once the incentive securities have vested and ceased to be held under the plan's terms.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Media Test.
why_it_matters: Even where the approval regime is found to apply, a bank-facing collar could be refused as a discretionary reputational matter regardless of legal compliance.

clause: Where approval is withheld, the Employee is to keep that fact confidential and not disclose it to anyone. ... A clearance to trade may be withdrawn if circumstances change.
why_it_matters: A granted clearance for collar execution can be revoked before completion and any refusal must be kept confidential, creating execution timing risk for the bank counterparty.

clause: Associates of the above. An Associate would include immediate family members, people or entities (including SMSFs) over which the Employee may exert influence in investment decisions.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through an SMSF or family member does not escape the Policy's approval regime, which the Business Approval Table expresses as applying to 'Person (including Associates)'.

clause: Derivative has the meaning in section 761D of the Corporations Act and includes options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, cash settled swaps, caps and collars
why_it_matters: The Policy's own definitions expressly contemplate a 'collar' as a Derivative caught by the Trading regime, confirming an OTC put/call collar over Company Securities is ordinary Trading requiring the standard approval process rather than an unaddressed novel structure.

clause: No Director or Restricted Employee may enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities, or grant lenders any rights over their Company Securities without first obtaining prior written approval.
why_it_matters: Unlike many ASX peer policies, secured financing is not prohibited outright; a bank loan secured by pledge of the collared shares is expressly permitted subject to Designated Officer approval and ongoing disclosure.

clause: (Involuntary disposals caused by margin lender) An involuntary disposal of Securities that results from a margin lender or similar financier exercising its rights under a margin loan or similar funding arrangement.
why_it_matters: A forced sale by the bank under the collar's secured loan is excluded from the Prohibited Period trading ban, though the Policy notes that approval/notification requirements nominally 'continue to apply' to Trading under this exception.

clause: The Directors and Restricted Employees must inform the Company Secretary of any material change in their margin loan or similar funding arrangements e.g. movements in the LVR occasioned by drawdowns or price movements, and at least annually, of the amount drawn and securities covered.
why_it_matters: The bank facility's LVR, drawdown amount and collateral must be disclosed to the Company Secretary on an ongoing and at-least-annual basis, a compliance burden the executive and bank should factor into servicing covenants.

clause: This Securities Trading Policy (Policy) regulates Trading by Directors and Employees of the Company and its subsidiaries (the Group) in Company Securities or Securities of other companies.
why_it_matters: The Policy defines no 'Associate' or 'Connected Person' concept and does not expressly bind spouses, family trusts or controlled entities, so a collar or loan routed through such a vehicle is not captured by this Policy (though insider trading law would still apply to those persons independently).

topic: tax liability not an exceptional circumstance
clause: A tax liability relating to Securities received under an employee incentive scheme would also not normally constitute severe financial hardship or otherwise be considered an exceptional circumstance for the purpose of obtaining proper written approval to sell or otherwise dispose of Securities during a Prohibited Period.
why_it_matters: An executive cannot rely on a tax-driven liquidity need (e.g. funding a collar premium or loan interest) as grounds for in-window approval; entry, roll or unwind must otherwise fit within open trading windows or ordinary clearance.

topic: restricted trading is clearable, not banned
clause: unless written prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure
why_it_matters: None of short-term trading, hedging or margin lending/security-granting is an absolute ban in this Policy; each is expressly permitted with prior written clearance from the Company Secretary, materially easing the path to a funded collar and its secured loan compared with policies that ban these outright.

clause: (no clause addresses a secured lender's enforcement sale during a Black-out Period)
why_it_matters: If the bank needed to enforce its security and sell the collared Units during a Black-out Period, the Policy contains no express exclusion for that scenario, so it would need its own exceptional-circumstances clearance or fall within an open window.

clause: Unit(s) means: i. any unit or other interest in any LIT ...; ii. an option over an unissued unit ...; and iii. a renounceable or unrenounceable right to subscribe
why_it_matters: A bank-issued OTC put/call is not itself a 'Unit', so it sits outside the core Trade/Unit definition and section 1's general clearance trigger, but is separately caught (and permitted with clearance) via the broader hedging restriction in 6(ii).

clause: A clearance to trade can be given, withdrawn, or refused without a reason being given. ... Any clearance refusal or withdrawal must be kept confidential ... A clearance to trade is valid for five (5) business days.
why_it_matters: Execution timing risk for the bank: clearance for the collar's legs can be withdrawn or refused without reason, must be kept confidential by the executive, and lapses after 5 business days.

topic: Connected Persons must clear through the EQT/LIT Person
clause: a Connected Person must seek clearance through their EQT Person, LIT Person or LIT Partner in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure prior to trading in Units
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the clearance requirement.

clause: LIT Partners and LIT Persons may trade in a LIT's Units provided ... the trade has been executed in accordance with the LIT Partner's trading policy, procedures and/or controls which have been agreed with the Responsible Entity.
why_it_matters: If the relevant executive is engaged through a LIT Partner rather than directly as an EQT Person, the governing document for a collar is the LIT Partner's own agreed trading policy (which must meet at least this Policy's Black-out Periods), not this Policy directly.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even where clearance is otherwise available for the collar's legs, approval can be refused on a purely reputational/perception basis.

clause: The approver, having consulted with members of management as appropriate, may ... impose conditions on the dealing in their discretion.
why_it_matters: The Chair, MD or ARC Chair can attach bespoke conditions to approval of the derivative legs or the margin lending arrangement, such as tenor, disclosure, or unwind triggers.

topic: margin loan account transfer is a dealing
clause: transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account
why_it_matters: Moving the collared shares into a margin account to serve as the bank's collateral is itself treated as requiring the same prior approval as entering into the loan arrangement.

clause: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities
why_it_matters: The clause is framed around a conventional 'margin lending arrangement'; whether a bespoke bank loan secured by pledge of the collared shares (not structured as a margin loan) falls within 4.5's approval requirement, or escapes Policy control altogether, is not addressed.

clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a Secured Lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: If the bank enforces its security and sells the collared shares, that disposal is excluded from the blackout, approval and short-term dealing rules, reducing execution risk on enforcement.

clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: The Company will look past the formal labelling of a collar or loan to its economic substance, so structuring to avoid characterisation as 'hedging' or a 'margin lending arrangement' is unlikely to succeed.

clause: This clause does not apply to family members who are financially independent from the Restricted Person.
why_it_matters: A financially independent family member could potentially hold the collar or loan without being swept in as a Connected Person, though this is a narrow carve-out.

clause: Short selling includes any transaction where a person seeks to profit from a decline in the Company's share price, including through derivatives or other financial instruments.
why_it_matters: A purchased put, which profits when the HM1 share price falls, is capable of being characterised as prohibited short selling under this broad wording even though it functions as a hedge, so Board approval should expressly address and carve the put out of the section 9.3 prohibition.

clause: Restricted Persons must not include the Company's securities in a margin lending arrangement without prior written approval from the Company without prior approval of the Board.
why_it_matters: The internally inconsistent drafting leaves unclear whether Company approval, Board approval, or both are required for the loan leg of a funded collar, so the safest course is to obtain Board sign-off before the loan is put in place.

clause: This policy sets out the legal obligations and internal procedures relating to the buying and selling of Hearts and Minds Investments Limited ('the Company') and other securities.
why_it_matters: HM1 is a listed investment company with no equity incentive plan referenced and no minimum shareholding requirement, so a funded collar over a director's or executive's holding is assessed purely as an ordinary Restricted Person dealing, not against unvested-security rules.

clause: The Board retains absolute discretion to impose a trading embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their associated parties at any time, regardless of whether the trading window is open.
why_it_matters: Entry into, unwind of, or settlement under the collar can be blocked at any time at the Board's unfettered discretion, independent of the scheduled Trading Window/Blackout Period structure.

clause: any Restricted Person must furnish HM1 with broker statements or activity statements in relation to securities accounts that the Restricted Person has control over if requested to do so.
why_it_matters: HM1 can compel disclosure of the bank collar and loan account statements if it suspects a breach, so the arrangement cannot be kept confidential from the Company on request.

clause: a disposal of Hansen's securities on a case by case basis, that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement. On a case by case basis the Board will assess the rules that are applicable to key management personnel with respect to entering into agreements that provide lenders with rights over their interests in Hansen's Securities.
why_it_matters: The Policy contemplates secured lending arrangements broader than margin loans and gives the Board case-by-case discretion over the rules that apply, so a bank collar with a security interest over the shares could be assessed and potentially accommodated by the Board rather than being an outright prohibition, but there is no pre-set approval path or criteria.

clause: Should approval be given for entry into a margin lending arrangement Hansen may, where appropriate or required by law, disclose to the ASX the fact and nature of the margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: A funded collar structured with a secured loan analogous to a margin lending arrangement could result in public ASX disclosure of the fact and nature of the financing at Hansen's discretion.

topic: no hedging or equity plan concept
clause: Insider trading means the buying and selling of shares, other securities, derivative products or other price sensitive products (Securities) on the basis of price-sensitive information that is not generally available to others.
why_it_matters: The 2010-vintage Policy predates any specific hedging prohibition or reference to an executive equity incentive plan (only a passing reference to 'employee incentive scheme' options in section 5(g)), so a collar over vested shares is assessed purely as an ordinary dealing in Securities, not against a hedging or unvested-security rule.

clause: Securities Trading Policy - December 2010
why_it_matters: The policy is dated 2010 and may have been superseded by a later, unlodged version; the terms above should be confirmed as current before relying on them for the transaction.

clause: granting, accepting, acquiring, disposing, exercising or discharging an option or other right or obligation to acquire or dispose of securities
why_it_matters: Both legs of an OTC collar with a bank are 'dealing in securities' under this limb regardless of whether the option itself is a 'financial product of the Company', so the transaction needs Approving Officer clearance and must sit outside the blackout periods (or fall within the narrow disposal-only exemption).

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested/restricted holdings
clause: Employees may not enter into any transaction which would have the effect of hedging ... the risk of any fluctuation in the value of: (i) shares in the Company which are subject to a restriction on disposal under an employee share or incentive plan; or (ii) options or performance rights ... granted under an employee share or incentive plan.
why_it_matters: The absolute hedging ban is confined to unvested or disposal-restricted incentive securities; once shares vest and any disposal restriction lifts, section 12 no longer bars a collar over them, leaving only the general dealing-clearance and blackout regime to satisfy.

clause: The board must be made aware of any agreement or rights placed over a Specified Persons Company Securities prior to the person entering into the agreement.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares needs only prior Board notification, not Board consent or a veto right, and the lender's eventual enforcement sale is itself exempted from the Policy's dealing and blackout restrictions.

clause: This policy was approved and adopted by the board on 23 December 2010.
why_it_matters: PolyNovo lodged an 'Updated Share Trading Policy' with the ASX on 30 April 2026, but the full text of that update could not be located (both the ASX filing and the company's investor-hub governance page returned only a cover announcement); this extraction is based on the last full text available (23 December 2010) and must be reconfirmed against the 2026 update before being relied on.

clause: The Policy never defines 'Dealing' or 'Trade'; trading is described in the Purpose clause only as 'buy or sell', and the section 6 Definitions list has no entry for either term.
why_it_matters: Whether creating an OTC put/call, granting security, lending shares or short selling counts as 'trading' at all is left genuinely open, so a bank should not assume any of these are automatically caught or automatically exempt.

topic: hedging ban limited by vesting definition
clause: Hedging Transactions means any transaction or arrangement which partly or totally offsets the risk relating to a current holding, or an element or remuneration, that either has not vested or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: On its face the outright hedging ban in section 2.3 does not reach fully vested, unrestricted shares (holding lock lifted), so a collar over those shares is not an express 'Hedging Transaction' and instead only needs ordinary Derivatives clearance.

clause: This Policy regulates how and when Employees can trade in the Company's Securities, Derivatives and other secured financing arrangements ... / If You possess Inside Information about the Company's Securities, Derivatives and other secured financing arrangements, You are prohibited from trading.
why_it_matters: Secured financing arrangements (which would include a loan secured on collared shares) are named as subject matter for the insider-trading ban but are never prohibited, defined, or brought within the section 3 clearance regime, leaving the collar's loan leg without an explicit approval pathway or bar.

topic: extended no-clearance window for Restricted Persons
clause: Trading clearance will not be given to Restricted Persons in the periods between 30 June and the trading day after the Company releases its full year financial results, or 31 December and the trading day after the Company releases its half year financial results unless exceptional circumstances apply.
why_it_matters: This is materially longer than the 5-business-day Blackout Periods in section 2.2 and constrains when a Restricted Person can obtain clearance to enter, unwind or roll a collar.

clause: Clearance is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if You become aware of Inside Information prior to trading.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be executed within the 5-business-day validity window and can become unexecutable if inside information arises first.

clause: Each director and member of the Executive Team is obliged to ensure that each of their related or associated entities complies with this Policy.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled company does not escape the Policy for Directors/Executive Team members, though the same is not stated for ordinary Employees' families.

clause: This Policy applies to all staff within the RE Services business unit and governs all personal trading by RE Services staff in schemes administered by the RE Services business unit ("non-Perpetual securities").
why_it_matters: The document governs only the outsourced Responsible Entity's administrative staff dealing in the Fund's units; it never mentions the Fund's own directors, the investment manager's personnel, or any equity/incentive arrangement, so it is unclear this is the operative trading policy for the population a bank would target for a director/executive funded collar.

topic: no derivatives, hedging or financing coverage
clause: RE Services staff ... are within the scope of the definition of non-Perpetual Securities: (a) Prohibition of Insider Trading (b) Prohibition on front running (c) Prohibition on procuring or encouraging third parties to trade (d) Conflicts of interest (e) High volume personal trading.
why_it_matters: None of derivatives, hedging, margin lending, encumbrance, short selling, stock lending or CFDs are named anywhere; the substantive content sits in the separate Group Policy referenced but not included, so no leg of a funded collar can be confirmed as permitted or prohibited from this document alone.

clause: Approval granted pursuant to this Policy is valid for that business day only. Where the RE Services staff member has failed to act on that approval, a new approval must be sought to trade on another business day. ... Any trades submitted after 12 noon will be denied.
why_it_matters: If a collar or its unwind is treated as 'trading' under this Policy, each leg would need fresh same-business-day approval, which is operationally awkward for a multi-leg OTC structure with a bank counterparty.

clause: This Policy will be reviewed at least every two years and updated as required from time to time.
why_it_matters: No date of adoption, approval or lodgement appears anywhere in the document, so its currency and ASX Listing Rule 12.10 status cannot be confirmed from the text alone.

clause: Company Securities means Securities issued by the Company. Derivative has the meaning in section 761D ... includes options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, cash settled swaps, caps and collars.
why_it_matters: Because Company Securities is confined to instruments issued by Nuix, a bank-written OTC put/call referencing Nuix shares is arguably not itself 'Company Securities', so the Trading Window, Prohibited Period and margin-loan/secured-financing restrictions (all framed by reference to Company Securities) may not directly bite on the derivative legs of a collar, though the underlying insider trading law and clause 3.8's hedging ban (framed around the shares held, not the instrument's issuer) still apply.

clause: An involuntary disposal of Securities that results from a margin lender or similar financier exercising its rights under a margin loan or similar funding arrangement, entered into with prior approval under this Policy.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that treat a lender's enforcement sale as a breach, NXL expressly excludes an involuntary sale by a properly pre-approved secured financier from the Trading Window/Prohibited Period restrictions, so a bank enforcing security under a pre-cleared collar loan would not itself put the executive in breach.

clause: The Company's decision to refuse approval is final and binding on the person seeking the approval and if approval to enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement is refused, the person seeking the approval must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: If the Designated Officer declines to approve the collar's secured loan, there is no appeal, and the executive cannot disclose the refusal (including, on a strict reading, to the bank) which complicates deal negotiation and any explanation for withdrawing from a term sheet.

clause: The Directors and Restricted Employees must inform the Company Secretary of any material change in their margin loan or similar funding arrangements e.g. movements in the LVR occasioned by drawdowns or price movements, and at least annually, of the amount drawn and Securities covered.
why_it_matters: A funded collar's loan-to-value ratio moving with the put/call value would need to be reported to the Company Secretary as a material change, and the facility amount and shares covered must be disclosed at least annually, creating an ongoing compliance channel between the executive, the Company and (indirectly) the bank.

clause: A tax liability relating to Securities received under an employee incentive scheme would also not normally constitute severe financial hardship or otherwise be considered an exceptional circumstance for the purpose of obtaining proper written approval to sell or otherwise dispose of Securities due to Exceptional Circumstances.
why_it_matters: An executive cannot rely on the Exceptional Circumstances gateway to justify entering a collar or selling shares primarily to fund tax on vesting equity, narrowing the practical urgency arguments available if ordinary windows are closed.
