clause: After vesting and the cessation of any applicable escrow arrangements, a holder of the relevant securities may undertake any transaction of a type referred to in this section provided they obtain written clearance in the manner described in sections 5.3 and 5.4 and comply with all applicable laws (including insider trading laws) and the other provisions of this policy.
why_it_matters: This extends the Designated-Person-style clearance regime (Chairman/Board/CEO approval, 7-day validity, confidential and unreviewable refusal) to every holder of vested former-plan securities, not just Designated Persons, so a funded collar over an executive's vested equity always needs prior written clearance regardless of the executive's seniority.

clause: Prohibited conduct includes writing forward contracts or put or call options over the underlying securities, trading in derivative products or entering into other arrangements intended to hedge a "profit" in those securities, a margin loan or similar funding arrangement or other financial transaction which can give rise to pledging, lending or using the securities as collateral.
why_it_matters: This single clause names, almost verbatim, every component of a funded collar (put, call, derivative trading, margin loan, pledge/collateral) and bans all of them outright while the underlying plan securities are unvested or in escrow, with no clearance route at all - the collar can only be built once vesting and escrow have ended.

clause: Designated Persons may trade in Imricor securities outside of Blackout Periods if they obtain prior written clearance as follows: (a) for trading by directors of Imricor - from the Chairman; (b) for trading by the Chairman - from the Board; and (c) for trading by employees (who are not also directors) - from the Chief Executive Officer.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that only require pre-clearance during closed periods, IMR requires Designated Persons to obtain prior written clearance for every trade, year-round, so a director or KMP entering a funded collar needs Chairman/Board/CEO sign-off even in an otherwise open period.

clause: The clearance may be given or refused by the Clearance Officer in their discretion, with or without conditions, and with or without giving any reasons. A decision to refuse clearance is final and binding on the Designated Person, and the Designated Person must keep the decision and any reasons given confidential.
why_it_matters: If clearance for the collar or its loan leg is refused, there is no appeal and the executive cannot disclose the refusal (including, on its face, to the bank), which constrains how a declined deal can be discussed or restructured.

clause: Where clearance is given, the relevant trading must occur within the 7 days beginning on the day after the clearance.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar (or its unwind) must be priced and executed within 7 days of clearance, requiring tight coordination between the executive, the company and the bank.

clause: Clearance to trade will not be granted if the Clearance Officer believes that Imricor is likely in the short term to release a periodic financial report or other financial data, or make an announcement of market sensitive information under ASX Listing Rule 3.1.
why_it_matters: Clearance for collar entry, adjustment or unwind can be refused even outside the formal Blackout Periods if an announcement is imminent, adding timing uncertainty beyond the fixed windows.

clause: 29Metals Personnel are not permitted to use hedging or derivatives (such as caps, collars, warrants or similar products) or other products which alter the economic benefit or risk derived by them in relation to any 29Metals securities held by or on behalf of them.
why_it_matters: Both legs of a funded collar (purchased put, written call) are expressly named derivatives products and are banned outright for all personnel and Connected Persons regardless of vesting, with no clearance or exemption route.

topic: secured financing / power to compel sale
clause: 29Metals Personnel are not permitted to enter into funding arrangements where the lender is granted the power to sell or compel the sale of 29Metals securities held by the 29Metals Personnel.
why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on the collared shares in the ordinary way (giving the bank enforcement/sale rights on default) is itself prohibited, independent of the derivatives ban, so the financing leg fails even if the collar were somehow permitted.

clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could the proposed dealing be perceived by the market as taking advantage of my position in an inappropriate way? ... Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even for ordinary share dealings that do obtain clearance, a subjective reputational filter applies on top of the objective rules, adding an extra veto point for any bank-related transaction.

clause: The designation of an additional Blackout Period is confidential to 29Metals and must not be disclosed outside of the Company.
why_it_matters: An undisclosed extra blackout could freeze any dealing (were derivatives ever permitted) at a time the bank cannot verify, adding execution timing risk.

clause: This Policy also extends to persons with whom 29Metals Personnel have a close relationship or connection (a 'Connected Person') ... companies, trusts, partnerships or other entities which are managed, or directly or indirectly controlled, by the 29Metals Personnel or a family member, or were set up for the benefit of the 29Metals Personnel or a family member.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the loan through a family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the hedging/derivatives or secured financing bans.

clause: Clearance cannot be obtained for an acquisition of securities for exceptional circumstances.
why_it_matters: Even the narrow hardship/court-order carve-out from a Blackout Period could not be used to enter into the put or call legs of a collar (an acquisition/creation of rights), only to sell existing shares outright.

clause: This General Trading Policy and the restrictions on trading in shares of the Company set out below applies to each Executive and senior manager (Restricted Persons).
why_it_matters: On a literal reading, Directors are not 'Restricted Persons' and so may fall outside the trading-window, notification and embargo provisions of Section 1 entirely, leaving only the bare insider-trading prohibition in Section 2 to govern a director's funded collar, which is an important threshold ambiguity to resolve with the company before structuring.

topic: no derivatives, hedging, margin lending or secured financing regime
clause: (Absence of any provision on hedging, derivatives, margin lending, security/encumbrance, or secured financing anywhere in the document.)
why_it_matters: Nothing in this policy expressly or impliedly prohibits an OTC put/call collar or a loan secured over the shares; the only constraints are the overriding statutory and policy bar on dealing while possessing inside information, the narrow 5-day blackout, any ad hoc Board embargo, and (for Restricted Persons) the prior written notification obligation.

clause: Restricted Persons and their associated parties are prohibited (unless otherwise agreed to by the Board) from dealing in shares during the five business days before the announcement of a dividend or any other capital management initiative that might have a material impact on the share price.
why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX trading policies, there is no standing blackout tied to half-year or full-year results, so a collar's execution, unwind or roll window is far less constrained by fixed dates, subject only to the 5-day dividend/capital-management window and any discretionary embargo.

clause: The Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and their respective associated parties trading in the Company's shares at any time.
why_it_matters: This open-ended, undated embargo power (with no stated confidentiality or duration limit) could still freeze execution or unwind of a collar at any time at the Board's discretion, even though it is not tied to a specific event.

topic: margin lending / secured financing subject to Board approval
clause: Relevant Persons are prohibited from entering into Margin Lending arrangements, whereby lenders are provided with rights over their interests in the Company's securities, without prior written Board approval.
why_it_matters: Unlike an outright ban, this policy permits a loan secured on the collared shares (or any arrangement giving the bank rights over the shares) if the Board gives prior written approval, making the financing leg of a funded collar structurally available subject to Board sign-off.

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested plan securities
clause: Relevant Persons must not engage in hedging arrangements ... over unvested Securities issued pursuant to any employee or Director option or share plan. In addition, any hedging over vested Securities must comply with this policy.
why_it_matters: Because a collar would be written over already-vested shares, the absolute hedging ban does not apply; hedging of vested shares is only subject to the general framework (blackout periods, Director notification, no inside information), not a substantive bar or a dedicated approval step.

topic: financial products swept into blackout ban
clause: Designated Persons ... may NOT trade in the Company's securities on the ASX or financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities during, nor for twenty four (24) hours following the end of, the following Blackout Periods.
why_it_matters: The four quarterly Blackout Periods (plus a 24-hour buffer) expressly extend to derivative trades, so entry, unwind or settlement of the collar must fall within Open Periods unless the Chairman directs otherwise or Exceptional Circumstances clearance is obtained.

clause: Unless specified otherwise, clearance to trade outside a trading window will apply for a period of ten (10) business days from the communication to the Relevant Person of the clearance to trade.
why_it_matters: If a Closed Period exception is needed to execute or unwind the collar, documentation must complete within a 10-business-day window from grant of clearance, a tight timetable for a bank transaction.

clause: Notice lodged with the ASX must provide the following information: whether the trading occurred outside a Trading Window, when prior written clearance was required; whether clearance was provided to allow the Trade to proceed; and on what date clearance was provided if granted.
why_it_matters: A Director's entry into or unwind of a collar becomes a public ASX disclosure that flags whether it occurred outside the trading window and whether clearance was needed and granted, which the bank and director should factor into transaction timing and market messaging.

clause: The company's share trading policy regulates dealings by directors, officers, and employees, in shares, options and other securities issued by the company.
why_it_matters: The policy only restricts buying and selling of company-issued securities; it contains no sweep-up definition of 'dealing' catching derivatives, encumbrances or financing arrangements, so a bank-written OTC put/call and a loan secured on the shares fall outside its express scope.

clause: Buying and selling company securities by directors, officers, and employees outside the above trading window is prohibited.
why_it_matters: Any step that does involve buying or selling the underlying shares (e.g. physical delivery on collar unwind or default) would need to occur within one of the four scheduled windows or the Board-permitted 'Other' period, or require the exceptional-circumstances sign-off.

topic: Board discretion to open extra periods
clause: Other: At any such other times as the Board of Directors of the company permits.
why_it_matters: The Board can create an additional open period at its discretion, giving flexibility to time collar execution or unwind outside the four scheduled windows.

clause: each director has agreed to provide notice of such dealings to the company within five business days of any such dealing to enable the company to comply with its corresponding obligation to notify the ASX.
why_it_matters: Any share movement a director makes in connection with the collar (e.g. delivering shares on settlement) must be reported to the company within five business days for Appendix 3Y purposes, even though the collar derivatives themselves are not covered by the policy.

clause: prohibited, at any time, from granting, directly or indirectly, any form of security ... over any of Objective’s Securities where the shares or rights to shares have yet to vest or be issued
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a collar can never be secured on unvested shares or rights, for anyone, and there is no exemption authority for this specific ban.

clause: in any margin loan, unless prior approval is provided by the CEO or Board in writing
why_it_matters: If the bank's secured loan is structured as a margin loan over vested shares, a Designated Officer can proceed with prior written CEO or Board approval – the only named route to secured financing on vested shares.

clause: Designated Officers are not permitted to use any of Objective’s Securities as follows: ... (ii) in any margin loan ... (iii) in any share lending arrangement
why_it_matters: Margin loan and share lending restrictions target only Designated Officers; for other vested-share holders, secured financing on vested shares is not addressed at all, though the general insider trading and (non-binding) short-term trading guidance still apply.

topic: hedging scope limited to unvested plan shares
clause: prohibited from entering into any transaction which operates to hedge the exposure of shares or share rights that are unvested or have yet to be issued
why_it_matters: The derivative legs of a collar over vested shares fall outside the named hedging prohibition entirely; they are only potentially caught, if at all, by the undefined general insider trading and short-term dealing rules.

topic: notification not preclearance for ordinary trades
clause: The person who receives the notice of intention to buy or sell shares, is not authorised to prevent a Designated Officer from trading, but will provide guidance
why_it_matters: Outside Non-Trading Periods, a Designated Officer need only give 7 days' prior written notice (not obtain approval) before dealing, and cannot be blocked, so entering collar derivatives faces a low procedural bar once outside a blackout.

clause: everyone at Objective is expected to demonstrate integrity when dealing with shares, options, debentures (including convertible notes) and other securities (collectively, Securities)
why_it_matters: Because the Policy never defines 'Dealing' or 'trade' to expressly capture derivative creation or agreements to deal, an OTC put/call over Objective shares arguably sits outside the Policy's operative provisions except via the general insider-trading prohibition, creating interpretive uncertainty for a bank counterparty.

clause: (no provision addressing a financier's or lender's forced sale during a Non-Trading Period)
why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, there is no express breach trigger if a lender enforces security and sells during a blackout, leaving that risk entirely unaddressed rather than expressly prohibited.

topic: derivatives/hedging ban absolute for Designated Personnel
clause: Designated Personnel are prohibited from dealing in any financial products issued or created over the Securities by third parties or dealing in associated products. In addition, Designated Personnel may not enter into a transaction that operates to limit the economic risk of their security holding in SHAPE.
why_it_matters: Both legs of a funded collar - the bank-created put/call and the risk-limiting effect of the structure - are expressly and unconditionally prohibited for Designated Personnel (directors, SLT, Company Secretary, finance-report preparers), and none of the six Exempt Transactions in section 7 applies, so the collar cannot proceed for this tier under the current Policy.

clause: SHAPE Personnel are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Securities as the terms may require the Securities be sold when the Personnel possesses inside information.
why_it_matters: The secured loan leg of a funded collar, if structured as a margin loan, is banned outright for the entire personnel population (not just Designated Personnel) with no exemption route, on stated concerns about forced sale while holding inside information - a concern a bespoke bank facility could try to address contractually but the Policy gives no carve-out for that.

clause: SHAPE may, in exceptional circumstances, provide written approval to a Designated Person seeking to trade in the Securities during a Prohibited Period. No exceptional circumstances approval will be provided during the Prohibited Trading Periods set out in section 5.1 of this policy.
why_it_matters: The Policy appears to grant, then immediately withdraw, hardship-based relief for trading during the actual closed windows, so a forced unwind or margin-call-driven sale cannot rely on this exception while a blackout is in effect.

clause: (the Policy does not distinguish unvested from vested Securities anywhere in sections 4 or 5)
why_it_matters: Because the derivatives and hedging bans in 5.3 apply to 'their security holding' without qualification, they extend equally to vested shares that would otherwise be freely tradeable, closing off the OTC collar route for Designated Personnel regardless of vesting status.

topic: no clearance regime below Designated Personnel
clause: All personnel have an individual responsibility to ensure that they comply with the law relating to insider trading and this policy.
why_it_matters: For SHAPE Personnel who are not Designated Personnel, there is no notification or preclearance system at all, so a collar over vested shares held by such a person turns only on the margin lending, short-term trading and short-selling prohibitions, with no derivatives-specific bar.

topic: secured lender forced sale excluded and insider-trading-safe
clause: Dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excepted from Blackout Periods]. ... Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
why_it_matters: If the bank enforces its security and sells the collared shares on default, that sale is expressly excluded from the Blackout Period prohibition and expressly stated not to breach insider trading laws even if the executive held inside information at the time - a materially favourable feature for the loan's enforcement mechanics.

clause: Where the exercise price of options is being provided by a margin loan or other form of lending arrangement then there may be a risk that the KMP or Personnel may need to sell shares ... Where this occurs at a time when the person possessed inside information, then the sale of the Company's securities would be a breach of insider trading laws, even though the person's decision to sell was not influenced by the inside information that the person possessed.
why_it_matters: A sale that the executive chooses to make to meet a margin call (rather than the lender itself enforcing its security) is not protected - it remains a breach if made while holding inside information - so the facility should be structured so any price-triggered sale is the lender's own enforcement action, not the executive's voluntary instruction.

clause: “dealing in securities” means to buy or sell shares, options or other securities in the Company, or enter into transactions in relation to shares, options or other securities in the Company.
why_it_matters: With no hedging clause and no OTC-derivative-specific treatment, a bank-written put/call is assessed only under the broad dealing definition, needing the standard Chairman/Company Secretary no-impediment check and Blackout Period avoidance, but facing no derivative-specific prohibition.

clause: (the Policy nowhere prohibits or conditions entry into a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement)
why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, entering into the secured loan itself is not restricted or subject to a distinct approval requirement, so the bank's financing leg of the collar is not blocked by this Policy.

clause: Where the Chairman wishes to deal in securities, he has contacted a Non-Executive Director, or in his absence, the Company Secretary and notified them of their intention to do so and the Non-Executive Director or Company Secretary indicates that there is no impediment to them doing so.
why_it_matters: If the collar counterparty is the Chairman personally, clearance is sought from a Non-Executive Director instead of the Chairman, otherwise the mechanics mirror the standard process.

clause: The entering into of all types of “protection arrangements” for any Universal Store securities (or Universal Store products in the derivatives markets): (a) is prohibited at any time in respect of any Universal Store securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock; and (b) otherwise, requires consent under paragraph 4.2.
why_it_matters: A funded collar's put/call legs are squarely 'protection arrangements' (limiting economic risk and enabling profit from a price decrease); over unvested or holding-locked shares they are banned outright with no ordinary clearance route, but over vested, unrestricted shares they proceed with the standard 4.2 Authorising Officer consent.

topic: exceptional-circumstances override may reach the unvested ban
clause: In exceptional circumstances the Authorising Officer, has discretion to approve dealings in Universal Store securities during a Blackout Period, or other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy.
why_it_matters: This relief is unusually broad - not confined to Blackout Period trading - and its wording ('other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited') could arguably extend to the absolute unvested/holding-lock protection-arrangement ban, giving a possible, though untested, route to collar unvested shares with Authorising Officer approval on hardship or similar grounds.

topic: secured lender enforcement exempted but must still be notified
clause: a disposal of Universal Store securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement [is an exemption available at any time]. ... If a Universal Store Person undertakes any of the actions described in paragraph (a), that Universal Store Person must advise the relevant Authorising Officer
why_it_matters: If the bank enforces its security and sells the collared shares, that disposal is exempt from the Blackout Period and consent requirements, but the executive must still notify the Authorising Officer after the fact; there is no separate breach consequence stated for this scenario, unlike some peer policies.

topic: no margin lending or general secured financing provision
clause: (the Policy does not name margin lending and does not otherwise restrict entering a secured financing arrangement over Universal Store securities)
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, if secured on vested shares, is not restricted by this Policy at all; only the resulting enforcement disposal is addressed, as an exemption.

clause: Under no circumstances should Universal Store Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in Universal Store securities. This prohibition includes short term direct dealing in Universal Store securities as well as transactions in the derivative markets, involving exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.
why_it_matters: A short-tenor collar or one with early-termination features risks being characterised as short-term or speculative derivative-market trading, which is banned outright with no stated clearance route, so tenor and unwind mechanics should avoid that characterisation.

clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of collared shares under the loan security is expressly excluded from the policy's trading restrictions, so it is not a breach even during a Blackout Period, unlike policies that treat forced sales as a breach.

clause: You must not put in place a non-discretionary trading plan in respect of Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance ... You must not cancel any such trading plan during a Prohibited Period, unless the circumstances are exceptional.
why_it_matters: If the collar's settlement or unwind mechanics are structured as a standing instruction/plan, establishing or cancelling it is separately regulated and needs its own clearance.

clause: A Connected Person means your spouse or partner, child or step-child under 18 years, a parent, an unlisted body corporate which you are a director of, a trust of which you are a trustee ... or any other person over whom you have significant influence or control.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the clearance requirements, as the executive must procure the Connected Person's compliance.

clause: You must not trade in Securities at any time ... unless you first obtain prior written clearance from [the Approving Officer]
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that only require clearance during blackout windows, every leg of the collar (entry, unwind, and the secured loan) needs fresh written clearance regardless of timing, each valid for only about 5 business days.

clause: The determination ... will be made, where circumstances permit, within two (2) business days of receipt of the application ... Where a waiver of this policy is granted, the Designated Person must execute the proposed trade within five (5) trading days after the day on which the waiver is granted.
why_it_matters: If collar entry or unwind needs an exceptional-circumstances waiver during a closed period, the decision is relatively fast (about two business days) and confidential, but the trade must then be executed within a tight five-trading-day window.

clause: In this policy "Company Securities" include: ... derivatives and other financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: The bank-written put and call are themselves 'Company Securities' under this policy, so entering into, adjusting or unwinding the collar is treated identically to trading the underlying shares for closed-period, insider-information and clearance/notification purposes.

clause: This policy does not mention margin lending, security interests, encumbrances or any form of secured financing.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar and the grant of security over the collared shares are not expressly regulated, leaving the bank without company-policy comfort on enforcement, forced-sale, or disclosure treatment; those risks must be managed contractually rather than by reference to this policy.

clause: Company Securities includes shares in the Company, options over those shares and any other financial products of the Company traded on ASX.
why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put and call over Meteoric shares are not 'financial products ... traded on ASX' and are not issued 'of the Company', so on the document's wording they are not 'Company Securities' and the dealing, clearance and announcement-day restrictions do not apply to the derivative legs of a funded collar.

clause: Broker credit (beyond T+3), margin lending or leveraged equity providers (by whatever name and under whatever guise) must not be used ... without the fully informed consent of the Board.
why_it_matters: Unlike the derivative legs, the anti-avoidance wording ('by whatever name and under whatever guise') means the loan secured on the collared shares is caught regardless of how it is structured, and needs full Board consent rather than mere Disclosure Officer clearance.

clause: The policy's only carve-out from 'dealing' is joining or subscribing under a dividend reinvestment plan (para 5.2); there is no exempt-dealing list of the kind other policies use for secured-lender forced sales.
why_it_matters: If the bank ever enforces its security and sells the collared shares, that sale is an ordinary 'dealing in Company Securities' by the executive (or is treated as if by them) with no stated exemption, so it would still require Disclosure Officer clearance and could be blocked on an ASX announcement day.

clause: enter finance arrangements involving the Company's securities as collateral, such as options, warrants, derivatives, futures or any other financial products issued over the Company's securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions
why_it_matters: This clause is squarely on point: a bank-written OTC put/call combined with a loan secured on the shares is precisely a 'finance arrangement involving the Company's securities as collateral' using derivatives 'issued ... by third parties such as banks', an absolute and unwaivable prohibition.

clause: This restriction also applies to Company securities held beneficially (including, for example, in trust or under any Company incentive plan) on the Designated Person's behalf.
why_it_matters: The hedging ban is not limited to shares already legally held outright — it expressly extends to unvested or plan-held securities, closing off any argument that pre-vesting shares could be hedged.

clause: Unless a Clearance has been obtained, Designated Persons ... [engage in short-term or speculative trading; multiple sales] — contrasted with items (a)-(d) which carry no such 'unless Clearance obtained' qualifier.
why_it_matters: The drafting contrast confirms the finance-arrangement, hedging, margin-lending and short-selling bans cannot be cleared or approved by any officer of the Company, unlike the short-term trading restriction.

topic: hedging and margin lending bans have no carve-outs
clause: Sections 1.1.3, 1.1.5, 1.1.6 and 1.2.1 of this Policy do not apply to: (a) participation in an employee, executive or director equity plan ... (b)-(d) [DRP/SPP/rights issue/takeover/no-change-of-interest/non-discretionary-plan dealings]
why_it_matters: Sections 1.2.2 (margin lending) and 1.2.3 (hedging) are not among the excluded sections, so both absolute bans apply even to securities acquired under an incentive plan, DRP, rights issue or non-discretionary plan — there is no route to a funded collar regardless of how the underlying shares were acquired.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even for dealing that is not otherwise banned, any approval needed for the share-settlement leg of a structure can be refused on reputational grounds alone, at the approver's unreviewable discretion.

topic: approval and waiver both lapse in 5 business days
clause: the approved dealing must occur within 5 business days following approval, otherwise the approval is no longer effective, and fresh approval must be sought ... the duration of the waiver to deal in securities will be 5 business days.
why_it_matters: Any approved share-level leg (entry, unwind or delivery) must be executed within a tight 5-business-day window across every approval pathway in this policy, constraining settlement timing.

clause: transactions or arrangements which have a substantially similar economic effect as the sale or purchase of a SKYCITY security, or which operate to limit the economic risk of a Restricted Person's interest in SKYCITY securities
why_it_matters: An OTC collar (purchased put and written call) over vested shares is squarely caught for a Restricted Person and needs prior written consent, executed within 10 trading days of consent and only within the open trading window unless a hardship waiver is obtained.

clause: a disposal of SKYCITY securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of collared shares under the loan is expressly excluded from the window-period and consent regime, so lender enforcement is not blocked by the Policy even during a closed period.

clause: whether the sale or purchase, or transactions or arrangements, would have the effect of limiting the economic risk of the Restricted Person's entitlement to SKYCITY securities that have not vested
why_it_matters: Hedging or collaring unvested equity is an express factor weighed against consent, so a funded collar is realistically available only once the underlying shares have vested.

clause: The Additional Restrictions do not apply to staff who are not designated as Restricted Persons.
why_it_matters: If the bank's counterparty director or executive is not a Restricted Person, no consent, window or approval regime under this Policy constrains entry into a collar or its secured loan at all, subject only to the general insider trading prohibition.

clause: This Policy covers certain provisions and procedures that apply to SKYCITY directors and employees but does not constitute an exhaustive set of statements about the law.
why_it_matters: No express prohibition on margin lending, other secured financing or granting security over SKYCITY securities exists anywhere in the Policy, so the loan leg of a funded collar is not itself barred by this document.

clause: Designated Persons may not ... use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.
why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on the collared shares is a 'similar funding arrangement' and is banned outright for Designated Persons and their deemed-associate spouses, dependants and controlled entities, with no clearance route or exemption anywhere in the Policy, which kills the financed leg of a collar.

clause: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock
why_it_matters: Bars any hedge, collar or short-selling-style arrangement over unvested or holding-locked shares outright; a collar is only conceivable once the shares vest and any holding lock lifts.

clause: otherwise, requires approval under clause 6
why_it_matters: Even over vested, unrestricted shares, a collar (an arrangement limiting economic risk or enabling profit from a price decrease) is not prohibited but is squarely captured and needs prior written Chair/Board approval, outside Black-out Periods.

clause: Any decision to grant or refuse to grant Disposal Consent ... may be made in the Approval Officer's or Board's absolute discretion
why_it_matters: The Disposal Consent hardship/court-order waiver applies only to Black-out Period dealing, not to the margin loan or protection-arrangement prohibitions, so severe financial hardship cannot unlock a funded collar structure that relies on encumbering the shares.

clause: in relation to those persons identified in paragraphs (a), (b), (c) and (d) above, the following people are also deemed to be Designated Persons: their spouse ... a person financially dependent on or acting in concert ... a trust or company which they or any close family members control or have an interest in
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust, or controlled company does not escape the margin loan or protection-arrangement bans.

clause: the order must be completed within five trading days otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied
why_it_matters: Constrains the timing of any collar unwind or settlement order placed shortly before a Black-out Period begins.

topic: margin loan / share-secured loan ban with Board carve-out
clause: Save where expressly permitted by the Board, Relevant Persons are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Company Securities or in relation to which Company Securities may be used as security against loan repayments.
why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on the collared shares is a margin lending arrangement caught by clause 17 and is prohibited by default; it can only proceed with the Board's express, discretionary permission.

topic: caps and collars named as Derivatives
clause: Derivatives ... includes ... put or call options, forward contracts ... swaps, contracts for difference ... caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement
why_it_matters: An equity collar (put and call) is squarely and by name a Derivative under this Policy, governed by clause 16: banned over unvested securities but permitted over vested securities subject to Clearance.

clause: A Clearance ... will remain in force for the date of approval only, unless otherwise notified by the Clearance Officer (if the Dealing is not placed within this time, the Clearance will no longer have effect and a new Clearance must be requested and obtained)
why_it_matters: Execution of a cleared collar with the bank must occur on the day Clearance is given, or a fresh Clearance request is needed, requiring tight coordination between the Relevant Person, the bank and the Clearance Officer.

clause: What will the public perception be if it were reported on the front page of the newspaper?
why_it_matters: Even a cleared, vested-share collar could be refused Clearance, or criticised after the fact, if it would fail this broad reputational test, adding a discretionary filter beyond the black-letter rules.

clause: If a Relevant Person may not Deal in Company Securities, he or she must also prevent such Dealing by his or her Associate.
why_it_matters: A collar or secured loan cannot be routed through a spouse, family trust or controlled company to escape the derivatives or margin-lending restrictions, since the Relevant Person must actively prevent the Associate from dealing.

clause: enter into any arrangement where a security interest is granted over their Securities that could result in the disposal of their Securities without their consent, without receiving clearance from the Chairman (in respect of Directors) or the Company Secretary (in respect of all other Employees)
why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies that ban all secured financing outright, this Policy expressly permits granting a security interest over Emeco shares -- the funded collar's loan leg -- provided prior written clearance is obtained, giving a workable approval pathway for the loan.

topic: absolute hedge ban on remuneration securities
clause: enter into any transaction intended to hedge Employee's exposure to Securities, which have been issued to the Employee as part of the Employee's remuneration by Emeco
why_it_matters: Hedging (and by extension a collar) is banned outright, with no clearance override, for any Securities issued as remuneration -- a collar can only be considered over Securities held outside of incentive-plan issuance, e.g. shares bought on-market.

topic: acquisition financing vs. security over existing shares
clause: fund the purchase of Securities with margin loans (7.2(a)) ... a security interest is granted over their Securities that could result in the disposal of their Securities without their consent ... without receiving clearance (7.2(b))
why_it_matters: Distinguishes acquisition financing (banned outright) from encumbering already-held shares (clearable) -- a funded collar over existing vested shares is not a 'margin loan to acquire securities' and so is not caught by the absolute ban.

clause: a security interest is granted over their Securities that could result in the disposal of their Securities without their consent
why_it_matters: A bank's standard enforcement or forced-sale right under the collar's loan squarely triggers the clearance requirement, so the loan documentation and clearance request should address that risk up front.

clause: those restriction and prohibitions also apply to each close family member and any company or trust which the Employee or close family member may control or influence
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled company does not avoid the hedge ban or the clearance requirement for encumbrance.

clause: The Policy contains no definitions section; it refers only to KMPs dealing/trading/transacting in 'the Company's securities' without defining 'deal', 'securities' or 'relevant interest' beyond the beneficial-interest reference in the transfer exclusion.
why_it_matters: There is no express or definitional hook sweeping OTC derivatives, hedging, margin lending or encumbrance into the Policy's restrictions, so on its face a funded collar with a bank is not caught by anything beyond the general insider-information and closed-period rules; this also means the analysis rests on an absence of prohibition rather than a clear permission, which the bank should confirm with the company.

clause: KMP's are not permitted to trade in the Company's Securities during the period from the end of a calendar month until the day after the release of the monthly Net Asset Backing Announcement.
why_it_matters: As a listed investment company Whitefield issues a monthly NAB announcement, so this closed period recurs every month and materially narrows the windows available to execute, adjust or unwind a collar if entry/settlement is treated as 'trading' in the shares.

clause: The Policy applies only to 'private dealings in Whitefield's issued securities by Key Management Personnel' with no reference to options, rights, or vesting.
why_it_matters: There is no unvested/vested-locked distinction to navigate; any WHF shares held by a KMP can be treated as unrestricted for Policy purposes, subject only to the closed periods and the insider information ban.

clause: Key Management Personnel may at any time dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement ... a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is expressly excepted from the Closed Periods and from the insider trading prohibition, which is favourable for the secured loan leg of a funded collar.

clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company securities (ie a volume ... in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller ... or ... in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume ... for the preceding 20 trading days) ... needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
why_it_matters: If the collar or its unwind involves delivering more than 10% of the executive's holding or of 20-day average volume, a mandatory Board and legal-adviser discussion (with a documented file note) precedes execution, adding process and potential delay for the bank.

clause: it is not permissible to provide the exercise price of options by selling the shares acquired on the exercise of these options unless the sale of those shares occurs outside the periods specified in paragraph 4.1.
why_it_matters: If the collar structure is layered onto option-exercise shares, a cashless/sell-to-cover exercise must be timed outside the Closed Periods.

clause: The Policy defines covered transactions only as 'the sale and purchase of any securities of the Company' and never addresses derivatives, hedging or CFDs.
why_it_matters: An OTC put and call are not expressly named, so whether they are caught depends on whether 'securities' or 'dealing' is read broadly; the bank should have the company confirm treatment before relying on the absence of an express rule.

clause: The insider trading prohibition extends to dealings by individuals through nominees, agents or other associates, such as family members, family trusts and family companies (referred to as "Associates").
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the secured loan through a family trust or company does not avoid the approval and notification requirements.

clause: The ASX Listing Rules require the Company to notify the ASX within 5 business days after any dealing in securities of the Company ... which results in a change in the relevant interests of a Director.
why_it_matters: Granting security over the shares to the bank, or settling the collar, may change the Director's relevant interest and trigger an Appendix 3Y disclosure within 5 business days.

clause: Key Management Personnel may at any time dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement ... a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is expressly excepted from the Closed Periods and from the insider trading prohibition, which is favourable for the secured loan leg of a funded collar.

clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company securities (ie a volume ... in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller ... or ... in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume ... for the preceding 20 trading days) ... needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
why_it_matters: If the collar or its unwind involves delivering more than 10% of the executive's holding or of 20-day average volume, a mandatory Board and legal-adviser discussion (with a documented file note) precedes execution, adding process and potential delay for the bank.

clause: it is not permissible to provide the exercise price of options by selling the shares acquired on the exercise of these options unless the sale of those shares occurs outside the periods specified in paragraph 4.1.
why_it_matters: If the collar structure is layered onto option-exercise shares, a cashless/sell-to-cover exercise must be timed outside the Closed Periods.

clause: The Policy defines covered transactions only as 'the sale and purchase of any securities of the Company' and never addresses derivatives, hedging or CFDs.
why_it_matters: An OTC put and call are not expressly named, so whether they are caught depends on whether 'securities' or 'dealing' is read broadly; the bank should have the company confirm treatment before relying on the absence of an express rule.

clause: The insider trading prohibition extends to dealings by individuals through nominees, agents or other associates, such as family members, family trusts and family companies (referred to as "Associates").
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the secured loan through a family trust or company does not avoid the approval and notification requirements.

clause: The ASX Listing Rules require the Company to notify the ASX within 5 business days after any dealing in securities of the Company ... which results in a change in the relevant interests of a Director.
why_it_matters: Granting security over the shares to the bank, or settling the collar, may change the Director's relevant interest and trigger an Appendix 3Y disclosure within 5 business days.

clause: Directors of the company are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the company's securities.
why_it_matters: A bank loan secured against the collared CWP shares, if characterised as a margin lending arrangement, is an absolute prohibition for a Director, so the collar's financing leg for a Director participant faces a real risk of being unavailable unless structured to avoid that characterisation or specifically approved by the Board.

clause: securities means ... derivatives (such as swap options, warrants) and other financial products issued by third parties in relation to CWP shares, options and financial instruments; dealing means ... hedging or acquiring options over unvested securities.
why_it_matters: The bank-written put and call are themselves 'securities' under this policy and entering into them is 'dealing', so the whole collar structure (not just any sale of underlying shares) needs one trading day's notice, Company Secretary clearance, and must sit outside the closed periods.

clause: Dealing in the following circumstances is exempted from the Share Trading Policy: (a)-(h) [list of exceptions, none addressing a secured lender's enforcement sale].
why_it_matters: Unlike some peer policies, CWP has no carve-out for a lender's forced sale on default; if the bank enforces its security and sells the collared shares during a closed period, that sale appears to breach the policy, so enforcement timing should be addressed contractually or via a Board-approved exception.

clause: connected person means ... spouse/de facto spouse and any child ... under the age of eighteen ... and shall include any trust of which any such individuals are trustees or beneficiaries and any company over which they have control.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a connected person's trust or company does not escape the policy, since dealing by connected persons (and procuring or advising them) is expressly covered.

clause: The Chairman must be informed of the following information when applying for written approval for a margin loan: a) the number of the Company's securities involved; b) key terms and trigger points of the margin loan; c) the rights of the lender to sell securities; and d) any other material information.
why_it_matters: The bank's secured loan against the collared shares must be disclosed to the Chairman in detail (size, terms, trigger points, and the bank's enforcement rights) before the executive may proceed, giving the company visibility into, and an effective gate over, the collar's economic terms.

clause: This Policy covers trading in shares in the Company, derivatives related to the Company's shares, whether issued by the Company or not and to any traded Company options.
why_it_matters: The bank-written put and call are themselves covered 'securities' regardless of who issues them, so the whole collar structure (not just any share transfer) requires the Chairman's prior written clearance.

clause: Key Management Personnel must not use derivatives and hedging arrangements in relation to unvested securities. ... Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration scheme.
why_it_matters: There is no clearance route around this: a funded collar can only be written over already-vested Focus Minerals shares.

clause: A disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their security rights for example under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from this policy]. Even if trading is excluded from this Policy, Key Management Personnel must not trade in the Company's securities if they are possession of insider information.
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is excluded from the Policy altogether (including during Blackout Periods), which is favourable for the loan leg, though the KMP-level insider information caveat is preserved as a residual risk.

clause: Directors and executives are also excluded from dealing in securities within the period from receipt of the Board Pack and the Directors' Meeting.
why_it_matters: This recurring, unscheduled blackout (tied to board cycle rather than calendar dates) further narrows the windows available to enter, adjust or unwind the collar.

topic: hedging ban is the binding constraint
clause: any arrangement that has the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to a holding of WQG Securities in a Relevant Account (including unvested options)
why_it_matters: This is an absolute, substance-based ban with no clearance or Exceptional Circumstances carve-out, so a purchased put or a collar over vested or unvested holdings is prohibited outright regardless of any financing question.

clause: Relevant Account means all accounts: (a) in which a Key Management Personnel has any form of ownership interest (including with other entities); (b) that a Key Management Personnel has the power, directly or indirectly, to effect or influence decisions regarding transactions in the account.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or a secured loan through a family trust, SMSF or controlled entity does not escape the hedging, margin lending or short-term trading bans.

clause: margin lending over any WQG Securities
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that ban 'any secured financing arrangement', this ban is limited to the named activity of margin lending; a bespoke bank loan secured over shares that is not badged a margin loan is not expressly captured, though the hedging ban would independently block the collar leg that the loan is meant to finance.

clause: Other than transactions excluded by virtue of clause 3.4, any trading in WQG Securities may only be done during the following periods as applies to the relevant WQG Securities
why_it_matters: Even a permitted derivative dealing (outside the hedging ban) could only be entered, unwound or rolled inside narrow post-results/AGM/weekly-NTA windows, materially constraining execution timing for a bank counterparty.

topic: secured loans not limited to margin lending
clause: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.
why_it_matters: This bans any bank loan secured over the collared shares outright, not just broker margin facilities, so the funded leg of a collar cannot be structured under this policy regardless of tenor or approval.

clause: The Company does not operate any equity-based remuneration schemes.
why_it_matters: There is no unvested KMP shareholding to consider; any collar would be over ordinary, already-vested shares, so the vesting-state distinction in the schema is largely moot for MIR.

clause: KMP must use all reasonable endeavours to ensure that, if they have a reportable interest in the Company's securities as defined by the ASX Listing Rules and Corporations Act due to a relationship with a third party, that third party complies with this policy as if it were a KMP.
why_it_matters: A collar or loan booked through a related third party (trust, SMSF, spouse) does not escape the secured-financing ban if the KMP has a reportable interest in the shares.

clause: A KMP ... may request and be given clearance to sell (but not purchase) the Company's securities when they would otherwise be prohibited ... if they are in severe financial difficulty or other exceptional circumstances apply.
why_it_matters: Even absent the secured-financing ban, entering a collar (writing a call, buying a put) during a prohibited period could not rely on the exceptional-circumstances carve-out, which only ever authorises an outright sale.

topic: no definition of dealing or securities
clause: [No Definitions section in the policy]
why_it_matters: Because 'dealing' and 'the Company's securities' are never formally defined, whether an OTC put/call over MIR shares is caught at all is genuinely ambiguous, creating interpretive risk for a bank counterparty independent of the express secured-financing ban.

clause: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Tivan securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock; and (b) otherwise, requires consent under clause 4.3.
why_it_matters: Once the executive's shares are vested and free of any holding lock, both the derivative legs and the secured loan of a funded collar move from an absolute ban to a clearance-based regime, making the structure achievable in principle post-vesting.

clause: a disposal of Tivan securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is expressly excluded from the policy altogether, so it is not a breach and is not blocked by a Blackout Period or the notification regime - a materially more collar-friendly enforcement position than policies that treat lender enforcement as a breach.

clause: For the avoidance of doubt and without limiting the generality of this policy, entering into protection arrangements includes entering into transactions which: (a) amount to "short selling" ...; (b) operate to limit the economic risk ...; or (c) otherwise enable a Tivan Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.
why_it_matters: The definition is purposive and would clearly catch a purchased put and written call as a collar, regardless of how the bank documents or labels the trade.

clause: Tivan may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on trading in Tivan's securities ... Any restriction communicated ... must be kept strictly confidential.
why_it_matters: Entry, unwind or roll of the collar can be blocked at any time by an undisclosed restriction, creating timing risk the bank cannot see coming or verify.

topic: clearance revocable and voided by later inside information
clause: can be withdrawn (if clearance has been given) if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances ... If a Tivan Person comes into possession of Inside Information after receiving a clearance to trade, they must not trade despite having received the clearance.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar trade or its financing can become unexecutable between approval and execution/settlement if inside information arises or the Authorising Officer withdraws consent.

clause: Restricted Persons and other employees covered by this policy are required to disclose any margin lending or other secured financial arrangements to the Company, so that the Board and senior management are not caught unaware if there is a default.
why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, USL does not ban margin lending or secured financing over Company Securities at all - the loan leg of a funded collar is permitted subject only to disclosure to the Board, a materially more favourable starting point than an outright prohibition.

clause: This Policy prohibits any person affected by this Policy from entering into a hedging transaction.
why_it_matters: Despite the permissive financing stance, this standalone sentence bans any hedging transaction outright with no vesting carve-out, which independently blocks the put/call legs of a collar over vested, unrestricted shares.

topic: secured lender default sale confirmed lawful
clause: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
why_it_matters: Gives the bank comfort that its enforcement sale of the collared shares on default will not itself constitute insider trading or a policy breach, and is separately listed as an excluded dealing (5.14(l)).

clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company Securities (i.e. a volume ... in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller ... or ... in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume ... for the preceding 20 trading days) ... needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
why_it_matters: Unwinding or delta-hedging a sizeable collar position by the bank or the executive could trigger this pre-sale governance discussion and file-note requirement, adding a step beyond ordinary clearance.

clause: the dealing must be conducted within five (5) business days from the date of approval (or such other period of time as specified by the Approver). If the Restricted Person does not deal in securities within this time period, the approval will lapse.
why_it_matters: Execution of the collar (once cleared) must be completed within a short, defined window or fresh approval is required, constraining the bank's execution timeline.

topic: absolute derivatives ban overrides the whole policy
clause: Notwithstanding any other part of this policy, TPW People must not at any time: (a) trade in derivate products issued over or in respect of TPW Securities
why_it_matters: This is a permanent, non-waivable prohibition with no vesting-state carve-out and no exceptional-circumstances or clearance override anywhere in the policy, so a purchased put or written call over TPW shares can never be executed under this policy regardless of timing or approval.

topic: hedging and short selling equally absolute
clause: TPW People must not at any time: ... (c) engage in the practice of "short selling" TPW Securities; or (d) enter into any hedging arrangements that limit the TPW Person's economic risk of holding TPW Securities.
why_it_matters: Even if the derivatives ban were somehow avoided by structuring, the collar would independently be a prohibited hedging arrangement, with the same absolute, non-waivable character.

clause: Any TPW Person who enters into margin lending arrangements or otherwise encumbers their TPW Securities (Security Arrangements) is required to provide details of those Security Arrangements to the Company Secretary upon entering into, and on any change ... occurring to, the Security Arrangements.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is not banned - only gated by ordinary dealing clearance and a disclosure obligation - but this is irrelevant given the derivative legs cannot be entered into at all.

clause: a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender unilaterally exercising its rights of sale, for example, under a margin lending arrangement in relation to a margin call (or similar) or default by the TPW Person
why_it_matters: Confirms a bank's enforcement sale on default or margin call would not itself breach the policy, though this is moot while the collar's option legs remain prohibited outright.

topic: front page test governs all discretionary approvals
clause: approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the "front page" test
why_it_matters: Any residual clearance-gated activity connected to a bank-structured product would face a qualitative optics screen in addition to the express prohibitions.

clause: This policy applies to trading in the Company's shares on the ASX ... Restricted Persons ... must restrict their buying and selling of Company's shares.
why_it_matters: Because the policy never defines 'Dealing' or 'Securities' to extend beyond shares themselves, an OTC put/call and a share pledge to a bank are not expressly named or swept in by any definition, so a funded collar sits in a gap this document does not address rather than being either cleared or barred by it.

topic: external Insider Trading Policy not in scope
clause: In addition to the requirements of this General Trading Policy, all Restricted Persons ... must also comply with the Insider Trading Policy of the Company in section 6 of the Corporate Governance Charter.
why_it_matters: The substantive controls on derivatives, hedging, margin lending, encumbrance and secured financing that a typical ASX trading policy contains may instead sit in the externally incorporated Corporate Governance Charter, which is not in this document and must be obtained and reviewed before relying on any 'not_addressed' conclusion here.

clause: give clearance for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) shares in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so
why_it_matters: Even if a collar were otherwise permitted, the only express relief from a prohibited-period restriction is for an outright share sale, not for entering into a put/call or a security interest, so it gives no comfort for executing collar legs during a blackout.

clause: The Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or employees and/or their respective associated parties trading in the Company's shares at any time.
why_it_matters: An ad hoc embargo of unstated duration and confidentiality could freeze entry, roll or unwind of a collar without notice or an available relief route (relief under section 8 is sale-only).

clause: 'associated parties' (being immediate family (including a spouse (or equivalent) or dependent), family company or trust)
why_it_matters: Because associates are limited to immediate family and family entities, a bank-side special purpose vehicle or nominee used to structure the collar would likely fall outside this definition and outside the policy's reach altogether, absent guidance from the external Insider Trading Policy.

topic: financing permitted with clearance, not banned
clause: Designated Persons must not enter into agreements that provide lenders with rights over their interests in securities of the Company without first seeking and obtaining prior written clearance from the Chair.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies with an outright secured-financing ban, IPD permits a loan secured by a pledge of Company securities (the collar's financing leg) with prior written Chair clearance, ongoing collateral-sufficiency assurance, annual disclosure, and an immediate-notice trigger if a forced sale becomes likely.

clause: deal at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or under this policy.
why_it_matters: This standalone express prohibition is not limited to unvested or holding-locked incentive remuneration and has no described clearance pathway of its own, so the put and call legs of an OTC collar over any Company securities (vested or not) appear to be prohibited outright for Designated Persons and their closely related parties.

clause: (lender disposal) a disposal of Company securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights.
why_it_matters: If the bank's security interest becomes enforceable, its exercise and resulting sale of the collateral shares is wholly excluded from the Prohibited Period regime and may occur at any time without breaching the policy, unlike jurisdictions where forced sales during a blackout are a breach.

clause: Designated Persons and their closely related parties (as defined in the Corporations Act) must not ... deal at any time in financial products over or in respect of Company securities.
why_it_matters: The financial-products/hedging ban extends to 'closely related parties' under the Corporations Act definition, a broader class than the glossary 'Associate' definition, so routing collar legs through a related trust or entity does not avoid it.

clause: A confirmation confirms that the proposed dealing by the Designed Person is within the terms of the Trading Policy but does not otherwise constitute approval or endorsement by the Company or the Notification Officer for the proposed dealing.
why_it_matters: Even where a clearance/confirmation is obtained (e.g. for the financing leg under 4.1), the executive remains personally responsible for the transaction and for assessing insider trading risk; the Company's clearance does not indemnify the arrangement.

clause: Notification Officer: [Chief Executive Officer/Chairperson of the Audit & Risk Committee] ... [The Chairperson of the Board] ... [Chief Executive Officer/Chairperson/Company Secretary] ... [Chief Executive Officer/Company Secretary]
why_it_matters: The lodged policy retains unresolved drafting brackets identifying alternative Notification Officers for each tier, so the bank should confirm operationally who the actual approver is for the relevant executive before relying on any clearance timeline.

clause: Employee includes an employee, director (other than a non-executive director), contractor or representative of Perpetual. ... RE Services provides services for the following entities: Perpetual Trust Services Limited; The Trust Company (RE Services) Limited; and The Trust Company (Sydney Airports) Limited (collectively referred to as the ‘Perpetual Entities’).
why_it_matters: This policy regulates personal trading by staff of Perpetual's outsourced Responsible Entity business (the trustee administering the scheme behind OPH), not by OPH's own directors, the fund's investment manager, or its Compliance Committee; a funded collar offered to those actual decision-makers would not be governed by this document, so the bank should confirm whether a separate trading policy applies to them before relying on this analysis.

clause: (none present)
why_it_matters: As an externally managed trust, OPH's own governing document set has no employee equity incentive scheme referenced here, so the unvested/vested-locked/vested-unrestricted distinction central to a funded-collar analysis over incentive equity does not arise on this document; any collar would be over units held outright.

clause: Approval granted pursuant to this Policy is valid for that business day only. Where the RE Services staff member has failed to act on that approval, a new approval must be sought to trade on another business day.
why_it_matters: Even for the one tier that can obtain clearance (RE Services staff), any cleared leg of a collar must be executed the same business day it is approved, so multi-leg execution or a settlement delay would require fresh clearance for each leg.

clause: Redemptions: Position must be held for at least three months.
why_it_matters: If the bank or the executive needed to redeem (rather than sell on-market) units within three months of an RE Services staff member's acquisition, that would breach this minimum holding period; collar and financing tenor for such a counterparty should exceed three months.

clause: securities include all financial instruments including: ... exchange traded and OTC derivatives and contracts for difference (CFD)
why_it_matters: An OTC put/call written with a bank over non-Perpetual securities (which would include OPH units) is squarely within scope of the Policy Principles for all Employees and within the pre-approval regime for RE Services staff, so its treatment does not turn on any separate 'dealing' definition.

clause: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into hedging ... margin lending ... or short-term or speculative trading ... unless ... clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.
why_it_matters: All three collar-relevant activities – the derivative hedge, the security grant for the loan, and any early unwind – are expressly permitted subject only to prior clearance, none is an outright ban, making this one of the more funded-collar-friendly policies reviewed, provided clearance is obtained and the blackout/insider-trading conditions are separately satisfied.

topic: refusal confidentiality duty on the applicant
clause: Any clearance refusal or withdrawal must be kept confidential by the person who sought clearance, and may not be disclosed to anyone.
why_it_matters: Unusually, it is the executive (not the Responsible Entity) who must keep a refusal or withdrawal confidential, so the executive could not explain to the bank counterparty why a scheduled collar leg did not proceed without itself breaching the policy.

clause: EQT Persons may trade in a LIT's Units provided they are not in the possession of Inside Information, the trade does not take place during a Black-out Period, and written prior clearance to trade has been approved.
why_it_matters: Clearance alone cannot authorise trading during a Black-out Period; only the Chair-level 'exceptional circumstances' process (Section 8) can potentially permit that, so collar entry, unwind, roll or settlement should be timed for open windows or a bespoke Chair-level exception sought.

clause: (No exclusion for a lender-exercised or forced disposal appears in Section 7's list of excluded trades.)
why_it_matters: Unlike some peer policies, there is no express exemption if the bank needs to enforce its security and sell the collateral Units during a Black-out Period; absent a bespoke waiver, that sale would need Section 8 exceptional-circumstances clearance from the Chair.

clause: Trade or Trading means to buy, sell or transfer any economic interest in Units, including electing to vary a dividend reinvestment plan ("DRP") participation.
why_it_matters: The substance-based 'any economic interest' test means an OTC derivative referencing the Units, and not just an on-market sale, is treated as a Trade subject to the general blackout/clearance regime in addition to the specific Section 6 hedging clearance.

clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities at any time, including in the exceptional circumstances referred to in section 6, unless the Restricted Person first obtains prior written clearance from [an Approving Officer].
why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies where clearance is only needed for exception trades, every single trade by a Restricted Person requires prior written clearance, valid for 5 business days by default, so both legs of a collar and any later unwind each need a fresh clearance request timed to fall within that window.

clause: A Restricted Person is not permitted to trade in Company Securities unless such trading occurs within a designated Trading Window ... the two-month period commencing on the next trading day following the announcement to ASX of the Company's full year [or half year] financial results.
why_it_matters: DUR restricts ordinary trading to two 2-month windows per year rather than being open by default subject to blackouts; outside those windows, executing or unwinding a collar is only possible via the section 6 exceptional-circumstances clearance route.

topic: unvested equity hedge ban is absolute
clause: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.
why_it_matters: Unlike the general hedging clause (clearable), hedging unvested incentive equity is a non-clearable, outright prohibition, so a collar can only be written once the relevant equity has vested.

clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: If the bank enforces its security and sells the collateral shares, that disposal is expressly excluded from the trading-window restriction (though the insider trading prohibition still applies), giving the bank comfort that its own enforcement will not itself breach the Company's policy even outside a Trading Window.

topic: family transfers excluded from window restriction
clause: transfers of Company Securities between a Restricted Person and their spouse, civil partner, child, step-child, family company, family trust or other close family member ... are excluded from the restrictions outlined in section 5.
why_it_matters: Transfers to a related family vehicle are excluded from the trading-window restriction even though beneficial ownership changes; this could be relevant if part of a collar or financing structure is routed through such a vehicle, though the hedging and secured-lending clearance requirements would still apply on the substance of the arrangement.

clause: Restricted Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.
why_it_matters: The prohibition has no stated time threshold and, unlike hedging or margin lending, no clearance carve-out is mentioned, so confirmation should be sought from the Company Secretary on what tenor and structure would not be regarded as short-term or speculative before finalising collar timing.

clause: This document is Perpetual Limited's internal staff conflicts-of-interest policy governing 'RE Services' personnel trading in securities other than Perpetual's own (i.e. third-party and client-fund securities, which would include Metrics Income Opportunities Trust units). It is not a bespoke director/officer dealing policy issued by or for the Trust or its responsible entity, contains no closed periods, no preclearance system, and no scheme-specific carve-outs.
why_it_matters: There is no clear, dedicated regime addressing whether a director or senior executive connected with the Trust may enter a funded collar over their MOT holding; any restriction would have to be found in the generic insider trading, front running and conflicts prohibitions rather than in tailored dealing rules.

clause: The policy contains no reference to hedging, monetisation, margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing of any securities.
why_it_matters: A funded collar with a bank-secured loan is not restricted by this document at all, so a bank cannot rely on it for comfort that the structure is permitted, only that it is not expressly prohibited.

clause: This policy is issued in the name of Burson Group Limited, which was later renamed Bapcor Limited (ASX: BAP); the ABN and trading windows/mechanics are otherwise unaffected.
why_it_matters: Confirms the document is the correct, applicable policy for BAP notwithstanding the different company name on its face.

clause: a disposal of Burson securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
why_it_matters: Gives the bank confidence that if it enforces its security and sells the collared shares, that disposal is an exempted dealing under the policy (only after-the-fact notice to the Authorising Officer is required), not a breach or a dealing needing fresh consent.

clause: For the avoidance of doubt, the ACL Person seeking authorisation cannot be their own Authorising Officer.
why_it_matters: The bank must identify the correct independent Authorising Officer for the specific director/executive entering the collar; the Chair of the Board, for instance, cannot approve their own collar and must go to the Audit Committee chair.

clause: prior to dealing in ACL securities outside a Blackout Period the person must notify the relevant person in paragraph 4.2(c) (the Authorising Officer) and the Company Secretary, by email, of their proposed dealing and obtain consent to trade from the Authorising Officer
why_it_matters: Both the Authorising Officer and the Company Secretary must be notified before the collar is entered into, adding an extra notification step compared to policies with a single approver.

clause: a disposal of ACL securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
