why_it_matters: Gives the bank confidence that if it enforces its security and sells the collared shares, that disposal is an exempted dealing under the policy (only after-the-fact notice to the Authorising Officer is required), not a breach or a dealing needing fresh consent.

topic: absolute margin loan / secured financing ban
clause: All directors and executives are prohibited from obtaining a margin loan using GWA securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for the loan or entering into any secured financing arrangement in respect of GWA securities.
why_it_matters: This forecloses the loan leg of a funded collar entirely for any director or executive, regardless of vesting status, with no clearance or exceptional-circumstances pathway referenced anywhere in section 4.8.

topic: no vesting carve-out for secured financing
clause: Section 4.8 does not distinguish vested from unvested securities, unlike the hedging ban in 4.7 which is limited to unvested holdings.
why_it_matters: Even fully vested, unrestricted GWA shares cannot be pledged as loan collateral by a director or executive, a materially stricter position than the hedging restriction alone.

clause: a disposal of GWA's securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: This legacy carve-out sits awkwardly with the absolute 4.8 ban on ever entering such an arrangement; a bank should not treat it as confirmation that secured financing over GWA shares is achievable.

clause: Directors are required to notify the Chair of intended trading in GWA securities, by themselves or their associated parties, prior to such intended dealings.
why_it_matters: Even a permitted hedge dealt within the Window Period requires a director to separately notify the Chair beforehand, on top of any Closed Period written approval.

clause: The policy contains no provision on margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, or borrowing against Securities of any kind.
why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, there is no express ban on secured financing, so the loan leg of a funded collar is not itself prohibited by this document; it would only be caught, if at all, as a 'transaction in relation to Securities' requiring the ordinary notification and Closed Period clearance.

clause: The insider trading prohibition extends to dealings by individuals through nominees, agents or other associates, such as family members, family trusts and family companies.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the notification obligations or Closed Period restrictions.

clause: Parties covered by this policy should not procure others to deal during Closed periods.
why_it_matters: A bank counterparty executing hedge trades on the executive's behalf or instruction during a Closed Period could itself be a breach by the executive as 'procuring' a dealing.

clause: Short-term trading is considered to be trading where the acquisition and disposal of Securities occurs within 6 months of each other ... Such a period will be considered a Closed Period.
why_it_matters: A written call that could result in disposal of the underlying shares within 6 months of vesting (acquisition) would breach the short-term trading ban absent a hardship waiver, so collar tenor and any early-exercise risk should be structured to fall outside that 6-month window.

clause: A contravention of this policy by a person to whom this policy applies may result in summary dismissal.
why_it_matters: Breach of the notification, Closed Period or short-term trading rules through collar execution or unwind carries employment consequences beyond the transaction itself.

clause: "TOWER Securities" means ... any other listed securities of TOWER or its subsidiaries, and any listed derivatives ... created by third parties over TOWER's ordinary shares.
why_it_matters: An OTC collar written bilaterally by a bank is arguably not a 'TOWER Security' or 'Restricted Security' under these defined, listed-only terms, so the blackout, trading-window and consent regime may not apply to it on a literal reading; the bank should not rely on this gap, however, given the separate absolute hedging ban and overriding insider trading law.

clause: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions in relation to associated products of TOWER Securities which operate to limit the economic risk of their TOWER Securities.
why_it_matters: This clause is broader than the listed-only definitions and squarely catches an OTC collar; it bars the structure outright for directors and executives with no consent process or hardship exemption analogous to the blackout waiver.

clause: The policy contains no provision on margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, or borrowing against TOWER Securities.
why_it_matters: A share-secured loan is not itself prohibited by this document, but the absolute hedging ban already defeats the collar structure for Restricted Persons regardless of financing terms.

clause: the applicant does not intend to sell the TOWER Securities within 6 months of when they are purchased.
why_it_matters: Even where hedging were permitted, consent to acquire shares is refused unless the holder intends to retain them for 6 months, constraining any short-dated collar unwind on newly purchased shares.

clause: Restricted Persons should ensure that any Restricted Securities trading which is prohibited by this policy is not undertaken by their spouse or partner, immediate family members ... a company or trust over which the Restricted Person has influence or control.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a family trust or controlled entity does not escape the hedging ban, which the Restricted Person must also police against connected persons.

clause: any securities (i.e. shares or options) in the Company, its subsidiaries or related companies.
why_it_matters: The written acknowledgement/clearance gate, and by extension the Prohibited Period regime, textually applies only to shares or options; a bank-written OTC put or call is not itself a 'security' requiring written acknowledgement under section 8, though it is still caught by the absolute hedging ban in section 9 if it operates to hedge Company securities.

clause: any hedging over vested securities must comply with this Policy.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies with a blanket hedging ban, SMI expressly permits hedging of vested shares (subject to the written acknowledgement process and Prohibited Periods), so a collar over vested, unrestricted shares is not banned outright.

clause: The policy contains no provision on margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, or borrowing against Company securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is not independently restricted by this document.

clause: All Restricted Employees have a personal responsibility to ensure that his or her associates comply with the same respective restrictions as apply to them.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a spouse or related private entity does not escape the Prohibited Period or hedging restrictions.

clause: The Policy does apply, however, to any sale of Company Securities acquired on the exercise of options, including sales as part of a broker-assisted cashless exercise of an option, or any other market sale for the purpose of generating the cash needed to pay the exercise price of an option.
why_it_matters: Sales of shares around option exercise (which may coincide with collar entry or unwind) remain subject to the written acknowledgement and Prohibited Period regime even though the exercise itself is typically exempt.

clause: clearance may be given for them to sell (but not to purchase) Company securities when they would otherwise be prohibited from doing so.
why_it_matters: A hardship-based clearance could permit unwinding (selling) collared shares during a Prohibited Period, but could not be used to buy back shares, limiting how a distressed collar unwind involving a repurchase could be executed.

clause: Derivative has the meaning in section 761D of the Corporations Act and includes options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, swaps, caps and collars.
why_it_matters: The very instrument a funded collar comprises is expressly captured as a Security requiring clearance (or banned outright as hedging where unvested or holding-locked), removing any definitional ambiguity.

topic: absolute margin loan and encumbrance ban
clause: No Director, Restricted Employee or Closely Connected Person and Entity may enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities ... or grant lenders any rights over their Company Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is prohibited outright for Directors, Restricted Employees and their connected persons, with no clearance or Exceptional Circumstances route, unlike ordinary Closed Period trading.

clause: Directors and Restricted Employees must not use ... any Derivatives ... which operate to limit the economic risk of holding unvested Company Securities or Company Securities which are subject to holding locks.
why_it_matters: Once shares vest and any holding lock lifts, hedging (and by extension collaring) becomes permissible subject to ordinary clearance and Closed Periods; the fatal blocker to a funded structure is the financing leg, not the derivative itself.

clause: Any decision of the Designated Officer to refuse clearance to Trade is final and binding and must be kept confidential by the Director, Restricted Employee or Closely Connected Person and Entity. The Designated Officer is not required to give reasons should clearance be refused.
why_it_matters: The executive cannot challenge, appeal, or disclose a refusal, so bank-timed collar entry could be blocked without recourse or explanation.

clause: If any Director, Restricted Employee or Closely Connected Person and Entity comes into possession of inside information after receiving a clearance to Trade, they must not Trade despite having received the clearance.
why_it_matters: A cleared derivative leg must be executed within the 21-day validity window and can become unexecutable if inside information arises before signing.

topic: connected persons bound as if Director/Restricted Employee
clause: Directors and Restricted Employees must also take reasonable steps to advise their Closely Connected Persons and Entities of this Policy and procure that they comply with this Policy as if they were a Director or Restricted Employee.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not escape the margin loan ban, hedging ban, or clearance and Closed Period requirements.

clause: Where any clearance to trade approval is required for a trade under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the trade would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even a technically compliant collar clearance request can be refused on a subjective reputational/optics test, adding an unpredictable gate beyond the objective rules.

topic: absolute margin lending and encumbrance ban
clause: enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is barred outright with no exemption route analogous to the short-term trading dispensation or the Black-out Period sale-only relief.

topic: absolute hedging ban regardless of vesting
clause: enter into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Securities.
why_it_matters: Unlike some peer policies, EQT draws no distinction between vested and unvested holdings: a collar (put plus call limiting economic risk) is banned outright at all times for all EQT Persons and Connected Persons, with no clearance or exceptional-circumstances route.

clause: A clearance to trade may be withdrawn or refused by the Approver at their absolute discretion, without giving reasons. The decision is final and binding. If clearance to trade is refused by an Approver, this must be kept confidential.
why_it_matters: There is no appeal and no disclosure right if a collar-related clearance request is refused.

clause: the Securities are not subject to a specific disposal restriction.
why_it_matters: Incentive securities under a separate escrow or holding lock cannot be traded, hedged, or sold even via the hardship exception while that restriction remains in place.

topic: connected persons must clear through the EQT Person
clause: EQT Persons must ensure that their obligations under insider trading laws and this Policy are complied with by their Connected Persons. For the avoidance of doubt, a Connected Person must seek clearance to trade through their EQT Person.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a spouse or controlled entity does not escape the clearance, Black-out Period, hedging or margin lending restrictions.

clause: In addition, stock lending or any other arrangements involving Chalice securities where the lender or other third party is granted a right to sell, or compel the sale of all or part of any Chalice’s securities is prohibited.
why_it_matters: A bank's standard security documentation for a funded collar's loan leg typically grants the lender a right to sell the pledged shares on default; read literally next to the section 12 permission for 'margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements' with clearance, this sentence creates real doubt whether the Approving Officer can lawfully clear a facility that gives the bank an enforcement right of sale.

clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: If the loan is validly cleared, the bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is excluded from the trading policy altogether (not a breach even in a blackout period), though the tension in section 12 above must still be resolved before that facility can be put in place.

clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could the proposed dealing be perceived by the market as taking advantage of my position in an inappropriate way? ... approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the ‘front page’ test.
why_it_matters: Even where a funded collar and its financing are otherwise permissible, the Approving Officer can refuse clearance purely on optics grounds, adding a discretionary layer beyond the structured tests.

clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities at any time ... unless the Restricted Person first obtains prior written clearance
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that require clearance only in closed periods, every leg of the collar (entry, adjustment, unwind) needs a fresh written clearance from the Approving Officer regardless of when it occurs.

clause: Any written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for the period of 3 business days ... Written clearance can be withdrawn by the Approving Officer at any time prior to the order for dealing being lodged or otherwise authorised, if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
why_it_matters: The bank and executive must be ready to execute each collar leg within a 3 business day window, and a cleared trade can still be pulled before execution if circumstances change.

clause: Any Restricted Person who holds Company Securities subject to binding restrictions on transfer (either as ASX restricted securities or through voluntary escrow arrangements) must comply with the terms of any applicable escrow arrangements.
why_it_matters: Shares still under ASX or voluntary escrow cannot be pledged, hedged, or otherwise dealt with for a collar until the escrow ends, regardless of vesting status.

clause: Where this policy requires a Restricted Person to do an act or thing, the relevant Restricted Person must do that act or thing, or procure that the act or thing is done, in respect of the Connected Person.
why_it_matters: Structuring the loan or derivative through a spouse, controlled company, or family trust does not avoid the clearance requirement or the section 12 right-to-sell restriction.

clause: Shares or derivatives issued by Australian Ethical Investment Limited (AEI Securities).
why_it_matters: The policy's core operative rules are framed around 'AEI Securities', defined as shares or derivatives issued by AEI itself; a bank-written OTC put/call is not literally 'issued by' AEI, so there is a real argument the collar derivatives fall outside the policy's scope entirely (leaving only the general insider trading law to apply), though a purposive reading would likely still treat them as regulated trading.

clause: (no provision addresses margin loans, security, charges or secured financing anywhere in the Policy)
why_it_matters: Granting security over vested AEI shares to fund the collar's loan leg is not listed as regulated 'Trading' and is not prohibited, restricted, or subject to any named clearance or disclosure process under this policy.

clause: The Restricted Trading List includes any securities for which Australian Ethical has either received a sounding or has information that is not in the public domain therefore these securities will not be approved for personal trading.
why_it_matters: Even outside a blackout period, approval for the collar could be refused without explanation if AEI shares are confidentially placed on the Restricted Trading List at the time of the request.

clause: Where approval is granted, directors, independent committee members, employees and contractors must immediately notify, and in any event not more than 1 business day after the trade occurs, the Company Secretary (via email) of any dealings in AEI Securities.
why_it_matters: Each leg of the collar (entry, adjustment, unwind) must be reported to the Company Secretary within 1 business day of execution.

clause: Employees (and their close family/related persons where there is direct or indirect control over investment decisions or employee holds a beneficial interest) ... must seek approval
why_it_matters: Routing the collar through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the approval requirement.

clause: You are not permitted to enter into a margin loan or other financing arrangement where there is a risk that Cooper Energy Securities will be traded pursuant to the terms of the margin loan or financing arrangement (together a Margin Loan), unless you have obtained prior written consent of the Chairman.
why_it_matters: Although styled around 'Margin Loans', this sweeps in any financing arrangement carrying a risk that the pledged shares will be sold under its terms, so the bank's loan secured on the collared shares needs the Chairman's prior written consent regardless of how the facility is labelled.

clause: the right of the lender to sell the Securities unilaterally
why_it_matters: The Chairman must be told upfront that the bank has a unilateral enforcement right to sell the collared shares on default, and the policy gives no criteria constraining refusal, so consent is fully discretionary.

clause: If you are the Chairman and you intend to enter into a Margin Loan, you must obtain the prior written consent of two of the other directors or the Board to enter into the Margin Loan and disclose to those directors or the Board (as applicable) the Loan Information.
why_it_matters: If the Chairman is the executive seeking the collar financing, approval escalates to two other directors or the full Board rather than a single approver.

clause: that they are not hedging the risk of any fluctuation in value of any unvested entitlement in Cooper Energy Securities
why_it_matters: The standard pre-dealing confirmation for KMP/CCPE/Other Designated Persons only requires disclaiming hedging of unvested entitlements, supporting that a collar over vested shares is contemplated as permissible subject to ordinary consent.

clause: Options in the Company may be exercised at any time in accordance with their terms of issue (including during a Closed Period) subject to the insider trading prohibition. Any subsequent sale of Securities issued on exercise of options will be subject to the terms of this Policy.
why_it_matters: Vesting/exercise of underlying options is not itself blocked by a Closed Period, but the shares delivered on exercise (and any collar transaction over them) remain subject to the ordinary consent and Closed Period regime.

clause: Personnel in all circumstances are also prohibited from entering into any agreement that provides lenders with rights over their interests in Securities.
why_it_matters: This is an absolute ban, with no clearance route or exemption authority, applying to every tier of Personnel regardless of vesting status; the loan leg of a funded collar necessarily gives the bank a security right over the collared shares and is therefore prohibited outright.

clause: a disposal of securities of the entity that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: This carve-out from the general trading restrictions presupposes a secured lending arrangement can validly exist, which is inconsistent with the outright ban on granting lenders rights over Securities; it appears to be inherited boilerplate rather than a genuine exception, and should not be relied on to structure a facility.

clause: Senior Management and Directors ... are prohibited from dealing in JMS Securities without providing the Chief Executive Officer (and the Chairman in the case of the Chief Executive Officer) with prior written notice of their intent to deal in JMS Securities.
why_it_matters: For the derivative legs (if the encumbrance ban were somehow not engaged), the regime is a notice-and-confirm procedure rather than a discretionary approval, so there is no named right of refusal for the CEO/Chairman beyond the Trading Window and MNPI constraints.

clause: No trading in JMS Securities may occur outside of these Trading Windows (Closed Periods) without the permission of the Chairman.
why_it_matters: Directors and Senior Executives can only deal (including entering derivative legs) during four discrete 4-week windows a year tied to results, the AGM, and offer periods, materially compressing available execution dates.

clause: EOL Staff (including Connected Parties) are not permitted to undertake any short-term, short selling, speculative, hedge or derivative type trading in Company securities.
why_it_matters: This is an outright, unqualified ban on all derivative and hedge transactions in EOL securities for every EOL Staff member and Connected Party, with no clearance route and no vesting-state carve-out; both legs of an OTC collar (the purchased put and the written call) are 'derivative type trading' and 'hedge ... trading', so the collar structure itself cannot be entered into, regardless of how the loan leg is treated.

clause: EOL Staff must not enter into agreements that provide lenders with rights over their interests in securities in the Company without first seeking and obtaining prior written approval from the Chairman.
why_it_matters: The loan/security leg alone (e.g. a conventional margin loan on unencumbered vested shares) is not banned and can be approved by the Chairman, confirming that the blocker is specifically the derivative/hedge ban rather than secured lending as such.

clause: Any clearance to trade: May be granted, refused or withdrawn at the sole discretion of EOL and without further explanation; Is final and binding on the person requesting the clearance; Must be kept confidential by the person seeking clearance and not disclosed to anyone.
why_it_matters: Even for the permissible financing leg, any approval obtained can be withdrawn without reasons and must be kept secret by the executive, limiting the ability to coordinate openly with the bank about clearance status.

clause: For the purposes of this Share Trading Policy the Executive Leadership Team will have the same obligations in terms of this policy as KMP (even though the respective ELT member may not be KMP from a financial reporting perspective.
why_it_matters: The heightened Chairman pre-approval and scrutiny regime for KMP extends to the whole Executive Leadership Team, broadening the population facing the strictest process (though this does not affect the outright derivative/hedge ban, which applies to all EOL Staff regardless).

clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights).
why_it_matters: Unlike the margin lending provisions, section 1.10 provides no Board consent or exceptional-circumstances route, so the put and call legs of a funded collar cannot be cleared under any circumstance.

clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any clearance granted in accordance with this section 1.11 conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, in regards to the circumstances in which the securities in the Company may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: Even a plain loan secured on the shares (without derivatives) is subject to bespoke Board-imposed conditions on when the bank may force-sell collateral, potentially constraining standard default remedies.

clause: The Chairperson may not give clearance under the exception in section 1.8 if there is a matter about which there is inside information in relation to securities in the Company ... when the Restricted Person requests clearance or proposes to deal.
why_it_matters: A hardship-driven unwind of any collar-adjacent position can only be effected as a sale, never a repurchase, and is unavailable whenever inside information exists.

clause: The Board has absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their respective associated parties trading in the Company's securities at any time.
why_it_matters: An unannounced Board embargo could block entry, roll or unwind of a collar-related transaction at any time, independent of the scheduled blackout window.

clause: Each Restricted Person has a personal responsibility to ensure that his or her 'associated parties' (being immediate family (including a spouse (or equivalent) or dependent), family company or trust) complies with the same respective restrictions as applied to Restricted Persons.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or family company does not avoid the hedging ban or the margin-loan consent requirement.

clause: Restricted Persons are required to notify the Company of intended dealings in the Company's securities, by themselves or their associated parties, prior to such intended dealings.
why_it_matters: Even outside a scheduled blackout, any dealing connected to a collar (such as the loan itself, or an unwind) must be pre-notified to the Company Secretary and Chairperson.

clause: Designated Persons may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.
why_it_matters: The margin loan/secured-financing ban applies to 'Designated Persons', a term never defined in clause 2; on the safer reading it covers all Company Officers, meaning the loan leg of a funded collar secured on the shares is prohibited outright with no clearance route.

clause: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars)
why_it_matters: The Policy expressly names 'collars' as a regulated Derivative, so a bank-funded equity collar is unambiguously subject to clause 7.2's vesting-based prohibition/permission regime.

clause: The processes for notification of an intention to Deal in Company Securities ... do not provide for [approval by] the Approval Officer. At all times, the person intending to Deal in Company Securities is personally responsible for any decision to Deal and compliance with this Policy and the law.
why_it_matters: Even when the derivative and disposal legs are permitted over vested, unrestricted shares, the Approval Officer's confirmation is not a substantive sign-off, so compliance risk for the collar structure remains entirely with the individual.

clause: Buy or sell orders for Company Securities which are placed but not completed outside of a Black-out Period ... the order must be completed within 5 trading days otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
why_it_matters: A collar leg or unwind order placed just before a Black-out Period begins must complete within 5 trading days or lapse, and cannot be resized or repriced once inside the blackout.

clause: At any time on an ad hoc basis by direction of the Approval Officer and/or a majority of directors, the Dealing of Company securities may be restricted. The restriction of Dealing is not necessarily required to be communicated to Company Officers.
why_it_matters: An undisclosed ad hoc trading restriction could block collar entry, roll or unwind without notice to the executive.

clause: disposal of securities by a secured lender under a loan agreement secured by the securities
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is excluded from the policy altogether, so it is not restricted by prohibited periods or subject to any approval requirement — materially more favourable than most ASX trading policies.

clause: Where a KMP has entered into an agreement where Company securities are held as collateral for a loan facility, the KMP must notify the Chairman ... in order that the Board can ascertain whether the arrangement is material and if so, the Company will disclose the key terms of the arrangement to the market.
why_it_matters: Entering the secured loan leg of a funded collar requires no prior clearance at all, only post-entry notification for a materiality assessment, which could nonetheless result in the collar's key financing terms being disclosed to the market.

topic: hedging approval equated to trading approval
clause: Any KMP seeking to enter a transaction or arrangement to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company must obtain approval in the same way as if they traded in the underlying securities direct.
why_it_matters: The put/call overlay of a collar is treated identically to an ordinary share trade for approval purposes (same approval group, five-trading-day validity), not subject to any separate or stricter hedging regime.

clause: The Company prohibits hedging of any unvested securities.
why_it_matters: A collar cannot be written over unvested equity incentive holdings, but faces no hedging-specific restriction (beyond ordinary trade approval) once vested.

clause: Any trades resulting from approval must be immediately reported by the KMP to the approval group.
why_it_matters: Execution of any collar leg or unwind must be reported immediately to the Chairman/Managing Director/Company Secretary group.

clause: Designated Officers are prohibited from entering into arrangements giving a third party the right to require them to sell Company Securities (eg, margin loans).
why_it_matters: The ban is framed functionally around any arrangement giving a third party a forced-sale right, not just formally labelled margin loans, so a bank loan secured on the collared shares with standard enforcement or margin-call rights would likely be caught outright for Designated Officers, with no clearance or exemption route.

clause: Securities includes shares, units, options, rights and other interests considered to be securities for the purposes of the Australian Corporations Act.
why_it_matters: The defined term 'Securities' may not clearly extend to an OTC put/call referencing the shares; outside the section 8 unvested-incentive-scheme hedging ban, the Policy does not expressly regulate derivatives over vested shares, though a Designated Officer would still be expected to seek approval under the general 'deal' definition and Blackout Period regime.

clause: approval is to be granted or withheld as a matter of absolute discretion and without reason ... if approval is refused, the relevant Designated Officer (and their Connected Persons) must keep that information confidential.
why_it_matters: Approval for the derivative or dealing leg of a collar can be refused without reasons, must be kept confidential if refused, and can be withdrawn even after being granted if circumstances change.

clause: Following approval, Designated Officers (or their relevant Connected Persons) must undertake the proposed dealing within five business days or as otherwise notified by the person providing such approval.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar trade must be executed within five business days of approval or a fresh approval is required, tightening the window available to lock in pricing.

clause: Connected Person means ... an immediate family member ... a company, trust or other entity ... controlled by the Designated Officer ... [or] the trustee of a trust ... of which the Designated Officer ... is a beneficiary.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family member, family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the Blackout Period, approval or margin-loan prohibitions, which extend expressly to Connected Persons.

clause: If a Designated Officer obtains a substantial shareholding in the Company's Securities by virtue of any dealing (more than 5% of the Company's issued capital), the Designated Officer must also notify the ASX within two business days of the change.
why_it_matters: Unwinding or settling a large collar position that moves a Designated Officer across the 5% substantial-holder threshold triggers a separate ASX notification obligation.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the approver does not consider that the dealing would satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even a technically compliant collar and loan structure can be refused clearance on a subjective reputational test, with no right to reasons if refused.

clause: Short term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 6 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
why_it_matters: The Policy expressly cites forward contracts as an example of banned 'short term dealing'; a bank collar structured via forward-type OTC derivatives risks being characterised as prohibited short-term or speculative dealing regardless of its stated tenor.

clause: A Restricted Person must not be party to a margin loan facility that gives the lender the right in specified circumstances to dispose of shares in the Company held by or on behalf of the Restricted Person.
why_it_matters: This newly added clause (December 2025) targets the lender's contractual right to dispose of pledged shares; a standard bank loan secured on the collared shares with customary enforcement/margin-call rights would squarely breach it, with no exemption or clearance route stated.

clause: The Restricted Person is not entitled to receive any reasons for why the dealing request has been denied. If approval is denied, the Restricted Person must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: A refused clearance for the collar's derivative leg comes with no explanation and cannot be discussed, complicating any attempt to restructure and reapply.

clause: They must not structure arrangements or procure third parties to deal in securities of the Company to circumvent the operation of this Policy.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through an associate, intermediary or synthetic wrapper to avoid the margin loan ban or clearance requirement is expressly prohibited.

clause: Prohibited Period means all times outside of the periods mentioned in paragraph 7.1 ... In order to obtain prior written clearance ... in accordance with sections 7.1 or 7.2 of this Policy.
why_it_matters: Internal cross-references still point to superseded section numbers (7.1/7.2) rather than the current sections 9 and 10, an artefact of the December 2025 renumbering when clause 16 was inserted; the intended meaning is clear from context but the drafting is imprecise.

clause: Restricted Persons must not, without the prior written consent of a Designated Officer: (a) enter into any margin loan arrangements ...; (b) use the Company's Securities as collateral ... or grant or permit to exist any encumbrance ...; or (c) engage in any lending arrangements in respect of the Company's Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is not banned outright but needs prior written Designated Officer consent, with no stated criteria constraining refusal, so the bank's security interest is contingent on discretionary approval rather than a policy right.

clause: Deal means any transaction associated with subscribing for, buying, selling, transferring, disposing or converting a Security.
why_it_matters: Moving the collared shares into a custodian, margin or pledge account is itself a Dealing (a 'transfer'), requiring the same prior clearance as the derivative and loan legs and subject to the Open/Closed Period timing restrictions.

clause: A Manager may only Deal in the Company's Securities during the following 'Open Periods' [post-AGM, post-half-year, post-final results, post-31 March quarterly report, post-disclosure document, or Board-determined].
why_it_matters: For Directors and senior executives (the most likely collar counterparties), collar entry, unwind, roll or restructuring is confined to a handful of 4-6 week windows a year rather than any time outside a blackout, materially constraining execution timing.

clause: Approvals once granted are valid for ten (10) Trading Days, unless otherwise notified by the applicable Designated Officer.
why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the collar and loan documentation must be completed within the 10 Trading Day clearance window or fresh clearance must be sought.

clause: if the Restricted Person is a Director they will resign immediately from the Board ... or if the Restricted Person is an Employee they will resign immediately from the Company ... without any claim ... other than for unpaid but due fees or salary.
why_it_matters: A second failure to obtain clearance for the collar, loan or any transfer step carries automatic forced resignation/termination, so execution and documentation discipline around this Policy's consent steps is a material counterparty risk for the bank.

clause: a Restricted Person must not directly or indirectly, enter into, trade in, acquire, dispose of, vary or otherwise deal in any Litigation Event Contract ... regardless of whether the relevant litigation ... involves the Company.
why_it_matters: This absolute, non-waivable ban is confined to contracts referencing litigation outcomes, not price-referenced equity derivatives, so a standard OBL-share collar is not itself a Litigation Event Contract, but it shows the Board is willing to hard-ban derivative-like products outright with no consent route.

clause: Designated Persons are not permitted to deal at any time in financial products designed to track, hedge or in any other way take a position associated with the future value of the Company's Securities (including options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over the Company's Securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions) if such dealings would breach applicable laws.
why_it_matters: A funded collar (put and call) with a bank is squarely a 'financial product issued over the Company's Securities by third parties such as banks' under 4.1, which is only prohibited if it independently breaches insider trading, market rigging or misleading conduct laws; there is no separate clearance, black-out or notification gate on the derivative legs themselves.

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested plan securities
clause: Designated Persons must not enter into a transaction or arrangement or otherwise deal in financial products which operate to limit the economic risk of the unvested Company Securities issued under a Plan.
why_it_matters: The absolute hedging ban only reaches unvested Plan securities, so a collar over vested Plan shares or ordinary on-market shares is not caught by this clause and falls back to the more permissive conditional rule in 4.1.

clause: The Policy contains no clause addressing margin lending, encumbrance, collateral or any other secured financing arrangement in respect of Company Securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, has no express policy bar, clearance requirement or notification obligation under this document, though it predates the hedging/derivatives drafting common in more recent ASX policies and the bank should confirm no newer version has since been adopted.

topic: black-out and notification for the share leg
clause: Directors and Designated Persons must submit a request in the form of Schedule 3 ... Any approval given will be valid for seven days.
why_it_matters: If the structure requires the executive to deal directly in BFG shares or options (e.g. delivering shares against the loan or into a custody arrangement), that dealing needs prior written notification and Authorisation Officer approval valid for only 7 days, and cannot occur in the two annual black-out periods absent a hardship-based sale approval.

clause: Approved by the Board on 26 October 2010.
why_it_matters: This is a 2010 policy predating common ASX hedging and derivatives drafting; the bank should check BFG's current website version before relying on the permissive 4.1 analysis.

topic: OTC derivative falls outside Securities definition
clause: Scentre Group Securities means (collectively) ... any Financial Products issued over or in respect of the above securities which are able to be traded on a financial market.
why_it_matters: A bespoke, bilateral OTC put/call written by a bank is not 'able to be traded on a financial market', so it falls outside 'Scentre Group Securities' and the general blackout/clearance regime in sections 3-9 does not apply to entering it; only the free-standing 11(d) short-term ban and the statutory Insider Trading Prohibition still apply.

topic: secured financing carved out of margin lending ban
clause: The above restriction includes all arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements but does not extend to other types of loan arrangements which may be secured by a security interest granted in respect of Scentre Group Securities ... they should obtain the prior approval of the Company Secretary.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, if structured as a bespoke secured facility rather than a margin loan, is expressly permitted subject only to prior Company Secretary approval, not the outright ban in 11(a).

topic: secured lender enforcement excluded from blackout
clause: a disposal of Scentre Group Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights. For the avoidance of doubt, in relation to Key Management Personnel, this does not extend to the exercise by a lender of rights under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: If the bank's facility is not a margin loan, its enforcement sale of the collared shares during a blackout period is excluded from the trading restriction, giving a workable enforcement path even in a closed period; this protection would not apply if the facility were characterised as a margin loan for a KMP.

topic: short-term ban reaches OTC derivatives regardless
clause: Restricted Persons must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in Scentre Group Securities or in derivative or other Financial Products issued over or in respect of Scentre Group Securities. Short-term means in less than a 3-month period.
why_it_matters: Because this prohibition names 'Financial Products' rather than 'Scentre Group Securities', it catches the OTC collar even though the collar itself sits outside the Securities definition, so collar tenor should exceed three months and the underlying shares should already be held for 3+ months.

topic: excluded trading list limited to blackout
clause: The following dealings are excluded from the trading restrictions in sections 3 and 4
why_it_matters: The standard carve-outs (trading plans, super fund transfers, rights issues, DRPs, etc.) excuse only blackout-period trading; none of them excuses the section 11 margin lending, short selling or short-term/speculative bans, so the collar cannot rely on these exclusions to escape section 11.

topic: hedging substance is in an external policy
clause: These prohibitions are outlined in the Group's Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy.
why_it_matters: The operative hedging prohibition for unvested and holding-locked/deferred incentive awards is not set out in this document; the bank must obtain and review that separate policy before structuring a collar touching any unvested or locked incentive securities.

clause: Although the Board may introduce restrictions in the future, there is no restrictions on: (a) Restricted Persons entering into hedging arrangements
why_it_matters: An equity collar (purchased put and written call) over the Restricted Person's Propel shares is a hedging arrangement expressly unrestricted under the current Policy, subject only to the overriding Inside Information ban; the Board's express reservation of a future right to restrict hedging means the bank should obtain fresh confirmation for each transaction and consider a policy-change trigger in its documentation.

clause: there is no restrictions on: ... (b) Restricted Persons including his or her securities in the Company in margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities of the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, faces no policy-based bar since margin lending and related secured dealing in Company securities is expressly unrestricted; again this is the Board's current position only and could change.

topic: notification scope unclear for hedge/loan legs
clause: Restricted Persons are required to notify the Company of intended dealings in the Company's securities ... prior to such intended dealings.
why_it_matters: It is unclear whether entering the collar or margin/secured loan itself (as opposed to any on-market dealing in the underlying shares) falls within the notification duty, given clause 1.9 treats hedging and margin lending as outside the Policy's restrictions; the bank should seek written confirmation from the Company Secretary or Chairperson on whether notification is expected.

clause: The Policy contains no clause restricting short-term or speculative dealing.
why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX trading policies, there is no minimum holding period or tenor restriction that would constrain how quickly a collar could be entered, unwound or rolled.

topic: absolute derivatives/hedging ban with no waiver route
clause: Employees must not engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements that limit the economic risk related to holdings in the Company's securities or other unvested entitlements under an Employee incentive scheme. For the purposes of this Policy, this prohibition applies to any contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: This is an absolute, universal ban on entering any derivative (including an OTC put/call collar) over the Company's securities, covering Directors, KMP and all Employees, over both vested and unvested holdings, with no cross-reference to the section 5 Exceptional Circumstances relief that the short-term trading rule expressly has, so there is no policy-based approval route to write or buy the collar's derivative legs.

topic: secured financing expressly permitted for Designated Employees
clause: Designated Employees may enter into secured financing agreements where Company securities are used as security over that finance.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a facility secured by a pledge over the shares is expressly contemplated and permitted for Designated Employees with prior approval, but this is only useful for an unhedged securities-backed loan, since the derivative overlay that would make it a collar remains absolutely banned.

clause: ensure that any secured financing agreement: is subject to, and does not fetter or impact, the Board's powers within any claw back or malus policy ... and the Employee makes provisions for alternative funding to meet a call for collateral should the Board exercise any powers within any claw back or malus policy over securities
why_it_matters: Any secured facility must preserve the Board's clawback/malus rights over incentive securities, and the executive must independently fund any resulting collateral shortfall, so the bank cannot treat clawback-eligible shares as unencumbered security.

topic: no voluntary disposal to meet a call in a closed period
clause: ensure that they do not dispose of Company securities to meet a call for collateral on a secured financing agreement whilst in possession of inside information or during a Closed Period
why_it_matters: If a collateral call arises during a Closed Period or while the executive holds inside information, the executive personally cannot sell the pledged shares to meet it; only a genuinely non-consensual financier-enforced sale is excluded from the Policy's restrictions.

clause: Once a relevant approver has provided approval for a Designated Employee to enter into a secured financing agreement, such approval cannot be revoked on the use of those securities for that purpose.
why_it_matters: Gives the bank comfort that approval for the secured facility, once given, cannot later be revoked as to the securities already pledged, though the approver can refuse any further/future use of securities.

clause: The Company Secretary will maintain a record of any secured financing agreement entered into by a Designated Employee and the Board may, in respect of such agreements entered into by Directors of the Company, make those details available publicly.
why_it_matters: A Director's secured financing arrangement with the bank may be made public at the Board's discretion, which should be factored into the parties' confidentiality expectations.

clause: Applicable Personnel are prohibited from entering into lending (including margin lending), borrowing or other secured financing arrangements in respect of the Company's securities, without approval of the Company (pursuant to clause 5.1).
why_it_matters: Unlike an outright ban, the loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is structurally available here provided the Chairman/Board approves it, is entered outside a Closed Period, and the executive holds no inside information.

clause: Applicable Personnel are prohibited from trading ... during Closed Periods; and ... without approval of the Company ... in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: The put and call legs of an OTC collar are expressly dealt with as approvable financial products rather than banned outright, so both legs and the loan can in principle be approved together as one transaction.

clause: Applicable Personnel must not, except in exceptional circumstances, deal in securities or derivatives of the Company during the following periods ...
why_it_matters: The Closed Period ban expressly extends to derivatives, and the financial-hardship/exceptional-circumstances exemption in 5.5-5.8 is worded only for 'sell or otherwise dispose' of securities, so it is unclear whether an exemption route exists to enter or unwind a collar (as opposed to a share sale) inside a Closed Period; entry/unwind should be scheduled in an open window to avoid the point being tested.

clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company securities (i.e. a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume of the shares of the Company on the ASX for the preceding 20 trading days) by an Applicable Personnel needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale
why_it_matters: Physical settlement or a lender's sale on default that exceeds 10% of 20-day ADV triggers a mandatory prior discussion with the Board and legal advisers, which should be factored into unwind/settlement mechanics and timing.

topic: no financing carve-out for closed period forced sale
clause: Applicable Personnel are prohibited from entering into lending (including margin lending), borrowing or other secured financing arrangements in respect of the Company's securities, without approval of the Company.
why_it_matters: The policy is silent on what happens if a lender needs to force a sale during a Closed Period (e.g. on a margin call or collar breach); this is a gap the bank's facility documentation should address contractually since the policy gives no exemption route for a third party's enforcement sale.

clause: The Company may at its discretion vary this rule in relation to a particular Closed Period by general announcement to Applicable Personnel either before or during the Closed Periods.
why_it_matters: Trading windows for collar entry, adjustment or unwind are not fixed with certainty and can be varied by Company announcement, adding scheduling risk.

clause: if any Applicable Personnel is in possession of price sensitive information which is not generally available to the market, then he or she must not deal in the Company's securities at any time it is in possession of such information
why_it_matters: Approval to enter or unwind the collar can be granted but becomes unusable if the executive holds undisclosed price-sensitive information at the intended execution time, regardless of window or clearance status.

topic: encumbrance and margin lending permitted with clearance
clause: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on Units is not banned outright; it is structurally available subject to prior written clearance from the Company Secretary, unlike policies with an absolute secured-financing prohibition.

clause: A clearance to trade is valid for five (5) business days.
why_it_matters: The collar (put, call and any encumbrance) would need to be priced and executed within 5 business days of clearance being granted, which is tight for negotiating bank documentation and may require re-clearance if timing slips.

topic: clearance refusal is unreasoned and final
clause: A clearance to trade can be given, withdrawn, or refused without a reason being given. The decision is final and binding.
why_it_matters: The Company Secretary has unfettered, unreviewable discretion to refuse or withdraw clearance for the collar or loan, and any refusal must be kept confidential by the applicant, so approval cannot be assumed or appealed.

clause: Any clearance to trade is not an endorsement of the proposed trade and that the person doing the trading is individually responsible for their investment decisions and compliance with insider trading laws.
why_it_matters: Obtaining clearance does not shift insider trading risk to the Responsible Entity; the executive and the bank must independently confirm no Inside Information exists at signing and settlement.

clause: In the event that any of the Black-out Periods specified in clauses i, ii, or iii above apply concurrently, the Black-out Period specified in clause iii will apply.
why_it_matters: PDS/prospectus-related Black-out Periods (up to 28 days before lodgement) can override and extend the standard half-year/year-end windows, adding scheduling uncertainty for collar entry or unwind.

clause: Where the Responsible Entity undertakes a buy-back of units in a LIT, the EQT Persons who have knowledge of the buy-back and are involved in the day to day management of the buy-back, are subject to a further Black-out Period.
why_it_matters: An executive involved in a unit buy-back faces an additional, deal-specific trading freeze beyond the standard calendar windows.

topic: narrow trade definition excludes derivatives and financing
clause: In this policy, "trade" includes buying or selling listed securities or agreeing to do so, whether as principal or agent.
why_it_matters: Because 'trade' is confined to buying/selling the shares themselves, an OTC put, written call and a loan secured on the collared shares are not named and are not swept in by this definition, so the policy as drafted does not restrict entry into a funded collar; general insider trading law still applies regardless of the policy's silence.

clause: you must, in writing: (a) notify the Commercial Manager of your intention to trade Gentrack shares and seek consent to do so ... A consent is only valid for a period of ten trading days after notification.
why_it_matters: If the collar's written call is physically settled by delivering shares to the bank, that delivery is a 'sale' and therefore a trade requiring prior notice, consent (valid only 10 trading days), confirmation of no material information, and avoidance of blackout periods; cash settlement would avoid this.

topic: no safe period with material information
clause: There are no "safe" periods for trading in Gentrack shares. You may never trade in Gentrack shares if you have material information -- even if you are not in a blackout period.
why_it_matters: Even outside a blackout period and with consent obtained, any share delivery/settlement under the collar cannot proceed if the executive holds material information at that time.

clause: Persons who leave Gentrack will remain subject to this policy, and will be deemed to remain subject to this policy for a period of six months after their date of departure.
why_it_matters: If the executive departs while the collar or loan is still outstanding, the policy's trading-related restrictions (though not the financing/derivative legs themselves, which are unaddressed) continue to apply to any share delivery for six months post-departure.

clause: Gentrack may monitor the trading of directors, employees and advisers as part of the administration of this policy.
why_it_matters: Gentrack may become aware of collar-related share deliveries or off-market transfers through its own trading surveillance even though the policy does not require pre-clearance for the derivative or loan legs themselves.

topic: secured financing conditional on ASX disclosure
clause: Any approval for a Director, officer or Designated Officer to enter into a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement in respect of the Company's securities is in the absolute discretion of the designated approver and may be subject to the condition that the Company be permitted to disclose to the ASX the existence of the margin loan or secured financing arrangement, and where the Company considers appropriate, any relevant terms such as the trigger points or the right of the financier to sell unilaterally.
why_it_matters: Approving the loan leg of a funded collar may come bundled with a condition that the bank's security, LVR trigger points and unilateral sale rights be disclosed to ASX, which the executive and bank should anticipate in structuring and negotiating confidentiality.

clause: an involuntary disposal of Company securities that results from a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under the arrangement
why_it_matters: A forced sale by the bank on default or margin call is excluded from paragraph 2 (including blackout periods), so enforcement is not itself a breach, though the underlying insider trading prohibition still applies regardless of any exclusion or approval.

topic: hedging approval applies to all Relevant Persons
clause: Hedging of Company securities by a Relevant Person is subject to the following overriding prohibitions ... Relevant Persons are permitted to hedge Company securities on the following conditions.
why_it_matters: Unlike ordinary dealing (where non-Designated Employees need no pre-approval), hedging via a collar requires prior written approval from the designated approver regardless of tier, so no Relevant Person can enter a collar without clearance.

clause: Company securities must never be hedged prior to the vesting of those Company securities; and Company securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee incentive plan operated by the Company.
why_it_matters: The collar can only be written over shares that have both vested and cleared any plan holding lock; these are absolute prohibitions with no approval override.

clause: Upon receipt of approval, a director, officer or Designated Officer must undertake the proposed dealing within 10 business days (or such other period agreed by the designated approver). If the dealing is not undertaken within this time, the approval will no longer have effect and new approval will be required.
why_it_matters: The put, call and secured loan must all be executed within 10 business days of approval (or an agreed longer period), requiring the bank's documentation to be ready before applying for clearance.

topic: approval is discretionary and refusal confidential
clause: Any approval for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities: is in the absolute discretion of the designated approver and can be refused without giving any reasons ... If approval is refused, the person seeking the approval must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: There is no right to reasons or appeal if the collar or loan is refused, and the executive cannot disclose a refusal, which affects how the bank should sequence term sheet negotiation around the approval process.

clause: you are prohibited from purchasing or using, directly or indirectly, financial instruments (e.g., swaps, collars, forward contracts, etc.) that are designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market value of AVITA Medical securities, including both vested and unvested securities.
why_it_matters: The exact product the bank wants to offer -- a collar -- is named and banned outright for every person covered by the Policy and for both vested and unvested holdings, with no clearance route, waiver, or exception anywhere in the document.

topic: no exceptions to MNPI trading ban
clause: There are no exceptions to this general prohibition. Small transactions and transactions that may be necessary or justifiable for an independent reason (e.g., raising money for a charity or an emergency) are not excepted.
why_it_matters: Even if the hedging ban were somehow structured around, there is no hardship or emergency-funding exception available to justify entering a collar or loan while holding material non-public information.

clause: For the avoidance of doubt, no person covered by this Policy is permitted to trade or otherwise conduct transactions in AVITA Medical securities outside of the designated open window periods.
why_it_matters: Even setting the hedging ban aside, entry, adjustment or unwind of any structure would need to occur inside one of the quarterly open windows, and AVITA Medical can unilaterally shorten, modify or cancel a window at any time for any reason.

topic: forced sale risk while holding MNPI
clause: If your AVITA Medical securities are held in a margin account or pledged as collateral, they may be sold without your consent under certain circumstances. As a result, a margin or foreclosure sale of AVITA Medical securities could occur when you are otherwise in possession of material non-public information.
why_it_matters: The Policy itself flags that a lender's enforcement sale on the pledged shares could occur at a moment when the executive holds material non-public information or is otherwise outside an open window, which is precisely why pre-clearance is required before entering the arrangement at all.

clause: The General Counsel is responsible for administering this Policy and all determinations and interpretations of this Policy by the General Counsel are final and not subject to further review.
why_it_matters: There is no appeal from a General Counsel refusal of pre-clearance for the margin/pledging leg, and separately no override exists for the hedging ban regardless of General Counsel's view.

clause: a Designated Officer may only deal in Company Securities ... during the following periods ... Periods other than those stipulated in paragraph 7.1b are closed periods when clearance to deal will generally not be given
why_it_matters: The policy is structured as a whitelist of three narrow 4-week open windows (post half-year results, post full-year results, post AGM) rather than a blacklist, so a collar's entry, roll and unwind must all be scheduled inside these windows or a Board-declared additional period.

clause: Any breach of this prohibition will also constitute a breach of the conditions of grant and would result in the forfeiture of the relevant shares, options or performance rights.
why_it_matters: Hedging unvested equity does not merely breach the policy but automatically forfeits the grant, so a collar must not be written until full vesting is confirmed.

clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any consent granted conditional upon such terms and conditions as it sees fit.
why_it_matters: The Approving Officer can attach bespoke conditions (e.g. LVR caps, lender identity, disclosure) to consent for the loan leg of a funded collar, so terms should be pre-cleared with the Company before documentation is finalised.

clause: otherwise deal in Company Securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: Unlike policies with a broad 'any secured financing arrangement' prohibition, this policy only reaches arrangements fitting 'margin lending', leaving genuine ambiguity as to whether a collar-secured bank loan needs consent at all, though prudent practice is to seek it by analogy.

clause: if the value of the securities is more than 1% of the issued capital of the Company
why_it_matters: Only relevant if the collar counterparty is a senior Team Member rather than a Designated Officer; below the 1% threshold no consent is required at all for margin/secured lending.

clause: "deal in securities" means apply for, buy or sell shares, options or other securities in the Company, or enter into transactions in relation to shares, options or other securities in the Company.
why_it_matters: This 2010-era policy never mentions derivatives, hedging, margin lending, secured financing or collateral by name, so a funded collar and its loan leg would be regulated, if at all, only through this single broad 'transaction in relation to' phrase, leaving real interpretive uncertainty over the financing leg.

clause: Key Management Personnel should wait at least 24 hours after the relevant release before dealing in securities so that the market has had time to absorb the information.
why_it_matters: Non-binding ('should') but relevant to timing the collar's entry immediately after results are released, on top of the formal closed period ending at release.

clause: Key Management Personnel should consider this policy to be binding on them in the absence of specific exemption by the Board.
why_it_matters: Suggests the Board could grant a bespoke exemption to facilitate a collar structure, though no process is specified.

clause: Key Management Personnel "dealing" includes associates of Key Management Personnel dealing in securities, and it is incumbent on each member of Key Management Personnel to ensure that an associate does not deal in circumstances where the dealing could be attributed to the member concerned.
why_it_matters: A collar written through a spouse, family trust or related entity would still be attributed to the Key Management Personnel member and subject to the same clearance and closed-period rules.

clause: disposal of SKY securities due to a secured lender exercising their rights, for example under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: This expressly protects a bank's enforcement sale of collared shares even during a Prohibited Period, which is unusually favourable for a funded collar's lender compared to most policies that treat forced sales as a breach.

topic: no hedging or secured financing prohibition
clause: 17.1.1: officers and employees of the company may not buy or sell securities in the company while they are Information Insiders
why_it_matters: The policy's only general restriction on 'dealing' is buying or selling while an insider; nothing in the chapter prohibits granting security over shares or entering hedging/derivative arrangements, so the collar's equity and loan legs face no express bar outside Prohibited Periods.

clause: Control should be given a broad meaning, and you will be considered to control an entity if you can influence decisions made by that entity.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar through a family trust or holding company controlled by the executive does not escape the Prohibited Period restriction, since the entity's trading is attributed to the Key Management Personnel member.

clause: Any consent to trade given by the Sky's Company Secretary will be deemed to be withdrawn if the relevant Key Management Personnel becomes aware of Material Information prior to trading.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar entered into during a Prohibited Period on exceptional-circumstances consent could become unexecutable if Material Information arises before signing.

clause: A person is treated as a director or Officer for a period of 6 months after the date on which they cease to be a director or Officer, and must continue to comply with these disclosure obligations.
why_it_matters: Relevant Interest disclosure duties (including any interest created or discharged by the collar) continue for 6 months after the executive leaves the role.

clause: trading in shares of K&S Corporation Limited ("K&S Securities")
why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, 'K&S Securities' is defined as shares only, with no reference anywhere to options, derivatives or other financial products, creating a real argument that an OTC, cash-settled put/call over K&S shares is not 'dealing in K&S Securities' at all and so sits entirely outside the policy's Black Out Period and clearance regime.

clause: the sale of K&S Securities as a result of a secured lender to a Director or Senior Executive exercising its rights, eg, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is expressly 'excluded trading' permitted even inside a 60-day Black Out Period.

topic: notification not approval for secured financing
clause: the Company Secretary must be advised and the Company Secretary will inform all other Directors.
why_it_matters: Financing the holding via a margin loan or other secured arrangement (which would include a collar loan) requires only notification to the Company Secretary, not prior approval, making the loan leg comparatively easy to put in place.

topic: ASX disclosure of Black Out Period approval status
clause: whether the change occurred in a Black Out Period in circumstances where prior written approval of the Chairman or Deputy Chairman (as the case may be) was required; and if prior written approval was required, whether that approval was obtained.
why_it_matters: If the collar's derivative legs were ever treated as 'dealing' by analogy and executed in a Black Out Period, the market would be told via ASX notification that approval was required and whether it was obtained, adding public visibility to the transaction's timing.

clause: (other than a loan from K&S under the K&S Employee Share Plan)
why_it_matters: The section 11 notification regime is for third-party secured financing (like a bank collar loan); it does not apply to the Company's own ESP loans, which are a separate, distinguishable financing arrangement.

clause: Section 3 (The Trading Policy) addresses insider trading, close periods, clearance, dealing-volume limits and short-term dealing but contains no provision on margin loans, secured financing, encumbrance or hedging.
why_it_matters: Despite being a comprehensive, recently-adopted (2024) policy, it is entirely silent on collateralising CLINUVEL securities, so the loan leg of a funded collar has no express permission, prohibition or clearance pathway to point to.

clause: A director, employee or consultant may not sell securities exceeding one-third of the average daily trading volume for the last 180 days directly on the market in any one month. ... This limitation does not apply to any off-market transfers or transfers which occur via a "crossing" or similar such transaction.
why_it_matters: Any on-market unwind or delta-hedging sale by the bank tied to the collar would be constrained by this monthly volume cap, though off-market transfers and crossings are exempt.

clause: Directors, employees and consultants must not "shop" an excessive number of brokers and/or potential buyers or sellers so that the sale becomes widely known. They must proceed in a discrete manner when buying or selling securities.
why_it_matters: The bank should limit the number of counterparties or brokers approached when sourcing the hedge or unwinding the position, to avoid breaching this discretion requirement.

clause: The trade may proceed and must be completed within the next seven (7) business days following approval from the CEO or Chair, providing the Company, its directors, employees or consultants are not in possession of price-sensitive information which would prohibit trading.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be priced and executed within 7 business days and becomes unexecutable if price-sensitive information arises before signing.

clause: A director must ... seek to prohibit any dealing in securities of the Company during a close period ... by or on behalf of any person related to them ... which includes the director's spouse, de facto, family members, associated trusts, companies or other third parties.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar through a family trust or related company does not escape the close-period and clearance regime unless independent trustees, acting without the director's involvement, make the decision.

clause: ASX: CUV | Börse Frankfurt: UR9 | ADR Level 1: CLVLY
why_it_matters: CLINUVEL also trades via a Frankfurt listing and a US Level 1 ADR programme, but the Policy itself contains no jurisdiction overlay addressing US or German securities law implications of the collar.

clause: a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that treat a lender's forced sale as a breach, STX expressly excludes it from the operation of the whole policy, so a bank enforcing security over the collared shares (including in a Closed Period) does not put the executive in breach.

clause: A request for approval must provide details of the margin loan including the number of Securities involved, the trigger points, the right of the lender to sell the Securities and any other material details (and any other details required by the Chair).
why_it_matters: The Chair will require full economic terms of the bank's loan and enforcement rights before approving it, so the collar and loan documentation must be finalised and disclosed up-front rather than approved in outline.

clause: For other announcements (not specified above), Strike personnel are required to wait at least 4 trading hours before dealing in Securities ... so that the market has had time to absorb this information.
why_it_matters: Even outside the quarterly Closed trading periods, entry into or unwind of the collar must be timed to sit at least 4 trading hours after any market announcement.

clause: approval may be given by the Chair and at least one other non-executive Director for Strike personnel to sell (but not to purchase) Securities of the Company during a Prohibited Period
why_it_matters: If the collar needs unwinding for hardship reasons inside a Prohibited Period, only a sale of the underlying shares (not a new derivative purchase) could qualify for this narrow relief.

clause: Strike personnel must not Deal in Securities if they come into possession of Inside Information after obtaining approval. ... The Company may also withdraw approval if it receives new information or there is a change in circumstances after approval is given.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be signed within the 5-business-day validity window and can be revoked by the Company at any time before execution if circumstances change.

clause: Employees and directors are not permitted to deal at any time in financial products such as warrants, futures or other financial products issued over BCN securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions traded on either ASX markets or any other market.
why_it_matters: This absolute ban, with no waiver mechanism referenced, squarely covers a bank-structured OTC put and call over BCN shares, meaning the derivative legs of a funded collar cannot be entered into under the policy as drafted.

clause: An exception may apply where BCN securities form a component of a listed portfolio or index product.
why_it_matters: A bespoke bilateral bank collar is not a listed portfolio or index product, so this narrow carve-out cannot be used to structure around the section 4 ban.

clause: Any such approval must be obtained in advance. It cannot be given after the event.
why_it_matters: Even for ordinary share dealing during a Non Trading Period, collar entry or unwind approval must be secured before execution; retrospective ratification is unavailable.

clause: BCN may require an employee to provide confirmation of dealing in BCN securities by an employee or his/her associate(s).
why_it_matters: BCN can demand after-the-fact confirmation of any collar transaction entered into by the executive or an associate, including one routed through a spouse or trust.

clause: Where a waiver has been granted the details of the same must be recorded and reported to Directors at the next Board meeting.
why_it_matters: Any section 5 waiver permitting collar-related dealing becomes visible to the full Board, so confidentiality of the arrangement cannot be assured.

clause: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
