why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, AZY expressly authorises a secured lender's enforcement sale even while the executive holds inside information, and separately lists such a disposal as something KMP 'may at any time' do, including during a Closed Period - materially de-risking a bank's ability to enforce its security over the collared shares.

clause: This policy applies to both the sale and purchase of any securities of the Company and its subsidiaries on issue from time to time.
why_it_matters: The clearance and notification regime is built around buying, selling or exercising rights in the Company's own securities; entering an OTC put/call with a bank, or granting a mortgage/charge, may fall outside that regime altogether, though general insider trading law still applies independently of the policy.

clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company securities (ie a volume that would represent a volume in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller prior to the sale, or a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume of the shares of the Company on the ASX for the preceding 20 trading days) by a Key Management Personnel needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
why_it_matters: A collar-driven sale (e.g. on call exercise or unwind) exceeding either 10% threshold triggers a mandatory Board and legal-adviser discussion and a retained file note before execution.

clause: it is not permissible to provide the exercise price of options by selling the shares acquired on the exercise of these options unless the sale of those shares occurs outside the periods specified in paragraph 4.1.
why_it_matters: If the collared shares originate from option exercise, a sell-to-cover exercise cannot be used to fund the exercise price inside a Closed Period.

clause: Any exemption, if issued, will be in writing and shall contain a specified time period during which the sale of securities can be made.
why_it_matters: A collar unwind cleared under the hardship or exceptional-circumstances route during a Closed Period is time-boxed by the Board's written exemption, so execution must occur within that specified window.

clause: a reference to "securities" means securities in the Company and any other financial products of the Company quoted on the ASX or any other exchange or marketplace.
why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put and call referencing Coronado shares is not 'of the Company' and not quoted, so it falls outside the Policy's own 'securities'/'dealing' definitions; it is caught only via the separate, broader Hedging definition, leaving genuine doubt whether the blackout and 4.3 pre-clearance regime technically extends to it.

clause: Approval must be obtained by any Restricted Person in accordance with the procedure set out in section 4.4 for any: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; and transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar should be treated as requiring the same 4.4 approval as a conventional margin lending arrangement, even though a bespoke bank loan not documented via a margin account is not literally within the clause's wording.

clause: Specifically prohibited are purchases and sales of Company securities that are subject to Section 16(b) of the Exchange Act by the CEO and his/her direct reports, directors and any holder of 10% or more of the Company's issued and outstanding securities.
why_it_matters: For US-reporting insiders, any matching purchase and sale (or sale and purchase) within 6 months - potentially including collar unwind and rebuild - risks disgorgement of profit under Section 16(b), independently of this Policy's clearance process.

clause: Following receipt of approval to deal, the approved dealing must occur within 5 business days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective, and a new approval must be sought. ... [The approver] may revoke their approval at any time.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar must be executed within 5 business days of approval and remains subject to unilateral revocation by the approver at any time before execution.

clause: In the case of Directors, written confirmation should ideally be provided by close of business on the day the trade is entered into to assist the Company to comply with its disclosure obligations under the Exchange Act and ASX Listing Rules.
why_it_matters: A Director's collar trade needs same-day reporting to the Chief Legal Officer & Secretary to meet dual US/ASX disclosure timelines.

clause: Employees and directors must take appropriate steps to ensure that their "Connected Persons" only deal in securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, partner or a controlled entity does not avoid the blackout, clearance, hedging or margin lending restrictions.

clause: Financial Products means any structured financial products, swaps, futures contracts, contracts for difference, spread bets, options, warrants, depositary receipts or other derivatives over or related to the performance of any HMC Capital Group Securities.
why_it_matters: This is broad enough to expressly capture a bank-written OTC put and call over HCW units as HMC Capital Group Securities in their own right, so the collar's derivative legs sit squarely within the ordinary Trading/pre-approval regime rather than a definitional grey area.

topic: forced sale carve-back for unconsented margin loans
clause: an involuntary disposal of HMC Capital Group Securities that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights. However, this does not extend to disposal under a margin lending arrangement where such arrangement is prohibited by this Policy.
why_it_matters: The blanket exclusion for a secured lender's enforcement sale during a Blackout Period only survives if the underlying loan was itself properly consented under section 8 - an unconsented facility loses the benefit of the exclusion, so the bank's loan documentation must be cleared up-front to protect its enforcement rights.

clause: A Group Entity may, at its discretion, make any consent granted under section 8.1 conditional upon such terms and conditions that the relevant Group Entity sees fit (for example, specifying the circumstances in which HMC Capital Group Securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: The Group can dictate the trigger conditions under which the bank may sell the collared units on a margin call as a condition of consenting to the loan.

clause: selling HMC Capital Group Securities to satisfy a call under a margin loan except where the holder of the relevant HMC Capital Group Securities has no control over the sale.
why_it_matters: If the bank has a unilateral, uninstructed right to sell on a margin call, that sale escapes the section 8 consent requirement and relies instead on the general forced-sale exclusion; a loan giving the executive any discretion over which units are sold needs prior consent for each such sale.

clause: Any Employee who holds HMC Capital Group Securities subject to binding restrictions on transfer (either as ASX restricted securities or through voluntary escrow arrangements) must comply with the terms of any applicable escrow arrangements and will be unable to Trade in the relevant HMC Capital Group Securities during that time.
why_it_matters: Escrowed or ASX-restricted units cannot be pledged, collared or sold at all until escrow ends, regardless of vesting status.

clause: Were this to occur at a time when the person possessed inside information then the sale of Company shares would be a breach of insider trading laws, even though the person's decision to sell was not influenced by the inside information that the person possessed and the person may not have made a profit on the sale.
why_it_matters: A margin call or lender demand under the collar loan that forces a sale while the executive holds inside information breaches insider trading law regardless of intent, so any secured loan needs standstill/cure mechanics that avoid forced sales while UPSI could exist.

clause: In the instance where Company shares are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
why_it_matters: This only excuses the lender's enforcement sale from insider trading law, not from the Policy's own Closed Period dealing ban, so enforcement during a Closed Period could still be a Policy breach even though it is not a market-abuse offence.

clause: Directors and Employees may not enter into a transaction that is designed to limit the economic risk of a holding in unvested Kentor Gold Limited Securities.
why_it_matters: The hedging prohibition does not reach vested shares, so a collar over vested holdings is not caught by the express hedging ban and falls back only to the general Dealing/Closed Period/notice regime.

clause: clearance may be given for the Representative to sell (but not to purchase) securities when he/she would otherwise be prohibited from doing so.
why_it_matters: If unwinding or settling the collar during a Closed Period requires the executive to sell or deliver shares, hardship clearance is theoretically available, but any purchase-side step (e.g. buying back a leg) cannot be cleared this way.

clause: If no response is given within two business days, the person giving the notice does not have to wait until a response is given before trading.
why_it_matters: Directors' and Identified Employees' notice obligation is a soft timing mechanic rather than a hard preclearance gate, giving more execution certainty for structuring collar entry/exit dates than a discretionary approval system.

clause: Unless otherwise stated, any notice given under this section will automatically expire after five (5) business days.
why_it_matters: A collar trade notified by a Director or Identified Employee must be executed within 5 business days or the notice must be renewed, constraining execution timing with the bank's dealer.

clause: A Representative must seek to prohibit ... any dealing in securities of the Company during a Closed Period or at a time when the Representative is in possession of Unpublished Price-sensitive Information by or on behalf of any person associated with him (including the Representative's family, nominee companies, companies and family trusts)
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its loan through a family trust or investment vehicle does not escape the Closed Period/UPSI restrictions; the Representative must procure the associate's compliance.

clause: the periods commencing from the end of each quarter not covered under (a) or (b) above and ending on release of the Company's quarterly report as a mining entity.
why_it_matters: As a mining exploration entity, KGL has up to four Closed Periods a year (annual, half-year, and two quarterly), narrowing the open windows available for collar entry, roll or unwind.

clause: a court order or court enforcable undertakings in a bona fide family settlement to transfer Conquest Securities
why_it_matters: The reference to 'Conquest Securities' appears to be an uncorrected artifact from a template drawn from another company's policy, creating interpretive uncertainty about the scope of the exceptional-circumstances clearance.

clause: Paragraphs 3.3, 3.5, 3.6 and 4.1 of this Policy do not apply to: ... subject to paragraph 4.2, a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is excluded from the blackout, trading-window and short-term dealing restrictions, giving the lender genuine ability to liquidate collateral even during a closed period, though clause 4.2's ban on entering the arrangement in the first place must still be navigated.

clause: Any dealing in the Company's securities by Relevant Persons under a margin lending arrangement is prohibited.
why_it_matters: If the collar's loan leg is characterised as a 'margin lending arrangement' it is banned outright with no clearance route; a bilateral, non-margin-call secured facility is arguably outside this specific ban and only the (unaddressed) general dealing regime would apply, but this is a real characterisation risk to resolve before structuring.

clause: Dealing in securities is a broad concept ... It extends to exercising options over securities and entering into agreements to buy or sell securities.
why_it_matters: Because granting security (a pledge or charge) is not listed as a form of 'dealing', pledging the vested shares to the bank as collateral for the loan is not itself restricted by the blackout or trading-window rules, only the collar derivatives and any resulting transfer would be.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even where a collar and its secured loan are not expressly prohibited, an approver can refuse clearance if the arrangement would look like the executive exploiting their position, adding a subjective reputational filter to the funded structure.

clause: Where a Relevant Person enters into a hedging arrangement in respect of Company securities, the Company may, where appropriate, disclose the fact and nature of the hedge (e.g. in its annual report or to ASX).
why_it_matters: The bank collar may become publicly disclosed by the Company in its annual report or an ASX announcement, which the executive and bank should factor into confidentiality expectations.

clause: the Chair of the Board ... may direct the person who is proposing to deal in the Company's Securities not to deal, or to impose conditions on the dealing in their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons for any direction or condition.
why_it_matters: Even after notifying a collar trade in an open window, the Chair can block it or impose bespoke conditions without explanation, so execution timing cannot be treated as guaranteed once notice is given.

clause: the approved dealing must occur within 2 business days following approval (or any lesser period specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective and fresh approval must be sought.
why_it_matters: Both notification-based and approval-based clearances lapse quickly (2 business days), so the collar's pricing and execution with the bank must be tightly coordinated with the clearance date.

clause: This policy applies to private dealings in Whitefield's issued securities by Key Management Personnel (KMP).
why_it_matters: The Policy never defines 'Dealing' or 'Securities' and contains no attachment on either, so whether an OTC put/call, a hedge, or a secured loan over WHI shares is caught by the closed-period or UPSI prohibitions at all is genuinely unclear and would fall back on general Corporations Act insider trading concepts rather than this Policy's own text.

clause: KMPs must not deal in the Company's securities during prohibited periods (closed periods) unless exceptional circumstances apply and written approval is given to a transaction in advance.
why_it_matters: Outside a closed period and absent price sensitive information, the Policy imposes no notification or preclearance requirement at all on ordinary dealing, so a collar entered in an open window would not need any sign-off under this Policy.

clause: KMP's must not procure another person to deal in the Company's securities where they themselves are prohibited from dealing.
why_it_matters: A KMP cannot direct the bank (or anyone else) to execute a collar leg on their behalf during a period when the KMP is personally prohibited from dealing, even if the bank is acting as principal counterparty.

clause: Transactions which are outside the control of the KMP, including those which result from the application of law.
why_it_matters: This exclusion from Section 2 (the UPSI and closed-period bans) is broad enough to arguably cover a secured lender's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default, since that sale is outside the KMP's control, though the Policy does not use lender or security-specific language so this reading is not certain.

clause: Transactions conducted between a KMP and a close family member ... The following circumstances are excluded from the application of Section 2 of this Policy.
why_it_matters: On its face this excludes transactions between a KMP and a close family member from all of Section 2, including the UPSI-possession ban, which is an unusually broad carve-out; routing collar-related transfers through a family member should still be treated cautiously given the underlying insider trading law is unaffected.

clause: KMP's are not permitted to trade in the Company's Securities during the period from the end of a calendar month until the day after the release of the monthly Net Asset Backing Announcement.
why_it_matters: As a listed investment company, WHI has a monthly closed period on top of the half-year/annual one, materially narrowing the windows available each year for collar entry, roll or unwind.

clause: Pengana Associates may not enter into hedging or other financial arrangements (including derivative transactions) which operate to limit the economic risk or exposure associated with holding LIT Securities.
why_it_matters: Unlike the margin lending and short-term trading bans, this clause never references a Section 7 exemption, so the collar's put and call legs appear to be absolutely prohibited with no clearance pathway at all, regardless of vesting status or blackout timing.

clause: Pengana Associates may not enter into margin lending or any other secured financing arrangements in respect of its LIT Securities, unless an exemption has been granted in accordance with Section 7 of this policy.
why_it_matters: Even the loan leg secured on the collared units can only proceed via an Exceptional Circumstances exemption (hardship, court order, or an equivalent event), which is a materially higher and more discretionary bar than the routine trade-approval process used for ordinary dealing.

clause: These prohibitions apply at all times including to Permitted Trading, outside trading blackout periods and even where a trading approval or exemption has been given or granted under this policy. It overrides all other provisions of this policy.
why_it_matters: Even if a Section 7 exemption were obtained for the loan, the trade cannot proceed if the executive holds Inside Information at execution, so timing certainty for the bank cannot rely on the exemption alone.

clause: The Pengana Associate is not entitled to receive any reasons for why the trade is denied. If approval is denied, the decision is final and binding ... and the Pengana Associate must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: A refused exemption request for the loan or an approval request for the collar's ancillary trades cannot be explained to the bank, and the executive is contractually bound not to disclose even the fact of refusal.

clause: The power of veto is reserved to the PIML Chair and any other PIML Director. Acting jointly, the PIML Chair and any other PIML Director can: overturn any approval to a Pengana Associate to trade; or declare a trading blackout period without prior notice.
why_it_matters: Any clearance already obtained for a permitted leg of the structure (or an exemption for the loan) can be overturned at any time without notice, so execution and settlement timelines with the bank carry residual veto risk until completed.

clause: They must not structure arrangements or procure third parties to trade to circumvent the operation of this policy.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through an intermediary, trust or related entity to avoid the hedging or secured-financing bans would itself be a breach; the Personal Capacity definition also treats trades made in another person's or entity's name as the individual's own.

clause: Approvals to trade will be valid for five business days following the day on which approval was granted. ... approval is granted within five business days of a trading blackout coming into effect, in which case the approval will expire once the trading blackout comes into effect.
why_it_matters: Any ordinary dealing approval obtained around the collar (e.g. for a non-hedging incidental trade) lapses in 5 business days and can be cut short by an incoming blackout, requiring tight coordination of execution dates.

clause: This policy applies to both the sale and purchase of any securities of the Company and its subsidiaries on issue from time to time.
why_it_matters: Unlike sibling template policies (e.g. Kentor Gold's hedging ban), this Policy has no hedging or derivatives clause at all, and the approval regime is framed only around a person who wishes to 'buy, sell or exercise rights' in Company securities, so it is genuinely unclear whether entering an OTC put/call with a bank is caught by the Policy at all.

clause: Directors or Key Management Personnel may at any time: ... dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: This is an express, broadly worded exception (not limited to margin loans) from the Block Out Period restrictions, giving a bank real ability to enforce its security over the collared shares even during a closed period.

clause: Were this to occur at a time when the person possessed inside information, then the sale of Company securities would be a breach of insider trading laws, even though the person's decision to sell was not influenced by the inside information that the person possessed and the person may not have made a profit on the sale.
why_it_matters: A margin call or lender demand under the collar's loan that forces a sale while the executive holds inside information would still breach insider trading law regardless of intent, so the facility needs standstill or cure provisions to avoid forced sales during blackout or UPSI periods.

clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company securities (i.e. a volume that would represent a volume in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller prior to the sale, or a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume ... for the preceding 20 trading days) ... needs to be discussed with the board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
why_it_matters: Unwinding or hedge-related sales that exceed 10% of the executive's holding or 10% of 20-day ADV trigger a mandatory board and legal-adviser discussion, documented in a file note, before the bank can execute that leg of the collar.

clause: any Directors or Key Management Personnel who (or through his or her Associates) buys, sells, or exercises rights in relation to Company securities must notify the Company Secretary in writing of the details of the transaction within five (5) business days of the transaction occurring.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its collateral through a family trust or other Associate does not avoid the post-trade notification obligation, which must be met within 5 business days regardless of who executes the trade.

topic: policy does not override the law
clause: Compliance with these guidelines for trading in the Company's securities does not absolve that individual from complying with the law, which must be the overriding consideration when trading in the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: Because the Policy is largely silent on derivatives, hedging and secured financing, compliance with its express terms provides limited comfort; independent insider trading and market misconduct analysis is still required for the collar and loan.

clause: You must not trade in Securities at any time (including in the exceptional circumstances referred to in section 6) unless you first obtain prior written clearance
why_it_matters: Every leg of a funded collar (entry, roll, unwind) needs prior written clearance from the Chairman or CEO regardless of whether a Blackout Period is open, unlike policies that only require clearance in closed periods.

clause: You must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.
why_it_matters: The bank cannot be told why a clearance request is delayed or refused if an undisclosed Board-declared Additional Period is in effect, creating execution timing risk for the collar.

clause: trading not subject to this policy ... excluded from the restrictions outlined in section 5 [Blackout Periods]
why_it_matters: The carve-out for a secured lender's forced sale is drafted as an exclusion from the Blackout Period restriction only, not from the section 7 'at any time' clearance requirement, so a lender's enforcement sale under the collar loan may still technically require prior written clearance that the lender cannot itself obtain.

clause: Before entering into any transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of your security holding in the Company you must first obtain prior written clearance
why_it_matters: A collar (put plus call) squarely fits this broad hedging definition, so it needs the same prior written clearance as any other trade, and cannot be entered over unvested entitlements at all.

clause: You must take all reasonable steps to procure that your Connected Persons comply with this policy.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled company does not avoid the clearance or hedging restrictions.

clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights). Hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company.
why_it_matters: A funded collar's put and call legs are hedging arrangements under this definition and are banned outright for all Restricted Persons and associated parties, with no clearance route, no vesting-based carve-out and no stated exemption authority.

topic: margin loan consent and margin-call control
clause: A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Company's consent ... The Company may ... make any clearance granted ... conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, in regards to the circumstances in which the securities ... may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
why_it_matters: Even absent the hedging ban, the loan leg secured on the collared shares would need the Company's prior consent, and the Company can condition that consent on when the bank may sell the shares on a margin call, constraining enforcement of the bank's security.

clause: clearance may be given for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) securities in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so.
why_it_matters: Even if the hedging ban were lifted, the only prohibited-period clearance route permits a sale, not entry into a derivative or loan, so it offers no mechanism to establish the collar itself during a blackout.

clause: The Board has an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their respective associated parties trading in the Company's securities at any time.
why_it_matters: An undiscloseable Board embargo could block any residual dealing, unwind or refinancing step connected with the facility without notice.

topic: no venue or vesting limitation on hedging
clause: hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights)
why_it_matters: The ban is not limited to unvested or plan securities, so it also forecloses hedging fully vested, unrestricted shareholdings, unlike policies that only restrict hedging of unvested equity.

topic: collars are an expressly named Derivative
clause: Derivative has the meaning in section 761D of the Corporations Act and includes options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, cash settled swaps, caps and collars
why_it_matters: The Policy's own definitions name 'collars' as a Derivative within Securities, so a funded equity collar is squarely within the general Trading approval regime rather than a grey area requiring interpretation.

topic: approval still required for permitted dealings
clause: Please note that the Policy requirements with respect to prior written approval and subsequent notification continue to apply to Trading under one of these exceptions
why_it_matters: Even the Permitted Dealings exception for an involuntary sale by a margin lender enforcing its rights nominally still requires prior written approval and notification, which the bank as enforcing secured party cannot itself obtain, so the loan and collar documentation should address this practical gap.

clause: or grant lenders any rights over their Company Securities without first obtaining prior written approval
why_it_matters: This sweeps in the security interest granted to the bank under the collar's loan facility even if it is not styled as a conventional margin loan, so the whole financing structure needs prior approval, not just a facility labelled 'margin loan'.

clause: The Directors and Restricted Employees must inform the Company Secretary of any material change in their margin loan or similar funding arrangements e.g. movements in the LVR occasioned by drawdowns or price movements, and at least annually, of the amount drawn and Securities covered.
why_it_matters: Once the loan is approved, the executive must proactively report LVR-triggering movements and annual facility details to the Company Secretary, giving the Company (and indirectly the Board) ongoing visibility into the facility.

clause: The acquisition of Securities and subsequent resale within a 6 month period and the sale of Securities and subsequent repurchase within a 6 month period would be considered to be transactions of a short term nature.
why_it_matters: Unwinding, rolling or settling the collar (or dealing in the underlying shares) within 6 months of a relevant acquisition could itself be a prohibited short-term Trade unless the employee-incentive-scheme carve-out applies, so tenor and timing need care.

clause: for the avoidance of doubt, during the above periods Relevant Persons must not deal in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities (for example, exchange-traded options, contracts for differences and other derivatives).
why_it_matters: An OTC put/call and the written call leg of a collar are expressly covered as financial products created over AFG securities, so the blackout ban and the general dealing regime unambiguously reach the collar's derivative legs.

topic: margin lending approval irrespective of trading window
clause: Directors and senior executives must obtain approval in accordance with the procedure set out in paragraph 3.3 for any proposed dealing in the Company's securities in connection with a margin lending arrangement, irrespective of any trading window.
why_it_matters: Unlike an ordinary share trade (which needs only 48-hour advance notification inside an open trading window), the collar's secured loan always needs full prior approval, even when other trading in the same window would only need notification.

clause: Where a Relevant Person enters into a hedging arrangement in respect of Company securities, the Company may, where appropriate, disclose the fact and nature of the hedge (eg in its annual report or to ASX).
why_it_matters: The executive and the bank should expect the collar's existence and nature could become public via AFG's annual report or an ASX announcement, independent of any Corporations Act disclosure obligation.

topic: forced-sale carve-out conditional on prior compliance
clause: subject to paragraph 3.4, a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale is excused from the blackout/trading-window restrictions only if the underlying loan was itself approved under 3.4 when entered into, so obtaining that initial approval is a precondition to a clean forced-sale exit for the bank.

clause: A useful question to ask yourself is: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could my proposed transaction be perceived by the market as me (or my Connected Persons) taking advantage of my position in an inappropriate way?
why_it_matters: Beyond the black-letter rules, approvers are directed to weigh market perception, so an unusual structure like a funded collar should be flagged and explained in the approval or notification request.

clause: entering into protection arrangements includes entering into transactions which: amount to "short selling" ...; operate to limit the economic risk of any Koala Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) ...; or otherwise enable a Koala Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.
why_it_matters: This single, deliberately broad definition captures both legs of a collar (the purchased put profits from a price decrease; the structure as a whole limits economic risk), regardless of how the bank labels or documents the transaction.

topic: security over vested shares permitted with consent
clause: Koala Persons may, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Koala securities, to secure any obligation of that Koala Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Koala securities, with consent under section 6.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that ban all secured financing outright, Koala expressly permits granting security and margin lending over vested, unrestricted shares with prior consent, making the loan leg of a funded collar structurally available.

topic: forced-sale exemption needs no prior clearance
clause: Koala Persons may at any time: ... a disposal of Koala securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
why_it_matters: This is a true 'at any time' exemption from the Blackout Period restrictions requiring only post-hoc advice to the Authorising Officer, so a lender's enforcement sale under the collar loan is not itself blocked by Blackout Period timing, unlike several peer policies.

clause: the Koala Person seeking authorisation cannot be their own Authorising Officer
why_it_matters: For the Chair of the Board or a senior executive, clearance is pushed to a genuinely independent officer (e.g. the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee), relevant to sequencing sign-off for the collar.

clause: otherwise enable a Koala Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities
why_it_matters: This open-ended formulation means any bespoke or unconventional collar structure will still be characterised as a protection arrangement by its economic substance, so it cannot be engineered around the vesting-based prohibition or the consent regime.

clause: The following trades are excluded from the operation of this policy: ... 8.5 margin calls.
why_it_matters: A lender's forced sale on a margin call falls entirely outside the policy, so a bank enforcing security under a funded collar can sell the collared shares without breaching the trading window or clearance rules.

clause: All directors must notify the Company Secretary of any margin loan or similar funding arrangement entered into in relation to the Company's securities and any variations to such arrangements, including the number of securities involved, the circumstances in which the lender can make margin calls, and the right of the lender to dispose of securities.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is not prohibited and does not require prior clearance for directors, only post-inception notification to the Company Secretary disclosing the lender's margin-call and disposal rights; other Relevant Persons have no equivalent stated obligation at all.

clause: Directors, Officers and employees must not engage in hedging arrangements (including, for example, the use of put and call options or other derivative instruments) over unvested Securities issued pursuant to any employee or Director option or share plan.
why_it_matters: A collar can only be written over vested Securities; unvested plan securities cannot be the reference shares.

clause: Within 24 hours of ... trading in the Company's securities, full details of the director's notifiable interests in the Company's securities and changes in such interest must be advised to the Company Secretary so that a record is kept within the Company and so that necessary ASX notifications can occur.
why_it_matters: Entry into, or unwind of, the collar by a director must be reported to the Company Secretary within 24 hours for ASX notification purposes, in addition to any pre-trade clearance.

clause: Relevant Persons may trade in the Company's securities on ASX in the period of 10 business days commencing 24 hours following: the holding of the Annual General Meeting or any other General Meeting; the announcement of Annual or Half-Year results; the announcement of Quarterly Reports; and any other public announcement on ASX.
why_it_matters: This policy uses defined open trading windows rather than blackout periods; collar entry, unwind or roll must fall inside one of these 10-business-day windows (or be separately cleared by the Chairman under the exceptional-circumstances discretion) and clearance is only valid for 5 business days.

clause: Restricted Personnel must not enter into a hedging arrangement, deal in a financial derivative (including options) or enter into any other arrangement to protect against or limit the risk associated with a holding of Horizon Oil securities.
why_it_matters: This is an unqualified, venue-neutral ban on derivatives dealing that applies to every tier and every security state with no clearance route, so an OTC put/call collar with a bank cannot be entered under any circumstances envisaged by the policy.

clause: "Securities" include shares, derivatives and other financial products that can be traded on a financial market including financial products issued or created over Horizon Oil securities by third parties and products which operate to limit economic risk in securities holdings in Horizon Oil.
why_it_matters: Confirms a bank-issued OTC collar is squarely within scope of the section 9 ban, not merely an ancillary dealing caught incidentally.

clause: (no clause addresses margin loans, secured financing or encumbrance)
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares has no express treatment; absent the section 9 ban, it would fall back on the general dealing and notification rules as an ordinary transaction, but the point is moot given derivatives are already prohibited.

clause: The Directors of Horizon Oil are required to complete either Appendix 3X, 3Y or 3Z (as applicable) and provide it to Horizon Oil to be filed with the ASX in respect of their shareholding.
why_it_matters: Any change in a director's economic interest, such as one arising from an approved collar or loan, would still require ASX notification via these forms independent of the internal clearance process.

clause: The Board of Horizon Oil have an absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Personnel and / or employees and / or their respective associated parties trading in Horizon Oil securities at any time.
why_it_matters: Even if a derivatives exemption were somehow granted, the Board can impose an unscheduled embargo at any time, adding execution timing risk to any collar structure.

clause: Employees must not trade in any derivative products issued by the Company. Derivative products issued by the Company over its securities include warrants, options and contracts for difference.
why_it_matters: Read literally, the ban is limited to derivatives 'issued by the Company', which an OTC bank collar is not; but the section 2 definition of Securities extends to derivative products created by third parties over Company securities, so a bank is likely still caught by the combined effect of the two clauses, leaving only a narrow drafting-based argument against application.

clause: a disposal of the Company's securities that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights under a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement permitted by this Policy
why_it_matters: This Closed Period exception presupposes that some secured financing arrangements are 'permitted by this Policy', which is in tension with section 5.9's blanket ban; it most likely contemplates arrangements that pre-date the Policy or were separately approved, so a new bank-secured collar loan would still need to overcome the section 5.9 prohibition before this carve-out could ever apply to its enforcement.

clause: Where the Company's securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
why_it_matters: Confirms that if a security interest exists, the lender's enforcement sale on default is insider-trading-safe, but does not cure the section 5.9 prohibition on creating that security interest in the first place.

clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of the Company's securities (i.e. a volume ... in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller ... or a volume ... in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume ... for the preceding 20 trading days) by an Employee must be discussed with the Board prior to the execution of any sale.
why_it_matters: Unwinding or physically settling a sizeable collar could trip this 10% threshold, requiring a documented pre-sale discussion with the Board in addition to ordinary clearance.

clause: although this Policy only applies to Employees, the insider trading prohibitions set out in the Corporations Act apply to all persons (including family members of Employees). As such, it is the Company's expectation that Employees will obtain legal advice prior to family members of Employees trading in Shares when this Policy would prevent that Employee from undertaking the trade themselves.
why_it_matters: The Policy's express prohibitions (including the derivatives and secured financing bans) technically bind only Employees, not their associates, though statutory insider trading law and the Company's stated expectation of legal advice limit any structuring benefit from routing a collar or loan through a family member.

clause: Ultimate discretion rests with the Chair in respect of granting a waiver to the requirements of this Policy to allow Employees to trade in the shares of the Company, provided that to do so would not be illegal.
why_it_matters: This broad, generally-worded waiver power is the only visible route by which the Chair could permit an otherwise-banned derivative or secured financing arrangement, but it is entirely discretionary and final if refused.

clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could the proposed dealing be perceived by the market as the Director or Employee taking advantage of his or her position in an inappropriate way? ... Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Media Test.
why_it_matters: Even a structure that clears every express rule can still be refused approval on this subjective reputational standard, so a funded collar with a bank remains subject to discretionary compliance sign-off regardless of technical permissibility.

clause: (the Policy addresses hedging of un-vested securities and 'trading in Dexus securities'/'financial products managed by Dexus' requiring approval, but does not define Securities or financial product to expressly extend to third-party-issued derivatives referencing Dexus securities)
why_it_matters: Unlike comparable policies, DXC's policy has no explicit definition sweeping in bank-issued OTC puts/calls over vested securities, creating some ambiguity as to whether the collar's derivative legs are directly regulated at all, separate from the underlying share dealing and insider trading rules that plainly still apply.

clause: trading in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities
why_it_matters: The prohibition is worded narrowly around 'margin lending activities'; a bespoke bilateral loan from a bank secured by a share pledge, not routed through a margin lending facility, arguably falls outside the literal wording, though it would still need approval under the general 'trading in Dexus securities' clearance regime and would likely fail the Media Test in substance.

clause: Where approval is granted, the trade must be executed within 5 business days. If the trade is not executed within this timeframe, approval will need to be re-sought.
why_it_matters: Structuring, documenting and executing a collar (and its secured loan) within a 5-business-day approval window is tight; any delay requires re-applying for approval.

clause: reference to Dexus Securities includes reference to Dexus (ASX:DXS), Dexus Industria REIT (ASX:ADI1) and Dexus Retail Convenience REIT (ASX:DXC).
why_it_matters: This single policy governs dealings across the whole Dexus stapled group, so a DXC-specific collar for a director or executive is assessed under the same group-wide rules, approvers and trading windows as DXS and DXI.

clause: This policy also prohibits margin lending and other secured financing arrangements. [section 14] / Restricted Persons must not enter into agreements that provide lenders with rights over their interests in securities in the Company without first seeking and obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer. [section 10.5] / a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement where the arrangement has been approved by the Company in accordance with this Policy. [section 15(f)]
why_it_matters: Section 14's blanket 'prohibits' language could be invoked by the Company Secretary or an Approving Officer to refuse the loan leg of a funded collar outright, even though sections 10.5 and 15(f) both presuppose that a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement can be approved; a bank should treat approval of the secured loan as discretionary and not guaranteed, and should expect the Company to require a clearance application addressing this tension.

topic: explicit OTC derivative and CFD coverage
clause: This policy covers trading not only in the Company's securities ... but also in other rights and derivative products such as ... any warrant, exchange traded or over-the-counter option and any contract for difference issued in relation to the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: Removes any ambiguity that a bank-written OTC put/call collar over Omega shares is treated as dealing in the Company's securities, triggering the standing section 11 notify-and-clear obligation for Restricted Persons at any time (not only during Blackout Periods) as well as the section 10 Blackout Period regime.

topic: hedging permitted across all vesting states
clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding (including holdings of securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock or other escrow) in the Company without first seeking and obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that ban hedging of unvested or holding-locked securities outright, this Policy permits hedging of any security state, including unvested and locked holdings, with prior written clearance -- a materially more favourable starting point for negotiating a funded collar over any of the executive's holdings.

topic: standing pre-trade gate outside Blackout Periods
clause: Before trading, or giving instructions for trading or causing anyone else to trade, in the Company's securities, Restricted Persons (other than the Chairman or Directors) must: notify the Company Secretary of their intention to trade ...; confirm that they do not hold any inside information; have been advised by the Company Secretary that there is no known reason to preclude them from trading ...; and have complied with any conditions on trading imposed by the Company Secretary.
why_it_matters: Restricted Persons must clear every trade at any time, not just during Blackout Periods, so entry into, adjustment of, or unwind of a collar always requires this notify-and-clear step in addition to the section 10.5 clearance for the hedging and security elements.

clause: If I do not complete my Securities Transaction before the expiry of the 5 Business Day period from the date of grant of approval, or the date on which I subsequently become aware of Inside Information which has not been released to the market (whichever is the earlier) I must seek fresh approval.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar or loan must be executed within 5 business days of approval and can become unexecutable earlier if inside information arises before signing, requiring a fresh clearance application.

clause: This policy also prohibits margin lending and other secured financing arrangements. [cf.] Directors, officers and employees must not enter into agreements that provide lenders with rights over their Interests in securities in the Company without first seeking and obtaining prior written clearance ... [cf.] a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement where the arrangement had been approved by the Company in accordance with this Policy.
why_it_matters: The policy is internally inconsistent on whether a loan secured on the collared shares is banned outright (s15) or approvable with clearance (s10.5, s16.1(f)); a bank should seek the Board's own interpretation and written clearance before treating the collar's loan leg as permissible.

clause: Directors, officers and employees must not put in place a non-discretionary trading plan in respect of their securities in the Company without first seeking and obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
why_it_matters: If the collar or its unwind is structured as, or resembles, a non-discretionary trading plan, it needs prior clearance and cannot be entered into or amended during a Blackout Period, constraining timing and roll flexibility.

clause: Where ad hoc Blackout Periods are imposed by the Company, each employee and officer of the Company must keep the imposition of this additional restriction confidential.
why_it_matters: An undisclosed extra blackout can block execution, unwind or settlement of the collar at short notice without the bank being told why.

clause: such approval is valid for a period of 5 Business Days from the date of grant of approval or the time when I become aware of Inside Information which has not been released to the market (whichever is the earlier).
why_it_matters: A cleared OTC collar trade must be priced and executed within 5 business days, or fresh clearance must be sought, adding execution timing risk.

clause: companies, trusts and entities over which Key Personnel or their immediate family members have control ... immediate family members of Key Personnel (including spouses, de facto spouses and children).
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a family trust or controlled entity does not escape the policy; the same clearance and blackout restrictions apply.

clause: A reconciliation of restricted persons trades against the appropriate approvals and record in the register will be completed each month. Any discrepancies will be highlighted to the board and followed up.
why_it_matters: Settlement or physical delivery under the collar will be reconciled monthly against clearances on file, so any mismatch (e.g. an unapproved secured loan) is likely to surface to the Board.

topic: margin loan clearance then excluded forced sale
clause: Restricted Persons must not enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement ... without first obtaining written clearance ... [and] a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights ... (please note section 11 of this policy which prohibits Restricted Persons entering into such arrangements without first seeking prior written clearance).
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is not banned outright, only clearance-gated at inception; once cleared, an enforcement sale by the bank as secured lender would itself fall outside the trading restrictions and clearance procedure as excluded trading.

clause: Restricted Persons must not put in place a non-discretionary trading plan ... without first obtaining prior written clearance ... Restricted Persons must not cancel any such trading plan during a Prohibited Period unless the circumstances are exceptional.
why_it_matters: If the collar or its unwind is structured as a non-discretionary trading plan it needs prior clearance to establish, and (per the separate exclusion in s8.1(h)) cannot be entered into or amended during a Prohibited Period.

clause: Restricted Persons must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.
why_it_matters: An undisclosed Board-imposed Additional Period can block execution, unwind or settlement of the collar without notice to, or explanation for, the bank.

clause: A Connected Person means immediate family members living at the same address ... or an unlisted body corporate which the Senior Personnel, or Employee controls ... or a trust of which he or she ... is a beneficiary ... Where this policy requires a Restricted Person to do an act or thing, the relevant Restricted Person must ensure that any Connected Person also does that act or thing.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a family member, controlled company or family trust does not escape the clearance and Prohibited Period restrictions.

clause: Any written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for the period of 5 business days from the time which it is given.
why_it_matters: A cleared OTC collar trade (and the margin loan clearance) must be priced and executed within 5 business days or fresh clearance is required, adding execution timing risk.

clause: The Company's Securities Trading Policy prohibits the buying or selling of Company securities at any time by any director, officer, key management personnel, executive, contractor, consultant or employee ('Insiders') who possesses price-sensitive information about the Company.
why_it_matters: The policy never defines 'Company Securities' to include derivatives, and has no express or dealing-definition-based treatment of hedging, margin lending or secured financing; a funded collar therefore falls into a genuine textual gap rather than being expressly permitted or barred, so company-specific comfort should be sought before relying on silence.

clause: The Chairman or the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer may halt trading in the Company securities at any time and an email will be sent to those directors, executive management and employees who are affected.
why_it_matters: An ad hoc halt (not stated as confidential, but issued at will) could block execution, roll or unwind of the collar on short notice.

clause: The above restrictions on trading do not restrict participation in any Company share or option plans from time to time but apply in respect of the trading of the Company's shares which participants become entitled to under those plans.
why_it_matters: Once plan shares vest, ordinary trading rules (results blackout, notification, insider-information ban) apply to any disposal or hedge of them, but there is no separate express restriction distinguishing unvested from vested holdings for hedging or security purposes.

clause: the buying or selling of Company securities at any time by any director, officer, key management personnel, executive, contractor, consultant or employee ('Insiders').
why_it_matters: Unlike modern policies, there is no express extension of the notification/approval regime to spouses, family trusts or controlled entities, so on its face routing the collar or loan through such a vehicle may sit outside the policy's clearance mechanics (though general insider trading law would still apply if the individual procures the trade).

clause: Persons covered by this Policy must not trade through any member of their family, or though a trust or company over which they have influence or control, in circumstances where they would have been prohibited from trading in their own name.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a family member, trust or controlled company does not escape the black-out or clearance restrictions that would otherwise apply to the executive personally.

clause: a disposal of Company shares that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: No provision requires clearance to enter into a margin loan or grant security over shares, and the resulting enforcement sale is excluded trading; the loan leg of a funded collar therefore falls into an unregulated gap rather than being expressly permitted or barred.

clause: This Policy applies to all securities issued by the Company from time to time, including ordinary shares and options.
why_it_matters: Because 'securities covered' is limited to securities issued by the Company, a bank-written OTC put and call over the shares arguably fall outside the defined scope of this policy altogether, creating interpretive uncertainty as to whether the derivative legs of the collar are caught at all (as distinct from any subsequent dealing in the underlying shares).

clause: If approval is given, the trade must be executed within 2 business days of the approval.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar trade in the underlying shares (e.g. delivery on unwind) must be executed within 2 business days of approval or fresh clearance is required.

clause: Permission will be given for trading pursuant to this section 4 only after a written request for approval is provided ... and only if the approving person is satisfied that the transaction would not be ... seen by the public, press, other shareholders or ASX as unfair.
why_it_matters: Even where hardship or exceptional circumstances are shown, a bespoke bank collar entered during a black-out period could still be refused if perceived as unfair, adding discretionary approval risk beyond the strict legal tests.

clause: Derivatives has the meaning given in the Corporations Act and includes the following if they relate to or derive their value from Company Securities; put or call options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement.
why_it_matters: The policy expressly names 'caps and collars' as a covered Derivative, confirming a bank-written equity collar over the shares is squarely regulated as a Dealing, and is expressly permitted over vested shares subject to ordinary Clearance rather than left to interpretation.

clause: Save where expressly permitted by the Board, Relevant Persons are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Company Securities or in relation to which Company Securities may be used as security against loan repayments.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is prohibited by default; the bank should seek specific Board approval (a higher bar than the ordinary Clearance Officer sign-off used for the derivative legs) before the secured loan can proceed.

clause: A Clearance ... will remain in force for the date of approval only, unless otherwise notified by the Clearance Officer (if the Dealing is not placed within this time, the Clearance will no longer have effect and a new Clearance must be requested and obtained).
why_it_matters: Absent a specific extension, a cleared OTC collar trade must be executed the same day it is approved, creating tight execution timing that the bank must plan around.

clause: Any Dealing in Company Securities or Securities of another entity under this policy must not be made if that Dealing would fail the 'front page' test.
why_it_matters: Even a cleared and otherwise permitted collar could still be refused or later criticised on a subjective public-perception basis distinct from the strict legal and policy tests.

clause: Margin loans to support an investment in Company Securities (and other types of margin lending arrangements) can compromise compliance with this policy, as the loan's terms may compel the sale of Company Securities during a blackout period or when the Relevant Person has relevant Inside Information.
why_it_matters: Unlike some peer policies, there is no exclusion for a lender's forced sale; if the bank enforces the collar's security during a blackout period, that sale would likely be a breach of this policy rather than excluded trading.

clause: A Relevant Person must: inform any Associate of the periods during which the Relevant Person must not Deal in Company Securities; inform any Associate that he or she must not Deal in Company Securities on a speculative basis; and request any Associate to inform the Relevant Person immediately after Dealing.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a family member, trust or controlled entity does not avoid the restrictions; the Relevant Person remains responsible for the Associate's compliance.

clause: Designated Persons may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is expressly banned for Designated Persons with no vesting carve-out and no approval or exemption route.

clause: The Company prohibits the use of Derivatives in relation to unvested equity instruments ... and vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions (such as a 'Holding Lock'). Derivatives may be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions.
why_it_matters: Even absent the financing ban, the put and call legs of a collar can only be written over vested shares free of a holding lock, and only after Managing Director approval.

clause: In exceptional circumstances a Designated Person may seek written approval from the Managing Director ... to dispose of or transfer (but not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period.
why_it_matters: Because Disposal Consent covers sale/transfer only, a lender's enforcement sale during a Black-out Period could not be structured as an acquisition or a new derivative, and initiating a collar during a black-out is not possible even under hardship.

clause: Buy or sell orders for Company Securities which are placed but not completed outside of a Black-out Period ... the order must be completed within five trading days otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
why_it_matters: Any collar leg executed as an order must complete or lapse within five trading days if a Black-out Period begins mid-execution, constraining settlement timing near results and the AGM.

clause: their spouse or any of their children (including step children) under the age of 18 years; a trust of which they, any members of their family, or family-controlled company are a trustee or beneficiary; and a company which they or their family control.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, minor child's holding, family trust or controlled company does not escape the Designated Person's approval requirement or the secured financing ban.

clause: Securities to which this Policy applies include ... all ordinary shares (including shares subscribed for), share options, preference shares, debentures, convertible notes or any other form of security issued by any of the AGT Group Companies.
why_it_matters: A bank-issued OTC put or call over AGT shares is not itself a 'Security' issued by an AGT Group Company, so a cash-settled collar leg may sit outside the Policy entirely; only the encumbrance of the underlying shares (loan security) and any agreement to deliver them are clearly caught as Dealings.

clause: 'Deal' means to subscribe, purchase, sell, assign, transfer, encumber or otherwise alienate any right, title or interest in a security, or to enter into any agreement or arrangement to do so.
why_it_matters: Granting security over the collared shares for the bank loan requires Board approval (for Directors/CEO) or CEO approval (for Employees) and must be timed within a Window Period or approved as an exceptional circumstance.

clause: This Policy does not apply, and Dealings in Securities can be effected by Directors and Employees outside Window Periods, in the following circumstances: ... a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is expressly excluded from the Policy, so it is not blocked by Window Periods or the approval procedure even if it occurs at a closed time.

clause: Cover letter dated 15 December 2010 lodging the Board-adopted Securities Trading Policy with the ASX.
why_it_matters: This is a 2010-era policy with no derivatives, hedging or margin-lending-specific regime; confirm with the company whether a more recent policy has since superseded it before relying on this analysis.

clause: Personnel are prohibited from participating in or entering into any of the following under this policy: trading in derivative products over GDI Property Group Securities, including warrants, exchange-traded and over-the-counter options, and contracts for difference.
why_it_matters: This is an absolute, unconditional ban with no vesting carve-out and no approval route, so both the purchased put and the written call legs of an OTC collar are prohibited outright for every person the Policy covers.

clause: Margin lending poses special risks to the compliance by Restricted Persons with this policy, particularly where the terms of the margin lending arrangements may place the Restricted Person in a position of conflict with their obligations under this policy and/or with the insider trading laws (for example, if a call is made under the arrangements, which results in GDI Property Group Securities being sold while the Restricted Person possesses inside information).
why_it_matters: Even if the derivatives ban did not already block the collar, the Policy itself flags that a lender's forced sale on a margin call while the executive holds inside information would breach both the Policy and insider trading law, with no stated carve-out for enforcement sales.

clause: GDI Property Group Securities include the stapled securities comprising a share in GDI Property Group Limited and a unit in GDI Property Group Trust trading on the ASX under the code 'GDI' and any performance rights issued pursuant to the GDI Property Group Performance Rights Plan.
why_it_matters: The stapled structure and performance rights plan define exactly what 'securities' the derivatives, margin lending and short-selling prohibitions attach to; a collar over the stapled security is squarely within scope.

clause: A refusal to grant permission to deal is final and binding on the person seeking the permission. If permission is refused, the person must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone, to ensure that GDI Property Group manages its disclosure obligations.
why_it_matters: Unusually, the confidentiality duty on a refusal is imposed on the individual rather than just the Company, which would constrain how an executive could explain a declined clearance request to the bank.

clause: Designated Persons may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is expressly banned for Designated Persons with no vesting carve-out and no approval or exemption route.

clause: Derivatives may, subject to the approval of the Chairperson (or in relation to the Chairperson, subject to approval of the Board) and subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy, be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions.
why_it_matters: Unlike the general Dealing approval regime (limited to Designated Persons), this gate applies to any employee, consultant or contractor who wants to use a Derivative, meaning even non-Designated staff would need Chairperson sign-off for the option legs of a collar.

topic: hedging arrangement named in Derivatives definition
clause: any other transaction in financial products or hedging arrangement or other arrangement which operates to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities

clause: in exceptional circumstances a Designated Person may seek written approval from the Chairperson (Approval Officer) to dispose of or transfer (but not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period.
why_it_matters: Because Disposal Consent covers sale/transfer only, initiating a new collar (acquiring a put, writing a call, or granting security) cannot be done during a Black-out Period even under hardship.

clause: their spouse or any of their children (including step children) under the age of 18 years; a trust which they, any members of their family, or family controlled company are a trustee or beneficiary; and a company which they or their family control.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, minor child's holding, family trust or controlled company does not escape the Designated Person's approval requirement or the secured financing ban.

clause: securities includes: ... any derivatives of those securities, including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, whether settled by cash or otherwise.
why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put or call over KSL shares is itself a 'security' under this Policy, so the collar legs are directly and unambiguously regulated as dealings, not merely caught indirectly.

topic: margin lending ban is narrowly framed
clause: Any dealing in the Company's securities by Relevant Persons pursuant to a margin lending arrangement is not permitted. ... dealing includes: ... margin lending, stock lending or other financing arrangements related to securities.
why_it_matters: The absolute ban targets 'margin lending arrangements' specifically (including transfers into a margin account and margin-call sales); 'other financing arrangements related to securities' is separately listed and is only an ordinary Dealing requiring Trading Window clearance, not an outright prohibition. A collar loan not styled or characterised as a 'margin loan' may be able to proceed with clearance, though this depends on how the company's counsel characterises the facility and whether a substance-over-form approach is applied in practice.

clause: Where a Relevant Person enters into a hedging arrangement in respect of Company securities, the Company may, where appropriate, disclose the fact and nature of the hedge (eg, in its annual report or to POMSoX or ASX).
why_it_matters: The bank's collar counterparty arrangement risks becoming a public disclosure item, which the executive should factor into the structuring discussion.

clause: closely related parties (as that term is defined in the Australian Corporations Act 2001) of all Kina Personnel ... Where this Policy requires a Relevant Person to do something (eg, obtaining clearance ...), that person must also do so for their closely related parties.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not escape the executive's clearance obligations or the margin lending ban.

clause: For the avoidance of doubt, the above Trading Windows apply to trading on both POMSoX and ASX. However, ASX's trading day calendar will be used to determine the timing of the relevant Trading Window.
why_it_matters: Collar execution and settlement timing must be checked against ASX's trading calendar even though KSL is dual-listed with POMSoX.

clause: A Restricted Person may enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement in respect of any Company Securities (Funding Arrangements) but must disclose the existence, nature and terms of the Funding Arrangements to a Clearance Officer who will notify the Board.
why_it_matters: The secured loan leg of a funded collar is expressly permitted, not banned, provided it is disclosed to a Clearance Officer at inception.

clause: where a Restricted Person's Funding Arrangement involves 5% or more of the Company's shares, the Board and Company Secretary will make appropriate disclosure to the market of any key terms of the Funding Arrangements.
why_it_matters: A collar loan sized at 5% or more of Tolu's issued shares triggers public disclosure of its key terms, which the executive and bank should factor into deal size and confidentiality.

clause: an involuntary disposal of Securities in the Company that results from a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under the arrangement.
why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale on default is treated as an Excluded Dealing not requiring fresh clearance, though 9.3(b)'s insider-trading, short-selling, short-term and hedging bars still apply to it.

clause: Securities means: (a) shares; (b) debentures; (c) legal or equitable interests ...; (d) options to acquire, by way of issue ...; and (e) rights ... under a rights issue.
why_it_matters: Because OTC derivatives and CFDs fall outside 'Securities', the put and call legs of a funded collar likely sit outside the clearance/blackout regime entirely, though physical settlement transferring the underlying shares would itself be a Dealing requiring clearance.

clause: The Corporations Act prohibits Key Management Personnel and a closely related party of Key Management Personnel from entering into an arrangement if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the members remuneration that has not vested or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.
why_it_matters: For KMP the ban on hedging unvested or vested-but-holding-locked remuneration derives from statute, not just policy, so writing a collar before the lock lifts risks liability beyond a mere policy breach.

clause: trading in and out of Securities occurs within a period of less than two months.
why_it_matters: Any unwind or replacement dealing within two months of the shares' acquisition breaches the short-term trading ban, so collar tenor and early-termination mechanics must respect this minimum.

clause: Clearance may be given for such a person to sell (but not purchase) Securities of the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited by this Policy from doing so.
why_it_matters: Hardship or court-order relief only ever permits a sale, never an acquisition, during a Prohibited Period, limiting its use to unwind scenarios and not to establishing new collar positions.

clause: any Related Person or Related Entity (or an Associate of a Related Person or Related Entity) of a person referred in paragraphs (a)(1) and (b) above.
why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the regime, as such an Associate is itself a Restricted Person under the Policy.

clause: The Company prohibits the use of Derivatives in relation to unvested equity instruments, including performance share rights, and vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions (such as a 'Holding Lock').
why_it_matters: A collar cannot be written at all until the shares have both vested and cleared any Holding Lock.

clause: Derivatives may, subject to the approval of the Chairperson (or in relation to the Chairperson, subject to approval of the Board) ... be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions.
why_it_matters: Once vested and unrestricted, the put/call legs of a collar are achievable, but require a specific Chairperson (or Board) sign-off in addition to the ordinary Dealing approval process.

clause: Designated Persons may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.
why_it_matters: The funded leg of a funded collar cannot be implemented: pledging the shares as security for the bank's loan is an outright, unqualified breach with no disclosure-only or exception route, unlike some peer policies.

clause: any other transaction in financial products or hedging arrangement or other arrangement which operates to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
why_it_matters: Restructuring the collar's legal form (swap, CFD, forward, or bespoke agreement) will not avoid the Derivatives regime in clause 6.2, since the definition catches any arrangement limiting economic risk in any way.

clause: Buy or sell orders for Company Securities which are placed but not completed outside of a Black-out Period are subject to the following restrictions once the Black-out Period commences: the order must be completed within five trading days otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
why_it_matters: If execution of a collar-related order spans the onset of a Black-out Period, it must complete within five trading days or lapse, and its terms cannot be adjusted, constraining timing flexibility.

topic: deeming of family and related entities
clause: their spouse or any of their children (including step children) under the age of 18 years; a trust of which they, any members of their family, or family-controlled company are a trustee or beneficiary; and a company which they or their family control.
