why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, minor child, family trust or family company does not avoid the restrictions, as these are deemed Designated Persons in their own right.

topic: no fixed clearance validity or SLA
clause: All requests to Deal in Company Securities ... must include the intended volume of securities to be Dealt in and an estimated time frame for the Dealing.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies with a fixed clearance validity window, execution timing here is whatever timeframe is stated in the approval request, adding uncertainty for coordinating trade dates with a bank counterparty.

clause: Restricted Employees and Directors must not purchase or create any hedge and/or derivative attached to or based on Myer Securities.
why_it_matters: This single sentence rules out the put and call legs of a funded collar for Directors and Restricted Employees at any vesting state, with no exception or clearance route.

topic: extended ban to Closely Related Parties
clause: All Restricted Employees and Directors must not (and must ensure that their Closely Related Parties do not) use, or allow to be used, any derivatives or other products which operate to limit the economic risk of Myer Securities under an employee incentive scheme that are unvested or vested but subject to disposal restrictions.
why_it_matters: Routing a hedge on unvested or lock-restricted incentive shares through a spouse, family trust or controlled company does not avoid the ban.

clause: That person's Designated Superior may, at the Designated Superior's discretion, make any clearance for the purposes of this section 4.6 conditional on such terms and conditions as the Designated Superior sees fit.
why_it_matters: A plain secured loan against vested Myer shares (not styled as a derivative) can proceed with Designated Superior clearance, but this only supports the loan leg, not the banned hedge legs of a true collar.

clause: Subject to section 4.6, a disposal of Myer Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale on default is a pre-cleared Excluded Dealing that can occur outside a Trading Window, provided the original financing was cleared under 4.6.

clause: Securities includes Myer's American Depositary Receipts which are able to be traded in the US through a Sponsored Level 1 American Depositary Receipt program.
why_it_matters: Structuring around Myer's ASX-listed shares by referencing the US ADRs instead does not escape the Policy, as ADRs are expressly within 'Securities'.

clause: In each case where a clearance is granted, the duration of that clearance to deal in Myer Securities will be no more than 2 working days.
why_it_matters: Even where a waiver or clearance for the loan leg is obtained, execution must occur within a very short window (2 working days for exceptional-circumstances clearance, 5 working days for ordinary clearance), requiring tight coordination with the bank.

clause: Myer adopts the broader concept of "dealing" for the purposes of this Policy. Myer considers Dealing to include, without limitation, Securities transactions such as transfers of beneficial ownership and trading (either directly or indirectly).
why_it_matters: Signals that indirect or intermediated structures used to access economic exposure to Myer shares will still be treated as Dealing/Trading.

topic: narrow dealing concept excludes derivatives and financing
clause: This policy applies to both the sale and purchase of any securities of the Company ... Any Key Management Personnel ... wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities must obtain the prior written approval.
why_it_matters: Because the Policy's approval, notification and Closed Period regime is keyed only to buying, selling or exercising rights, entering an OTC put/call collar, or the loan securing it, is arguably outside the Policy's operative scope altogether, subject always to the overriding insider trading law.

topic: mortgage/charge and forced sale expressly contemplated
clause: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
why_it_matters: The Policy affirmatively contemplates the shares being pledged as security and treats the lender's enforcement sale as compliant and excluded from Closed Period restrictions, favouring the secured-loan leg of a collar.

clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company securities (ie a volume that would represent a volume in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller prior to the sale, or a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume ... for the preceding 20 trading days) ... needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
why_it_matters: Unwinding or settling a collar by a large share sale (over 10% of the executive's holding or of 20-day ADV) triggers a mandatory pre-sale discussion with the Board and lawyers, an added process step though not a prohibition.

topic: option exercise price funded by share sale
clause: it is not permissible to provide the exercise price of options by selling the shares acquired on the exercise of these options unless the sale of those shares occurs outside the periods specified in paragraph 4.1.
why_it_matters: If the collar or its funding is linked to an option exercise, any cashless-exercise sale to fund the exercise price must occur outside a Closed Period.

topic: Associates bound by same notification duty
clause: any Key Management Personnel who (or through his or her Associates) buys, sells, or exercises rights in relation to Company securities must notify the Company Secretary in writing of the details of the transaction within two (2) business days.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or a sale through a family member, family trust or family company does not avoid the notification duty, though it also does not create any additional restriction beyond that duty.

clause: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding LIT Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.
why_it_matters: Unlike an absolute ban, the put/call legs of a collar are achievable with prior written clearance, making this one of the more collar-friendly policies in the batch.

clause: EQT Persons , LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.
why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the Units is similarly achievable with prior clearance rather than banned outright.

clause: The following types of trades ... are excluded from this policy: Those that do not result in a change to the beneficial interest in the Units ...; an acquisition of Units under the LIT's distribution reinvestment plan.
why_it_matters: Unlike several peer policies, there is no express exclusion for a secured lender's enforcement sale on default, so a forced sale occurring during a Black-out Period risks being treated as a breach; the bank's default remedies need bespoke clearance planning.

clause: A clearance to trade is valid for five (5) business days.
why_it_matters: Any clearance obtained for the hedge or loan legs lapses after 5 business days, requiring tight coordination of execution timing with the bank.

clause: LIT Partners and LIT Persons may trade in a LIT's Units provided ... the trade has been executed in accordance with the LIT Partner's trading policy, procedures and/or controls which have been agreed with the Responsible Entity.
why_it_matters: If administration of the LIT involves a LIT Partner, ordinary trades follow that partner's own policy, but the collar and loan (as clause 6 restricted trading) must still be cleared through the Responsible Entity's own Trading Request Procedure and Company Secretary.

clause: Where the Responsible Entity undertakes a buy-back of units in a LIT, the EQT Persons who have knowledge of the buy-back and are involved in the day to day management of the buy-back, are subject to a further Black-out Period commencing from the date the Responsible Entity makes the decision to buy-back the units in a LIT, to the next full business day after the buy-back has been completed.
why_it_matters: Personnel managing a unit buy-back face an additional, event-driven blackout on top of the standard periodic Black-out Periods, further narrowing available execution windows for the collar.

topic: Connected Persons clear through the EQT/LIT Person
clause: a Connected Person must seek clearance through their EQT Person, LIT Person or LIT Partner in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure prior to trading in Units.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the regime, since the Connected Person must clear through the same EQT/LIT Person channel.

clause: does not include a bona fide mortgage over the securities
why_it_matters: A genuine security interest granted over vested shares that does not replicate the margin loan definition's loan-to-value/forced-sale mechanic may fall outside the 'Dealing' concept entirely, potentially letting the loan leg of a collar be documented without clearance or Prohibited Period restriction.

clause: a facility that provides for the borrowing of money against the value of Starpharma securities, where the loan is secured by those Starpharma securities, and the lender may be entitled, or the client may be required, to dispose of some of the Starpharma securities to reduce the loan-to-value ratio of the facility.
why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on the collared shares with any loan-to-value top-up or forced-sale right is squarely banned as a margin loan; the facility must be structured without that feature to avoid the outright prohibition in 3(f).

clause: key management personnel (including Directors) and their closely related parties are prohibited from entering into Hedging Transactions by the Corporations Act 2001.
why_it_matters: Even for vested, unrestricted holdings, KMP and their closely related parties (a wider class than the policy's own 'associate') face a separate statutory hedging ban that must be checked independently of this policy.

clause: If it is not a Prohibited Period, unless you are a Designated Person or Director, you are permitted to trade in Starpharma securities without prior approval provided you have given at least 48 hours’ notice
why_it_matters: Executives eligible for a collar are almost always Designated Persons or Directors, so in practice they face a discretionary, refusable approval regime rather than the lighter notice-only regime available to rank-and-file employees.

clause: if clearance to trade is refused, you must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: A bank counterparty cannot be told why a collar clearance was refused, which complicates diligence and timing certainty for trade execution.

clause: Securities include: ... any other financial products traded on ASX.
why_it_matters: The formal 'Securities' definition is limited to ASX-traded products, but the standalone Prohibited Period ban on 'derivative products' has no such limit; treat an OTC-only put/call collar as caught out of caution given the express, unqualified reference to derivative products.

clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
why_it_matters: Even a fully compliant, adequately disclosed collar could be refused clearance if it might be perceived by the market as the executive exploiting their position, a subjective and unappealable filter.

clause: Restricted Persons must not under any circumstances: (1) enter into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; or (2) transfer securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar for any director, KMP or senior executive is banned outright with no clearance or exceptional-circumstances carve-out; 4.2's hardship exemption applies only to blackout-period dealing, not to this separate, unconditional ban.

clause: a disposal of securities of the Company by employees other than Restricted Persons, that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: Employees below Restricted Person status are not banned from margin lending, but they are unlikely to be the audience for a bank-funded collar, which is typically offered to directors and senior executives who are Restricted Persons.

clause: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: A purchased put and written call collar is squarely 'Hedging' under this broad, instrument-agnostic definition, so the ban on hedging unvested or holding-locked plan securities applies with full force to an OTC structure.

clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: A collar or financing structure engineered to sit just outside the letter of the margin lending or hedging definitions is still likely to be caught if it achieves the same economic effect.

clause: the cleared dealing must occur within 5 business days following clearance (or such other time specified in the clearance), otherwise the clearance is no longer effective and fresh clearance must be sought.
why_it_matters: A collar's derivative legs must be priced and executed within 5 business days of clearance, requiring tight coordination with the bank counterparty.

clause: Table of contents heading '9 Short selling and Hedging' versus the executed section 9, which contains only '9.1 Key Management Personnel are prohibited from short selling the Company’s securities.'
why_it_matters: The executed policy appears to have lost its hedging clause when adapted from a template. There is no operative restriction on hedging vested shares, so an OTC collar's economic-hedge character is not independently banned by a hedging-specific rule and falls to be assessed only under the general securities/dealing definition and the section 6 notification regime.

clause: Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into a margin loan or other security arrangement in respect of the Company's securities, unless they obtain the prior written approval of the Designated Officer (in its absolute discretion).
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that ban only 'margin loans', this reaches any security arrangement over the shares, so the loan leg of a funded collar is not banned outright but is subject to a single discretionary approval gate with no fixed criteria.

clause: Any approval by the Designated Officer may be subject to the condition that the Company be permitted to disclose to the ASX the existence of the margin loan or security arrangement, and where the Company considers appropriate, any relevant terms such as the trigger points or right of the financier to sell unilaterally.
why_it_matters: A bank collar loan approved under section 8 may need to be publicly disclosed, including price triggers or the bank's unilateral sale rights, which affects deal confidentiality and market-signalling risk.

clause: “securities” includes: ... (h) any derivatives including but not limited to options in respect of any of (a) to (f) above.
why_it_matters: There is no venue limitation, so an OTC-only put and call collar is unambiguously 'securities'/'dealing', subject to the ordinary notification (open period) or Designated Officer approval (Prohibited Period) regime.

clause: Key Management Personnel must, prior to dealing in the Company's securities, provide the Company Secretary on behalf of the Designated Officer written notification ... of their intention to deal
why_it_matters: Outside a Prohibited Period, entering the collar's option legs requires only prior notice, not discretionary approval, which is comparatively favourable for timing certainty relative to policies requiring consent for every trade.

clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights under a loan agreement
why_it_matters: If the bank as secured lender needs to enforce and sell the collared shares, that disposal is expressly excluded from the Prohibited Period ban and the general notification requirement, reducing enforcement friction relative to policies that treat a lender's forced sale as a breach.

clause: derivatives and other financial products issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares, debentures and options.
why_it_matters: An OTC put and call written by a bank are expressly 'Company Securities' under the policy's own definition, so a funded collar's option legs are unambiguously regulated as ordinary dealings rather than falling into a definitional gap.

topic: hedging folded into dealing, no vesting concept
clause: entering into agreements or transactions which operate to limit the economic risk of a person's holdings in Company Securities
why_it_matters: There is no separate hedging ban and no vesting- or holding-lock-based prohibition, since the policy has no equity incentive plan restriction concept at all; a collar is simply an ordinary deal requiring Chairman/Board/Managing Director approval (Key Management Personnel) or notification (other employees).

clause: The Policy contains no clause addressing margin loans, security arrangements, encumbrance or secured financing anywhere in its text.
why_it_matters: This 2010-era policy is silent on margin lending, pledges, charges or any other secured financing; the loan leg of a funded collar is not restricted, approved or even contemplated, which is unusually favourable but also means there is no established approval process or disclosure condition the bank can rely on.

clause: The Policy contains no clause restricting short-term or speculative trading and no minimum-holding-period provision.
why_it_matters: There is no tenor constraint on the collar or its unwind analogous to the 3-month rules common in more modern policies.

clause: Employees who are not Key Management Personnel may deal in Company Securities at any time provided the Employee notifies the Company Secretary before commencing the transaction
why_it_matters: Only directors, executives, senior managers and AASB 124 KMP face the approval and Closed Period regime; the likely audience for a bank-funded collar sits within this tier and so faces the fuller regime.

clause: PDMRs or Applicable Employees are prohibited at all times from Dealing in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's Securities (including, but not limited to, hedge arrangements). For the avoidance of doubt this clause does not apply to an option over unissued capital granted by the Company.
why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies that merely require clearance for a derivative, SVM bans PDMRs and Applicable Employees from any financial product created over the shares at all times, including outside Closed Periods; a bank-written put and call collar is squarely caught and there is no clearance route to permit it — the only listed carve-out is a Company-granted employee option, not a third-party derivative.

clause: PDMRs or Applicable Employees are prohibited at all times from entering into margin lending or similar arrangements in respect to Company Securities they hold or in which they have a Relevant Interest.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is banned outright and permanently, not just during Closed Periods, and the 'similar arrangements' language is broad enough to catch most secured-lending structures against the shares, with no clearance or exceptional-circumstances override in this section.

clause: details of all contracts (other than contracts to which the Company is a party) to which the PDMR is a party or under which the PDMR is entitled to a benefit, and that confer a right to call for or deliver shares in ... the Company
why_it_matters: Even if a collar or financing arrangement were otherwise permissible, the put/call contracts with the bank would likely need to be disclosed to the Company Secretary as PDMR disclosures under Schedule 5 and reported to ASX/AIM/the FCA, increasing transparency and timing constraints around any such structure.

clause: Under MAR, dealings in Company securities over EUR5,000 within a calendar year by PDMRs or a PCA must be notified promptly, and in any event within three (3) business days, on AIM and to the FCA through its website.
why_it_matters: Any dealing that were somehow permitted would trigger public MAR disclosure of the transaction to the market within 3 business days, and a UK AIM Rule 7 lock-in agreement (if any) could independently block Closed Period sale clearance.

clause: the exercise (but not the sale of securities following exercise) of an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme ... where the final date for the exercise ... falls during a Closed Period
why_it_matters: The policy has no separate unvested/holding-locked share category for hedging purposes; the section 6.3 and 6.4 bans apply identically 'at all times' regardless of vesting status, so there is no window where hedging or financing becomes available merely because shares have vested.

clause: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars)
why_it_matters: The Policy's own Derivatives definition expressly names 'collars', so a purchased put/written call structure is unambiguously caught and follows the 7.2 vesting-state rules (banned unvested/locked, clearance-only once vested and unrestricted).

clause: Margin Loan ... means any lending or similar arrangement allowing a person to borrow money to invest in securities using existing investments as security.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar (borrowing against the collared shares) plausibly falls within 'similar funding arrangement' under 7.5(b) even though the loan proceeds are not being used to buy more securities, creating a real risk the financing leg is banned outright with no approval route.

clause: A person who possesses Inside Information is prohibited from trading and this applies even where ... Disposal Consent has been given under this Policy (whether in exceptional circumstances or otherwise).
why_it_matters: Any collar entry, unwind or settlement remains unlawful if the executive holds inside information, regardless of any clearance already obtained from the Chair.

clause: Buy or sell orders for Company Securities which are placed but not completed outside of a Black-out Period ... the order must be completed within five trading days otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
why_it_matters: If a Black-out Period commences while a collar leg is still executing, the unexecuted portion must complete within five trading days or lapse, and cannot be re-struck, constraining execution timing.

clause: The Company may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on Dealing ... even where the proposed Dealing would otherwise take place outside a Black-out Period ... must be kept strictly confidential.
why_it_matters: An undisclosed ad-hoc restriction can block collar entry, roll or unwind at any time with no visibility to the bank counterparty.

topic: no stated clearance validity or SLA
clause: clause 6 approval regime contains no stated response timeframe and no stated expiry period for an approval to Deal (contrast the Disposal Consent under 5.2, which is issued for 'a specified time period')
why_it_matters: Absent a defined clearance window, the executive and bank cannot rely on a fixed execution period once approval is granted, adding timing risk to trade date certainty.

clause: Where Company Securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that treat a secured lender's enforcement sale as a serious breach, this Policy expressly treats it as lawful and excepted at any time, including in a Prohibited Period, which materially de-risks the bank's enforcement mechanics under a funded collar.

topic: margin loan funding of option exercise
clause: where the exercise price of options is being provided by a margin loan or other form of lending arrangement then there may be a risk that the Restricted Person may need to sell shares to avoid providing additional capital or security to the lender in the event of a decrease in the value of the shares.
why_it_matters: The Board evidently tolerates debt-funded, share-secured arrangements involving Company Securities generally, supporting the view that a bank loan secured on collared vested shares is not itself objectionable under this Policy.

clause: The placing of orders is prohibited. Restricted Persons must accept the bid or the asking price matching the available number of shares that are bid or offered when trading in the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: This on-market execution constraint should not apply to a privately negotiated OTC collar with a bank, but would constrain any on-market delta-hedge or true-up trade the Restricted Person executes personally.

clause: The Policy does not distinguish unvested, vested-but-locked, or vested-unrestricted Company Securities anywhere in the operative dealing rules.
why_it_matters: There is no express carve-out barring a collar or security interest over unvested performance rights/shares, though in practice a lender would still require vested, unencumbered shares capable of being charged.

clause: PDMRs are prohibited at all times from Dealing in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's Securities (including, but not limited to, hedge arrangements). For the avoidance of doubt this paragraph does not apply to an option over unissued capital granted by the Company.
why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC collar is squarely a 'financial product ... in respect of' the Company's Securities and is banned outright for PDMRs at all times, with no vesting-state carve-out and no clearance route; the only carve-out is for options the Company itself grants under its incentive plans.

clause: PDMRs are prohibited at all times from entering into margin lending or similar arrangements in respect to Company Securities they hold or in which they have a Relevant Interest.
why_it_matters: A loan secured on the PDMR's collared shares (even fully vested) falls within 'similar arrangements' to margin lending and is banned outright with no clearance path, closing off the funded leg entirely for PDMRs.

clause: Sections 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 13 also apply to PCAs of PDMRs, meaning, for each PDMR, PDMRs must take appropriate steps to ensure that their PCAs do not breach this Policy.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled company does not escape the derivatives or secured financing bans, since the PDMR is responsible for ensuring the PCA also complies.

clause: details of all contracts (other than contracts to which the Company is a party) to which the PDMR is a party or under which the PDMR is entitled to a benefit, and that confer a right to call for or deliver shares in, debentures of, or interests in a managed investment scheme made available by, the Company
why_it_matters: Any option/forward contract referencing Company shares, including a bank collar, would itself need to be disclosed to the Company within 1 business day of entry, change or the PDMR ceasing to hold office, even if the Company were not otherwise consulted.

clause: The Approving Officer may give clearance during a Closed Period for a PDMR to sell (but not buy) Company shares (but not other Company Securities) in Exceptional Circumstances.
why_it_matters: Even the narrow hardship/court-order relief is limited to selling ordinary shares; it gives no route to enter, unwind or settle a derivative during a Closed Period.

clause: This document is headed 'Securities Trading Policy, October 2016' for Prairie Mining Limited (now GreenX Metals Limited, ASX: GRX), and refers to dual ASX/LSE/Warsaw listings, UK MAR and FCA notification.
why_it_matters: As the only policy text available it has been extracted in full, but given its age and the Company's apparent rebrand and any subsequent LSE/WSE delisting, the current policy in force should be confirmed before relying on this analysis.

topic: Company Securities definition narrower than PC2-style policies
clause: Company Securities includes shares, options, warrants, derivatives and interests in shares (including vested options and vested performance share rights) linked in any way to the underlying price of shares in the Company.
why_it_matters: Only 'vested' options/performance rights are called out; the definition does not say 'vested or unvested', creating ambiguity as to whether unvested equity awards are 'Company Securities' at all, even though clause 7.3(a) still refers to Company Securities 'which are unvested'. A collar should in any event only be structured over vested shares, but this drafting gap adds uncertainty for any unvested-related structuring.

clause: The Policy contains no dedicated Derivatives section (contrast PC2-style policies); an OTC derivative is regulated only via the Company Securities definition and, where it limits economic risk, the 'protection arrangements' ban in 7.3.
why_it_matters: Absent an express blanket ban on derivatives over unvested equity, the analysis for a collar rests entirely on whether it is a 'protection arrangement' under 7.3, which a purchased put/written call collar squarely is given it operates to limit economic risk.

clause: Margin Loan ... means any lending or similar arrangement allowing a person to borrow money to invest in securities using existing investments as security.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar plausibly falls within 'similar funding arrangement' under 7.4(b) even though the loan proceeds are not used to buy more securities, creating a real risk the financing leg is banned outright with no approval route.

clause: The designated Black-out Periods in clause 3.2(b) cover quarterly, half-year and full-year results and Chair-determined periods, but do not include a fixed period around the Annual General Meeting (unlike some comparable policies).
why_it_matters: There is one fewer scheduled closed window to plan collar entry, roll or unwind around, though ad-hoc Black-out Periods can still be declared by the Chair at any time.

clause: must be kept strictly confidential by the Designated Person and not disclosed to any other person (unless otherwise required by law or the ASX Listing Rules).
why_it_matters: An ASX Listing Rule disclosure obligation (e.g. a director's interest notice) could require public disclosure of a Disposal Consent used to unwind or settle a collar, despite the general confidentiality requirement.

topic: margin loans permitted with clearance, not banned
clause: You must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
why_it_matters: Unlike many comparable ASX policies that ban margin lending/secured financing outright, this Policy merely requires clearance, materially improving the prospects for a funded-collar loan secured on the Restricted Person's shares.

clause: a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default or margin call is expressly excluded from the trading restrictions (including the Blackout Period regime) and needs no fresh clearance, materially de-risking enforcement mechanics.

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested entitlements
clause: You are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.
why_it_matters: The absolute hedging ban only bites on unvested equity remuneration; a collar over vested, unencumbered shares needs only ordinary clearance under 8.1, not an outright bar.

clause: The Company Secretary will maintain a register of clearances given in accordance with this section 7, and must report all clearances given to the Board at its next following meeting.
why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, there is no explicit personal obligation on the Restricted Person to notify the Company Secretary after dealing; any director-level ASX/Corporations Act notification obligations apply independently of this Policy.

clause: The Policy contains no clause restricting short-term or speculative dealing.
why_it_matters: There is no minimum holding period or anti-speculation objection that could otherwise constrain the tenor of a collar.

clause: Clauses 4 and 5 (Blackout period; Exceptional circumstances) cross-reference 'the procedure for prior written clearance described in section 7', while the clearance procedure is itself headed as section 6 and the exceptions list as section 7.
why_it_matters: Likely a drafting artefact from renumbering; it does not change the substantive rule that clearance must always be sought before trading, including during a Prohibited Period.

clause: This document is a 13 July 2020 ASX announcement by Golden Rim Resources Ltd (ASX: GMR), the entity that appears to now trade as AS1.
why_it_matters: As the only policy text available it has been extracted in full, but its age and the apparent company rename/ticker change warrant confirming the current policy in force before relying on this analysis.

clause: Sections 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3 of this Policy do not apply to the following types of dealings (Exempt Transactions).
why_it_matters: The absolute 4.3 ban on derivatives and economic-risk-limiting transactions only lifts for the seven listed Exempt Transactions (family/super transfers, takeover disposals, pro-rata/DRP/bonus/incentive-scheme acquisitions), none of which cover a bank-written collar.

clause: Arrangements prohibited include: (a) entering into a lending arrangement in respect of CUP securities; (b) transferring CUP securities into an existing margin loan account; or (c) selling CUP securities to satisfy a call under a margin loan except where the holder of the CUP securities has no control over the sale.
why_it_matters: A bank loan secured by pledge of the collared shares falls within limb (a) as a 'lending arrangement in respect of CUP securities' and is banned outright, so the loan leg of a funded collar cannot be secured on CUP shares; even if it existed, a lender-forced sale is only excused where the executive has no control over that sale.

clause: Any Employee holding CUP securities subject to binding restrictions on transfer, either as ASX restricted securities or through voluntary escrow arrangements, must comply with the terms of any applicable escrow arrangements and will be unable to Trade in the relevant CUP securities during that time.
why_it_matters: Vested shares still under ASX or voluntary escrow cannot be pledged, sold or have derivatives written over them for a collar until the escrow period ends.

clause: If approval is granted in writing in accordance with this section, the Employee must complete the Trade within 7 days of receiving such approval, or such earlier time as determined. Approval may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
why_it_matters: Even for a Trade type that were clearable, execution would need to complete within 7 days and could be revoked before signing if inside information emerges, compressing the window to price and execute any collar leg.

clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement. In this circumstance, the Designated Officer or Employee must have informed the Board of the Company prior to entering into such an arrangement over the securities.
why_it_matters: A bank loan secured by pledge of COG shares (the loan leg of a funded collar) is not prohibited; it only requires Board notification before the pledge is granted, after which the bank's enforcement sale is Excluded Trading even during a Closed Period.

clause: Company Securities includes shares in the Company, options over those shares and any other financial products of the Company whether traded on ASX or unlisted.
why_it_matters: Put and call options (the two collar legs) are expressly captured regardless of listing status, so they are subject to the ordinary dealing/Closed Period/clearance rules; a CFD or swap is more doubtful since the residual limb is confined to products 'of the Company'.

topic: no clearance needed outside Closed Period
clause: a Designated Officer may only deal in Company Securities outside of a Closed Period unless Written Clearance has been obtained under Paragraph 11.
why_it_matters: Outside the two Closed Periods (and any ad hoc Listing Rule 3.1A period), a Designated Officer can enter, unwind or roll a collar without any clearance step, only the general insider trading prohibition applies.

clause: An Employee who deals in the company's securities should use only one broker. Employees may not use broker credit unless written approval has been obtained from the Board of the Company prior to execution of such credit.
why_it_matters: Execution of the option legs through a bank counterparty may need to route through a single nominated broker, and any broker credit used in the structure needs prior Board approval.

topic: always-on pre-clearance for Directors and ELT
clause: At all times, members of the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) and all Employees who report directly to the ELT must submit a request for approval in writing ... to the Chief Executive Officer before trading ... Directors must submit a request for approval in writing ... to the Chairman before trading.
why_it_matters: Unlike ordinary Employees, a Director or ELT member needs written pre-approval before every trade at any time of year, so each leg of a collar (entry, roll or unwind) requires case-by-case Chairman/CEO sign-off regardless of the Closed Period calendar.

clause: Executive and non-executive Directors are not permitted to enter into transactions with Securities (or any derivative thereof) in associated products which limit the economic risk of any unvested entitlements under any equity-based remuneration schemes offered by the Company.
why_it_matters: The derivative/hedging ban binds only Directors and only over unvested equity-incentive entitlements; it does not reach a Director's vested, unrestricted shares or restrict ELT/other Employees at all, so a funded collar over vested shares is not caught by this clause for any tier.

topic: no notice condition on secured lending
clause: a disposal of securities of the entity that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: This Policy, unlike some peers, does not require prior notice to the Board before entering a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement, and a lender's enforcement sale is excluded from the trading restrictions outright, reducing procedural friction for a bank-secured loan leg.

topic: narrow Securities definition excludes third-party derivatives
clause: Securities include Shares as well as options, warrants, debentures, and any other security on issue from time to time.
why_it_matters: Because 'Securities' is limited to instruments issued by the Company, a bank-written OTC put/call or CFD referencing SVR shares arguably falls outside the Policy's dealing, insider-trading and Closed Period machinery altogether, other than the general legal insider-trading prohibition.

clause: senior staff members / designated officers of the Company will be prohibited from entering into transactions in financial products which operate to limit the economic risk of both vested or unvested holdings in the PPS securities.
why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, this expressly bans Directors and KMP from any transaction limiting the economic risk of already-vested, unrestricted holdings, not just unvested entitlements, so the put/call legs of a collar are prohibited outright for this tier regardless of vesting status.

clause: As a minimum requirement, whether or not a Closed Period ... or Trading Ban is in place, all staff who wish to trade must submit a request in writing to the Company Secretary prior to trading in PPS Securities.
why_it_matters: Every trade by every Director or Staff member needs prior written clearance valid for at most 10 trading days, so even where hedging is not separately banned, both entry and unwind of a collar leg must be freshly cleared and executed within a short window.

clause: The existence of a trading ban outside a Closed Period need not be published generally.
why_it_matters: The Board can impose an undisclosed trading ban at any time, creating timing risk that a cleared collar transaction could become unexecutable without public notice.

clause: (not addressed anywhere in the policy)
why_it_matters: The policy is silent on margin lending, encumbrance and secured financing, so a bank loan secured on the collared shares faces no policy-specific procedural barrier beyond the general trading clearance and short-term-trading ban.

clause: Restricted Persons must not deal at any time in financial products such as derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps, contracts for difference or other financial products issued or created over or associated with Company securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions.
why_it_matters: Directors and KMP are absolutely banned from any third-party derivative over Company securities, with no clearance or exemption route (other than a listed-portfolio/index carve-out), which directly and completely prohibits the put and call legs of a funded collar.

topic: secured financing other than margin loans expressly permitted
clause: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where Company securities may be included as security.
why_it_matters: Unlike the derivatives ban, the margin lending prohibition is expressly confined to margin loans; a loan secured on the collared shares that is not classified as a margin loan is not itself prohibited for Restricted Persons.

clause: An exception applies where Company securities form a component of a listed portfolio or index product.
why_it_matters: Only an exchange-traded fund or index product containing Company securities as one component escapes the derivatives ban; a bespoke single-stock OTC collar with a bank does not qualify.

topic: forward contracts named as short-term dealing
clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a three month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
why_it_matters: Forward contracts are separately flagged as an example of prohibited short-term dealing for all Employees, so even setting aside the Restricted Persons derivatives ban, a forward-style monetisation risks being independently characterised as short-term/speculative dealing.

clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
why_it_matters: Structuring a collar or loan to avoid the letter of the margin lending or derivatives bans would not avoid the restriction if its economic substance is a hedge or a margin loan.

clause: A Restricted Person must not engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to Pacific Current Securities including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of Pacific Current Securities.
why_it_matters: This is a flat, unwaivable ban naming put and call options specifically, so the hedge legs of a collar cannot be entered into by any Director or Senior Executive regardless of vesting state or clearance.

topic: waiver does not reach substantive bans
clause: the Restricted Person must apply to the Authorising Officer described in section 4.3.4 for a waiver from compliance with the provisions in sections 4.3.4 or 4.3.5.
why_it_matters: The only waiver mechanism excuses clearance/notification procedure, not the section 4.3.7 hedging ban itself, so financial hardship cannot be used to obtain a collar exemption.

clause: Restricted Persons must ensure they have sufficient available cash or collateral to meet margin calls, including in periods of volatility.
why_it_matters: Even though the loan leg is permitted with clearance, the bank/borrower must maintain buffer collateral, which is a covenant point for structuring a secured facility.

clause: an involuntary disposal of securities that results from a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement that has previously been approved in accordance with this policy.
why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale under a pre-approved secured facility is excluded from the Blackout Period ban, so the loan (if it existed without the banned hedge) could be enforced at any time without breaching the policy.

clause: Trading consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of inside information prior to trading. ... If approval to trade Pacific Current Securities is refused, the person seeking the approval must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: Any cleared leg of a transaction (e.g. the loan) must complete within 5 trading days and lapses on inside information, and a refusal cannot be disclosed to the bank counterparty.

clause: your associates include: your spouse or partner ... any trustee of a trust ... any company in which you hold (directly or indirectly) a majority of the shares or otherwise control.
why_it_matters: Routing a collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled company does not escape the section 4.3.7 hedging ban, since Associates of Restricted Persons are themselves Restricted Persons.

topic: absolute margin loan and security ban
clause: Any CYM Personnel may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is banned outright for every CYM Personnel (not just Designated Persons) with no approval route and no vesting-state carve-out.

clause: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock; and otherwise, requires approval under clause 6.
why_it_matters: Even if the loan ban were somehow avoided, the put/call hedge itself cannot be written at all over unvested or holding-locked shares, and needs Chair (or Board) approval even over vested unrestricted shares.

clause: a Designated Person may seek written approval from the Chair (Approval Officer) to dispose of or transfer (but not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period
why_it_matters: The only exceptional-circumstances relief covers disposals/transfers during a Black-out Period, not acquiring options, hedging or margin lending, so it cannot be used to unlock a collar structure.

clause: their spouse (including a de facto spouse) or any of their children ... under the age of 18 years; a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with any of those persons; and a trust or company which they or any close family members control or have an interest in.
why_it_matters: Family members, dependants and controlled trusts/companies are themselves Designated Persons, so the margin loan and hedging bans cannot be sidestepped by routing the collar through them.

clause: the Company may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on Dealing ... even where the proposed Dealing would otherwise take place outside a Black-out Period ... must be kept strictly confidential.
why_it_matters: An undisclosed ad-hoc restriction can block an otherwise-cleared transaction (or its unwind) at any time without the executive being told why.

clause: the order must be completed within five trading days otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
why_it_matters: A collar leg placed but not settled before a Black-out Period begins has a hard five-trading-day completion window and cannot be amended, constraining execution timing.

topic: absolute hedging ban outside waiver reach
clause: A Restricted Person must not engage in transactions designed to hedge their exposure to Company Securities.
why_it_matters: This ban has no built-in clearance mechanism (unlike the adjacent margin lending sentence) and the only waiver process in the policy (rule 6.9) is expressly limited to rules 6.5(b)/6.6, so it cannot be used to authorise a hedge.

clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities, unless the prior approval of the Chairman (or his or her delegate) has been obtained.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a structure secured on Company Securities is achievable with Chairman approval, but pairing it with a collar hedge fails because the hedge itself is separately and absolutely banned.

clause: where a Restricted Person has been granted approval to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements (see rule 6.11), an involuntary disposal of securities that results from the margin lender or financier exercising its rights under the arrangement.
why_it_matters: A lender's enforcement sale under a pre-approved secured facility is excepted from the blackout period restriction, so the loan (absent the banned hedge) could be enforced without breaching the policy.

clause: a family company or family trust that the Restricted Person or their close family members may control or have an interest in ... Each Restricted Person must ensure that any trading by their Closely Connected Persons are undertaken in accordance with this policy.
why_it_matters: Routing a collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or family company does not escape the section 6.11 bans, since the Restricted Person remains responsible for their compliance.

clause: The confirmation may specify a period of time within which trading is to occur.
why_it_matters: Any cleared leg of a transaction (e.g. the loan) may be time-boxed by the Company Secretary's confirmation, constraining execution timing.

topic: hedging ban overrides the whole policy
clause: Notwithstanding any other part of this policy, Designated Persons must not at any time enter into transactions in associated products which operate to limit the economic risk of security holdings in the Company.
why_it_matters: The put/call hedge legs of a collar cannot be entered into under any circumstance, including the exceptional-circumstances clearance in clause 8, because clause 11.1 is drafted to prevail over every other provision of the policy.

clause: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where Appen Securities may be included as security.
why_it_matters: Unusually, only 'margin lending arrangements' are banned; a bespoke bank loan secured on the collared shares that is not characterised as a margin loan is not itself restricted by this policy, so the loan leg of a structure is comparatively unconstrained even though the hedge leg is banned outright.

clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: Unlike policies that merely except forced sales from blackout periods, this exclusion removes such a disposal from the operation of the whole policy, so a lender's enforcement sale is not a breach regardless of timing.

clause: securities includes shares in the Company, options over those shares and any other financial products of the Company traded on ASX ... dealing in securities includes ... trading in financial products issued or created over securities of the Company ... entering into transactions in financial products which operate to limit the economic risk of security holdings.
why_it_matters: Although 'Securities' is defined to exclude OTC products (traded-on-ASX only), the separate 'dealing' definition catches OTC derivatives and hedges without a venue limit, so an OTC collar cannot escape the policy by pointing to the narrower securities definition.

clause: "Associates" include your relatives, entities that you control and entities you are acting in concert with.
why_it_matters: A Director cannot structure the collar or loan through a relative or a controlled or concert-party entity to avoid the clause 11.1 hedging ban, since they must take reasonable steps to prevent an associate's contravention that could be attributed to them.

topic: hedging ban confined to ESOP options
clause: No director, officer or employee issued with share options under the Company's Employee Share Option Plan shall enter into arrangements that limit their exposure to losses that would result from share price decreases.
why_it_matters: The only anti-hedging rule in the policy targets unexercised Employee Share Option Plan options, not ordinary vested shares held outright, so a collar over vested, unencumbered shares falls outside its express wording.

clause: This policy applies to all securities issued by the Company from time to time, including ordinary shares, preference shares, debentures, options, convertible notes, etc. ... apply for, acquire, or dispose of securities in the Company
why_it_matters: The policy's substantive prohibitions are framed around securities issued by the Company and buying/selling them; it does not expressly reach a third-party OTC put/call or a bank loan secured on the shares, so the funded collar structure is not obviously regulated by this document at all.

clause: (no provision addressing margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, short selling, stock lending or CFDs appears anywhere in the policy)
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the shares is not restricted by this policy, though the company's general disclosure obligations (ASX Listing Rule 3.19A/3.19B notifiable interests) and the standing duty to advise the Chairman would still apply.

clause: Persons included under this policy must not trade through their family or through a trust or company in which they have influence or control, in circumstances where they would have been prohibited in trading in their own name.
why_it_matters: A collar or loan cannot be routed through a family member, trust or controlled company to escape a restriction that would otherwise apply to the individual.

clause: 2 business days after the release of any ASX announcement.
why_it_matters: Unlike the results-specific blackout weeks, this blackout is triggered by any ASX announcement at all, creating frequent short closed windows that could interrupt entry into or unwind of a collar.

clause: the trading is not likely to be seen by the public, press, other shareholders or ASX to be unfair or inappropriate
why_it_matters: Even where a transaction is not expressly prohibited, the Chairman/Managing Director could decline to countenance a collar or secured loan on the subjective ground that it would look unfair or inappropriate to the market.

clause: Deal and Dealing Covers any type of transaction in a company's securities, including purchases, sales, the exercise of options and using securities as collateral for a loan
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar (pledging vested shares as collateral) is expressly a 'Dealing' requiring prior written clearance from the Company Secretary rather than being prohibited outright, giving a workable path subject to timing and closed-period constraints.

clause: An employee will not ordinarily be given clearance to Deal in Company Securities during any period when there exists any matter which constitutes inside information or during a closed period.
why_it_matters: Entry into, or unwind of, the collar and its secured loan should be scheduled outside closed periods and while the executive holds no inside information, since clearance will not ordinarily be granted otherwise.

clause: If an employee is granted clearance, they must deal within two (2) working days of receiving clearance.
why_it_matters: The collar and loan must be priced and executed within a 2 working-day window of clearance, requiring tight coordination between the bank and the executive's clearance application.

clause: The employee must request that their PCAs do not Deal ... in Company Securities during Closed Periods and not to deal on consideration of a short-term nature. A sale of Company Securities which were acquired less than a year previously will be dealing of a short-term nature.
why_it_matters: If the collar or its unwind is routed through a PCA (e.g. spouse or family trust), the PDMR must ask the PCA to avoid disposals within 12 months of acquisition, so a tenor of at least a year is advisable where associates are involved.

clause: If an employee acts as the trustee of a trust, they must speak to the Company Secretary about their obligations in respect of any Dealing in Company Securities carried out by the trustee(s) of the trust.
why_it_matters: If the collar or loan is booked through a family trust of which the executive is trustee, separate consultation with the Company Secretary is required before dealing.

clause: An employee should seek further guidance from the Company Secretary before transaction in: ... Financial instruments which provide exposure to a portfolio of assets which has or may have an exposure to Company Securities
why_it_matters: Even indirect derivative exposure to the Company's shares (as in a bank-structured product referencing a basket including the stock) should be pre-cleared with the Company Secretary.

clause: Notifiable Transaction ... captures every transaction which changes a PDMR's or PCA's holding of Company Securities, even if the transaction does not require clearance under this code.
why_it_matters: If collar settlement or loan enforcement changes the PDMR's shareholding, it must be notified to the Company (and ASX/FCA as applicable) even in circumstances where fresh clearance was not required.

clause: “Healius Securities” means the following types of securities: ... any other securities of Healius including debentures, options, rights, derivatives or any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market.
why_it_matters: If a bespoke bilateral OTC put and call with a bank is not itself 'able to be traded on a financial market', it may fall outside the definition of Healius Securities altogether, which would place the collar's derivative legs outside the trading-window and clearance regime (though the general insider trading prohibition in Clause 3 still applies to the underlying shares).

clause: Prohibited Persons must not enter into a hedging arrangement, or enter into any other arrangement which limits the economic risk related to any Healius Securities.
why_it_matters: The purchased put and written call that form the collar are squarely an arrangement limiting economic risk in Healius Securities and are expressly and absolutely banned for every Prohibited Person, with no vesting-state carve-out and no clearance or exemption route, which is a threshold obstacle independent of how the loan is structured.

clause: a disposal of Healius Securities on-market that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
why_it_matters: A bank's on-market enforcement sale of the collared shares following a loan default is automatically exempt from the closed-period prohibition, so the bank's enforcement rights are not blocked by trading windows even if the executive is otherwise restricted at the time of enforcement.

topic: exceptional circumstances gate for closed-period clearance
clause: “exceptional circumstances” are: (i) severe financial hardship; (ii) a pressing financial commitment that cannot reasonably be satisfied otherwise than by selling the Healius Securities; (iii) an arm's-length party exercising contractual rights to require the Prohibited Person to buy or sell; or (iv) any other circumstances the designated decision-maker deems exceptional.
why_it_matters: Outside an open trading window, discretionary collar or loan entry is not automatically clearable; it would need to be brought within one of these narrow exceptional-circumstances categories (or a decision-maker's residual discretion) or else wait for the next open window.

clause: Either the Managing Director of Healius or the Directors may at any time partly or wholly restrict the trading windows in paragraphs A-E inclusive of Clause 6.1, during which restrictions all of the provisions of Clause 6.2 of this document apply despite the fact that a trading window is open.
why_it_matters: A collar entry timed for an open trading window can be abruptly converted into a closed period at the discretion of the Managing Director or the Board, adding execution timing risk.

topic: no liability / no representation on clearance
clause: The terms of this Policy, and actions taken by any person under or in reliance on it, including dealing ... on the basis of a prior written clearance ... do not constitute a representation or approval by or on behalf of Healius about the legality or appropriateness of the relevant dealing and Healius is not liable to the person so dealing.
why_it_matters: Obtaining trading-window clearance for the collar does not immunise the executive (or the bank as counterparty) from underlying insider trading liability, which Healius expressly disclaims responsibility for.

clause: The Directors require that in interpreting the terms of this Policy ... Prohibited Persons and designated decision-makers follow the rules of interpretation in ASX Listing Rule 19.2, namely: ... by looking beyond form to substance.
why_it_matters: Any argument that the OTC collar is not 'hedging' in form is unlikely to succeed given the express substance-over-form interpretive mandate, reinforcing that Clause 6.5 will be read to catch the collar's economic effect.

clause: (c) transfers of Healius Securities from a Prohibited Person to an (d) an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme ...
why_it_matters: Clause 6.3(c) is incomplete/truncated in the version of the policy lodged with ASX, leaving its scope unknowable; it should not be relied on as an exemption for the collar structure without clarification from the Company Secretary.

clause: Derivatives include: (a) derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars); and (b) any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
why_it_matters: The Policy expressly names 'collars' as an example of a regulated Derivative, confirming that a bank-structured collar is squarely caught by clause 6.2's vesting-based prohibition/permission regime rather than needing to rely on a general dealing-definition sweep.

topic: absolute margin loan / secured financing ban
clause: Designated Persons may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.
why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar (borrowing against, or pledging, the collared shares) is an outright prohibition for Designated Persons with no clearance path, no listed exception and no vesting-state carve-out, which independently defeats the funded structure even where the derivative legs would otherwise be permitted on vested, unrestricted shares.

topic: derivatives permitted on vested unrestricted shares
clause: Derivatives may be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy.
why_it_matters: An unfunded collar (put and call without a secured loan) could be entered on vested shares free of a Holding Lock, subject to prior Chair/Board approval, timing outside Black-out Periods, and post-dealing notification to the Company Secretary.

clause: Buy or sell orders for Company Securities which are placed but not completed outside of a Black-out Period are subject to the following restrictions once the Black-out Period commences: the order must be completed within five trading days otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
why_it_matters: If collar orders are placed but not completed before a Black-out Period commences, they must complete within five trading days or lapse and cannot be varied, creating execution risk for multi-leg trades straddling a blackout.

clause: In exceptional circumstances a Designated Person may seek written approval from the Chair (Approval Officer) to dispose of or transfer (but not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period (Disposal Consent).
why_it_matters: Even in hardship or court-order circumstances, the Chair may only consent to a disposal or transfer, not an acquisition or other dealing, so it cannot be used to authorise entry into a collar or a secured loan during a Black-out Period.

clause: Designated Personnel are prohibited from dealing in any financial products issued or created over the Securities by third parties, or dealing in associated products.
why_it_matters: This clause targets bank-structured products referencing the Company's shares directly; it independently and absolutely prohibits a Designated Person from entering an OTC put/call with a bank regardless of vesting state, with no listed exemption or clearance route.

clause: Designated Personnel may not enter into a transaction that operates to limit the economic risk of their securityholding in the Company.
why_it_matters: This is a freestanding hedging ban additional to the third-party product ban; it would independently catch the put/call legs of a collar even if structured as a bilateral contract rather than a 'financial product issued by a third party'.

clause: Employees and directors are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Securities as the terms may require the Securities be sold when the employee or director possesses inside information.
why_it_matters: The stated rationale (forced-sale risk while holding inside information) is not conceptually limited to conventional margin lenders and would apply with equal force to a bank loan secured on the collared shares, so the ban should likely be read to extend to any securities-backed financing even though only 'margin lending' is named.

clause: that dealing must be completed within 7 days from the date of the clearance, unless it specifies otherwise.
why_it_matters: Both the ordinary clearance and the exceptional-circumstances approval require any permitted dealing to complete within 7 days of clearance, requiring tight coordination with the bank for any leg of a structure that is not itself independently banned.

clause: Where the Board or the Chairperson of the Board notifies a Designated Person in writing that they are subject to a blacklist in relation to the securities of a particular entity (Blacklisted Securities), that person must not deal in the Blacklisted Securities from the time period specified in the notice.
why_it_matters: If the bank counterparty itself, or a related entity, were ever the subject of a blacklist notice to the executive (e.g. due to a related transaction giving rise to inside information about the bank), dealing with that bank could be independently blocked.

clause: Non-compliance with this Policy will be considered as serious misconduct and may result in disciplinary action and/or termination of employment or engagement.
why_it_matters: Breach of the section 4.3 bans through a collar structure exposes the executive to disciplinary action including termination, independent of any separate insider trading liability.

clause: Securities... Includes shares (ordinary shares and reset preference shares), options, rights, convertible notes, derivatives and any other financial product able to be traded on PNGX and / or ASX or another stock exchange, whether or not such securities are created by the STC Group or issued or created by or directly associated with any proposed transaction involving the STC Group (including margin lending or collars).
why_it_matters: This is an unusually explicit textual hook: the Policy expressly names 'collars' and 'margin lending' as within-scope transactions, closing off any argument that a bespoke bank-issued OTC collar or secured loan falls outside the definition merely because it is not itself listed or exchange-tradable.

clause: Means any acquisition, disposal or transfer of, or offer to acquire, dispose of or transfer, or creation of pledge, charge or any other security interest in, any securities of STC or any entity whose assets solely or substantially comprise securities of STC...
why_it_matters: Granting security over the collared shares to the bank is expressly a 'Dealing' in its own right, triggering the full Blackout Period/Trading Window and notification/consent regime for that step alone, separately from the derivative legs.

topic: absolute hedging ban for Directors/Senior Executives
clause: must not engage in transactions or arrangements in products which operate to limit the economic risk in STC's Securities held by a Director or Senior Executive e.g. hedging
why_it_matters: Regardless of Trading Window timing, Directors and Senior Executives are absolutely prohibited from any transaction or arrangement that limits the economic risk of their STC shareholding, which independently bars the put/call legs of a collar for this tier with no clearance route at all.

clause: enter into a margin lending arrangement only if they have compiled with this Code (in particular, in regards to restrictions on transactions in products which operate to limit the economic risk of holding STC's Securities)
why_it_matters: Unlike peer policies with an outright margin-lending ban, STC expressly contemplates Directors/Senior Executives entering margin lending arrangements provided they otherwise comply with the Code, so the loan leg is not itself prohibited — though it cannot be paired with a risk-limiting derivative given the absolute hedging ban.

clause: The Chairman, Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, Managing Director or Company Secretary (as applicable) will generally refuse consent for a Director or Senior Executive to apply for, buy or sell STC Securities or enter into transactions or arrangements in risk limiting products during a Blackout Period unless special circumstances exist.
why_it_matters: Outside a Trading Window (and during any Blackout Period), consent to deal is generally refused absent special circumstances such as financial hardship, so execution timing for any permitted leg (e.g. the loan) is effectively confined to the 6-week Trading Windows following results announcements or the AGM.

clause: The restrictions on Dealings by a Relevant Person contained in this Code will be regarded as equally applicable to any dealings by the Relevant Person's Connected Person. It is the duty of the Relevant Person, therefore, to seek to avoid any such Dealing at a time when he or she is not free to deal.
why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family member, controlled company or discretionary trust does not avoid the Code: dealings by a Connected Person are treated as the Relevant Person's own.

clause: an involuntary disposal of securities that results from a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement that has previously been approved in accordance with this policy
why_it_matters: If the bank's loan is pre-approved as a secured financing arrangement, its enforcement sale of the collared shares is an excluded dealing that can proceed even during a blackout period, materially de-risking enforcement of the collar's security.

clause: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that would have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with Company Securities including Securities which are unvested, subject to a holding lock or issued pursuant to an equity-based remuneration scheme.
why_it_matters: Confirms the hedging ban (and hence any collar) reaches unvested and holding-locked incentive securities, not just freely tradeable shares, so prior written approval is required regardless of vesting status.

clause: Trading consent is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of inside information prior to trading.
why_it_matters: A cleared collar could become unexecutable if inside information arises between approval and signing or settlement.

clause: Any approval to trade can be given, withdrawn or refused by the Company in its discretion without giving any reasons. A decision to refuse approval is final and binding ... the person seeking the approval must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
why_it_matters: The bank or executive cannot compel approval of the collar or challenge a refusal, and the executive cannot disclose a refusal to the bank without itself breaching the policy.

clause: Restricted Persons must ensure they have sufficient available cash or collateral to meet any margin calls in relation to any approved margin loans, including in periods of volatility.
why_it_matters: Even with an approved loan, the executive bears an ongoing obligation to maintain collateral buffers, relevant to sizing the collar/loan LVR.

clause: If granted, trading consent is only valid for a period of 5 business days after notification of approval.
why_it_matters: The put/call trade and loan drawdown must occur within 5 business days of clearance, or fresh clearance must be sought.

clause: provide prior written notice of their intention to deal ... obtain prior written clearance ... at least two trading days before the proposed dealing.
why_it_matters: Collar execution must be scheduled at least two trading days after the clearance application, adding lead time to any bank transaction timetable.

clause: Key Management Personnel are prohibited from trading during the Closed Period in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: The put and call legs of a collar are barred outright for KMP inside a Closed Period, and 4.5's flat prohibition makes no reference to the 4.2 exceptional-circumstances approval route available for ordinary share trades.

topic: no preclearance regime outside closed periods
clause: Employees intending to deal in the Company's securities should, prior to so dealing, enquire of the Company Secretary or the Chairman as to whether any announcements of price sensitive information are anticipated.
why_it_matters: Outside the twice-yearly Closed Periods there is no mandatory preclearance system for KMP or other employees, so the collar's derivative legs, margin loan, and any sale can be executed without seeking company approval, subject only to actually possessing inside information.

clause: should not enter into margin loans which could cause a forced trade by a margin lender during a Closed Period.
why_it_matters: Framed as a 'should not,' not an outright ban, with no consent or notification requirement, so a loan secured on RHI shares appears permissible provided its terms would not force a lender sale during a Closed Period.

clause: Trading is prohibited at any time if the Employee possesses inside information, irrespective of whether it is outside the Closed Period or is excluded from operation of this policy.
why_it_matters: Even a fully off-Closed-Period or exception-based collar or loan transaction remains void if the executive or the bank's counterpart possesses inside information at signing.

clause: the exercise of an option, where the final date for the exercise of an option, falls during a prohibited period and the Company has had a number of consecutive Closed Periods to the extent that the Key Management Person could not reasonably have been expected to exercise the options at a point in time in which they were able to do so.
why_it_matters: Relevant if the collar is written over unvested options nearing expiry, since the policy permits exercise in this narrow circumstance despite consecutive Closed Periods.

topic: hedging ban limited to unvested/locked shares
clause: A Restricted Person must not at any time enter a transaction that operates or is intended to operate to limit the economic risk of holdings of unvested securities of the Company or vested securities of the Company which are subject to holding locks.
why_it_matters: The express hedging prohibition does not reach vested, unrestricted shares, so a collar over such shares is not banned outright and only needs the ordinary prior clearance under section 7, materially improving feasibility versus policies with a blanket hedging ban.

clause: A Restricted Person is prohibited from including securities in the Company in a margin lending arrangement.
why_it_matters: The funded collar's loan leg cannot be structured as a margin loan; it must instead be framed as a different form of secured lending to fall within the more flexible case-by-case regime in 8.1(g).

clause: On a case-by-case basis the Board will assess the rules that are applicable to Relevant Persons with respect to entering into agreements that provide lenders with rights over their interests in the Company's securities.
why_it_matters: This is the most plausible route for the bank's loan and any enforcement sale, but it requires bespoke, discretionary Board sign-off rather than a pre-set clearance process, and provides no certainty of outcome.

clause: A Restricted Person must not at any time enter a transaction ... (6.15); A Restricted Person is prohibited from including securities ... (6.17)
why_it_matters: Section 2 defines only 'Relevant Person' and 'Connected Person'; the undefined term 'Restricted Person' used for the hedging and margin-loan bans creates interpretive uncertainty that should be clarified with the Company Secretary before relying on any narrower reading of scope.

clause: Directors should also be aware of the substantial holder provisions contained in section 671B of the Corporations Act which require certain notices to be served on the Company and the ASX when a person and their associates have a relevant interest in at least 5% of the issued voting shares in the Company and any change of more than 1% to those relevant interests occurs.
why_it_matters: A collar or loan that changes a director's relevant interest by more than 1% (where holdings exceed 5%) triggers separate substantial holder notice obligations outside the Trading Policy's own clearance regime.

clause: If a waiver is refused, the Relevant person must keep that confidential.
why_it_matters: If clearance for the collar is refused under the exceptional-circumstances process, the executive cannot disclose that refusal, limiting the ability to renegotiate timing openly with the bank.

clause: If approval to deal in the Company's securities is granted, the dealing must be conducted within five business days from the date of approval (or such other period of time as specified by the Approver). If the Relevant Person does not deal in securities within this time period, the approval will lapse.
why_it_matters: The put/call trade and loan drawdown must be completed within 5 business days of approval (unless the Approver extends this), or fresh clearance must be obtained.
